title: Keep traced fields of stack-backed classes alive
description: Caxecraft's Castle Underworks to Forge Archive transition triggers a collector pass while a nonescaping stack-backed RuntimeVoxelModelCatalog remains live. Its Array<RuntimeVoxelModel> field is collector-managed, but the generated C roots neither the stack owner nor that traced field. The collector reclaims the live Array; the next RuntimeVoxelModelCatalog.find aborts in hxc_array_ref_length/get. Fix the reusable class representation/lifetime rule, not Caxecraft.
acceptance_criteria: A focused ordinary-Haxe fixture is red before the fix: one long-lived nonescaping local class owns Array<ManagedNode>, a helper allocates enough objects to force collection, and a later method still reads the original entries. Pinned Eval is the behavior oracle. Generated HxcIR/C must keep all collector-managed fields reachable for the exact stack-object lifetime, or conservatively promote the owner class to managed(gc); strict C, forced collection, and ASan/UBSan pass. Existing stack-class and Array<Class> behavior remains deterministic. The unchanged Underworks-to-Forge runtime path crosses the old crash and retains its representative content journey.
notes:
Pre-fix flagship red: live Caxecraft agent played Castle Underworks through the coolant relay, opened underworks.archive-gate, then crossed zone.archive-antechamber. Native macOS process aborted. Crash report caxecraft-2026-08-12-063510.ips points to RuntimeVoxelModelCatalog_find -> draw -> StatefulObjectRenderer after the Forge Archive handoff. Generated C stack-allocates RuntimeVoxelModelCatalog while its Array<RuntimeVoxelModel> is collector-managed; that field is not an exact root. Independent expected behavior comes from ordinary Haxe object-field reachability and will be checked under pinned Eval plus a forced native collection.
Root cause confirmed: a stack-backed Haxe class could retain a collector-managed Array field without an exact root, so a later collection reclaimed the live field. The focused pre-fix generated program hung after collection pressure for the intended reason; the Haxe Eval oracle exited 0. The compiler now conservatively promotes such containing classes to collector-managed storage, reusing normal trace descriptors. Verification: npm run test:array-runtime passed Haxe Eval, deterministic split/package/unity generation, strict Clang native execution, and sanitizer lanes. The original Caxecraft Underworks-to-Forge transition remains the separate product proof.
close_reason: Fixed the reusable class-field lifetime rule; focused native and sanitizer evidence passes.

title: Lower nullable Bytes locals with explicit ownership
description:
Why

The canonical Caxecraft ZIP exporter naturally holds an optional asset-inventory byte buffer while it scans a validated package manifest. Eval accepts the Null<Bytes> local, but haxe.c rejects its null initializer before generating C, blocking the Haxe-authored export path.

What

Admit the smallest sound Null<Bytes> local/flow slice without encoding null as an empty buffer or changing Caxecraft to compiler-shaped sentinel state.

How

Extend the existing managed Bytes representation and HxcIR ownership model with explicit null identity. Cover initialization, assignment from a borrowed/fresh Bytes value, null checks, proven non-null use, branch joins, replacement cleanup, and function-exit cleanup. Reuse target-owned typed operations and structural CAST; do not special-case Caxecraft or erase ownership.
acceptance_criteria: A focused ordinary-Haxe Bytes fixture is red first for TConst(TNull:requires-nullable-reference-or-direct-optional-context); Eval and generated strict C agree for null initialization, non-null assignment, null equality, guarded use, fresh/borrowed assignment, replacement, branch joins, and cleanup; null is observably distinct from Bytes.alloc(0); HxcIR validates explicit nullable Bytes state and rejects unproved use or wrong lifecycle; generated C is structural and deterministic; ASan/UBSan and allocation accounting show no leak, double release, or use-after-free; neighboring Bytes/String/Array/HxcIR suites pass; the unchanged Caxecraft package-zip-export tracer advances beyond the null initializer.
notes:
Intended product red: npm run test:caxecraft-package-zip-export reaches ContentPackageZipExport.hx:94 and fails with HXC1001 TConst(TNull:requires-nullable-reference-or-direct-optional-context). Haxe Eval already passes the complete 9,488,899-byte deterministic ZIP round trip, so the format/data behavior is not the failure.
Focused pre-fix red (2026-08-02): node_modules/.bin/haxe -cp test/differential/bytes-runtime/generated -lib reflaxe.c -main Main -D hxc_project_layout=split --custom-target c=/tmp/haxe-c-null-bytes-focused-red exits 1 at Main.hx:142 on `var optional:Null<Bytes> = null` with HXC1001 TConst(TNull:requires-nullable-reference-or-direct-optional-context). The same fixture passes twice under the pinned Eval oracle, so the expected ordinary-Haxe behavior is independently established.
Second focused red (2026-08-02): after the null-storage owner became green, the unchanged exporter advanced to ContentPackageZipExport.hx:114 and failed on `assetInventoryBytes == null ? Bytes.alloc(0) : assetInventoryBytes` with HXC1001 TIf(result-type:haxe-bytes-reference). The reduced ordinary-Haxe fixture command `node_modules/.bin/haxe -cp test/differential/bytes-runtime/generated -lib reflaxe.c -main Main -D hxc_project_layout=split --custom-target c=/tmp/haxe-c-null-bytes-conditional-red` exits 1 at Main.hx:163 for the same reason. Expected behavior: the false branch borrows the proven-present optional payload, the true branch moves a fresh empty Bytes owner, and the join yields exactly one owner; pinned Eval is the semantic oracle.
Green evidence (2026-08-02):
- npm run test:bytes-runtime: passed pinned Eval twice, validated HxcIR, deterministic generated projects, strict C11 O0/O2, C++17 consumers, native ownership/allocation checks, ASan/UBSan, and selective symbols on Apple Clang; optional gcc was honestly skipped because the installed gcc command identifies as Clang.
- npm run test:hxc-ir, npm run test:body-lowering, npm run test:aggregate-lowering, npm run test:string-runtime, npm run test:array-runtime, npm run test:typed-boundaries, and npm run test:fixture-policy all passed.
- The unchanged vertical owner npm run test:caxecraft-package-zip-export advanced beyond both intended compiler reds and passed Eval, generated strict native C, and sanitizers for the complete 9,488,899-byte archive. End-to-end observed time was 113.92s; the case uses a bounded 120s native-observer timeout because the former shared 20s cutoff expired during linear full-package hashing/copying.

Independent oracle/provenance: pinned Haxe Eval owns Null<Bytes> identity and conditional behavior; manually authored HxcIR assertions own explicit tagged state and exactly-one ownership flow; the target-owned allocator counters plus ASan/UBSan own native lifetime failures; Caxecraft's unchanged authored package scenario is the real product-boundary observer. No expected value is generated by haxe.c.

Distinct high-risk review: assertion sensitivity, oracle independence, negative lifecycle cases, real/native boundaries, selector ownership, scorecard separation, and claim scope were challenged. One accepted finding showed that the optional helper initially named only a digest, so HxcIR could prove a helper was well formed without proving it belonged to Bytes. The implementation now names the bytes lifecycle family, and a negative fixture changes only that family and fails with HXC9000. No mocks replaced the compiler/runtime boundary; compiler-admitted-slices and runtime-memory-lifetime scorecards were updated independently. ABI and portability claims remain unchanged.

Implemented scope is deliberately local storage whose erased Bytes type still has a written null initializer, plus proven unwrap/replacement and Bytes conditional joins. Nullable Bytes parameters, returns, fields, and other erased-null storage shapes remain unsupported rather than inferred from this green slice.
close_reason: Implemented explicit nullable Bytes local ownership and Bytes conditional joins with focused Eval/HxcIR/native/sanitizer proof; the unchanged Caxecraft exporter now crosses the real boundary. Broader nullable storage shapes remain unsupported.

title: Carry managed Bytes across compiler-generated switch joins
description:
Why

The natural ZIP-source probe binds a Bytes result from a value-producing switch whose failure arm returns early. Pinned Haxe rewrites that expression as an empty compiler temporary plus assignments. haxe.c recognizes this carrier shape, but its managed carrier family omits haxe.io.Bytes and tries to invent a direct default, failing with HXC1001 result-type-without-direct-default.

What

Admit reference-counted Bytes in the existing compiler-generated managed flow-carrier protocol. This is the same ownership shape already proved for String and Array, not a ZIP or Caxecraft special case.

How

Add Bytes to carrier recognition, exact runtime retain/destroy selection, fresh-versus-borrowed acquisition, move materialization, local cleanup ownership, and runtime-feature reasons. Keep explicit source uninitialized Bytes locals, read-before-acquire, duplicate moves, incomplete branches, and unsupported failure edges closed.
acceptance_criteria: A minimal ordinary-Haxe fixture binds a value-producing switch to Bytes with one successful branch and one early-return branch and is recorded red with the exact result-type-without-direct-default diagnostic; Eval and generated strict C agree for fresh and borrowed Bytes arms, selected-arm order, later repeated reads, return/argument use, and early return; HxcIR declares one bytes managed carrier, every rejoining arm acquires exactly one owner, the first read moves it into one cleanup-owned local, and native ASan/UBSan show no leak, double release, or use-after-free; malformed read-before-acquire, duplicate move, incomplete join, and authored uninitialized Bytes remain fail closed; existing String, Array, record, enum, bytes-runtime, control-flow, deterministic layout, and full backstop owners pass; the unmodified ZIP-source probe advances beyond this diagnostic.
notes:
Intended real-tracer red (2026-08-02): `npm run test:caxecraft-package-zip-source` failed during Haxe-to-C lowering at ContentPackageZipSourceProbe.hx:166-169. HXC1001 rejected `TVar(equalArchive:flow-carrier)(result-type-without-direct-default)`. Eval passes the same source. Source inspection shows managedFlowCarrier and managedCarrierImplementation omit localMapping.bytesValue(), while ordinary Bytes locals already have exact retain/release and fresh-owner tracking.
Focused red (2026-08-02): after adding the minimal BytesChoice fixture to the existing bytes-runtime owner, `haxe oracle.hxml` passed. `haxe -cp . -lib reflaxe.c -main Main -D hxc_project_layout=split --custom-target c=<temp>` then exited 1 at Main.hx:106-110. The source joins one borrowed or fresh Bytes arm while Missing returns early, then passes and rereads the selected value. This reproduces the Caxecraft failure without ZIP code.
Green and distinct review (2026-08-02): test:bytes-runtime passes Eval, generated strict C11 O0/O2, C++17 header consumers, exact HxcIR ownership markers, allocation rollback, sanitizers, and selective symbols. The unchanged test:caxecraft-package-zip-source tracer now passes with identity=105070, direct payload bytes=42943, and 31 archive rejection scenarios. Added a direct valid HxcIR Bytes carrier plus a malformed runtime(string) variant; test:hxc-ir now rejects the wrong destroy and both wrong retains with exact bytes-runtime diagnostics. test:string-runtime, test:array-runtime, test:aggregate-lowering, test:enum-lowering, test:function-lowering, test:project-layout, test:fixture-policy, and test:all-sources pass. The lowering-objects shard stopped only because borrowed_forward expected a later safe-rejection detail; an isolated git archive of HEAD produced the same earlier TNew(stack-reference-escape:static-call-argument:0,target=function.Main.forward), proving stale baseline expectation rather than this patch. The corrected negative-only owner passes. The Caxecraft shard passed ZIP, package, content generation, runtime loader, campaign runtime, and all later focused owners; it stopped only on expected full-domain snapshot drift from the simultaneously in-progress ZIP/package source. The owned snapshot update was semantically reviewed and validated across Eval, split/package/unity, O2 native, 32 properties, and zero-runtime expectations. title: Retain private inline C-import declarations
description:
## Why
Caxecraft's natural typed Raylib/Raygui adapters use module-private extern helpers to give an existing C text function an explicit c.CStringRef signature. Haxe inlines the public facade call, but haxe.c's retained TypedProgramInput omits the private helper declaration while the C-import contract still references it, so the real playable fails with source-positioned HXC3000: The retained typed declaration is missing.

## What
Retain the smallest declaration and field facts required by a reached private extern direct-C call after Haxe inlining/DCE. Preserve private source visibility and existing direct-import validation; do not expose the helper publicly, weaken missing-contract failures, or claim general private-type support.

## Scenario
Given a public inline Haxe facade whose body directly calls a module-private extern function with c.CStringRef, when an application calls the facade with runtime text, then haxe.c retains the exact private declaration, validates the direct C ABI, emits the checked call-scoped string borrow, and the native observer receives the expected bytes. A truly missing or unreachable declaration must still fail closed.
design: Fix retention at the typed-program/C-import seam. Preserve enough typed declaration identity before DCE or recover it from an authoritative typed source already captured by the compiler; do not reconstruct function types from strings or relax requireDeclaration globally. Keep the private helper absent from generated public Haxe/C API while its reached imported call contributes normal include, ABI, symbol, and lifetime facts.
acceptance_criteria: Record the current Caxecraft HXC3000 command and source position as red evidence; add a minimal ordinary-Haxe fixture with a module-private extern helper reached only through an inline facade; use an independent native text observer as oracle; make split and unity strict C builds pass with the checked CStringRef borrow and exact private helper C symbol; retain negatives for genuinely missing declarations and invalid CStringRef escape/retention; keep public direct imports, static c.CString, and Caxecraft generated-binding checks unchanged; rerun the real Caxecraft playable compile far enough to pass this former HXC3000 boundary.
notes:
RED 2026-08-02: npm run test:caxecraft-playable fails during Haxe-to-C compilation at examples/caxecraft/src/caxecraft/app/CaxecraftApp.hx:1305 on drawUiText(uiCatalog, ...) with HXC3000: The retained typed declaration is missing. The reached inline path is CaxecraftApp.drawUiText -> Raylib.DrawTextString -> module-private extern RaylibRuntimeText.drawText(c.CStringRef,...). The focused c.CStringRef native oracle itself passes; this failure is declaration retention, not string-borrow semantics.
GREEN 2026-08-02: Root cause was declaration identity, not missing type retention: Haxe records a private secondary extern under an internal _Module path while typed C contracts and reached references use the authored module path. CImportRegistry now indexes the same retained typed declaration under both identities. A second intended red appeared after that fix: Caxecraft imports DrawText through static c.CString and checked c.CStringRef views, which previously collided. Compatible external-function aliases now share one C symbol only after their lowered C ABI signatures match; an Int/Bool mismatch remains fail-closed with HXC3000. Independent oracle: manually authored text_observer.c compares exact bytes, and the fixture runs split/unity strict native builds plus sanitizers. Review assertions prove two calls use one external symbol request and private Haxe helper names do not enter generated C headers. Green commands: python3 test/differential/string-runtime/run.py --toolchain clang; npm run test:typed-c; npm run test:c-import; npm run test:hxc-ir; npm run test:typed-boundaries; npm run test:caxecraft-playable. The playable now passes its former HXC3000 boundary and registered snapshots. Host contention made elapsed times unsuitable for performance claims.
close_reason: Private inline C imports retain their typed declaration, compatible lifetime views share one proven C ABI symbol, focused/native negatives pass, and Caxecraft passes the former compiler boundary.

title: Borrow owned Haxe String for one C text call
description:
## Why
Caxecraft now loads UI text as validated runtime Haxe String values, but direct C imports accept c.CString only from static literals. The playable renderer therefore cannot consume runtime catalog text without retaining the obsolete generated-literal authority or crossing an unmodeled native lifetime boundary.

## What
Add the smallest reusable typed carrier that lends an owned or borrowed Haxe String to exactly one direct imported const-char consumer. Preserve the String owner through the call, reject embedded NUL before the native function runs, and keep static c.CString behavior unchanged.

## Scenario
Given validated runtime UI text, when the app draws it through Raylib, then the native call observes the exact UTF-8 bytes and the Haxe String remains alive for the call only. Given text containing embedded NUL, the call fails closed and the native consumer is not invoked.
design: Model an explicit call-scoped immutable CString borrow rather than widening implicit String-to-c.CString conversion. Reuse managed String length/byte storage and typed HxcIR lifetime/cleanup. The carrier must be accepted only as a direct import argument, cannot be stored, returned, or retained, and must distinguish validation failure from a legitimate empty string. Add focused ordinary-Haxe and native oracle fixtures before resuming Caxecraft integration.
acceptance_criteria: A focused test is red for the current missing carrier; Eval/manual expectations and a native observer agree for empty, ASCII, non-ASCII, borrowed, and fresh Strings; embedded NUL prevents the imported call; HxcIR proves owner-tied call scope and exact cleanup; escape, wrong-carrier, missing-intrinsic, and parameter-kind negatives fail closed; static c.CString and mutable CStringBufferRef suites remain unchanged; Caxecraft can pass RuntimeUiCatalog text to Raylib without generated literals or raw C; strict C11, sanitizers, HxcIR, typed-boundary, capability, and relevant full backstops pass.
notes:
RED 2026-08-02: HAXE_NO_SERVER=1 node_modules/.bin/haxe -cp test/differential/string-runtime/native_text -lib reflaxe.c -main Main -D hxc_runtime_diagnostics=off --custom-target c=<temp>/out reported Type not found : c.CStringRef at TextObserver.hx:12 and Main.hx:26. This is the intended pre-fix failure: ordinary runtime String has no explicit call-scoped immutable C-text carrier yet. Independent expectations are manually authored UTF-8 byte arrays in native/text_observer.c; no expected value is generated by haxe.c.
GREEN 2026-08-02: The explicit c.CStringRef.to(text) carrier now lowers one owned/static Haxe String through string/borrow-cstring to exactly one direct non-retaining native argument in the same basic block. The emitter keeps the owner live, calls hxc_string_borrow_cstring, and exposes only the validated data pointer; HxcIR rejects storage, return/edge escape, missing checked producer, and parameter-carrier construction. Static c.CString literals and mutable c.CStringBufferRef remain separate contracts.

Tracer/oracle: test/differential/string-runtime/native_text compiles ordinary Haxe through haxe.c, strict native C, hxrt, and the real C observer. Manually authored UTF-8 byte arrays in native/text_observer.c independently cover empty, ASCII, Unicode, caller-borrowed, suffix-view, and fresh runtime Strings. No expectation is generated by haxe.c.

Distinct safety review: embedded NUL and an interior non-NUL-terminated substring both abort before the C observer; source negatives reject escaping the carrier and a non-String owner; HxcIR negatives reject invented and parameter-carried values. The review found the missing interior-view case and added it. No mocked boundary, implicit String widening, retained pointer, snapshot-only semantic oracle, or broadened general FFI claim remains.

Verified: python3 test/differential/string-runtime/run.py --toolchain clang; npm run test:hxc-ir; npm run test:runtime-features; npm run test:c-import; npm run test:typed-boundaries; npm run test:capabilities; npm run format:haxe:check; npm run test:string-output; npm run test:static-initialization; npm run test:virtual-dispatch; npm run test:body-lowering; npm run test:function-lowering; npm run test:arithmetic-semantics; npm run test:aggregate-lowering; git diff --check. The compiler capability is complete; the parent Bead still owns wiring RuntimeUiCatalog through Raylib and removing generated Caxecraft content authority.
close_reason: Implemented in 240dd62. The independent native UTF-8 observer, fail-before-C negative cases, strict C/C++, sanitizers, and focused string-runtime suite pass on the current checkout. RuntimeUiCatalog/Raylib integration remains owned by parent haxe_c-xge.20.4.3.8.

title: Publish complete Caxecraft runtime content atomically
description:
## Why
The repository can now construct one verified pack/UI/map owner, but Caxecraft still discards it and publishes a map-only LoadedContentGeneration built with BaseContentRegistry. Runtime registry and catalog lifetime therefore are not tied to the active game generation.

## What
Add one complete active owner that publishes RuntimeContentGeneration atomically, exposes only call-bounded session/registry/catalog views, rejects older or duplicate complete candidates, and keeps the previous generation usable after a failed load or publication.

## Scenario
Given verified generation 1 is active, when malformed generation 2 fails before candidate construction or a duplicate/older complete candidate is offered, then generation 1 retains the same identity, registry proof, UI text, and world-state trace. When a valid generation 2 is published, all four observations switch together exactly once.

## Oracle
Generation ordering comes from ContentGenerationId. Pack proof, reviewed UI text, and CaxeMap world-state expectations are independently owned by the existing runtime schema and level probes. The publication test manually records the combined before/after observations and must not derive them from the active owner implementation.
design: Wrap the complete immutable candidate rather than widening the lower map-only publication owner. Candidate construction receives no active state. Validate ordering and construct the result before one non-failing reference assignment. Product code borrows one complete RuntimeContentGeneration snapshot per operation and derives registry, catalog, level/session, and receipt from that object; a retained snapshot truthfully remains the retired generation after publication. Keep the fast owner scenario on Eval and extend the existing real package-generation native tracer with one successful swap plus old and duplicate rejection, so the complete package graph is compiled only once. Renderer managed String to c.CString borrowing remains a separate compiler boundary if natural app integration exposes it.
acceptance_criteria: A focused Eval/native owner records an intended missing-owner red; one ActiveRuntimeContent or equivalently cohesive owner retains the complete RuntimeContentGeneration; failed load and out-of-order publication preserve the previous generation; successful publication swaps level, registry, catalog, and receipt identity together; the app startup can consume the complete owner without BaseContentRegistry in its runtime-load path; lower map-only ActiveContent tests remain independent; no renderer CString workaround, generated authority deletion, timeout increase, or public claim broadening is introduced.
notes:
2026-08-01 correction and vertical/app evidence: native does not load the package twice. Eval loads two real complete candidates; generated native loads one verified real package and uses a test-only owner-module helper to rebuild only a distinct generation-2 level/session from the same immutable registry, catalog, plan, presentation, and receipt. The isolated exact Haxe-to-C pass selected the expected 13-feature closure and completed in 108.59s while aggregate host CPU remained roughly 900-1100%; the unchanged official 60s frontend bound therefore still times out on this saturated host. Reusing that single artifact, strict native and ASan/UBSan both emitted 0,2,132089,3528,-1715484850,18389; strict runtime was 9.80s and sanitized runtime 4.01s under the unchanged 20s observer. CaxecraftApp now opens the staged complete package, calls loadRuntimeContent, constructs ActiveRuntimeContent, borrows one coherent RuntimeContentGeneration, and derives the initial session from its level before Raylib. C-target type checking and the durable application source boundary pass; the app runtime-load path no longer constructs BaseContentRegistry or ActiveContent. Generated BaseContentPack gameplay consumers and generated UiCatalog rendering remain intentionally owned by haxe_c-xge.20.4.3.8, so live renderer publication and arbitrary package claims remain false.
2026-08-01 final targeted review and disposition: removed the redundant standalone generation-ID getter so product callers must derive all claim-bearing views from one RuntimeContentGeneration snapshot. Focused and native probes now assert the exact offered candidate became active and differs from the retained retired candidate, in addition to independent pack/UI/world/receipt observations. Negative coverage retains malformed load, older candidate, and duplicate candidate; no parser, package-store, native compiler, or application boundary is mocked. Selector review maps the fast owner only to runtime-memory-lifetime and preserves the existing generation tracer across compiler, ABI/native, runtime, and downstream scorecards. Final exact Haxe-to-C generation selected 13 features for 7520 typed roots in 80.29s under sustained host contention; reused strict and ASan/UBSan runs emitted 0,2,132089,3528,-1715484850,18389 in 7.26s and 2.98s. The formatted Linux full-detail playable render completed in 84.62s, passed generated-playable validation, matched all 54 registered snapshots, called RuntimeContentGeneration_loadRuntimeContent exactly once, retained ActiveRuntimeContent, and contained no BaseContentRegistry or map-only ActiveContent startup construction. Governance passed 222 tests, all-sources passed 220 modules, six changed Haxe files and the full 798-file formatter guard passed, the pilot/source boundary passed, and focused publication measured 1.08s cold-process / 0.80s immediate repeat. haxe_c-xge.20.4.3.7.5 owns restoring the unchanged official 60s frontend budget on representative load; haxe_c-xge.20.4.3.8 still owns generated gameplay/UI authority removal. Public claims remain unchanged.

title: Admit core Array construction and primitive compound update
description:
## Why
The pinned haxe.crypto.Sha256 implementation begins with `new Array<Int>()` and updates words with indexed `|=`. haxe.c already admitted typed empty literals, checked Array reads, primitive bitwise operations, and typed writes, but these two ordinary source spellings did not reach those existing semantic owners.

## What
Admit the exact zero-argument core Array<T> constructor as the existing empty managed Array operation, and admit indexed compound assignment only for primitive Array elements as an ordered checked read, typed primitive operation, and typed set. This does not admit arbitrary generic classes or authored uninitialized locals.
design: Recognize only TNew of the root core Array class with zero arguments after the closed Array<T> representation has been prepared. Lower it through the same create-literal path as [] so allocation failure, fresh-owner tracking, collector/reference-counted selection, and runtime feature planning remain identical. Add focused ordinary-Haxe source evidence; retain generic-class constructor negatives for every other class.
acceptance_criteria: The ordinary-Haxe Array fixture is red first at new Array<Int>() and then at values[0] |= 1 for the recorded reasons; Eval and native results agree; HxcIR records typed empty creation, exact owner cleanup, checked get, bitwise operation, and typed set; Array<Int> and Array<String> construction preserve their respective lifetimes; strict generated C, sanitizers, deterministic discovery/server output, traced Array<Class> neighbors, and existing negative cases pass; arbitrary generic-class construction and general authored uninitialized locals remain fail closed and are not claimed.
notes:
Red evidence (2026-08-01): `node_modules/.bin/haxe -cp test/differential/array-runtime/generated -lib reflaxe.c -main Main -D hxc_project_layout=split --custom-target c=<tmp>` exited 1 at Main.hx:75 `new Array<Int>()` with HXC1001 `TNew(generic-class-constructor-requires-specialization:Array)`. No generated project was accepted. Expected reason: core generic Array construction reaches nominal generic-class construction instead of the already-admitted typed empty-Array owner path. Independent behavior oracle is pinned Haxe Eval; HxcIR/runtime ownership is checked by the existing Array suite.
Second red after empty construction lowered (2026-08-01): the same focused fixture then failed at `values[0] |= 1` with HXC1001 `TArray(collection-local-outside-admitted-slice:values)`, matching Sha256.bytes2blks. This narrows the remaining capability to primitive Array indexed compound assignment. Implementation must evaluate receiver/index/RHS once in Haxe order, use checked get plus typed set, and remain closed for managed elements.
Green evidence (2026-08-01): `npm run test:array-runtime` passed in 302.22s under the pinned Eval oracle, Clang strict C11, ASan/UBSan, deterministic and warm-server renders, allocation-failure/lifecycle rollback, and traced Array<Class> backstops. Caxecraft advanced through empty construction and indexed compound update, then stopped at the separate TVar(a:uninitialized) boundary now owned by haxe_c-0h4.4.
close_reason: Closed

title: Propagate static-call ownership requirements
description:
## Why
Caxecraft passes a LevelContentResolver interface through RuntimeLevelLoader into ScenarioValidator. ScenarioValidator stores that interface in a short-lived validation context. The inner parameter therefore owns the interface for that object lifetime, but the outer static helper was initially labeled as a borrow because its own body only forwarded the value. Native lowering then correctly rejected a borrowed value being passed to an owning parameter.

## What
Propagate direct static-call ownership requirements backward through the named call graph before HxcIR lowering. A read-only helper stays borrowed. A helper that forwards to a retaining callee becomes owning, as do earlier forwarding helpers, so the original caller keeps the concrete object alive for the complete retained use.
design: Start with each parameter own-body proof, then run a monotonic fixed point over direct non-generic static calls. The pass may only revoke a borrow; it never creates one. Constructor/default initialization begins absent; field reads borrow or copy with exact presence guarding; replacement captures/retains the new optional before destroying the previous present payload and is self-assignment safe; class destruction releases a present payload exactly once. Preserve the existing optional lifecycle registry as the single retain/destroy authority, HxcIR ownership facts, source evaluation order, and selective runtime planning. Do not turn the record into a class, split its fields into parser-specific scalars, box all optionals, or special-case Caxecraft.
acceptance_criteria: A focused ordinary-Haxe fixture owns a mutable Null<Record> class field where the record contains a managed enum/String path. It covers default absent state, present assignment, read/match, replacement, self-assignment/aliasing where expressible, clearing to null, early return, and owner destruction. Eval and generated C agree. HxcIR and generated C show the existing tagged optional plus presence-guarded retain/destroy; strict GCC/Clang C11 O0/O2 and ASan/UBSan show no leak, double release, or use-after-free; malformed ownership fails closed; split/package/unity and deterministic output pass. The real Caxecraft content-json probe compiles without changing its typed parser model.
notes: Implemented the general nullable managed-record class-field path. The fix distinguishes object-owned fields reached through a borrowed receiver from the borrowed object itself, settles direct managed enum payload facts before enclosing records consume them, and recognizes StringBuf.toString as a runtime String creator. The focused fixture covers absent/present/replacement/clear, nested result-enum discovery, managed String retain/release, layouts, warm server, C++ layout, and sanitizers. HxcIR, typed-boundary, and formatting gates pass. The unmodified parser model now advances beyond the class-field audit to a distinct owned-class result transfer at ContentJson.parse, tracked separately as haxe_c-djl.22. Local focused native evidence used the available Clang toolchain; the repository CI remains the independent GCC lane.
close_reason: Nullable managed diagnostic records now work in ordinary class fields with exact enum/record/optional/String lifecycle and borrowed-receiver field ownership. Focused Eval/native/layout/server/sanitizer evidence passes; Caxecraft advances to separately owned haxe_c-djl.22.

title: Make exhaustive switch result initialization visible to strict GCC
description: GNU GCC 16.1 rejects Caxecraft generated C with -Werror=maybe-uninitialized for values assigned by exhaustive Haxe enum switches. Eval and Clang accept the source, but generated C does not make the impossible-tag path explicit enough for GCC dataflow. Fix general HxcIR/CAST switch-result lowering so every C path either assigns the result or terminates through a typed fail-stop/unreachable edge. Do not initialize Caxecraft locals speculatively or weaken warnings. Add a minimized enum-switch result fixture, strict GCC/Clang evidence, sanitizer behavior, deterministic C inspection, and the Caxecraft runtime-level-loader integration proof.
close_reason: Exhaustive Haxe tag switches remain semantically default-free in HxcIR, while C projection emits a fail-stop default and inert zeroed join storage. The full enum owner and all 105 Caxecraft translation units pass strict Homebrew GCC 16.1 at O2; Clang link evidence passes.

title: Keep generated locals distinct from compiler-owned C typedef names
description: GNU GCC 16.1 rejects generated C when an ordinary Haxe parameter or local named status becomes hxc_status while a selected runtime header defines typedef hxc_status. Clang did not diagnose this. Fix the compiler naming boundary so source locals and parameters are deterministically disambiguated from visible compiler/runtime-owned ordinary C identifiers. Do not rename Caxecraft source or add raw-C workarounds. Add a focused runtime-using fixture, strict GCC/Clang -Wshadow -Werror evidence, deterministic generated-name checks, and the Caxecraft native runtime-level-loader integration proof.
close_reason: Ordinary Haxe locals and parameters now use the distinct hxc_l_ namespace. Symbol, String-output, enum, and full 105-translation-unit Caxecraft generated C pass strict Homebrew GCC 16.1; Clang product linking also passes.

title: Admit receiver-tied spans from rooted collector-managed classes
description:
## Why

The native content-generation owner makes GameSession collector-managed. Its existing `worldView()` method still returns the same read-only span into receiver-owned fixed storage, but HxcIR validation currently requires the receiver to appear in the stack-borrow list. A collector-managed receiver is instead protected by an exact managed root, so the old check rejects a safe natural program.

## What

Extend the existing receiver-field borrowed-span contract to accept either a caller-owned borrowed class parameter or an exact directly rooted collector-managed class parameter. Keep the immediate receiver-field origin, read-only result, one-return, direct-call owner resolution, and nonescaping consumption checks unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: A focused schema-23 HxcIR program with a collector-managed class receiver, exact direct managed root, immediate fixed-array field borrow, and read-only span return validates; removing the root or borrowing a local still fails with a stable diagnostic; the existing stack-borrowed receiver contract remains valid; Caxecraft `GameSession.worldView()` compiles when GameSession is owned by LoadedContentGeneration; generated root/frame and span lifetime evidence passes without extending span escape or using raw C.
notes: Schema-23 HxcIR now accepts a receiver-tied read-only span only when the collector-managed receiver has the exact direct root; removing that root remains a stable negative and the existing stack-borrowed contract still passes. The full HxcIR owner passes, Caxecraft compiles with LoadedContentGeneration owning GameSession, and the native runtime-level-loader plus sanitizer suite exercises worldView without raw C or broader span escape.
close_reason: Exact rooted collector-receiver span contract, stable negative, existing borrowed receiver compatibility, HxcIR owner, Caxecraft integration, and sanitizer evidence all pass without expanding span escape.

title: Stabilize fresh managed record receivers before field projection
description:
## Why

The native Caxecraft application naturally reads a field from a managed record returned by a method: `plan.player().transform`. haxe.c projects the field but leaves the fresh outer record owner unconsumed until function finalization rejects it. Rewriting the application to expose one method per field would shape its API around a compiler gap.

## What

Give a fresh managed record receiver one compiler-owned lifetime before field projection. The field read borrows from that stable owner, while normal and failure exits destroy the outer record exactly once through its prepared lifecycle plan. Preserve direct-record and already-owned local reads without added retain/release.
acceptance_criteria: A focused ordinary Haxe fixture projects a direct field from a freshly returned managed record; Eval/native results match; the receiver expression runs exactly once; HxcIR names one stable owner and typed cleanup; generated strict C destroys the outer record exactly once on normal and applicable failure exits; borrowed/local and unmanaged record field reads remain byte-stable or prove no redundant ownership work; the natural Caxecraft `plan.player().transform` expression compiles without a wrapper or raw C.
notes: Implemented fresh managed-record receiver stabilization before field projection. The focused managed-record constructor fixture now covers buildReading().reading, proves one evaluation and exactly-once lifecycle cleanup under Eval/native strict local Clang C11 and sanitizers, and the natural Caxecraft plan.player().transform expression compiles. The complete native runtime-level-loader suite also passes. The local gcc command identifies as Clang, so real-GCC CI evidence remains before closure.
close_reason: Implemented fresh managed-record receiver stabilization. The focused managed-record constructor owner passes Homebrew GCC 16.1 O0/O2, sanitizers, deterministic module order, exact ownership cleanup, and the natural plan.player().transform consumer.

title: Lower typed runtime String values through Sys.println
description:
## Why

Caxecraft runtime content loading must report the selected logical path, input hash, and generation ID from values computed after startup. haxe.c currently lowers only literal Sys.println calls even though hxrt already accepts a borrowed hxc_string. A Caxecraft-only raw-C logger would hide this ordinary Haxe gap.

## What

Admit Sys.println for statically typed String expressions while preserving the existing literal fast path. Lower the expression exactly once, keep a fresh managed String alive through the hosted output call, run its typed cleanup on normal and output-failure exits, and reject non-String or dynamic shapes.

## Scope

This bounded slice does not add arbitrary Dynamic printing, trace formatting for runtime values, exception recovery, or a new runtime ABI. It reuses hxc_io_println and the existing String ownership model.
acceptance_criteria: Borrowed and freshly constructed typed String arguments print exact UTF-8 bytes under Eval and generated native C; argument evaluation occurs exactly once; fresh managed owners are released exactly once after success and on native-status failure; literal Sys.println output and artifacts remain unchanged; non-String/Dynamic arguments remain fail-closed; runtime selection and HxcIR validation distinguish the runtime-String operation; Caxecraft provenance reporting compiles without raw C or target-specific application code.
notes: Implemented typed runtime-String Sys.println while preserving the literal fast path. The focused string-output suite passes Eval/native exact bytes, one-time evaluation, success and fail-stop cleanup, HxcIR/runtime-plan distinctions, diagnostics, deterministic rendering, strict local Clang C11 O0/O2, and sanitizer coverage. The runtime feature graph and stdlib ledger pass, and Caxecraft now prints runtime provenance without raw C. The local gcc command identifies as Clang, so the identity-distinct real-GCC lane remains CI-required before closure.
close_reason: Implemented typed runtime String Sys.println. The full string-output owner passes Clang and Homebrew GCC 16.1 with exact bytes, one-time evaluation, cleanup, diagnostics, fail-stop I/O, and Caxecraft provenance output.

title: Admit managed conditional results through typed flow carriers
description:
## Why

After fresh managed record constructor arguments were stabilized, the natural Caxecraft runtime loader advanced to its test-only conditional selection between LoadedContentGeneration.build and buildWithFault. Both branches return the same managed payload enum, but haxe.c emits an uninitialized ordinary local for the conditional result. HxcIR validation correctly rejects that local because managed direct values require an explicit managed flow-carrier lifecycle.

## What

Lower a conditional whose result has managed enum, aggregate, optional, Array, Bytes, String, interface, or class ownership through the existing typed flow-carrier protocol appropriate to that value. Preserve left-to-right condition/branch evaluation, initialize exactly one selected branch, and release or transfer ownership exactly once. Keep unproved joins fail-closed.

## How

Minimize the two-call conditional into a focused control-flow/HxcIR fixture. Reuse the existing managed-flow-carrier declaration, branch initialization, move, and cleanup operations instead of declaring an unmanaged direct local or adding a Caxecraft source rewrite.
design: The result local must be selected from CBodyValueType ownership facts before emitting IRISUninitialized. Managed reference-counted values use declare/acquire/move/release; collector-traced values use an exact root or traced aggregate carrier. Each branch transfers its fresh result owner into the same carrier. The join moves one result out, leaving no branch-local owner live. Validate failure and early-return edges as well as normal execution.
acceptance_criteria: A conditional expression selecting between two fresh values of the same managed payload-enum type compiles and matches Eval/native behavior; HxcIR contains a legal managed carrier rather than an uninitialized unmanaged local; exactly one branch result is moved and every nonselected or failed path has balanced cleanup; representative managed aggregate/optional/reference neighbors either share the proved typed rule or retain exact fail-closed diagnostics; strict GCC/Clang C11 O0/O2, ASan/UBSan, deterministic render, and validator negatives pass; the natural Caxecraft RuntimeLevelLoader testing conditional compiles without a source workaround.
close_reason: Implemented collector-bearing tagged-enum conditional carriers while retaining fail-closed neighboring shapes. The full enum owner passes Homebrew GCC 16.1, C++17, sanitizers, all layouts, managed payloads, and the Caxecraft runtime loader.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: Implemented the proved collector-bearing tagged-enum conditional slice. CBodyValueType now recognizes collector payloads; lowering selects a zero-initialized direct enum carrier, HxcIR admits that tagged-enum default initialization, and generated roots follow only the active payload tag. Focused enum evidence passed Eval/native behavior, deterministic layouts, local strict Clang C11/C++17, ASan/UBSan, and generated-shape assertions. The registered HxcIR suite passes with the updated diagnostic. The natural Caxecraft runtime-level-loader integration now passes Eval/native C plus sanitizers without a source workaround. Reference-counted enum carriers remain on their existing move/retain protocol; unproved aggregate/optional/reference neighbors remain fail-closed. Required real GCC evidence remains for CI, so this issue stays open.

title: Terminate complete compiler process trees on bounded test timeouts
description: Focused Haxe subprocesses are launched through the repository's Node/Lix wrapper. Python subprocess.run(timeout=...) terminates the wrapper process, but the real pinned Haxe child can remain alive at 100% CPU. Repeated timeout/retry cycles therefore create hidden contention and make later feedback slower or misleading.
design: Introduce one reusable non-shell command runner that starts an isolated process group/session, captures bounded stdout/stderr, and terminates then force-kills the complete owned process tree on timeout. Preserve exact timeout diagnostics and never signal unrelated compiler servers or processes. Migrate the focused function-lowering path first, then audit equivalent Haxe launch helpers.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture that deliberately exceeds its timeout leaves no wrapper, Haxe child, or descendant process; the diagnostic names the command phase and timeout; successful output and exit handling remain byte-compatible; repeated timeout tests do not increase live process count or host CPU; POSIX and Windows behavior is explicitly implemented/tested; focused suites retain their existing time budgets.

title: Stabilize fresh managed record arguments across constructors
description:
## Why

After mutable parameter lowering let the native Caxecraft map loader progress, haxe.c rejected a fresh RuntimeLevelReceipt record passed to RuntimeLevelCandidate.new. The record owns managed String fields. Constructor argument lowering stabilizes fresh String, Array, and Bytes values, but omits managed record, enum, and optional values, leaving the record owner live in freshManagedAggregateValueIds at function exit.

## What

Admit fresh managed record constructor arguments through the existing typed retain/destroy and cleanup model. Audit the equivalent named-local, unnamed receiver, collector-managed, and super-constructor paths so the same ownership rule does not depend on construction spelling. Keep unsupported ownership shapes fail-closed.

## How

Minimize the RuntimeLevelReceipt shape into a reusable constructor-lowering fixture. Materialize each fresh managed record argument in a caller-owned automatic local before the constructor call, let the constructor retain its independent field/parameter owner, and release the caller temporary on normal and failure paths. Reuse HxcIR retain/release and cleanup actions; add no Caxecraft special case or raw C.
design: Extend the existing stabilizeFreshManagedAggregate path to every compiler-known constructor argument loop that already stabilizes String, Array, and Bytes. Include managed enum and optional neighbors only when the same focused differential proves their identical ownership transfer. Verify evaluation order, exact one-owner transfer/copy, constructor failure cleanup, nested managed fields, and deterministic generated C.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh closed record containing managed String and Array fields can be passed directly to a stack or collector-managed class constructor; Eval/native behavior agrees; HxcIR shows caller-owned stabilization before the call, callee retention when stored, and exactly-once cleanup on success and injected constructor failure; named local, unnamed receiver, managed construction, and super-constructor spellings either share the proved rule or retain exact fail-closed diagnostics; strict GCC/Clang C11 O0/O2, ASan/UBSan, layouts, deterministic renders, and ownership negatives pass; the natural Caxecraft RuntimeLevelCandidate construction compiles without a source workaround.
notes: Implemented the existing stabilizeFreshManagedAggregate rule in every constructor argument loop: named stack construction, immediate receiver, collector-managed construction, super calls, and inline owned-child fields. Added focused success and throwing fixtures with String+Array record fields and a narrow npm test. The focused lane passed Eval, schema-23 HxcIR lifecycle checks, reversed typed-module determinism, strict local Clang C11 O0/O2, ASan/UBSan, and actual failure cleanup. Caxecraft advanced past RuntimeLevelCandidate construction to independent managed conditional-result issue haxe_c-t98x. Managed enum and optional constructor arguments were deliberately left fail-closed because this record differential does not prove those neighboring lifecycles. Full split/package/unity/warm-server integration is registered in the exhaustive constructor suite; real GCC remains CI-required because local gcc identifies as Apple Clang.
close_reason: Implemented fresh managed-record constructor-argument stabilization across the proved spellings. The focused owner passes Homebrew GCC 16.1 O0/O2, sanitizers, success/failure cleanup, deterministic typed-module order, and the RuntimeLevelCandidate consumer.

title: Lower ordinary reassignment of mutable Haxe parameters
description:
## Why

Caxecraft's runtime map loader exposed valid ordinary Haxe that haxe.c rejects: a helper that folds bytes reassigns its Int accumulator parameter inside a loop. The compiler currently emits HXC1001 with parameter-assignment-not-yet-lowered even though local reassignment, parameter reads, and primitive assignment already exist separately.

## What

Admit assignment to mutable function parameters through explicit target-owned mutable storage while preserving Haxe evaluation order, parameter initialization, representation, and ownership. Keep immutable/captured/borrowed or otherwise unsafe parameter shapes fail-closed until their exact ownership rule exists.

## How

Add a minimized Eval/HxcIR/native differential with direct, compound, looped, and value-result parameter assignment. Materialize each assigned parameter into a deterministic mutable local at function entry, route all later reads and writes through that place, and retain the original immutable argument carrier only as the initializer. Validate the HxcIR definition/use and generated strict C shape; do not special-case Caxecraft or rewrite its natural source.
design: Extend the existing captured-parameter shadow-place pattern into a general assigned-parameter local plan. Discover assigned parameter IDs before body lowering, create deterministic locals initialized left-to-right at function entry, and make both lowerValue(TLocal) and lowerPlace(TLocal) resolve the same local. Primitive direct carriers are the first bounded slice; do not introduce raw C or mutate the immutable HxcIR argument value in place.
acceptance_criteria: Direct reassignment of primitive Int and Bool parameters, compound reassignment of primitive Int and Float parameters, repeated loop updates, assignment-expression results, and unchanged read-only neighbors are supported; Eval and generated C agree under strict GCC/Clang C11 at O0/O2 and sanitizers; HxcIR explicitly initializes one mutable local before its first read/write and validator negatives still reject use-before-definition or incompatible assignment; split/package/unity and deterministic render pass; captured managed borrowed optional rest and otherwise unproved parameter mutation remains fail-closed with exact diagnostics; the natural Caxecraft RuntimeLevelLoader hash helper compiles without a source workaround.
notes: Local evidence on 2026-07-30: the registered function-lowering and arithmetic-semantics snapshot owners passed their full Eval, HxcIR, deterministic-render, strict Apple Clang C11 O0/O2, and sanitizer lanes; npm run test:hxc-ir, test:capabilities, and test:typed-boundaries passed. The local gcc executable identifies as Apple Clang, so the independent real-GCC lane remains CI-required. The natural Caxecraft runtime loader advanced past parameter assignment and now stops at the separately owned haxe_c-5mm6 fresh managed-record constructor-argument boundary. During the first run, a wrong Eval oracle caused a deliberate fixture loop to run forever; that expectation was corrected, and haxe_c-5sd.7.4 now owns terminating the complete compiler process tree when a bounded test times out.
close_reason: Implemented typed mutable-parameter storage. The registered function-lowering and arithmetic native matrices pass Homebrew GCC 16.1, including O0/O2, UBSan, strict C11, and the natural RuntimeLevelLoader consumer without a source workaround.

title: Lower child-interface values to parent-interface values
description:
## Why

Ordinary Haxe permits a value typed as an interface to flow to one of that interface's parents. haxe.c currently rejects the conversion because the child fat value carries the child table while the parent value needs the parent table. Caxecraft reaches this with LevelContentResolver -> ActorContentResolver.

## What

Add a closed-world, type-safe child-interface upcast that preserves the concrete object, selects the exact reachable parent table, and never performs an unchecked C cast.

## How

Represent the conversion explicitly in HxcIR, validate declared interface ancestry and table compatibility, emit readable deterministic C, retain borrowed/managed object lifetime, and keep downcasts and unrelated casts fail-closed.
acceptance_criteria: A focused child-interface -> parent-interface program matches Eval; inherited and multiple-interface tables remain deterministic and unused tables stay absent; HxcIR explicitly records the conversion and validates source/target/table compatibility; generated strict C11 is readable and passes GCC/Clang O0/O2 plus sanitizers; borrowed stack objects remain call-bounded, managed objects keep exact roots, downcasts/unrelated casts fail source-positioned with no output; Caxecraft passes LevelContentResolver to ActorContentResolver without an application workaround.
notes:
Implemented explicit schema-23 HxcIR child-interface upcasts. Lowering retains nominal Haxe ancestry, constructs a complete stable source-table -> same-concrete-class parent-table map, rejects downcasts/unrelated conversions, and structural C emission preserves the object pointer without unchecked casts. Evidence: registered virtual-dispatch snapshot updater passed cold/server deterministic HxcIR/report/C generation, split/unity native execution, and child-interface upcasts across Counter and AlternateCounter; registered hxc-ir owner passes valid mapping plus fail-closed omitted/wrong-target-table diagnostics; Caxecraft resolved-level-plan Eval/native strict-C11/sanitizer probe passes. Local host exposes Apple Clang but not an identity-distinct GCC, so required GCC-family CI evidence remains pending before closure.
Added focused source-positioned negative programs for explicit parent-interface -> child-interface downcast and unrelated-interface cast. The suite-owned warm-server negative checker passes all four dispatch negatives and confirms no output tree. Exact diagnostics are TCast(interface):unsafe-interface-downcast-needs-runtime-type-proof:ReadableView->MutableView and TCast(interface):unrelated-interface-conversion:ReadableView->ResetView.
After formatting changed source anchors, the registered virtual-dispatch snapshot updater was rerun and passed the complete owner with refreshed HxcIR/report positions plus the new downcast/unrelated negatives. This preserves deterministic cold/server/profile/layout/native evidence rather than relying on the earlier manual probes.
The registered owner now includes an explicit Haxe Eval run for the same two-implementation child-interface program; the focused Eval check passes silently and generated native C already passes the suite. Both intentional unsafe casts are source-exact negative-test entries in typed-boundaries.json; test:typed-boundaries passes with zero unapproved seams.
Final review also verified the documented architecture boundary: the implemented private Caxecraft resolver consumes LevelContentResolver as ActorContentResolver naturally, while authoring/package code cannot import the plan. No additional semantic or diagnostic gap was found. Kept open solely for the acceptance criterion's identity-distinct GCC-family CI run; the local macOS gcc executable identifies as Apple Clang.
close_reason: Implemented explicit child-interface upcasts and completed the identity-distinct GNU GCC gate: the registered virtual-dispatch native matrix passes GCC O0/O2/C++ coverage, while prior Eval, HxcIR, Clang, sanitizer, negative-cast, and Caxecraft resolver evidence remains valid.

title: Lower local records that group non-null class references
description:
## Why

The natural Caxecraft resolved-level result destructures two non-null class references and groups them in one local immutable record. haxe.c currently rejects the record field during shared-body planning as shared-body-plan:TVar(values).field:plan:reference-... even though each reference is already supported independently. Rewriting the application into parallel locals would make compiler limitations shape ordinary Haxe.

## What

Teach shared-body/local aggregate planning to carry supported non-null class references inside a closed local record, preserving their existing ownership and cleanup semantics.

## How

Add a minimal positive fixture with two supported class references in one immutable local record, preserve fail-closed behavior for unsupported or escaping managed shapes, lower through HxcIR and structural CAST, and verify Eval/native behavior plus generated-C ownership/cleanup.
acceptance_criteria: A focused fixture groups two supported non-null class references in one closed local record and reads both fields; HxcIR records the exact managed/reference representation without raw C; generated strict C passes O0/O2 and sanitizers with no leak or double release; unsupported neighboring shapes remain fail-closed; the Caxecraft resolved-level-plan native test passes without rewriting the record into parallel locals.
notes:
Implemented closed local records containing exact collector-managed class references, including managed-root path derivation and defensive zero initialization for traced branch carriers so GC never observes indeterminate pointers. Evidence: aggregate-lowering owner passed Eval/HxcIR/generated-C, O0/O2, strict layout, managed-root, negative interface-record, and sanitizer coverage; Caxecraft resolved-level-plan Eval/native strict-C11/sanitizer probe passes. Keep open until final integrated gate review because this dirty worktree also contains neighboring compiler changes.
Final review found no remaining implementation or focused-test gap. The registered aggregate owner and Caxecraft consumer pass on the available Apple Clang toolchain, including O0/O2 and sanitizer coverage. Kept open for the same identity-distinct GCC/CI closure evidence required by the compiler task boundary; no application workaround remains.
close_reason: Implemented managed class-reference fields in closed local records. The registered aggregate native matrix now passes identity-distinct GNU GCC in addition to the existing Eval, HxcIR, Clang O0/O2, sanitizer, fail-closed neighbor, and Caxecraft resolver evidence.

title: Lift reusable haxe.c metal contracts exposed by POSIX package I/O
description:
## Why

The natural Haxe implementation of confined POSIX package reads exposed four general typed-C gaps: taking a call-scoped reference to initialized imported structs, calling an explicitly variadic declaration with only its fixed prefix, performing exact integer operations on C carriers, and structurally zero-initializing a complete header-owned struct. Keeping those gaps behind application-owned C would weaken Caxecraft as haxe.c's flagship compiler workload.

## What

Implement these operations through typed c.* APIs, target-owned HxcIR, validation, structural CAST emission, and exact C semantics. Keep optional variadic arguments, uninitialized or managed aggregates, temporary references, and unrelated ordinary Haxe records fail-closed.
design: c.StructInit.zero is a typed intrinsic, not memset, a cast, or raw C. It lowers to a schema-22 IRIOZeroAggregate and structural C compound literal after the validator proves a wholly unmanaged direct layout. @:c.variadic records a header fact but admits only the declared fixed prefix. c.Ref remains a one-call non-retained borrow. Exact C integer operators preserve the source carrier rather than converting through Haxe Int.
acceptance_criteria: The positive direct-import fixture uses c.Ref.to on an initialized imported struct, one @:c.variadic fixed-prefix-only call, exact admitted C integer comparisons/masks, and c.StructInit.zero on a complete unmanaged imported struct; negative fixtures reject rest-style or optional variadic arguments, temporary/escaping references, and zero initialization of an ordinary Haxe record; schema-22 HxcIR records and validates zero-aggregate; generated strict C passes native ABI behavior at O0/O2 without selecting hxrt; typed-C and HxcIR snapshots update through registered owners.
notes: Implemented and verified: c.Ref accepts initialized complete imported structs for one non-retained direct call; @:c.variadic records a fixed-prefix-only header contract while Haxe Rest remains rejected; exact fixed/ABI C integer operations preserve their carriers; c.StructInit.zero lowers to schema-22 IRIOZeroAggregate and structural compound initialization only for wholly unmanaged imported structs. The direct-import corpus passes deterministic rendering, positive/negative diagnostics, Clang strict C11 O0/O2 native ABI behavior, and runtime absence. Registered typed-C and HxcIR snapshot owners pass.
close_reason: Reusable typed metal capabilities implemented with schema-22 HxcIR, structural C emission, fail-closed negatives, and direct-import native evidence.

title: Preserve a retained String left operand across compound-assignment flow
description: Caxecraft ASCII path normalization uses ordinary Haxe compound String assignment whose right side is a conditional between String.fromCharCode calls. haxe.c retains the old String owner before evaluating the right side, but leaves the corresponding HxcIR value in the pre-branch basic block. The concat emitted in the conditional join therefore references a value unavailable in that block, and the independent validator correctly rejects it.
design: Preserve source evaluation order and the retained owner lifetime while staging the left String carrier in automatic storage whenever the right expression creates control flow. Reload that non-owning staged carrier only in the final block, then concatenate and transfer the fresh result into the target. Do not special-case Caxecraft, weaken value-availability validation, or reassociate the source expression.
acceptance_criteria: A focused ordinary-Haxe fixture covers String compound-add assignment with conditional right arms in both orderings and runtime-created Unicode scalars; validated HxcIR defines both concat operands in the join block while one retained old-value owner remains balanced; Eval/native output matches; deterministic layouts, strict available C compilers, and Clang ASan/UBSan pass; existing compound String and managed-flow tests remain green; Caxecraft package-store compilation advances without rewriting its source loop.
close_reason: Managed String compound assignment now stages its retained left carrier when the right expression creates control flow, then reloads both operands in the join block without reassociation. The focused Unicode conditional fixture proves one balanced old-value owner, deterministic HxcIR, exact concat/store order, Eval/native parity, split/package/unity output, strict Clang C11/C++17, and ASan/UBSan. The natural Caxecraft ASCII normalization loop now compiles unchanged, and the package-store native vertical passes.

title: Carry retained String views through managed conditionals
description: Caxecraft's natural package-path validation selects between a borrowed String parameter and a retained substring view. Lowering correctly retains the substring bytes, but records transferability only in lowering-local metadata; the independent HxcIR validator sees an ordinary load and rejects the outer move-fresh carrier. Make the retained borrowed view's ownership transfer explicit in existing typed HxcIR so later control-flow joins can validate it without application rewrites.
design: Use the existing managed-carrier protocol for the straight-line retain-and-transfer handoff as well as branch joins. Generalize its validator from a branch-only start to the instruction suffix after declaration, retaining exact acquire-before-move, no duplicate move, and no owned exit checks. Do not add a product special case, weaken fresh-value validation, or infer ownership from C syntax.
acceptance_criteria: A focused ordinary-Haxe String fixture covers both borrowed-or-substring and substring-or-borrowed conditionals; the substring result obtains one explicit retain-borrowed owner and transfers it through a structurally validated nested managed carrier; the outer conditional moves the fresh result without leaks, double retain, or use-after-free; Eval/native traces match; strict available C compilers and Clang sanitizers pass; HxcIR negative coverage continues to reject missing acquire, duplicate acquire/move, wrong lifecycle, and owned exits; Caxecraft's package-store compilation advances without rewriting its natural String expression.
close_reason: Retained borrowed String views now acquire and transfer one owner through the existing managed-carrier protocol, making freshness explicit in HxcIR instead of lowering-only metadata. The validator now proves the protocol from the instruction after declaration across straight-line and branched control flow. Focused positive and negative evidence covers both conditional arm orders, duplicate acquire, duplicate move, owned exit, missing acquire, and lifecycle mismatch. The complete String suite passed Eval/native parity, split/package/unity determinism, strict Clang C11 and C++17, ASan/UBSan, and selective runtime checks; the Caxecraft package store compiles and runs unchanged.

title: Initialize final primitive class fields in their declaring constructor
description: Caxecraft's typed package provenance receipt exposed that haxe.c rejects an ordinary constructor assignment such as this.byteLength = byteLength when the field is final and primitive. The compiler already has constructor-only initialization owners for final Strings, records, enums, Arrays, maps, Bytes, and managed values; add the missing ownership-free scalar rule rather than weakening the source model to mutable fields.
acceptance_criteria: A focused constructor fixture initializes final Int, Bool, and Float fields from constructor values and reads them after construction with Eval/native parity; HxcIR contains one typed store per field and generated C stores the scalar values structurally; only the first direct this.field assignment in the declaring constructor is admitted while later writes and non-constructor writes remain source-positioned immutable-place failures; strict GCC/Clang C11, O0/O2, eligible sanitizers, deterministic output, and the Caxecraft package provenance constructor pass without changing field mutability.
close_reason: Implemented the narrow constructor-only initialization rule for final primitive Int, Bool, and Float fields. The focused fixture proves exactly one typed HxcIR store per field, structural C assignment, Eval/native parity, deterministic typed-module order, O0/O2, and Clang ASan/UBSan; later or non-constructor writes remain fail-closed. Caxecraft package provenance constructors compile and run through all three project layouts. Formatter, all-source, and typed-boundary gates pass. This macOS host has no GNU GCC binary, so CI retains the separate GCC-family confirmation.

title: Compare imported C enum values without erasing their ABI type
description: Caxecraft package loading exposed that a direct imported C enum can be returned and passed through Haxe, but equality against its imported constants fails as a closed record primitive operation. Preserve the header-owned enum type, lower == and != as direct enum value comparisons, and keep other aggregate operators fail-closed.
acceptance_criteria: A focused direct-C fixture compares return/local/conditional imported enum values with imported constants using == and !=; HxcIR records a typed infallible enum comparison; generated C preserves the header-owned enum carrier and structural comparison; strict GCC/Clang C11, C++ consumer where applicable, O0/O2, and sanitizers pass; unsupported arithmetic/order operations remain source-positioned failures; the Caxecraft typed package-store status mapping compiles without integer erasure.
close_reason: Implemented typed equality and inequality for matching imported C enum carriers without erasing their header-owned ABI type. The focused pointlib fixture covers native return, local and conditional flow, direct comparisons, structural generated C, ABI probing, deterministic snapshots, and sanitizer-aware native execution. Caxecraft package-store status mapping now compiles and runs in split, package, and unity layouts. Verified locally with the registered c-import snapshot owner, Clang native-only evidence, package-store integration, formatter, all-source, and typed-boundary gates. This macOS host exposes Apple Clang through both clang and gcc command names, so the repository CI GNU GCC lane remains the required independent compiler-family confirmation.

title: Select literal-string runtime support for actor-event aggregate headers
description: The canonical Caxecraft aquatics owner fails both in the parallel exhaustive matrix and serially. Its generated program_types.h includes hxrt/string_literal.h through ActorControllerEvent/ContentId aggregate layout, but the runtime plan selects only runtime-base,status,alloc,array and emits no runtime include tree. Every generated translation unit then fails with a missing hxrt/string_literal.h. This appeared after authored actor-controller types entered GameSession and is a general runtime-requirement/header-closure defect, not an aquatics or CAXEMAP workaround opportunity.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime planning includes every hxrt header/implementation feature required by emitted aggregate, enum, nominal-abstract, and program-types declarations even when the value path is not executed by the entry point; the focused actor-event aggregate fixture and test:caxecraft-aquatics compile/run under strict GCC/Clang C11 with the exact minimal closure; split/package/unity, cold/server determinism, runtime-plan reports, and negative unsupported-profile behavior pass; Caxecraft source does not add a fake String operation or forced runtime feature.
notes: Runtime-backed String carriers stored only in reachable type declarations now contribute type-carrier requirements during semantic lowering and are independently reconciled from validated HxcIR aggregate, enum-payload, and class-field types. The fail-closed project root allowlist and runtime catalog admit that exact representation reason. Caxecraft aquatics verifies the string-literal/type-carrier/runtime-representation root, the generated program_types.h include, and the minimal runtime closure. runtime-feature-graph and aquatics split/package/unity passed with strict native compilation and sanitizers; the host's optional gcc identity remains Clang.
close_reason: Reachable stored String declarations now select and package their exact runtime carrier; focused Caxecraft and runtime graph evidence passes.

title: Restore exactly-once cleanup for fresh direct Array call arguments
description: The canonical test:array-runtime owner fails on the current base, both inside the parallel exhaustive pre-commit matrix and again serially on an otherwise idle host, with: fresh direct Array call lost exactly-once instance-call-argument-0 cleanup. The native CAXEMAP probe changes no compiler/runtime implementation, so this is an independent baseline semantic regression, likely near fresh direct-call argument lowering. It must remain fail-closed rather than being normalized as contention or bypassed for unrelated product work.
acceptance_criteria: The focused Array differential reproducer proves fresh direct managed Array arguments are released exactly once across success and every failure edge; Eval/native behavior, retain/release counters, strict GCC/Clang C11, ASan/UBSan, split/package/unity, and cold/server determinism pass; the complete test:array-runtime owner passes serially and in the bounded parallel toolchain; no call-site workaround or weakened cleanup assertion is introduced.
notes: Root cause was an over-constrained structural assertion, not a missing release. Validated HxcIR retained one exactly-once cleanup action and emitted the instance-call argument release immediately after the synchronous call because constructing the receiver closed the call-bounded owner scope. The focused assertion now counts the explicit post-call release and deferred return cleanup as mutually exclusive legal placements, still requires exactly one release, and rejects an eager release before the call. npm run test:array-runtime passed its complete Eval/native, layout/order, allocation-failure, strict Clang C11, ASan/UBSan, and reclamation lane (the host's optional gcc command identifies as Clang).
close_reason: Exactly-once Array cleanup is now asserted at its legal eager or deferred semantic location; the complete Array owner passes.

title: Remove generated Caxecraft content-pack authority
description:
## Why

The generated `BaseContentPack.hx` and semantic emission in `content_pack.py`
would otherwise remain a hidden second authority after runtime pack loading.

## What

Delete generated content-pack facts from the product path once the runtime
manifest/UI registry gate passes.

## How

Keep only generic handwritten registry/model interfaces and packaging,
schema-lint, receipt, or fixture orchestration that consumes the same runtime
bytes. A built-in package must be explicit and pass through the same parser and
validator. The deletion gate requires clean cold product generation, exact
Eval/native/package traces, malformed/stale/unlisted-file tests, CaxeTest
first-playable evidence, and no-build measurements for map, pack, and UI edits.
acceptance_criteria: BaseContentPack.hx content facts and semantic Haxe emission from content_pack.py are absent from the product path; generic handwritten registry/model interfaces remain; built-in bytes are selected explicitly and pass through the same runtime parser/validator; clean cold generation, exact Eval/native/package traces, malformed/stale/unlisted-file tests, first-playable CaxeTest and no-build map/pack/UI measurements pass; docs and capability claims name runtime bytes as authority without claiming later campaign breadth.
notes:
COMPLETION 2026-08-02: Caxecraft production Haxe now reads built-in pack mechanics and reusable UI text exclusively from one validated ActiveRuntimeContent generation. BaseContentPack.hx and UiCatalog.hx are absent from examples/caxecraft/src and from playable generated C; content_pack.py, check_content_pack.py, their standalone HXML/probes, npm entry point, and CI/shard policy were deleted. RuntimeContentRegistry supplies mechanics/item facts and RuntimeUiCatalog supplies owned Haxe strings borrowed as call-bounded c.CStringRef at Raylib/Raygui.

Behavior/oracle/red evidence: the real playable first failed at CaxecraftApp.hx:1305 with intended HXC3000 because a reached private inline C import declaration was not retained. Child haxe_c-xge.20.4.3.8.2 records that red command, source position, independent handwritten C text observer, compatible-ABI alias rule, negative mismatch oracle, and green compiler/flagship evidence. Product expectations come from the authored content.json, locales/ui.json, CaxeMap, closed Haxe schema invariants, receipt SHA-256s, and manually authored semantic assertions—not output generated by the implementation under test.

Tracer/vertical evidence: runtime-schemas and runtime-content-generation read the exact shipped pack/UI/map bytes through the confined package store, parse and validate them, publish one immutable generation, resolve the first-playable session, and pass Eval plus strict native generated C with ASan/UBSan. Actor-composition and resolved-level-plan also pass Eval/native/sanitizers. The exhaustive domain lane passes split/package/unity C at O0/O2/ASan+UBSan with exact Eval traces and 32 seeded properties. Playable source-shaped snapshots/direct-C invariants pass, and runtime publication passes.

No-build/feedback-loop evidence: the focused build-state owner passes 16/16 and proves packs/, locales/, and scenarios/ are absent from the compile request while exact changed bytes and a SHA-256 receipt are restaged before launch. Existing measured samples in docs/test-performance.md observed a changed runtime-content hash reaching launch preparation with zero Haxe, C compiler, or linker processes (662.2ms validation, 1.35s complete command under a contended host); this is diagnostic evidence, not a new speed promise. Formal unsaturated percentile work remains haxe_c-xge.20.4.3.9.

Maintenance delta: one 1,157-line product Haxe generator and a 352-line standalone Python checker are gone; only localization_catalog.py still generates product Haxe, and only for the deferred campaign-dialogue fallback. The old generated BaseContentPack values remain solely as an active test-only compatibility fixture so older compiler regressions keep diagnostic value; haxe_c-xge.20.4.3.8.3 owns replacing it and deleting the final module. This residue is not in the product build or package.
