Final gates: Haxe formatter 811 files; all-sources 221 modules; typed boundaries; runtime schemas/content generation/publication; actor composition; resolved level plan; localization; playable snapshots; Caxecraft domain full; snapshot catalog; and governance 225/225 all pass. Five independent product-surface scorecards remain green without broadening campaign, hot-reload, public ABI, Windows runtime package, full Haxe conformance, or platform claims.
close_reason: Runtime pack/UI bytes are now the only Caxecraft product authority; generated product mirrors and the Python pack generator/checker are removed, exact runtime/native/playable/no-build evidence passes, and the remaining test-only compatibility fixture is explicitly deferred to haxe_c-xge.20.4.3.8.3.

title: Load the bounded base content pack and UI catalog natively
description:
## Why

Native map loading alone still leaves `BaseContentPack.hx` and the UI catalog as
compiled/generated authorities. The parent runtime level/UI milestone cannot
claim a fully data-driven first playable while item, block, actor, mechanics,
or UI facts still require code generation.

## What

Read and validate the bounded built-in `content.json` and `locales/ui.json`
through repository-owned typed Haxe, build the immutable runtime registry and
catalog, and bind their identities to the same content generation as the map.

## How

Admit only the current closed schemas and limits. Reject unsupported versions,
duplicates, missing/wrong-kind mechanics, messages, localization, presentation,
asset, and pack references before candidate publication. Probe the exact
manifest parser and compiler/runtime needs rather than assuming general
reflection or arbitrary JSON. Eval and native emit the same registry and level
semantic trace.
acceptance_criteria: The packaged executable reads the current content.json and locales/ui.json through typed bounded schemas, builds an immutable registry/catalog, and binds map/pack/UI/asset-manifest schema identities and hashes into one generation; unsupported version, duplicate, missing/wrong-kind mechanics/message/localization/presentation/asset/pack references and stale/unlisted files fail before publication; Eval/native registry and level traces match; one pack/UI edit performs no compiler or linker work; no arbitrary Dynamic/reflection/JSON graph is admitted merely for this slice.
notes:
2026-07-30: The first Eval/native closed-JSON probe passes Eval and exposes a general haxe.c class-field gap before C emission: ContentJson.failure:Null<ContentJsonDiagnostic> is a nullable managed closed record. haxe_c-djl.21 owns the reusable lowering fix; application work remains paused at that exact natural-Haxe boundary.
2026-08-01 dependency correction: this aggregate's acceptance requires a pack/UI edit that starts no compiler or linker. haxe_c-xge.20.4.3.9 owns implementing and measuring that exact no-build loop, so the prior edge requiring .9 to wait for this aggregate was reversed. This aggregate now remains open until .9 supplies that evidence; .8 remains downstream of both.
2026-08-02 aggregate closure: all five implementation children are closed. The packaged application reads exact content.json, ui.json, map.caxemap, and receipt bytes through typed bounded Haxe schemas, constructs and publishes one immutable runtime generation, and retains malformed/stale/unlisted/duplicate fail-closed owners. Final no-recompile contract landed in 3871fc9: map/pack/UI paths are absent from the executable key, exact current bytes and SHA-256 receipt are restaged, and reuse identity starts no compiler/version processes. Runtime-content-generation passed Eval, strict native C, ASan, and UBSan; build-state 15/15, governance 224/224, all-sources 220, HxcIR, hello, and snapshot catalog passed. Formal <=2s percentile evidence remains unproven under open P3 haxe_c-xge.20.4.3.9 and supports no speed claim; it is not part of this correctness closure.
close_reason: The bounded base pack, UI catalog, map, and receipt now load and publish as one typed runtime generation; malformed inputs fail closed, Eval/native/sanitizer traces pass, and data edits remain outside the executable build key. Formal percentile measurement remains explicitly deferred in haxe_c-xge.20.4.3.9.

title: Remove the generated first-playable level authority
description:
## Why

Calling `FirstPlayableLevel.hx`, its Eval code generator, and the Python adapter
temporary is not enough: without an executable removal gate they remain a
second content authority and keep map edits in the Haxe/C build graph.

## What

After the native first-map gate passes, remove the generated per-level Haxe
module and ordinary-build adapter path, including stale generated-C artifacts.

## How

Require a packaged native load, Eval/native semantic-trace parity, focused
negative/fault/path tests, active-generation invariance, strict C/sanitizer
evidence, a clean cold build without the bridge, and a process audit proving a
map edit starts no Haxe, haxe.c, C compiler, or linker. Retain a renamed
test-only semantic-trace oracle only if mutation or regression evidence proves
it catches an independent defect without owning defaults or resolution.
acceptance_criteria: Normal caxecraft:play neither invokes level_adapter.py nor compiles a per-level Haxe module; FirstPlayableLevel.hx, its product generator/hxml, ordinary adapter path, and stale generated-C artifacts are removed from a clean build; packaged native load, exact Eval/native trace, negative/fault/path/publication evidence, strict C/sanitizers, and cold snapshot catalog pass; a map edit starts no Haxe, haxe.c, C compiler, or linker; any retained test-only trace probe has no defaults/resolution authority and demonstrably catches an independent defect.
notes:
Completed the generated-level authority removal. Normal play now has one runtime-package path: the executable reads scenarios/first-playable/map.caxemap through the repository-owned Haxe package store, parser, validator, resolver, candidate generation, and publication path. Removed FirstPlayableLevel.hx, FirstPlayableSessionLoader.hx, FirstPlayableLevelGenerator.hx, level-adapter.hxml, level_adapter.py, their package/CI entry points, and their registered generated-C artifacts. Kept only forbidden-marker checks so the bridge cannot silently return. Renamed the filesystem-free QA source from GeneratedBridge/GeneratedLevelBytes to InMemorySource/InMemoryBytes so it cannot be confused with product authority.

Evidence: npm run test:caxecraft-runtime-level-loader passed Eval/native with strict generated-C and sanitizers; npm run test:caxecraft-session passed its narrow Eval/native owner; the registered caxecraft-domain snapshot update passed Eval plus split/package/unity native differentials and removed both stale generated C files; python3 examples/caxecraft/play.py --check-snapshots passed; npm run snapshots:catalog reported 30 disjoint suites; a direct strict GNU C11 -Wall/-Wextra/-Werror/-pedantic-errors syntax pass covered all 92 generated playable translation units; Clang built and linked the packaged desktop executable. The first replacement build published runtime-package state. A controlled authored-map text edit then remained an unchanged-build hit after 662.2 ms validation, produced a different runtime content hash, and reached launch in 1.35 s with no Haxe, haxe.c, C compiler, or linker. The map was restored byte-for-byte afterward. The headless shell lacked a desktop display, so Raylib rejected window creation only after native content loading reported success; graphical product pilots remain independent evidence.

Final focused gates: Haxe format guard (781 files), 12 build-state/governance tests, CI policy, toolchain policy, 67-command shard topology, agent-instruction symlink guard, Python compilation, git diff whitespace, playable snapshot/direct-C validation, and snapshot catalog all passed. Timing evidence is recorded in docs/test-performance.md.
close_reason: The per-level generated Haxe/Python authority and stale generated C are removed; runtime package loading is the only normal play path, with cold/native/snapshot/fault and real no-build map-edit evidence passing.

title: Load the first Caxecraft map natively against the compiled registry
description:
## Why

The playable still imports generated Haxe facts from `FirstPlayableLevel.hx`.
Staging `map.caxemap` does not make those bytes the native runtime authority.

## What

Load the checked-in first-playable CAXEMAP through `ContentPackageStore`, the
shared codec, `ResolvedLevelPlan`, and `LoadedContentGeneration`, initially
resolving against the existing compiled `BaseContentRegistry`.

## How

During migration expose an explicit generated/native content-authority switch
and print the selected authority, logical path, input hash, and generation ID.
Both paths must share the same resolver and generation publisher. Headless
CaxeTest/PilotScript evidence proves terrain, fluids, Tideweave, spawn, Nia,
Mossling, dialogue/objective/flow bindings, and actor mechanics came from the
loaded map. Malformed and injected failures leave the active generation
unchanged; no window is required for parser negatives.
acceptance_criteria: A packaged native executable reads the staged first-playable map after startup, runs the shared codec/resolver, builds an inactive generation, and reports authority/path/hash/generation ID; headless CaxeTest/PilotScript proves terrain, fluids, Tideweave, spawn, Nia, Mossling, dialogue/objective/flow and actor mechanics originate in loaded bytes; malformed and injected failures preserve the active generation; Eval/native traces match; migration selection is explicit and no parser negative requires Raylib.
notes: Local product integration now satisfies the native-map path: ordinary caxecraft:play defaults to native authority, reads the staged CAXEMAP through ContentPackageStore and RuntimeLevelLoader, builds LoadedContentGeneration, and reports authority/path/input-hash/generation before Raylib initialization. The focused package-store and runtime-level-loader suites pass Eval/native C with sanitizers; the packaged macOS project compiled and linked as strict C11 with 105 translation units and no handwritten production C. The explicit generated authority still compiles as the migration fallback. Build-state schema 2 excludes runtime scenarios from compiler inputs, republishes content before every launch, and governance has 11 passing invalidation tests. A final-state unchanged launch reused generated C, all native objects, and the link product with zero compiler processes in 646.8 ms validation. This issue remains open until its dependency issues receive their identity-distinct CI/GCC closure evidence; bridge deletion stays separately owned by haxe_c-xge.20.4.3.6.
close_reason: Normal Caxecraft play defaults to native map bytes and runs the shared package store, codec, resolver, and atomic generation path before Raylib. Provenance, negative/publication, Eval/native sanitizer, no-build 646.8 ms, strict Clang link, and strict Homebrew GCC 16.1 checks over all 105 generated translation units pass. Generated authority remains only as the explicitly owned removal bridge in haxe_c-xge.20.4.3.6.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: Compiler blockers discovered by the natural runtime loader have advanced: mutable parameters, fresh managed-record constructor arguments, and collector-bearing tagged-enum conditional joins now have focused compiler fixes. The focused runtime-level-loader command passes Eval and native C with sanitizer execution. This proves the shared codec/resolver/generation path can construct the first map natively; remaining work is product integration of the packaged runtime authority, provenance reporting, complete headless content assertions, and explicit migration selection—not another parser or generated-content workaround.

title: Read confined Caxecraft package bytes through a typed hosted store
description:
## Why

Native Caxecraft needs exact package bytes without giving game code ambient
POSIX/Win32/Raylib authority or pretending that staged files are already
runtime-loaded. A raw path string or Raylib file helper does not by itself own
root confinement, short reads, changed-during-read behavior, or cleanup.

## What

Add the smallest repository-owned typed `ContentPackageStore` read boundary:
an application-selected root capability plus a normalized logical relative
path produces owned bounded Bytes and provenance, or one closed typed error.

## How

Start with one hosted adapter and keep target details below the game/editor
API. Reject absolute, drive/UNC/device, empty, dot, dot-dot, NUL, separator,
size, component, symlink/reparse, and root-escape cases before publication.
Read exactly from an opened handle, compare identity/size/change facts, retry a
changing file at most once, and release handles/buffers on every edge. Metal,
portable, WASI, Emscripten, and freestanding profiles must advertise an injected
provider or an explicit unsupported capability rather than plausible fake I/O.
acceptance_criteria: An application-selected root capability plus one normalized logical path returns exact bounded owned Bytes and provenance or a closed typed error; hosted tests reject absolute, drive, UNC/device, empty, dot, dot-dot, NUL, alternate-separator, over-limit, symlink/reparse, and root-escape cases; exact/short/changed reads, bounded retry, allocation and close failures clean every handle/buffer; Eval/native adapters preserve stable error categories; ordinary game/editor code imports no POSIX, Win32, Raylib, raw C, or c.* filesystem authority; unsupported profiles fail explicitly.
notes:
Architecture correction in progress: remove the repository-owned POSIX C implementation and keep confinement, identity checks, retry, exact reads, failure injection, and cleanup in Haxe compiled by haxe.c. The focused product pressure added reusable typed compiler capabilities for initialized imported-struct references, fixed-prefix-only variadic declarations, exact C integer operations, and schema-22 structural zero initialization. Handwritten C is being reduced to an independent ABI/export harness whose technical necessity and durable evidence ownership are documented separately.
Handwritten-C double justification for examples/caxecraft/test/native/content_package_store_harness.c: (1) technical necessity — an independent native compiler must compare the Haxe-selected carriers with the actual host size_t/ssize_t/dev_t/ino_t/mode_t/off_t/time_t ABI; generating this assertion from the compiler under test would be self-comparison. (2) durable ownership value — the same tiny file is a non-haxe.c consumer of the exported Haxe result envelope and generated main, proving ordinary C ABI interoperability. It contains no path/read/retry/cleanup/content algorithm. The package-store test owns it; remove it if an equally independent external ABI consumer and host-header oracle replace both jobs.
close_reason: Confined POSIX package-store behavior now lives entirely in Haxe compiled by haxe.c. Split/package/unity Eval/native strict-C sanitizer probes pass; handwritten C is reduced to a twice-justified independent ABI/export harness, and the former raw POSIX adapter is removed.

title: Build and publish complete Caxecraft content generations atomically
description:
## Why

The current application owns one lifetime-long `GameSession`, while the dirty
loader may write terrain, water, items, and player state before later actor
planning or result allocation can fail. That startup-only disposable-candidate
shape cannot provide editor reload or last-known-good recovery.

## What

Introduce one `LoadedContentGeneration` ownership boundary that builds a
complete inactive candidate and publishes it through one non-failing
main-loop/frame-boundary swap.

## How

Move every fallible resolution, allocation, binding, presentation check, and
candidate construction step before publication. Prefer a fresh managed
generation when haxe.c proves the lifetime; otherwise use two bounded
application-owned generation/session slots behind the same API. Failure
discards or resets only the inactive candidate. The active generation remains
observable until the exact commit point, and old-generation retirement is
explicit and sanitizer-tested.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh or inactive generation owns a complete candidate GameSession, validated content/plan metadata, stable bindings, and read-model facts; every fallible resolution, allocation, copy, resource check, and construction step occurs before one non-failing main-loop publication point; injected failure at every stage leaves the prior generation ID and semantic trace unchanged; repeated successful and failed loads have bounded memory and pass strict native/sanitizer evidence; a bounded double buffer is allowed only behind the same ownership API when an exact managed-generation compiler gap is recorded.
notes: Implemented the natural managed-generation path; no double-buffer fallback was needed. LoadedContentGeneration owns a fresh GameSession, immutable resolved plan/presentation facts, stable actor/item/flow bindings, and a target-neutral semantic trace. Construction preflights plan/presentation identity, then installs terrain, fluids, items, player, and actors only into the fresh candidate. Test-only typed stage faults are compiled out of ordinary builds. ActiveContent rejects out-of-order generations before mutation, constructs the publication result before commit, and performs one reference swap without callbacks or fallible semantic work afterward. Focused evidence passes Eval/native strict C11 and ASan/UBSan: seven injected pre-stage failures preserve the active ID/trace, a mutated last-known-good session survives rejection, stale publication is rejected, and 33 successful swaps remain deterministic. The independent strict-C harness runs with a 64 KiB collector threshold, proves pressure collections and reclamation occur during the repeated loop, proves peak live objects stay below total allocations, then forces a final collection and observes zero live managed objects. Governance assigns the focused owner to the exact Caxecraft shard; all 67 commands partition and all 186 governance tests pass. Ordinary caxecraft:play is intentionally not rewired here; haxe_c-xge.20.4.3.5 owns package-bytes integration.
close_reason: LoadedContentGeneration and ActiveContent now construct complete fresh candidates and publish through one non-failing reference swap. Injected failures preserve the active generation, repeated swaps remain bounded, strict native/sanitizer evidence passes, and the resolved-plan dependency is closed.

title: Resolve validated CAXEMAP into a private native construction plan
description:
## Why

The dirty `LevelLoadPlan` usefully separates authored data from session
construction, but it still mixes unresolved `ScenarioObject` actors, raw
integer storage codes, renderer presentation cells, and caller-mutable Arrays.
Freezing that shape would create a second, engine-shaped content format.

## What

Define a private, fully resolved `ResolvedLevelPlan` produced only from a
validated Scenario and the selected typed content registry. It is an ephemeral
construction plan, never an editable or serialized format.

## How

Resolve actor mechanics, nominal storage codes, capacities, player options,
stable authored bindings, items, fluids, terrain, and flow references before
session mutation. Keep presentation/resource requests in a separate read-model
plan. Give the plan sole/copy ownership of nested storage and expose no parser,
writer, filename, version, or public package API for it. Emit a deterministic
semantic trace shared by Eval and native tests.
acceptance_criteria: Only one resolver can produce the private construction plan; it contains fully resolved nominal terrain, fluid, item, actor, player, stable-binding, and flow facts with owned nested storage; it contains no raw ScenarioObject, source path/text, renderer/native handle or presentation cell, public integer tag, parser/writer/version/file extension, or serialized form; Eval/native semantic traces and missing/wrong-kind/capacity negatives match; authoring/editor/package code cannot import the plan.
notes:
Implemented the private resolver-only ResolvedLevelPlan and separate ResolvedPresentationPlan with copy-owned nested arrays, nominal storage/content facts, no paths/native handles/serialized plan surface, and deterministic semantic trace. The natural Caxecraft probe now passes Eval and generated native strict C11 with sanitizers. The probe exposed two reusable compiler defects (haxe_c-11cf class-reference records and haxe_c-049.4 interface-parent upcasts), both implemented with focused compiler evidence instead of application workarounds. Remaining before closure: inspect/complete missing/wrong-kind/capacity negatives and authoring-import guard, then rerun final focused owner under representative host load.
Final focused acceptance review completed: unknown-content, wrong-kind, 257-item capacity, invalid-player-option, copy-isolation, deterministic semantic-trace, and authoring/editor/package import-boundary checks all pass. The registered Caxecraft owner passes Eval and generated strict-C11 native execution with sanitizers. Architecture and modding docs now distinguish the implemented private resolver from the still-unimplemented runtime publication path. Implementation acceptance is complete locally; the issue remains open only because its compiler dependencies retain identity-distinct GCC/CI closure evidence.
close_reason: The private resolver-only ResolvedLevelPlan, separate presentation plan, copy-owned storage, semantic trace, wrong-kind/capacity negatives, import guard, and Eval/native sanitizer evidence are complete. Its identity-distinct GCC dependencies now pass and are closed.

title: Prove native CAXEMAP codec viability from embedded bytes
description:
## Why

The shared CAXEMAP lexer, parser, validator, and writer have strong Eval
evidence, but the native haxe.c path has not yet proved that the same ordinary
Haxe implementation can consume the first-playable bytes. Naming whole String,
Bytes, collection, and filesystem epics as blockers hides the exact missing
language or runtime shapes.

## What

Add one no-Raylib native fixture that embeds the checked-in first-playable
CAXEMAP bytes, runs the repository-owned lexer, parser, and validator, and emits
a small deterministic semantic trace. Compare that trace and a bounded negative
diagnostic corpus with Eval.

## How

Use the real shared codec without a second parser, generated per-level facts,
raw C, or Python-owned semantics. Record every exact typed-AST, HxcIR, runtime,
or stdlib failure as a focused child of its existing compiler owner. Do not make
the full broad epics dependencies unless this executable probe proves the
complete scope is required.
acceptance_criteria: A no-Raylib fixture runs the checked-in first-playable bytes through the exact shared lexer, parser, and validator under Eval and generated C; valid semantic traces and a bounded malformed/truncated/duplicate/missing/wrong-kind diagnostic corpus match exactly; GCC and Clang strict C11 plus eligible sanitizers pass; every failure is reduced to a focused reusable compiler/runtime owner; no alternate parser, raw C, Python semantics, or blanket dependency on whole stdlib epics is introduced.
notes: Implemented the no-Raylib production-codec probe. It embeds the exact 5,098 authored bytes as two C11-portable String chunks, and the shared runner fails closed if those bytes drift from scenarios/first-playable/map.caxemap. The same Haxe lexer, parser, validator, and a private validation-only content registry run on Eval and generated C. Eval/native compare a deterministic semantic trace (byte count, dimensions, palette/fluid/object/dialogue/objective counts), and the negative corpus covers malformed UTF-8, unknown version, truncation, duplicate content IDs, missing dialogue references, and wrong-kind entity content. The native harness runs the generated entry point so collector startup/shutdown match a shipped executable. Exact hxrt closure: runtime-base,status,alloc,array,string-literal,bytes,object,gc,int-map,string-scalar,string,string-map,string-split. Durable focused command: python3 examples/caxecraft/run_haxe_c_test.py scenario-native-codec [--cc clang|gcc]. Verified with Clang split plus sanitizers, explicit GCC split plus sanitizers, formatter, all-source, typed-boundary, fixture-policy, exact toolchain-policy/shard checks, and the full governance suite. Optional unity probing found the independent declaration-order bug haxe_c-z80q. An attempted canonical exhaustive run additionally exposed two reproducible base regressions, haxe_c-ie20 (fresh Array cleanup) and haxe_c-opqf (actor-event string-literal runtime selection); those independent bugs remain fail-closed and are not disguised as codec failures or application workarounds.
close_reason: The exact shared CAXEMAP lexer/parser/validator now runs on Eval and strict generated C, with byte-staleness protection, a deterministic semantic trace, the required negative corpus, GCC/Clang sanitizer evidence, and no alternate parser or broad speculative compiler dependency. The separate unity declaration-order defect remains tracked as haxe_c-z80q.

title: Run affected semantic owners before local compiler commits
description: The high-fanout pre-commit selector currently maps any staged change below central compiler IR/lowering/runtime directories to the complete 61-command toolchain plus native smoke. A real schema-20/runtime-planner checkpoint was interrupted after 55 minutes on a contended 12-CPU host while still inside constructor variants. This cadence prevents practical compiler development even though focused HxcIR, runtime-feature, span, Caxecraft snapshot/domain, formatting, and governance owners had already passed.
design: Use three evidence scopes. Pre-commit always stays bounded: central compiler/product/test/CI paths run governance plus a fixed four-owner smoke set that type-checks all owned Haxe, validates HxcIR, builds/runs Hello natively, and checks snapshot ownership. The route selector separately lists exact path-affected owners; contributors and agents run those focused owners while implementing the task, before reaching the hook. Unknown cross-cutting paths never select no evidence, but they also do not expand pre-commit. The complete cold toolchain shards, native families, sanitizers, platform jobs, and snapshot audits remain unchanged and mandatory in hosted pull-request/nightly/release workflows and available through explicit local commands. This follows the maintainer decision on 2026-07-30 after a one-line header-requirement fix invalidated every multi-hour local shard.
acceptance_criteria: Every central local change runs governance plus exactly the explicit bounded smoke set; no pre-commit route automatically invokes path-specific exhaustive owners or the complete repository matrix; the selector deterministically lists exact focused owners so task work can run the changed subsystem contract before commit; an unknown central or test-infrastructure path never silently selects no evidence; local output names every automatic smoke owner and why; complete cold toolchain shards, both native compiler families, sanitizers, platform lanes, and cold snapshot audit remain unchanged and mandatory in hosted CI and explicit manual workflows; unit/governance tests prove route coverage, fixed smoke bounds, affected-owner listing, deterministic order, and CI full-lane availability; local pre-commit targets p95 at or below 8 minutes without dropping required hosted evidence.
notes:
2026-07-27 exact staged-tree evidence: the old resource-aware exhaustive local commit was deliberately interrupted after more than 55 minutes on a contended host while still inside constructor variants. The new affected route selected governance plus all-sources, HxcIR, Hello native, snapshot catalog, body lowering, runtime features, span lowering, and Caxecraft domain. All passed in 464.47s wall / 339.03s user / 22.40s sys. Starting load was 5.73/9.82/10.05 on 12 logical CPUs. This is one observed run below the eight-minute target, not enough to claim p95. Unknown cross-cutting paths still select the complete matrix; CI/manual cold commands are unchanged.
2026-07-27 Raygui/c.Ref checkpoint exposed a known-family routing hole: src/reflaxe/c/interop/CImportRegistry.hx was classified as unknown cross-cutting, so the hook launched the 62-command exhaustive matrix even after c-import, Raygui, Caxecraft, governance, native build, and graphical smoke owners had passed. Add explicit interop/c.Ref and Raygui affected-owner mappings with deterministic tests; retain unknown-directory fallback and hosted cold coverage.
2026-07-30 maintainer decision: full-repository verification on every local commit is itself blocking development. A catch-up commit reran all shards after a one-line CBodyEmitter header fix; the cache invalidated unrelated project-emitter, Array, Raylib, constructor, Caxecraft, and native owners, and host load reduced the pool to one worker. The maintainer directed local smoke/focused checks with the deeper matrix on CI. Preserve fail-closed local smoke and required hosted full evidence; remove automatic local exhaustive execution.
2026-07-30 refinement: listing every affected owner is useful for task verification, but automatically running all of them still makes a large honest catch-up commit take tens of minutes. The hook therefore runs only the fixed four-owner smoke set. Focused owners remain an implementation responsibility and the selector lists them; hosted CI remains the merge authority for the complete matrix.
2026-07-30 independent review correction: the conservative local route now matches every path under scripts/ci/, scripts/test/, scripts/hooks/, and test/governance/, including files added after the selector was written. New-check/new-helper/new-policy fixtures prove those paths receive the fixed four-owner smoke rather than silently falling through to focused-only evidence. The full matrix remains required in hosted CI and is not restored to pre-commit.

title: Index runtime requirement reconciliation by stable key
description: The uncapped full-playable profile measured 59.386 seconds in runtime planning. RuntimeRequirementAnalyzer canonicalizes reachable runtime observations and typed source candidates, but then candidateFor linearly scans all candidates for every observation and hasObservation linearly scans all observations for every candidate. It also reconstructs feature/operation/source display keys repeatedly during sorting and lookup. This makes a correctness reconciliation approach quadratic as the flagship grows.
design: Compute each candidate and observation stable key once. Preserve the existing UTF-8 canonical order and duplicate/conflict checks, then build request-local StringMap indices for exact candidate lookup and observation membership. Keep the two-way proof: every HxcIR runtime observation must have exactly one typed source candidate, and every candidate must correspond to a reachable observation. Do not weaken diagnostics, omit the reverse check, change reason IDs/order, cache across requests, or special-case Caxecraft.
acceptance_criteria: Focused runtime-requirement fixtures preserve exact reason order, IDs, reachability counts, malformed/missing/conflicting diagnostics, runtime plans, and generated bytes; a large deterministic synthetic reconciliation fixture or operation counter proves near-linear lookup rather than observation×candidate scans; the full playable runtime-plan and manifest differ only for already expected source-position drift; an uncapped cold profile records the runtime-planning before/after on the same host class; runtime-features, HxcIR, Caxecraft snapshots/domain, strict compilers, deterministic/server, and governance gates pass.
notes: 2026-07-27 implementation evidence: RuntimeRequirementAnalyzer now computes stable candidate/observation keys once and reconciles them through request-local maps while preserving canonical sort/deduplication and the two-way fail-closed proof. The exact full-playable cold split request dropped runtime planning from 59.386s to 2.628s (95.6%) and target pipeline from 217.414s to 96.410s; output ownership remained negligible at 0.077s. A 4,096-intent deterministic forward/reverse fixture passes. Runtime-feature, HxcIR, span (72 requests; cold/warm server; strict Clang), Caxecraft Eval/split/package/unity native differential, snapshots, formatting, and governance owners pass. Generated C did not drift from the optimization; only already expected source-position artifacts changed.
close_reason: Indexed reconciliation preserves the two-way runtime proof while reducing exact full-playable runtime planning from 59.386s to 2.628s; large deterministic, focused compiler, cold/warm span, native Caxecraft, snapshot, formatting, and governance evidence passes.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: 2026-07-27 implementation/profile evidence: replaced the two observation×candidate linear scans with request-local stable-key maps and precomputed each source identity once. On the same host class and exact cold full-playable split request, runtime planning fell from 59.386s to 2.628s (95.6%); target pipeline fell from 217.414s to 96.410s and wall from 251.37s to 112.52s, though total-wall values remain contention-sensitive diagnostics rather than an unsaturated benchmark. A complete generated-project diff excluding Reflaxe activity metadata was byte-identical. The registered caxecraft-domain updater then completed split/package/unity semantic parity and native differential and updated only five source-position-owned JSON artifacts. Keep this issue open until a deterministic operation-count/large-fixture regression and the remaining named gates land.

title: Emit non-overlapping request-scoped compiler profiles
description: The current profiler names useful target phases, but broad parent spans overlap child spans and do not expose exclusive CPU cost, memory growth, entity visits, allocations, serialization volume, or filesystem calls. The measured 54s semantic, 26s runtime, 46s artifact, and 38s output observations therefore identify where to measure next but cannot be added or treated as independent bottlenecks.
design: Retain the existing opt-in text timing contract for compatibility and add structured JSON Lines records with request ID, span ID, parent span, phase, monotonic wall time, process CPU where available, inclusive and exclusive duration, failure status, and stable request/toolchain summaries. Add bounded counters only at semantic boundaries: typed/HxcIR/CAST/artifact entity counts, analysis visits and index builds, sorts/copies/stringifications/hashes/serialized bytes, output filesystem operations, and optional RSS snapshots. Profiling off must allocate no phase graph and produce byte-identical normal artifacts. Benchmark only under the repository unsaturated-host method.
acceptance_criteria: Successful and expected-failure compilations emit a valid nested profile with closed spans and non-overlapping exclusive totals; profiler-off artifacts and diagnostics remain unchanged; focused fixture, runtime-free Caxecraft, and full playable baselines publish at least five uncontended samples with host/toolchain identity, median, MAD, p95, CPU, maximum RSS, entity sizes, and saturation classification; the profile isolates the first repeated analysis, serialization, or filesystem cost that justifies the next optimization; existing timing schema/tests remain compatible or migrate explicitly.
notes: Implemented schema-1 request-scoped JSONL profiles while preserving legacy timing records. Runtime-free Caxecraft produced 5 cold and 5 warm byte-identical samples, but two cold samples were contended, so the required uncontended baseline remains open. Full-playable detail clocks isolated typed-body lowering at about 12s while finalization/value planning were below 0.2s; a rejected Type-to-representation cache either lost enum provenance or cost more when replaying it, so no cache remains. Further coarse attribution isolated symbol finalization at 9.861s and artifact project emission at 9.455s. Removing redundant GeneratedFile rehash reduced project emission to 5.081s. A 2026-07-27 contended follow-up split remaining costs: collision resolution 7.197s of 10.831s symbol finalization, and sidecar construction 4.787s of 4.955s project emission; request CPU was 50.895s and the exact 225-artifact digest remained de51d720add1179168963978c515dca3f5499586510db338088f88f2e473de8a. haxe_c-5sd.5.8 and .9 now own those measured hot paths. Five uncontended full-playable samples remain missing.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: Five fresh-process full-playable samples completed with exact 229-artifact parity at SHA-256 8b9f8c206d1bcd719d86f011a76b2e0dfe2f5a9ea9c104efd0988392ae016015. Wall median 29.397s, MAD 0.183s, p95 29.818s; request CPU median 19.838s; median cumulative Eval allocation 72.032GB; median observed RSS 1.113GB. The harness classified all five samples contended because host load rose from 6.604 to 7.403 on 12 logical CPUs, so this is stable diagnostic evidence and not the missing formal uncontended baseline. Report: examples/caxecraft/_build/compiler-profile-playable-five-cold.json (untracked benchmark output).

title: Validate and launch an unchanged Caxecraft build
description: The first practical edit-loop milestone is not cross-request compiler caching. When every semantic source, configuration, compiler, binding, ABI, native-toolchain, packaged-content, and generated-output input is unchanged, caxecraft:play should prove that the existing generation and executable still belong to that exact request, then launch without starting Haxe or a C compiler. Today the same command repeats a roughly 97-second Haxe-to-C compile before native work even when nothing changed.
design: Introduce a schema-versioned BuildInputSnapshot and state record. The snapshot uses content-complete normalized identities for HXML and defines, Haxe sources and declared macro inputs, pinned Haxe, haxe.c, vendored Reflaxe, target profile/layout, typed C and Raylib/Raygui bindings, runtime/ABI plans, native tools and flags, and runtime-loaded content. A hit requires exact key equality plus output-manifest and executable integrity. A missing, malformed, foreign, stale, or corrupt record is a visible miss or fail-closed root error. Keep an explicit cold/clean/no-server/no-cache path. Watcher events may accelerate later work but are never authority.
acceptance_criteria: A second unchanged caxecraft:play skips Haxe, haxe.c, native compilation, and linking; reports every reused layer and validation time; reaches launch preparation at p50 <= 1.0s and p95 <= 1.5s on a declared unsaturated host; representative edits to source, nested HXML, define/profile/layout, compiler/Reflaxe, bindings, runtime/ABI, C toolchain/flags, generated inventory, content schema, and executable bytes each produce the first exact miss reason; corrupt or partial state never launches; requested failed builds never silently launch last-good output; the authoritative cold path remains byte/behavior identical.
notes: Implemented a fail-closed schema-1 unchanged-build state for normal interactive Caxecraft play. The request now hashes 3,067 reviewed Haxe/HXML/compiler/Reflaxe/runtime/binding/content/tooling/Haxe-install inputs, exact configuration/environment and native tool identities; reuse also re-hashes 239 generated/staged/executable outputs and nine Raylib/Raygui headers/libraries. Missing, malformed, changed, or corrupt state reports the first miss and performs the ordinary build. State publishes atomically only after successful Haxe-to-C generation, native build/link, staging, and a second source snapshot. --no-build-cache bypasses executable reuse; --cold and HAXE_NO_SERVER=1 preserve fresh-process evidence. A real --cold run regenerated C, rebuilt/linked, published state, and the cold playable snapshot lane matched. The next unchanged npm command reached launch preparation in 1.09s. Under severe unrelated host load (27.32 on 12 logical CPUs), 20 direct hits had p50 349.0ms, observed p95 858.6ms, max 901.7ms. This is conservative contention evidence; the parent haxe_c-5sd.8 retains the authoritative unsaturated before/after requirement. Focused 9-test state suite, 157 governance tests, fixture/governance/CI/toolchain policies, Python compilation, and diff checks passed.
close_reason: Delivered complete-key unchanged-build launch with atomic fail-closed state, explicit cold/off controls, focused invalidation/corruption tests, cold rebuild and snapshot parity, and sub-second validation under severe contention.

title: Restore fail-closed Beads history scanning after Dolt migration
description: The reviewed Beads 1.1.0 history reader fails on 46 pre-migration issues because their dolt_history_issues rows project nullable text columns as NULL and the CLI scans them into plain strings. scripts/security/run-beads-gitleaks.sh correctly treats any history-read failure as fatal, so npm run beads:push cannot publish current audited state. The upstream defect is gastownhall/beads#4867; proposed fix PR #4912 remains open. A direct bd dolt push was also rejected by GitHub with HTTP 400 after constructing a large pack, but that transport failure must be retested only after the required history scan is restored.
design: Do not skip unreadable histories or accept a current-record-only scan. Prefer an immutable reviewed Beads release containing the upstream COALESCE fix, update the repository tool pin and provenance through the existing security-tooling process, and prove every current and historical issue decodes into the Gitleaks stream. If an interim patched binary is considered, treat it as a supply-chain change with exact source revision, minimal reviewed diff, reproducible build/checksum, and explicit removal condition; never silently bypass the guard. After scanning succeeds, retry the ordinary guarded Dolt push and separately reduce any remaining GitHub HTTP 400 transport failure.
acceptance_criteria: All issue histories, including the 46 migrated NULL projections, decode and reach Gitleaks; a simulated history query failure still stops publication; the reviewed Beads pin and provenance match the executed binary; npm run security:beads-history and npm run beads:push pass without bypass or force; refs/dolt/data advances; Git and audited Dolt state are synchronized; upstream issue/PR disposition is recorded.
notes: Observed on 2026-07-25 with reviewed bd 1.1.0 revision 8e4e59d39. Example: bd history haxe_c-fbq --json exits 1 with 'converting NULL to string is unsupported'; bd show still proves current data is intact. bd compact --dry-run reports 1431 recent commits and nothing eligible under the 30-day retention rule, so compaction is not a safe fix. Upstream: https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/4867 and https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/pull/4912.
close_reason: Implemented an exact-provenance, null-safe Dolt history reader; proved complete current/history scanning and fail-closed publication; passed 134 governance tests; published the 801-commit catch-up and a normal incremental update; and verified refs/dolt/data synchronization. Upstream Beads issue 4867 and PR 4912 remain linked as the removal trigger for the interim reader.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: 2026-07-25 recovery evidence: the exact Dolt 2.1.4 reader built from github.com/dolthub/dolt/go@v0.40.5-0.20260605230755-1bf533220ab0 (module sum h1:oPg5f5bYFy5x7Ws2qtVG7wiva96cIh9SFg7nrC4n7QA=) decoded and sent 23.96 MB of current records, dolt_log metadata, and every changed row from every base table to Gitleaks; no leaks were found. Focused fail-closed tests prove a table-query failure prevents bd dolt push. The first ordinary HTTPS publication built a roughly 32 MB Git-backed Dolt pack but GitHub rejected it with HTTP 400. A second guarded run used Git's process-local HTTPS-to-SSH URL rewrite, did not force or bypass scanning, and completed. Local Dolt main is now synchronized with origin/main; GitHub refs/dolt/data advanced from 3d26fd913a392fab47d8e1aa1e4d888e9dbfd812 to d1fd91573e898ff6cdbf2fcaf533cbf1cdf1050c. The next incremental guarded publication will retest the configured HTTPS path so the one-time transport recovery is kept separate from the nullable-history fix.

title: Preserve inlined span-store places across conditional values
description: Context: Caxecraft WaterSimulation.capturePending naturally calls an inline helper that stores a conditional UInt8 value into a dynamic Span index. After Haxe inlines the helper, haxe.c emits HxcIR whose conditional join uses the already-evaluated destination/index value without passing it through the join block, and HxcIRValidator correctly rejects it as HXC9000. This is a general lowering defect, not water-specific behavior. Requirements: HXC-COMP-003, HXC-SEM-004, HXC-MAC-001, HXC-QA-001. PRD: sections 10.5, 12.2, 17.1, 21, 29.2.
design: Preserve Haxe left-to-right evaluation and the place/value distinction. Add a focused source fixture for an inline helper that performs span[index] = condition ? a : b, including side-effect probes for destination, index, condition, and both value arms. Fix the HxcIR builder so every pre-conditional immutable value needed after the join is explicitly available there, normally by typed block parameters, or by an equally explicit sequencing design that does not reevaluate or reorder the place. Do not weaken validation, special-case Caxecraft, rewrite the application source, emit raw C, or repair the graph in CAST/printer code. Keep arbitrary stored/escaping spans rejected.
acceptance_criteria: A focused generated-Haxe fixture covers direct and inlined helper forms; HxcIR validates and shows explicit cross-block availability; destination/index/condition/chosen arm each execute exactly once in Haxe order; unchosen arm does not execute; Eval and generated native behavior agree; strict GCC and Clang C11 at O0/O2 and eligible sanitizer lanes pass; runtime plan remains empty; existing span escape negatives remain unchanged; Caxecraft water compilation passes without changing its natural conditional store.
notes: Implemented a target-owned HxcIR fix: when an assignment destination depends on block-local values and its right side creates control flow, lowering saves the already-checked nonescaping element address in an automatic local, then stores through it after the join. A narrow coalescing rule keeps the adjacent address initializer structural, yielding one readable C pointer local. The span suite covers direct and inlined conditional stores, both branch values, one checked address per store, runtime-free plans, strict Clang C11, and sanitizers. The existing evaluation-order differential suite owns call/condition/chosen-arm sequencing and unchosen-arm behavior; it also passes with the new address-coalescing proof. Registered snapshots were updated through their owning updaters. Existing stored-span escape negatives remain fail-closed.
close_reason: Fixed generally in HxcIR lowering with focused direct/inlined conditional-store semantics, C-shape, native, sanitizer, and runtime-free regressions.

title: Profile and reduce repeated Reflaxe.C whole-program build cost
description: The exact pinned Haxe 5 compilation-server experiment produced byte-identical Caxecraft artifacts but no meaningful end-to-end speedup, even for an unchanged split build to the same output directory. Keeping a process alive can reuse some Haxe frontend work, but every request still reaches Reflaxe.C whole-program capture, HxcIR lowering/validation, declaration/project planning, maintainability-facing emission, and the output transaction. We need phase attribution before choosing incremental plans or caches.
design: Instrument first and keep timings opt-in or test-owned so normal compiler output remains deterministic. Do not cache raw mutable Haxe compiler objects across requests. Prefer immutable source facts or validated plans keyed by complete semantic inputs only after proving their construction dominates. If target lowering rather than Haxe typing dominates, optimize that pipeline instead of adding more server plumbing. Treat split/package/unity as separate define contexts unless one-typing/multi-layout emission is deliberately designed and parity-gated.
acceptance_criteria: Add deterministic low-overhead phase timing that separates Haxe parse/type/cache work from typed-program capture, HxcIR construction/validation, analyses, CAST/project planning, printing, and output ownership; compare at least three cold and same-context warm Caxecraft builds on controlled/recorded host conditions; identify the dominant repeated phase with executable evidence; implement the smallest safe optimization only if it measurably improves repeat wall time; preserve byte-identical cold/warm artifacts, complete source/file invalidation, stale-file deletion, diagnostics, and fresh mutable CompilationContext state; retain cold recovery and do not enable unsafe Haxe server no-check policies.
notes:
Implemented opt-in request-local compiler phase timing and a 3-cold/3-post-prime-warm Caxecraft profiler with exact-pin, artifact-parity, host-load, and macOS Haxe timer-clock evidence. Source audit found three HxcIR-to-CAST body traversals on the ordinary acyclic path. Production now builds one normal body; the body fixture explicitly opts into the #line copy, and project planning re-emits only when non-returning call-cycle semantics require it. Post-change contended sample: cold median 18.408s, warm median 16.486s, 30 normal artifacts byte-identical; remaining dominant CAST body construction was 11.441s cold and 11.652s warm. Haxe server reuse is therefore retained for future dev/watch work as a roughly 10 percent edit-loop win, while direct cold builds remain the recovery/CI baseline. Created haxe_c-xge.30 for the remaining emitter bottleneck so it does not delay the next playable Caxecraft increment. Passing so far: profiler 3+3 parity, formatter, typed boundaries, all-sources, body-lowering, function-lowering recursive/layout/native lanes, project-layout, and Caxecraft Eval/split/package/unity/native O2 differential.
Final local verification also passed the playable Caxecraft snapshot/direct-C lane and full Governance (114 tests). Profiler documentation and report now explicitly state that its 18.4s/16.5s boundary ends at generated C and excludes Clang/GCC, native linking, Raylib, and game execution.
close_reason: Added opt-in exact target-phase profiling, proved byte-identical 3-cold/3-warm Caxecraft output, and removed two redundant HxcIR-to-CAST body traversals from the ordinary path while preserving explicit line-mapped fixtures and non-returning-cycle re-emission. Post-change medians are 18.408s cold and 16.486s warm under recorded contention; the server provides a measured roughly 10 percent edit-loop benefit. All focused compiler/layout/native/Caxecraft/playable/Governance gates pass. The remaining 11.4-11.7s CBodyEmitter cost is bounded by haxe_c-xge.30 and will not block Caxecraft feature progress.

title: Reuse one Haxe compilation server in the Caxecraft edit lane
description: The default Caxecraft domain gate launches a fresh Haxe process for the Eval oracle and each split/package/unity C render. Under shared-host load, an otherwise healthy package render exceeded its 90-second request timeout during pre-commit. The compiler already proves request-local warm-server behavior, but the normal edit loop uses HAXE_NO_SERVER=1 and does not benefit from it.
design: Keep Eval isolated because its target facts differ from the C target. Start one loopback-only ephemeral Haxe --wait process for the three normal C rendering requests, pass --connect explicitly, and terminate/reap it on every success or failure path. Confirm against the pinned Haxe source that cache contexts are define-signature-aware and files are invalidated by modification checks; do not enable unsafe no-check policies. Retain cold builds in the exhaustive determinism lane and compare cold/server artifacts byte-for-byte. Measure cold and server-backed runs before selecting the default. If different layout defines prevent a meaningful improvement, retain the server for same-layout dev/watch rebuilds and pursue one-typing/multi-layout compiler emission separately rather than claiming a speedup.
acceptance_criteria: The default edit lane and future watch/build path use one owned ephemeral server where measurement proves it faster; no orphan process or fixed-port collision survives success, timeout, SIGINT, or validation failure; generated files, HxcIR, manifests, snapshots, and native traces match cold output exactly; rejected requests do not leak compiler state; an explicit cold authority remains in the full lane; focused governance tests assert process/request ownership and cleanup; timing docs state what the server can and cannot cache; before/after timings and host load are recorded without claiming an unsupported p95.
notes: Implemented and real-probed an exact-pin native Haxe 5 server/client path: HaxeShim resolve-args retains scoped dependency resolution, while the native server binds only 127.0.0.1 on an ephemeral port and is reaped on success, failure, or interrupt. Byte-for-byte artifacts and HxcIR matched cold builds. Measurement rejected using it in the default edit gate: at starting load 9.66, cold split/package/unity totaled 147.026s while one server totaled 186.413s (-26.8% in this contended diagnostic sample); same-output split repeats at starting load 18.32 were flat at 52.759s, 52.933s, and 56.853s. Hosted evidence is also nearly flat (four cold 269.783s vs four warm 266.312s). Retain warm requests as determinism/state-isolation evidence, keep the normal lane cold, and move optimization to phase-attributed repeated target work rather than claiming process reuse is faster.
close_reason: Completed the conditional server evaluation and safe transport. The runner can now own an exact-pin native Haxe 5 server bound to ephemeral loopback, resolves scoped HXML through locked HaxeShim, reaps on success/failure/interrupt, and preserves cold artifacts/HxcIR byte-for-byte. Measurement rejected promotion into the default lane: cold three-layout 147.026s versus server 186.413s in one contended sample; same-output repeats stayed flat; hosted cold/warm evidence is also nearly equal. Warm requests remain exhaustive determinism/state-isolation evidence, default stays cold, and haxe_c-fbq owns phase-attributed target-pipeline optimization. Focused lifecycle tests, real native handshake, three-layout parity benchmark, CI/toolchain policy, Governance 111 tests, and docs pass.

title: Restore pinned-toolchain CI headroom after exhaustive Caxecraft QA
description: Governance run 29696206056 proved every focused/platform job green, but the serial pinned-toolchain umbrella reached its 30-minute cap during the final centrally owned snapshot regeneration. The log shows all suites through full Caxecraft passed; snapshots:check was still making progress when GitHub cancelled the job. Preserve the complete gate and set a measured timeout with reasonable headroom.
design: The original containment-only option was to raise the serial timeout. After the user explicitly required fast tooling as a directive and asked for GitHub CI setup, replace the serial mega-job with five isolated, exact-coverage toolchain shards and a stable fail-closed pinned-toolchain aggregate. Keep every canonical command and the independent central snapshot proof; use 30-minute per-shard containment and a 5-minute aggregate timeout. Verify the replacement Governance run completes every shard and platform job.
acceptance_criteria: The CI policy requires five exact toolchain shards, bounded per-shard and aggregate timeouts, and the stable fail-closed pinned-toolchain status; an executable partition guard proves every test:toolchain command appears exactly once and the canonical serial command remains intact; policy/governance tests pass locally; a replacement Governance run completes every shard plus native GCC/Clang, Raylib, formatting, provenance, and secret scanning.
close_reason: Replaced the serial 30-minute pinned-toolchain mega-job with five exact-coverage isolated GitHub shards plus the stable fail-closed aggregate. The canonical 38-command local lane and all snapshot/native/platform gates remain intact. Local evidence: npm run deps:verify, npm run test:governance (63 governance tests), exact shard coverage, CI/fixture policy, YAML validation, staged path/Gitleaks guards, and the complete pre-commit compiler/snapshot/native chain all passed. Hosted evidence: Governance run https://github.com/fullofcaffeine/reflaxe.c/actions/runs/29698408759 passed all 17 jobs in 8m07s; shard durations were objects 4m48s, Caxecraft 6m14s, contracts 6m35s, snapshots 7m17s, semantics 7m59s, and aggregate 3s. Snapshot compute de-duplication remains explicitly owned by haxe_c-xge.25.

title: Normalize the raylib core selection hash across CRLF checkouts
description: The required Windows clang-cl raylib desktop job checks out docs/specs/raylib-core-selection.json with CRLF bytes, while scripts/raylib/core_binding.py compares a raw-byte SHA-256 recorded from the LF checkout. The parsed closed JSON is identical, but validation fails with raylib core selection hash is stale before compilation. Preserve exact raw-byte hashes for upstream C headers; make only the repository-owned textual selection digest line-ending-stable, with fail-closed UTF-8/JSON validation and no weakening of semantic drift detection.

Discovered by Governance run 29685203819: Linux GCC and macOS Apple Clang raylib desktop lanes passed, but Windows clang-cl failed before compilation because the repository selection JSON raw-byte digest changed under CRLF checkout conversion.
Implemented a dedicated selection_sha256 text boundary that normalizes LF/CRLF/legacy-CR before hashing while leaving upstream header/archive/license hashes exact. validate_lock now accepts an explicit selection path for adversarial tests. Focused 12-test core binding suite, full 27-test raylib provisioning lane, governance 63-test lane, and git diff --check pass. The reviewed selection and lock digest did not change.

Added CRLF, semantic-drift, and malformed-UTF-8 regression tests. title: Enforce a generated-C maintainability rubric on showcase programs
description: Current snapshot and native gates prove bytes, compilation, execution, ABI, and determinism but do not fail when correct output degenerates into an unreadable CFG dump. Define executable, reviewable output-quality evidence and apply it to Caxecraft plus smaller canonical fixtures.
design: Use a small typed/reporting rubric rather than subjective prose alone. Measure source-to-output ownership, ordinary-name readability, digest/encoding incidence, temporary density, label/goto density by justified category, function/file size, and source mapping. Pair metrics with representative hand-written C baselines and structural assertions; do not reward semantic unsafety or game-specific formatting. Store reviewed thresholds and first offending coordinates in a deterministic report.
acceptance_criteria: A documented schema-validated report is emitted or generated by QA for Caxecraft and representative canonical fixtures; CI fails on unexplained regressions in name, temporary, goto, file, or function complexity; every allowed goto is categorized; snapshots cover split and unity shapes without deriving expected bytes from the printer; strict native/Eval behavior remains the overriding gate; the README/capability inventory does not call output showcase-quality until the rubric passes.
notes: Implemented the bounded generated-C maintainability contract. Replaced the old project-wide unique-name regex with a comment/string-safe lexer, closed report and policy schemas, exact ownership/function/source coordinates, independent declaration/reference budgets, name classifications aligned with the compiler's 12-64 hex collision suffix contract, typed goto authorities, and first-violation coordinates. QA now covers body lowering, evaluation-order production plus the complete 6 irreducible + 1 loop-switch goto taxonomy, Caxecraft split/unity exact snapshots and replay/parity, and two durable handwritten calibration kernels. Caxecraft records 53 functions, 514 temporary declarations, 757 references, 262 declarations per 1000 function code lines, 50-byte maximum identifier, and zero gotos. Validation passed the complete 38-command two-worker toolchain matrix; full Caxecraft O0/O2/ASan+UBSan; final focused body, evaluation, default Caxecraft, exact native-only replay/parity, 88 governance tests, snapshot catalog, Haxe formatter, schema/JSON/Python checks, and staged secret/whitespace scans. Fresh final review approved after fixing expanded collision suffix recognition and native-only split/unity parity. The reviewer was GPT-5 Codex family, so strict different-family review remains unavailable and is not claimed.
close_reason: Added and validated the closed generated-C maintainability rubric across body lowering, evaluation order, and Caxecraft split/unity output. Exact snapshots/replay, typed goto provenance, reviewed budgets, handwritten calibration, native/Eval correctness, full toolchain, governance, formatting, and fresh review all pass; claims remain explicitly bounded to the fixed corpus.

title: Preserve readable source identities and safely coalesce generated values
description: Caxecraft output exposes semantic hashes, encoded internal role strings, anonymous structural aggregate identities, and a stable C temporary for every load. The naming registry is collision-safe, but the chosen semantic bases and unconditional stabilization obscure source concepts. Preserve source-owned naming facts through lowering and introduce narrowly proven CAST-level value coalescing.
design: Capture module/type/typedef/field/function/local display identities before type expansion loses them. Allocate readable deterministic C names first and add compact suffixes only for real collisions, specializations, anonymous values, or length limits. Keep full semantic keys in reports, not ordinary spellings. Analyze validated HxcIR uses and mutation/effect barriers; inline or directly initialize only pure, total, nonvolatile, single-use values whose sequencing, aliasing, lifetime, and failure behavior is proven. Preserve stabilization around C operand/argument-order gaps and observable loads.
acceptance_criteria: Named Haxe records/classes/enums/functions/fields/locals produce recognizable C names; collision-free Caxecraft output has no long digest or zx-encoded internal-role spelling; genuine collisions remain deterministic and are explained in hxc.symbols.json; focused adversarial tests prove no delayed loads, reordered calls, volatile/foreign alias errors, lifetime changes, or lost failures; output-complexity metrics bound temporary/name noise; GCC/Clang O0/O2, Eval parity, warm/reordered determinism, and existing symbol/evaluation-order gates pass.
notes: Use the checked-in Caxecraft BlockCoord header as the concrete readability fixture. A collision-free named record emits a short path-derived guard, the recognizable hxc_caxecraft_domain_BlockCoord tag, and short hxc_x/hxc_y/hxc_z members. The hxc_ prefix is intentional compiler-owned namespace protection: the C preprocessor expands macros before C scope lookup, so bare source names such as bool, NULL, or NAN are unsafe in generated declarations. Full semantic keys remain in hxc.symbols.json; ordinary C spellings receive a compact hash suffix only for a real collision, anonymous identity, specialization, or length limit. Generated-file provenance may remain a short comment.
close_reason: Hosted run 29712727888 exposed a native-only fixture regression after readable symbols replaced the old hardcoded spelling. Added a registered, schema-validated native-symbols.json projection generated from hxc.symbols.json, and made both full and checked-in native replay consume that stable source-to-C mapping. Local native-only Clang O0/O2, full static initialization, exact snapshot, fixture/CI policy, formatter, and all 70 governance tests pass. Implementation is complete; final true GCC/Clang hosted validation will be observed before handoff.

title: Structuralize reducible HxcIR control flow before CAST emission
description: CBodyEmitter currently maps every HxcIR jump, branch, and switch edge directly to labels and gotos. That preserves semantics but makes ordinary Haxe if/while/switch code look like a compiler CFG dump. Add a validated structuralization boundary so common reducible regions become idiomatic C without collapsing or weakening HxcIR.
design: Analyze the validated function CFG and build a closed typed region plan for sequences, if/else, loops, switches, returns, and explicit escape edges. Emit structured CAST for proven regions. Permit goto only for shared cleanup/error exits, irreducible graphs, or a documented bounded case; never infer semantics from generated label spelling. Verify region coverage, dominance/post-dominance assumptions, block-parameter/value availability, completion, and cleanup ownership before emission. Fail closed or retain the validated fallback only where policy explicitly permits it.
acceptance_criteria: Focused fixtures cover nested if/else, while, do/while-equivalent shapes, break/continue, switches without fallthrough, early returns, short-circuit expressions, failure/cleanup exits, and an irreducible synthetic CFG; reducible functions contain no blanket block labels/gotos and the irreducible/cleanup cases use only documented edges; HxcIR dumps remain semantically unchanged; strict GCC/Clang O0/O2, Eval differential, sanitizer/UB, determinism, and negative malformed-region tests pass; the printer receives structural legal input and performs no semantic repair.
close_reason: Implemented and verified typed reducible-CFG structuralization before CAST. Ordinary generated control flow is now source-shaped and Caxecraft is enforced zero-goto; bounded switch-loop escapes and proven irreducible CFGs retain explicit authority. Full npm test, all 30 snapshots, Clang O0/O2/sanitizers, Caxecraft differential/determinism, formatting, and governance passed. GCC identity remains covered by CI because local gcc resolves to Clang.

title: Implement deterministic split and unity generated-C layouts
description: The production emitter currently funnels almost every reachable definition into include/hxc/program.h and src/program.c even though lowered functions retain module ownership and the typed project boundary supports multiple GeneratedFile values. Add explicit project layout selection and make source-shaped split output the human-facing default while preserving an amalgamated unity option.
design: Use one closed typed layout setting with at least split and unity variants. Split groups definitions by normalized Haxe module/package ownership, emits deterministic private headers/prototypes from complete-type/linkage dependencies, and keeps a small entry unit. Unity renders the same finalized declaration/function plan into one implementation unit. File assignment is a pure plan before printing; build manifests and output ownership consume the resulting artifact set. Recursive-cycle partitioning must be reconciled with both layouts rather than bypassed.
acceptance_criteria: A representative multi-package Haxe fixture and Caxecraft emit predictable source-shaped paths in split mode and a single implementation unit in unity mode; both consume the same validated HxcIR and symbol/representation plans; byte output is stable across root, locale, discovery order, repeated and warm-server builds; all headers compile independently where declared; GCC/Clang O0/O2 executables and Eval traces match in both modes; build manifests enumerate the exact selected files; switching layouts safely removes stale owned artifacts and preserves user files; documentation explains tradeoffs and defaults.
notes:
Implemented one typed semantic/declaration plan with split-default and unity file assignment. Split emits deterministic package/module headers and sources, a common representation header, small entry/support units, exact build manifests, portable path encoding, and safe stale ownership. Added multi-package split/unity QA and moved Caxecraft snapshots to the split tree. Caxecraft now has a fast local O2 lane and an exhaustive determinism/O0/O2/ASan+UBSan lane retained by test:toolchain and native-only CI. Verification: npm run test:toolchain passed all gates and 30 snapshot suites; npm run test:governance passed 63 tests; formatter and focused quick/full Caxecraft gates passed.
Independent review found and this change now fixes one false-cycle risk: complete type definitions retain hard owner-header edges, but aggregate/class/tagged-enum references in prototypes and extern declarations use common forwards; native enums remain hard because strict C11 cannot forward-declare them. HardRecord/SoftRecord proves the C-valid mixed hard/soft cycle under standalone GCC/Clang headers, split/unity, determinism, stale cleanup, and Eval parity. Package-coalesced HXC-COMP-011 scope is now explicitly owned by haxe_c-xge.18.5. The older full-toolchain note is superseded; closure still waits for the final stable-state full gate and refreshed review.
Final stable-state evidence now replaces the superseded pre-review run: npm run test:toolchain passed every compiler/runtime/native/differential gate, project-layout, full Caxecraft split+unity O0/O2/ASan+UBSan, and all 30 snapshot suites. Post-run npm run test:governance, npm run format:haxe:check, git diff --check, capability regeneration/check, and exact Caxecraft asset validation all passed. Fresh-context GPT-5 Codex same-family review reports no blocking flags. Structured control flow, readable names, rubric enforcement, and package-coalesced layout remain separately owned by haxe_c-xge.18.2, .18.3, .18.4, and .18.5.
close_reason: Implemented and verified deterministic split-default and unity generated-C layouts over the same validated semantic/declaration plans. Source-shaped module ownership, common forwards, hard/soft dependency legality, standalone headers, exact manifests, stale cleanup, cold/reverse/locale/warm determinism, GCC/Clang O0/O2 behavior, Eval parity, and Caxecraft full sanitizer parity all pass. Deferred readability and package-coalescing remain explicitly owned by haxe_c-xge.18.2-.18.5.

title: Deliver human-maintainable, source-shaped generated C
description: Caxecraft exposed that the validated production path emits one IR-shaped program.c with long internal names, a temporary for every load, and basic-block labels/gotos for ordinary structured Haxe. This is semantically honest but does not satisfy the product contract that generated C be readable, idiomatic, and useful to a C programmer who wants to inspect or continue the project. Close the gap in the general compiler; do not prettify checked-in snapshots or add Caxecraft-specific emitter branches.
design: Keep TypedExpr -> validated HxcIR as the semantic correctness boundary. Add a separately owned HxcIR-to-CAST presentation/legalization layer that preserves semantics while selecting readable names, structured reducible C control flow, proven-safe value coalescing, and deterministic project layout. Support split and unity layouts from the same finalized program. Retain labels/gotos only for documented cleanup/error exits, irreducible graphs, or another mechanically justified C pattern.
acceptance_criteria: The Caxecraft generated project is readable enough to map modules, declarations, functions, fields, and control flow back to Haxe without consulting HxcIR IDs; split and unity outputs compile and behave identically; ordinary reducible if/loop/switch source does not become blanket label/goto code; collision-free source names do not carry hashes or encoded internal roles; every eliminated temporary has an executable sequencing proof; generated-output rubric, deterministic snapshots, strict GCC/Clang O0/O2, Eval parity, runtime/ABI reports, and stale-file ownership gates pass; no raw C or example-specific compiler branch is introduced.
notes: All five children are complete. The production HxcIR-to-CAST path now emits readable source identities, structurally reconstructs ordinary reducible control flow instead of blanket gotos, safely coalesces proven values, enforces a generated-C maintainability rubric, and supports deterministic split, package, and unity layouts from one semantic plan. Unity remains the single src/program.c option. Caxecraft is the flagship product-level E2E/QA workload and retains exact snapshots, Eval/native parity, strict O0/O2 and sanitizer coverage, runtime-plan evidence, deterministic output, exact ownership/stale cleanup, and remote cold-snapshot verification. Package completion shipped in dcbb2e30227a201ae9ed851a76582f288e5a5fa0; Governance 29729525446 and Cold snapshot audit 29729525464 passed. Future readability or performance findings belong to their focused owners rather than keeping HXC-COMP-011 open.
close_reason: Completed the human-maintainable generated-C milestone across all five children. Generated C now preserves readable source identities, structurally emits ordinary reducible control flow, coalesces values only with sequencing proof, enforces the showcase maintainability rubric, and offers split, package, or one-file unity output from the same validated semantic pipeline. Caxecraft and focused fixtures prove deterministic snapshots, strict native compilation, runtime parity, sanitizer behavior, manifests, stale cleanup, and zero example-specific/raw-C shortcuts. Package completion is dcbb2e30227a201ae9ed851a76582f288e5a5fa0; remote Governance 29729525446 and Cold snapshot audit 29729525464 passed.

title: Decide whether reflaxe.c can safely pin Haxe 4.3.7
description: The user prefers stable Haxe 4.3.7 over Haxe 5.0.0-preview.1. Audit the actual 4.3.7 compiler source and executable behavior before changing the reviewed dependency contract. Determine whether 4.3.7 can activate reflaxe.c without inheriting Cross target.utf16/utf16 facts or losing the scalar UTF-8/custom-target platform contract; assess Reflaxe and macro API compatibility, stdlib surface drift, lifecycle/server behavior, provenance, and any explicit fork or carrier decision that would be required.
design: Do not treat this as a version-string edit. Preserve fail-closed target identity and ADR 0004 string semantics. If upstream 4.3.7 cannot satisfy the contract, present the smallest explicit alternatives and their costs instead of silently patching Haxe or relabeling another target.
acceptance_criteria: Record source-anchored and executable evidence for 4.3.7 activation/platform behavior; compare the current Haxe 5 custom-target path; decide upstream pin, explicit maintained fork/backport, alternate supported carrier, or retention of the preview pin; update/author the governing ADR; if migration is admitted, update every pin/provenance artifact and regenerate platform/stdlib snapshots; run package, cold/server lifecycle, typed stdlib, all-source, target, and full relevant gates.
close_reason: Re-audited official Haxe 4.3.7 source and executable behavior. It has no custom-target/setPlatformConfiguration path, falls through to Cross with unremovable UTF-16 facts, and current sources also use Haxe 5-only AccPrivateCall. Recorded alternatives and retained the exact Haxe 5 preview carrier; any Haxe 4 fork requires a new owner-approved ADR. Verified: direct 4.3.7 help/Cross/all-source probes; npm run deps:verify; npm run test:bootstrap; npm run test:hxc-ir; npm run test:governance-policy.

title: Make tracked Git hook wrappers propagate repository-hook failures
description:
Context: While committing E1.T08, scripts/hooks/pre-commit failed its all-source gate, but the tracked .beads/hooks/pre-commit wrapper continued into Beads integration and returned success. The same unchecked delegation exists in pre-push. This can allow a commit or push after a repository-owned policy gate fails.

Scope: Make both tracked Beads hook wrappers immediately return the exact nonzero status from their delegated repository hook, and add executable governance evidence that later Beads behavior cannot mask that result.

Non-scope: Changing which repository checks run, weakening Beads timeout behavior, or redesigning hook installation.

Discovered while completing haxe_c-jdo.
acceptance_criteria:
Both .beads/hooks/pre-commit and .beads/hooks/pre-push stop immediately and return the delegated scripts/hooks status when it is nonzero.
Executable tests run each wrapper in an isolated fake checkout, force the delegated hook to fail, and prove the Beads phase is not invoked.
Security/governance guards fail if failure propagation is removed.
The successful hook chain and public preflight remain green.
close_reason: Fixed the fail-open wrapper defect. Both tracked .beads hook wrappers now capture the exact nonzero status returned by scripts/hooks/pre-commit or scripts/hooks/pre-push and exit before Beads integration can mask it. scripts/ci/check_security_tooling.py now executes each wrapper in an isolated fake checkout, forces delegated statuses 73 and 74, verifies argument forwarding, and proves the fake bd command is never invoked. Evidence passed: sh -n .beads/hooks/pre-commit .beads/hooks/pre-push; python3 -m py_compile scripts/ci/check_security_tooling.py; python3 scripts/ci/check_security_tooling.py; npm run test:governance (57 tests); npm run public:preflight (formatter, 92-commit Git scan, decoded history for 148 Beads issues, governance); the real pre-commit and corrected pre-push chains; GitHub Governance run 29541071365. The repository-hook selection and Beads timeout/database behavior are intentionally unchanged.

title: [SECURITY] Harden repository for public visibility
description: Audit every reachable Git ref and GitHub repository surface before publication. Match or exceed the leak prevention used by the sibling public Haxe targets, pin CI actions and security tooling, enforce Haxe formatting and staged/full-history secret scans, verify private reporting, then change visibility only after all local gates pass.
acceptance_criteria: Tracked content and all reachable Git history pass Gitleaks and local-path review; active pre-commit formats Haxe and scans staged content; pre-push and CI scan full history with checksum-verified tooling; every external GitHub Action is commit-pinned; common credential files are ignored; GitHub secrets, variables, environments, artifacts, branches, issues, PRs, and releases are audited; repository becomes public only after the audit; private vulnerability reporting is enabled and SECURITY.md is updated after verification.
