Commits df1b6c3, 0668ad3, and 7112cba add exact Haxe formatter enforcement; staged, complete Git-ref, and decoded Beads-history Gitleaks gates; checksum-verified Gitleaks 8.30.0; full-commit GitHub Action pins; credential ignores; guarded Dolt publication; governance tests; and verified public disclosure documentation. Audits found no leaks across 9 MB of Git history including refs/dolt/data, 80.17 MB of decoded history for 147 Beads issues, and 7.84 MB of downloadable Actions logs; the two unavailable logs were zero-step billing failures. GitHub reports PUBLIC, zero secret alerts, empty Actions/Dependabot/Codespaces secret and variable stores, and no environments, deploy keys, webhooks, artifacts, releases, issues, or PRs. Secret scanning, push protection, Dependabot alerts/security updates, private vulnerability reporting, and read-only Actions defaults are enabled and verified. Optional validity and non-provider pattern scanning remain unavailable and are not claimed. npm audit found zero vulnerabilities; public Governance run 29528732210 passed all six jobs. No compiler, runtime, generated-C, or public-ABI behavior changed.

title: [HXC-DISC] Resolve the production Haxe carrier for C semantics
description:
Context: Pinned Haxe 4.3.7 uses its Cross platform when Reflaxe runs without a native Haxe output target. Cross irreversibly initializes target.name=cross, target.utf16/utf16, target.sys, static, and related platform facts before initialization macros. The public macro API can add or overwrite values but cannot remove a define, so relabeling Cross as C would type UTF-16 stdlib and application branches contrary to ADR 0004/0007.

Scope: Choose and implement a production Haxe carrier whose compiler configuration matches reflaxe.c semantics, or explicitly supersede the affected owner decisions with measured compatibility consequences. Evaluate at least an exact Haxe 4 compiler patch/fork, a Haxe version with supported custom targets, and a documented Cross-plus-overrides strategy.

Non-scope: Implement the C String runtime, broad stdlib parity, or relax the UTF-8 scalar contract silently.

Validation: Run an actual non-probe reflaxe.c typing invocation and structural stdlib report. Prove static C-appropriate typing, target.name=c, c, target.unicode, absence of target.utf16/utf16, no unrelated carrier conditional, and adapter-derived sys/thread/atomic capabilities under cold and compiler-server builds.

Compatibility: Preserve ordinary Haxe conditionals and fail closed until the selected carrier is reproducible on every supported development host. Any compiler fork or version move must update the immutable toolchain/provenance contract.

Documentation: Record the accepted alternative in ADR 0007 or a superseding ADR and reconcile toolchain, configuration, architecture, PRD, AGENTS, and downstream Beads evidence.

## Rationale

Compiler platform configuration controls nullability, scoping, capture, exceptions, standard-library precedence, Unicode units, and capability conditionals before Reflaxe lowering. A target-name-only rewrite would make reports look correct while preserving contradictory typed branches, so production bootstrap cannot proceed without an explicit carrier decision and executable evidence.

## Alternatives Considered

- Build and provenance-pin an exact Haxe 4.3.7 compiler patch that adds a C platform configuration. This could preserve the language pin but creates cross-platform compiler distribution and maintenance obligations.
- Move to a Haxe version with supported custom-target configuration. This could provide the cleanest upstream API but requires compatibility review of Haxe/Reflaxe/compiler behavior and a new immutable pin.
- Keep Haxe 4 Cross and override affected standard-library modules/conditionals. This minimizes compiler distribution work but cannot hide global cross/UTF-16 facts from arbitrary portable application source and is therefore not acceptable without a superseding compatibility decision.
- Use Eval or another built-in target as the production carrier. Current evidence rejects this as a silent import of unrelated type-system, stdlib, and capability semantics; Eval remains a test oracle only.
acceptance_criteria: An accepted decision names the production carrier and rejected alternatives; the exact pinned toolchain supplies a static C-appropriate platform configuration; actual target typing exposes target.name=c, c, and target.unicode without target.utf16/utf16 or an unrelated carrier conditional; sys/thread/atomic facts come only from the resolved adapter; upstream String/StringTools/UnicodeString branch snapshots and cold/server probes pass; E0.T04 remains blocked until this evidence is executable.
close_reason: Accepted exact official Haxe 5.0.0-preview.1 at revision 2c1e544e0a2c7524ef4c8e103f1b0580362ea538 as the production typing carrier. Direct builds use --custom-target c=<output>; automatic c.Init.init()/TargetPlatform configure a static, block-scoped, scalar-Unicode PlatformConfig before typing, derive sys only for hosted, and advertise no threads/atomics without adapter evidence. CompilerInit validates that snapshot and derives Reflaxe c_output from Compiler.getOutput(), rejecting missing or mismatched output. Actual non-probe registration reaches source-root HXC1000 and emits no artifact in cold and compiler-server builds; lifecycle, staged-package, non-C isolation, recovery, hosted/freestanding, and upstream String/StringTools/UnicodeString snapshots pass. ADR 0007, ADR 0004, PRD, README, AGENTS, architecture, configuration, toolchain, provenance, research, and checked plan now agree. Rejected Haxe 4 Cross because unremovable UTF-16 facts leak to application conditionals; rejected a Haxe 4 fork because of cross-host distribution/maintenance burden; retained Eval only for future hxc bootstrap, differential oracle, and isolation. Exact official platform artifact hashes are lock-checked. Evidence: npm test; npm run deps:verify; jq empty docs/specs/*.json; python3 -m py_compile scripts/ci/check_toolchain.py test/bootstrap/run.py test/typed_c/run.py; bash scripts/lint/whitespace_guard.sh; bd lint --json (0); bd dep cycles --json ([]); git diff --check.

title: [HXC-DISC] Validate C target identity and Unicode platform defines
description:
Context: ADR 0007 chooses c_output as the Haxe 4/Reflaxe activation signal, c/target.name=c as public identity, target.unicode without target.utf16, and capability-derived platform defines. The partial checkout cannot yet prove that these signals activate exactly once or select the intended Haxe 4.3.7 stdlib branches.

Scope: Under the pinned Haxe/Reflaxe toolchain, add focused macro/type-check probes for c_output and target.name activation, non-C no-op behavior, public/internal define visibility, Unicode/UTF-16 selection, and conflicting platform definitions. Record the resolved compiler configuration and typed upstream String/StringTools branches.

Non-scope: Implement the C string runtime, Unicode algorithms, or broad stdlib parity; E4.T03/E5 own those.

Validation: Positive and negative HXML/macro fixtures show exactly-once activation, c public identity, reflaxe_c implementation-only guidance, target.unicode=true, target.utf16=false, and source-positioned rejection of conflicting identities/capabilities. The pinned target-owned Haxe bootstrap type-check gate runs the probes reproducibly.

Compatibility: Ordinary Haxe conditionals use #if c; c_output stays a path-bearing build transport. Capability flags are never asserted merely because the target is C.

Documentation: Reconcile ADR 0007, configuration/agent guidance, and E0.T03/E0.T04 evidence if implementation constraints require a superseding decision.
acceptance_criteria: c_output and target.name=c activation probes initialize the compiler exactly once; non-C builds remain untouched; c and Unicode platform conditions select the documented Haxe 4.3.7 branches; conflicting identity/UTF-16/capability inputs fail at a source position; the result is integrated into the reproducible bootstrap type-check gate.
notes:
Created from E0.T01 as the deferred experiment required before bootstrap hardens ADR 0007. It blocks E0.T04 and is blocked by E0.T03; it does not own String runtime semantics or broad stdlib work.
E0.T03 established the lifecycle subset under the exact pin: cold and compiler-server probes cover c_output activation, non-C isolation, exactly-once registration guards, public c, implementation-only reflaxe_c, target.unicode, and absence/rejection of target.utf16. This discovery remains open for target.name/custom-target activation, conflicting identity and capability inputs, source-positioned diagnostics, and proof of the selected upstream Haxe stdlib branches.
Resolved evidence: CompilerInit now normalizes target.name=c only after carrier validation, records exactly-once bootstrap/init counts and the raw carrier, adds root-anchored HXC0003 conflicts, and never treats caller -D c as activation. test/bootstrap/expected/target-contract.json proves c_output and compiler-owned target.name activation, public c versus internal reflaxe_c, target.unicode without target.utf16/utf16, and the scalar typed fields from pinned upstream String/StringTools/UnicodeString under the explicit Eval lifecycle carrier. Negative probes cover reserved target.* CLI input, unrelated identity/carrier, UTF-16, atomics, freestanding capability leakage, and the actual Haxe 4 Cross carrier. Cross predefines unremovable UTF-16 facts, so production bootstrap remains fail-closed and decision haxe_c-od2.6 now blocks E0.T04 and E4.T03.
close_reason: Acceptance complete for HXC-SCAF-003, HXC-SCAF-007, and HXC-SEM-006 target-identity validation. CompilerBootstrap/CompilerInit now expose deterministic count=1 markers, validate the raw Haxe carrier before normalizing target.name=c, preserve c_output as transport and c as the public conditional, retain reflaxe_c as implementation-only, add target.unicode without adding capability flags, and issue HXC0003 at the compilation root for conflicting identity, UTF-16, unproven atomics, or freestanding carrier facts. test/bootstrap/TargetContractProbe.hx plus expected/target-contract.json structurally prove the pinned upstream String.hx, StringTools.hx, and UnicodeString.hx scalar branches, target.utf16=false/utf16=false, target.name=c, public/internal visibility, c_output and compiler-owned target.name activation, caller -D c non-activation, non-C isolation, duplicate idempotence, package/CWD behavior, and valid/invalid/valid compiler-server isolation. The experiment also proved a material pin constraint: real Haxe 4.3.7 Cross predefines target.name=cross and unremovable target.utf16/utf16 before macros. Production Cross now fails closed instead of typing the wrong program; new P0 decision haxe_c-od2.6 evaluates a pinned Haxe 4 patch, a supported custom-target Haxe version, or a superseding compatibility choice and blocks E0.T04/E4.T03. title: Add live JSON world observations for agent play
description: Why: Piloscript can drive a predetermined journey, but an agent cannot yet play Caxecraft interactively because screenshots do not expose enough semantic game state and the runner exits after one script. What: add the smallest persistent, pilot-only session that accepts bounded actions through the normal game input path and returns a versioned JSON observation plus an optional real screenshot. design: Behavior scenario: Given a pilot-enabled Caxecraft process is running, when an agent submits a bounded action batch and asks to observe, then the same process advances through the normal input/game loop and returns one sequence-tagged JSON document describing the rendered player state. The agent can request a screenshot and a bounded local terrain/object query, then continue playing without rebuilding or restarting. Oracle: the Haxe-owned simulation and RuntimePilotObservation are semantic authority; the rendered framebuffer is visual authority; the accepted Piloscript action vocabulary is action authority. The external JSON is a codec over that state, never an independently simulated oracle. Keep a stable schema version and deterministic field meanings. Do not dump the complete map every frame. If a temporary confined request file is required before stdin support lands, mark it private and transitional, link it to haxe_c-8al, and remove it when typed stdin/stdout can carry the protocol.
acceptance_criteria: A pilot-only persistent session can execute at least movement, look, use/talk, wait, observe, capture, and quit through normal game ownership; each response is valid versioned JSON with a monotonically increasing sequence and current mode/level, position/heading, objective/dialogue/journal summary, vitals, inventory summary, crosshair target, nearby actors/interactables, and recent events where available; an explicit bounded local inspection reports nearby terrain/objects without a full-world per-frame dump; screenshots come from the real rendered framebuffer; the host can record accepted action batches as reloadable Piloscript; malformed or oversized requests fail closed without mutating game state; ordinary play is unchanged and the bridge is disabled by default; focused codec/limit tests and one real persistent agent-play tracer pass; any transitional transport has a documented removal owner and does not become a public content format or handwritten C application shim.
notes: Checkpoint JSON and persistent agent play are implemented. Runtime checkpoints and live requests emit CAXECRAFT_AGENT_OBSERVATION JSON from committed Haxe game state. The observation includes schema version, sequence, frame and tick, screen and mode, level, objective, dialogue, journal, interaction, aquatic state, player position and heading, vitals, hotbar, crosshair target, nearby authored actors and mechanisms, recent events, a bounded surface map, and the matching screenshot. The host copies this JSON into reports without calculating gameplay. Native red evidence first rejected Math.sqrt in the distance projection, so the stable schema uses exact squared milliblock distance instead of a compiler workaround. Native red evidence also rejected a runtime Raylib screenshot path because that C argument needs static storage. Literal capture branches now preserve that ABI rule while JSON reports the selected path. The live command is npm run caxecraft:play -- --agent-session --raylib-configuration memory-software. One pilot-only process emits an initial observation, accepts JSON envelopes that contain exact Piloscript bytes, and returns another observation after each batch. Haxe polls the confined staged request while idle, fingerprints changed bytes, validates them with RuntimePilotScript, requires the agent-session- name prefix, executes accepted actions through the existing game loop, captures the real framebuffer, and waits without restarting. The request file is transitional and must move to inherited standard input when haxe_c-8al lands. The typed runtime already flushes standard output. Piloscript now accepts explicit action 0 quit and inspect-radius values from 0 through 6. The option --agent-record-dir copies each accepted request byte for byte into an independently reloadable Piloscript file. The host does not parse, merge, or rewrite action semantics. Live tracer evidence used one process to switch to Adventure, open campaign selection, select and load Frostmere, talk to Nia, and retain objective.wake-ember with its dialogue and journal state. A malformed impossible action returned an error. The next valid observation retained the same game state. A radius 6 request returned a bounded 13 by 13 surface view. Explicit quit returned a final observation and closed the process. Recording produced two exact reloadable request files. Focused evidence: npm run test:caxecraft-runtime-piloscript passed Eval and native C with sanitizers. Backstop evidence: npm run caxecraft:content -- --pilot adventure-journey --piloscript pilots/frostmere.piloscript --raylib-configuration memory-software reused the executable and passed. Ordinary bounded journeys remain intact. Remaining work is the definitive standard-input carrier under haxe_c-8al and subjective campaign fun and visual review outside this protocol issue.
close_reason: One persistent pilot-only process now accepts bounded Piloscript batches, returns ordered Haxe-owned JSON plus real screenshots, supports bounded inspection/recording/quit, rejects malformed requests without mutation, and preserves ordinary journeys. The documented confined file input remains a transitional carrier owned for removal when haxe_c-8al lands.

Visual review shows a clear walk-through arch and path split. Remaining finding: cliffs and stone shelves beyond the arch are still abrupt and need later composition/encounter work under the parent. The compact Evergrove map remains the tutorial entry; the broad map owns outdoor travel.
close_reason: The Rootway is now a distinctive, passable reloadable landmark with readable route bands, an optional ration reward, coherent lore, one existing journey, and visual review. Broader terrain and encounter polish remain with the open chapter parent.

title: Author the connected Evergrove-to-Western-Falls tracer region
description: Create the first complete 64x16x32 reloadable outdoor map slice. Join Evergrove and Western Falls through playable terrain instead of a menu or campaign exit, and make the route feel like part of one authored place rather than two arenas placed side by side.
design: Use only CaxeMap, CaxeFlow, and reloadable content records for campaign facts. Start from the existing lore and strongest landmarks. Establish one readable main route, one traversal choice, one optional discovery with a useful reward or lore payoff, one story beat that points toward the falls, and a loop or shortcut that reconnects. Preserve kid-friendly recovery and Minecraft-like world interaction. Do not add engine literals, broad new mechanics, brittle coordinate assertions, or a second Piloscript journey.
acceptance_criteria: One ordinary 64x16x32 map loads through the existing runtime path; Evergrove and Western Falls are traversable without a level transition; the route contains a recognizable landmark, a meaningful choice, an optional discovery, a coherent story beat, and a reconnecting path; existing interaction and content schemas express the slice without recompiling; one representative Piloscript journey protects only key milestones; free-play review records visual, pacing, and coherence findings; legacy maps are reclassified or retained with a clear purpose.
notes:
Behavior scenarios before broad automation: (1) Given the player has entered Adventure in compact Evergrove, when they talk to Nia and reach the west gate, then the authored evergrove-west exit loads the expanded Western Falls level through the existing campaign transition. (2) Given arrival on the old river road in the 64-wide level, when the player travels west, then a ridge path and a lower stream path both reveal the falls and reconnect near Moss/Fallskeeper. (3) Given the player explores away from the main route, when they find Ceesh’s survey note, then a short optional journal clue and nearby berry cache reward curiosity without changing required progression. (4) Given the player reaches the falls overlook, when the authored trigger volume is entered, then one short story beat establishes Browser, Ceesh, and the river route while the existing Fallskeeper/Tideweave progression remains intact. Oracle: accepted game-design lore, manually reviewed terrain height maps from the two shipped authored chunks, ordinary campaign/runtime validation, and one graphical Piloscript journey. Visual appeal and pacing remain free-play review.
Implementation evidence (2026-08-10): expanded Western Falls to one 64x16x32 map containing reviewed Evergrove and Falls terrain chunks. The compact Evergrove entry now gives a Nia-owned west-road objective and uses an authored zone to request the campaign transition. The broad map has ridge and streambank routes, a falls-overlook story trigger, and an optional Ceesh survey note with berries. The journey reached generation 3 with two publications and captured the overlook, while reusing the executable with no compile or link. The production loader and receipt checks pass. Visual review confirms a real connected landscape and clean seam, but it remains a rough tracer: more landmark variety, route polish, encounters, and play-time belong to the open parent. The unused Western-to-Evergrove manifest edge and prompt were removed rather than advertising return travel. The broad campaign-runtime backstop passed Eval/native/sanitizers under a temporary 120-second native allowance; haxe_c-xty2 owns its measured 185.26-second total cost.
close_reason: The connected tracer region is implemented and verified through reload-only production loading, one representative Adventure journey, receipt checks, native campaign backstop, and visual review. The broader chapter remains open for content expansion and polish.

title: Admit a 64-by-16-by-32 outdoor world envelope
description: Measure the current fixed world and renderer storage, record the decision against runtime logical dimensions and streaming, then admit the smallest larger finite envelope that can hold seamless Evergrove and Western Falls regions. Keep content reloadable and preserve exact chunk face capacity.
design: Use one fixed 64x16x32 physical simulation envelope. Admit authored maps at 32x16x32 and 64x16x32. Resolve a 32-wide map into the west half, add an unbreakable boundary column at x=32, and leave the unreachable east remainder empty. The terrain and water buffers remain 32 KiB each. Split the 32-chunk renderer face cache into two 16-chunk banks because one 98,304-byte fixed array exceeds haxe.c's reviewed 65,536-byte per-array limit. The connected outdoor map uses the full width. Do not add general dimensions, streaming, or campaign-specific engine branches.
acceptance_criteria: A checked design records measured current and projected storage, editor and generated-C effects, plus rejected alternatives; a focused test is red before the size change and passes on Eval/native C; the ordinary resolver loads both 32x16x32 legacy maps and one 64x16x32 map into the fixed envelope; narrow maps receive a safe generic boundary; terrain cache invalidation and exact checkerboard capacity remain proven in both banks; generated C keeps each fixed array within 65,536 bytes; content edits still need no Haxe or C rebuild.
notes:
Red contract: npm run test:caxecraft-terrain-chunks returned envelope 1 on current main. This is the intended failure: the focused owner still reports width 32, 16 chunks, and 49,152 total face slots instead of the admitted 64-wide, 32-chunk contract. Oracle: manually derived 8x16x8 chunk geometry over 64x16x32, plus haxe.c's documented 65,536-byte fixed-array ceiling.
Green implementation evidence (2026-08-10): the engine now uses a 64x16x32 physical envelope and accepts authored widths 32 and 64. Legacy maps resolve into the west half with a bedrock boundary at x=32; a synthetic 64-wide map resolves all cells. GameSession measures 66,736 bytes. TerrainChunkCache measures 393,632 bytes, split into eight 49,152-byte C arrays under the 65,536-byte compiler limit. The first bank-helper implementation was rejected for fixed-array indirection (HXC1001 fixed-array-requires-direct-literal); direct field-owned bank access is the natural supported Haxe shape. The wider water probe exposed and fixed an old width-32 bit-shift coordinate conversion. Passed: terrain-chunks, resolved-level-plan, water, session, cold domain split/package/unity differential, runtime-level-loader Eval/native/sanitizers, editor, compile-only playable, Adventure graphical journey, and independent renderer comparison with 5,296-face parity. Existing compact map edits still use runtime loading; no campaign literal entered the engine. The broad loader C generation exceeded 60 seconds twice and passes with a case-specific 120-second bound; haxe_c-xty2 owns measurement and remediation.
close_reason: The bounded wider-world engine contract is implemented and independently verified; connected campaign authoring remains with the parent.

title: Add the typed CaxeFlow campaign-exit action
description: Add the map-owned request half of authored campaign travel: a closed campaign-exit action parses, validates without requiring a campaign wrapper, writes canonically, executes deterministically, and emits a typed shell request.

acceptance_criteria: The focused codec red state is recorded; campaign-exit round-trips byte-identically; the action registry covers the constructor and argument role; the executor emits CampaignExitRequested; scenario-model and CaxeFlow Eval/native checks pass; no app-shell destination selection or loading-screen claim is made.

title: Build one broad connected outdoor Adventure chapter
description: Why: Evergrove, Western Falls, Frostmere, and Ashfall are currently separate 32x16x32 arenas even though the accepted design calls them regions of a broad outdoor journey. More decoration inside those boxes will not create exploration, continuity, or several hours of coherent play. What: establish a reviewed larger finite-world engine envelope, then re-author the first outdoor chapter as one connected reloadable CaxeMap with readable biome transitions, landmarks, loops, optional discoveries, puzzles, encounters, and story beats. Keep castle interior/boss or another genuinely distinct space as deliberate campaign level boundaries. How: first measure storage/render/water/editor implications and choose a bounded physical capacity plus logical dimensions or another evidence-backed seam; retain chunked rendering and content reload; build one narrow corridor-to-landmark tracer before expanding the full chapter.
design: Start with a cold audit of World, GameSession storage, water pending state, raycast/physics bounds, terrain chunk cache, renderer capacities, ResolvedLevelPlan, editor grids, and generated-C stack/static size. Prefer logical runtime dimensions inside a reviewed fixed maximum if it preserves simple bounded C and avoids recompiling content, but do not force that design if measured generated-C or compiler limitations make it unsafe. The content chapter should use the existing lore and authored route, borrow only general voxel-adventure pacing principles, and make travel itself produce decisions and discoveries. Art, pacing, and fun are play-review owners, not brittle visual assertions.
acceptance_criteria: A checked design compares runtime logical dimensions within fixed bounded C storage, a larger compile-time world envelope, and premature streaming, with measured memory/draw/rebuild/editor costs and a maintainer-readable decision; the engine loads at least two admitted world dimensions without campaign-specific branches, or records a narrower explicitly accepted envelope if haxe.c constraints require it; one connected outdoor CaxeMap contains at least Evergrove and Western Falls as seamless regions before later Frostmere/Ashfall expansion; the first tracer has a meaningful landmark, traversal choice, optional discovery, one coherent story beat, and a return/reconnect path rather than an empty corridor; content edits still relaunch/reload without rebuilding Haxe/C; engine contracts receive focused tests while content keeps only one representative Piloscript journey plus play review; the old small maps are retained only while they own a real dev/regression role and are removed or reclassified once superseded; no procedural infinite terrain, broad streaming engine, save-system completion, or several-hours claim is made until played evidence supports it.
notes: Completion audit (2026-08-10, current main 86ef147): haxe_c-xge.20.1.8.1 admitted the measured 64x16x32 physical envelope while preserving compact 32-wide maps. haxe_c-xge.20.1.8.2 joined compact Evergrove entry travel to one broad Evergrove/Western Falls map with two terrain chunks, route choice, optional Ceesh survey discovery, story beat, and one existing Piloscript journey. haxe_c-xge.20.1.8.3 added the Rootway landmark and optional ration. haxe_c-xge.20.1.8.4 added the one-block stepped reconnecting approach to Moss and the Fallskeeper while preserving the ridge and flooded grotto. Content edits passed executable reuse, shortest production loading, package receipts, graphical journey, and visual review. Compact Evergrove remains the tutorial/transition owner; Western Falls was expanded rather than duplicated. No streaming, save, infinite terrain, several-hours, or full-world claim is made. Loader build/runtime cost remains separately owned by haxe_c-xty2.
close_reason: Current main satisfies the bounded connected-chapter acceptance: measured wider engine, seamless Evergrove/Western terrain, landmark, choice, optional discovery, story beat, reconnecting approach, one journey, visual review, and no-rebuild content proof. Later Frostmere/Ashfall expansion remains with the broader world owner.

title: Drive Adventure travel from authored exit zones
description: Why: the current Adventure changes levels when the player presses N anywhere, so the campaign feels like disconnected debug arenas and the world does not own where travel happens. What: add one closed CaxeFlow action that requests a typed campaign exit, consume it through the generic game shell, and introduce an honest transition state before atomically publishing the destination. Add the missing Western Falls to Frostmere edge and one real authored gate tracer. How: trigger the request from an existing validated enter-zone rule; keep destination selection in campaign JSON, keep map content independently valid, and keep campaign names/coordinates out of compiled engine code. Scenario: given Adventure is playing Western Falls and the player is outside the authored north-road zone, ordinary movement does not travel; when the body enters the zone and CaxeFlow requests its exit ID, the app shows the destination transition state, loads and validates the matching campaign edge, then publishes Frostmere at its entrance; malformed or ambiguous exits keep the current level active with an actionable failure.
design: Independent oracle: the authored CAXEMAP rule and campaign manifest define the expected exit ID and destination; the focused expectation is manually authored from that closed contract, not generated by the implementation. Lowest faithful owners: CaxeFlow codec/executor for the action, campaign manifest lookup for edge selection, AppScreen/game shell for transition lifecycle, and one Piloscript for the real UI-to-world boundary. Preserve the existing N input only as an explicit dev-mode shortcut if still useful; it must not remain the ordinary Adventure progression path.
acceptance_criteria: A generic typed CaxeFlow campaign-exit request is parsed, validated, written canonically, executed, and observable without Raylib or campaign literals; one focused test is red before implementation for the intended missing action/transition reason; the campaign shell matches the requested exit only against outgoing manifest edges and rejects missing or ambiguous matches without replacing active state; the native app reaches Frostmere only after entering the authored Western Falls gate, not from arbitrary N input; a real transition screen/card names the destination and contains no fake progress; the map, campaign manifest, package receipts, and one narrow Piloscript journey remain reloadable; Eval/native focused checks and one real Raylib tracer pass; no broad save, branching editor UI, cutscene system, or larger-world claim is implied.
notes:
Red-state evidence 2026-08-10: after adding the focused ScenarioCodecProbe expectation, npm run test:caxecraft-scenario-model failed in Eval at the intended boundary. The parser rejected the campaign-exit action as UnexpectedRecord(do) at fixture line 93. This confirms the closed CaxeFlow codec lacks the action; no native or UI layer was involved. Independent expected syntax and meaning come from the manually authored map/campaign split in this issue: the map requests an exit ID and the campaign graph separately resolves it.
Completion evidence 2026-08-10: focused red states were recorded before implementation. npm run test:caxecraft-app-screen failed because Loading, beginLoading, finishLoading, and showsLoading did not exist. npm run test:caxecraft-campaign-runtime failed because CampaignManifest.transitionForRequest did not exist. Both failures were at the intended owner. The independent oracle is the manually authored split contract: CAXEMAP raises an exit ID, while the validated campaign manifest independently names its source and destination. The focused campaign probe proves current-level matching, unknown/wrong-level rejection, and duplicate-exit schema rejection. Western Falls now owns a trigger-zone and campaign-exit rule; campaign JSON owns the Frostmere edge and refreshed receipts. Release input no longer maps N to travel; that shortcut is dev-only. The app shows one destination card with no fake progress, then performs the existing checked load on the next outer frame. A rejected load clears the pending request and resumes the unchanged active level. Verification: app-screen Eval/native C with sanitizers passed; campaign-runtime Eval/native C with sanitizers passed; runtime-piloscript Eval/native C with sanitizers passed; content refresh --check passed; full native compile-only passed; Haxe formatter check passed. The real Raylib memory-software Adventure Piloscript passed twice with identical semantic evidence: 395 frames, Western Falls generation 2/publication 1, then authored gate to Frostmere generation 3/publication 2, final native framebuffer 1280x720. A direct measured sample took 17.9 seconds, so only runtime-content journeys use a bounded 25-second process timeout; short engine pilots retain 15 seconds. The host campaign screenshot check was reduced from fixed route/color rectangles to dimensions plus nonblank framebuffer liveness because Piloscript owns campaign semantics and layout pixels should not freeze content iteration.
Post-close package proof found one real closure gap: adventure-characters.png was declared runtime-packaged but omitted from caxecraft.package.json. Added its independently measured byte length and SHA-256 digest. The canonical ZIP test then passed Eval, generated native C, sanitizers, standard-reader handoff, and isolated native replay. The complete 11-asset native export took about 225 seconds on this machine, so only package-zip-export now has a bounded 240-second native timeout; ordinary focused/content lanes remain short.
close_reason: Authored Western Falls exit now drives the checked loading card and atomic Frostmere publication; focused, native, content, and two-run Piloscript evidence passed.

title: Load supplemental sprite and icon atlases without debug fallback
description: The generic runtime texture catalog and launcher receipt admit only tile-atlas. A content-declared sprite-atlas is staged but its 3x2 grid is flattened to 1x1 and the Haxe catalog skips loading it. StatefulObjectRenderer then draws the orange selection/debug cube; from close range it looks like a giant orange terrain surface. The Castle mechanism atlas exposed this after semantic/no-build checks passed.
design: Treat every validated grid atlas kind (tile-atlas, sprite-atlas, icon-atlas) as a runtime texture atlas. Preserve its authored columns/rows in the launcher receipt and let the typed Haxe catalog load it generically. Non-atlas image kinds remain 1x1 and the six legacy fixed owners remain excluded from supplemental loading. Keep the orange cube only as an honest missing-presentation diagnostic.
acceptance_criteria: A focused receipt test is red because selected sprite/icon grids are flattened; after the fix all selected atlas kinds preserve exact manifest grid dimensions; malformed grids remain rejected; the Haxe catalog loads supplemental sprite/icon/tile atlases without content IDs; the real Castle journey renders the mechanism sprite instead of the orange debug cube; no-build content feedback remains green; no campaign literal enters engine code.
notes:
Focused red: python3 test/governance/test_caxecraft_build_state.py CaxecraftBuildStateTests.test_runtime_asset_receipt_preserves_every_selected_atlas_grid. It expected castle-mechanisms=(3,2), entities=(4,5), HUD/items/adventure-items=(4,4), but the receipt reported each non-tile atlas as (1,1). Green evidence:
- The launcher now treats icon-atlas, sprite-atlas, and tile-atlas as validated grid assets and preserves their manifest columns/rows in the runtime receipt. Non-grid image kinds remain 1x1.

- The focused receipt test moved from the intended mismatch (castle-mechanisms 1x1 instead of 3x2, plus other flattened sprite/icon grids) to green. All 20 build-state tests, Haxe formatting, pilot policy, and the real Castle journey pass.
- The rebuilt 1280x720 final frame visibly shows the dark-slate/copper inner relay with its teal active path. The former giant orange fallback cube is absent. Two semantic pilot runs were identical.
- A subsequent --content-feedback run reused the verified executable, restaged current bytes, and passed with no build.
Oracle/provenance: manifest grid metadata is the independent layout authority; the real software framebuffer owns visibility; semantic object-state checkpoints own interaction state.
close_reason: Supplemental sprite, icon, and tile atlases now retain exact grids and render through the typed catalog; the Castle orange fallback is gone.

Runtime package bytes are staged and validated after startup, so treating asset additions as compiler inputs defeats the intended creator feedback loop without protecting generated C.

acceptance_criteria: The focused build-state owner proves assets are runtime inputs and cannot enter the compile fingerprint; compiler, Haxe source, binding, and launcher source remain build inputs; adding or changing a reviewed package asset passes --content-feedback with the already verified executable; the real Castle journey loads and displays the changed atlas; no compile or link fallback occurs.

Red command: python3 examples/caxecraft/play.py --content-feedback --raylib-configuration memory-software --pilot adventure-journey --piloscript pilots/castle-courtyard.piloscript. It failed before launch with: content feedback refused compiler or linker fallback; rebuild deliberately first: build input added: repo/caxecraft/assets/atlases/castle-mechanisms.png.

title: Carry by-value C imports through owned Haxe constructors
description: Caxecraft's generic runtime texture catalog naturally stores one Raylib Texture2D value in an owned Haxe atlas record. haxe.c rejects the constructor signature at RuntimeTextureAtlasCatalog.hx:171 with HXC1001 TFunction(constructor-argument:3-type-not-admitted:c-import:raylib.raw.Texture). Direct imported C calls and local by-value Texture2D values already work; passing the same header-owned by-value struct into a non-escaping owned Haxe constructor does not. Add the smallest reusable constructor/field carrier support without weakening pointer or borrow rules.
design: Reduce to a framework-neutral header-owned struct returned by one imported function, passed by value into an ordinary owned Haxe class constructor, stored in a field, borrowed for one imported observer call, and passed to one imported cleanup call. Preserve exact C struct spelling and value-copy semantics. Do not admit pointer-like imports, Dynamic, unchecked casts, or retained CStringRef. Then use the Caxecraft runtime texture catalog as the vertical Raylib proof.
acceptance_criteria: A focused fixture is red with the current constructor-argument diagnostic; Eval-equivalent semantics or an independently authored native observer proves the stored fields; generated strict C compiles and runs with the imported struct passed/stored by value; pointer-like and borrowed C imports remain rejected; existing constructor and c-import suites pass; Caxecraft compiles its natural RuntimeTextureAtlas record and the Castle gate renders; the Bead records the pre-fix command and concise failure reason.
notes:
Red/green evidence (2026-08-10 UTC):
- Pre-fix: python3 test/c_import/run.py failed on the reduced PointOwner constructor with HXC1001 TFunction(constructor-argument:0-type-not-admitted:c-import:Point).
- After admitting the signature, the same fixture failed at this.point = point with HXC1001 TBinop(OpAssign:immutable-place), proving the field initialization owner was still missing.
- Final behavior: the generated strict C constructor receives struct pointlib_point by value and stores it directly; the native header-owned observer and cleanup calls pass. Pointer-like and call-bounded imports remain outside CBVKImport.
- The canonical c-import snapshot/native/negative matrix passed, all 221 owned modules passed, and the real Caxecraft RuntimeTextureAtlas record compiled and rendered the Castle gate.
Broad verification also exposed a stale constructor negative left by the earlier mutable Array-field replacement feature: other.values = values is now intentionally valid. The fixture now protects the still-unsupported static-field escape instead, and python3 test/constructor_lowering/run.py --negative-only passes. The preceding full constructor run had completed the positive matrix before reaching that stale final negative.
close_reason: By-value header-owned C imports now cross owned Haxe constructors with focused native and Caxecraft vertical proof.

title: Load and render content-declared texture atlases generically
description: Adding a reviewed atlas to assets/manifest.json and caxecraft.package.json currently passes package validation, but play.py stages only the fixed RUNTIME_ASSET_IDS tuple and CaxecraftApp loads only eight compiled texture fields. StatefulObjectRenderer then recognizes only four hard-coded atlas IDs and falls back to a debug cube for any new content-owned atlas. The Castle portcullis visual exposed this gap: the journey passed while castle-gate.png was absent beside the executable. Make the validated runtime asset inventory own staging, loading, lookup, drawing, and cleanup so creators can add an atlas without editing Python or recompiling campaign-specific Haxe. Keep GPU lifetime explicit and generic; do not hard-code Castle names.
design: Start with one synthetic extra one-cell atlas as the tracer bullet. The package/asset manifest is the independent authority for path, digest, grid shape, and cells. Stage every reviewed runtime asset selected by the package closure, load it through one typed texture owner, resolve stateful-object presentations by validated asset ID and cell metadata, and unload each valid texture exactly once. Preserve dedicated title/HUD paths only where their product-global presentation contract genuinely differs. Then re-run the real Castle gate as the vertical proof and verify a second content-only art change reuses the executable.
acceptance_criteria: A new package-declared atlas is staged without adding its ID to play.py; the native app loads and draws its declared cell without an asset-name branch; malformed/missing/hash-drifted files fail before replacing the live content generation; valid textures have one owner and exactly one unload; a focused synthetic regression proves unknown/unready handling and grid dimensions; the Castle portcullis renders from castle-gate.png in a real Piloscript frame; after one engine rebuild, changing only that atlas or its content mapping passes --content-feedback with no compile or link; no campaign names enter generic engine code.
notes:
Implemented the generic runtime-atlas tracer through package selection, staging, typed GPU ownership, lookup, drawing, and reverse-order cleanup. play.py now derives staged assets from runtimeIntegration.packagedPrimaryAssets instead of a compiled ID tuple, verifies path/hash/kind/grid metadata, and writes the runtime receipt consumed by Haxe. RuntimeTextureAtlasCatalog loads supplemental tile atlases by validated content ID; StatefulObjectRenderer has no Castle-name branch.

Real tracer: castle-gate.png (SHA-256 0e0278630196ece89b231c538b2ab4a3ca2cb2d9319b552fc097348f0f6cf9f2) is declared in the asset/package manifests and drives the sealed portcullis state in Castle Courtyard. The memory-software Castle Piloscript passed twice after a cold build, the framebuffer visibly showed the gate without clipping/debug fallback, and --content-feedback restaged current bytes and reran the journey without compile or link.

Independent authorities: package manifest path/digest/grid metadata, Raylib's const-char*/Texture2D C ABI, the header-authored c-import native observer, and the real framebuffer. Asset, content, Raylib provisioning, Caxecraft pilot-policy, all-sources, c-import, and constructor fail-closed gates pass.

Residual before closing this Bead: add the focused synthetic malformed/unready/grid catalog regression promised by acceptance criteria. The six original product-global atlases remain on their dedicated typed paths and are deliberately excluded from supplemental loading; migrating those is cleanup, not required for new content-declared atlases.
Creator-loop follow-up: castle-mechanisms.png was added after the generic atlas engine build. The first --content-feedback attempt exposed haxe_c-xge.20.4.14.2 because the launcher still fingerprinted the whole assets directory. That bug is fixed and closed: after one tooling rebuild, the existing executable restaged the new atlas and passed the Castle journey with no compile or link. This is the required second content-only art change.
The Castle mechanism sprite exposed and closed haxe_c-xge.20.4.14.3: generic supplemental loading now covers validated tile, sprite, and icon atlases rather than tile atlases alone. The focused receipt owner preserves every selected manifest grid, and the real frame shows the active relay instead of the orange debug cube. No campaign ID was added to launcher or Haxe engine code.

title: Lower conditional values in managed Array indexed assignments
description: Caxecraft trigger-zone state exposed a compiler defect. Eval accepts an Array<Int> indexed assignment whose right side is an inline conditional, but haxe.c emits HxcIR that fails its own Array set type validation. Add a framework-neutral Array runtime regression, preserve single evaluation and the assignment result type, then prove Eval and native C agree. Red evidence: npm run test:caxecraft-runtime-level-loader reached generated C and failed with HXC9000 at GameSession.queueTriggerZoneTransitions because triggerZoneInside[zoneIndex] = inside ? 1 : 0 did not produce a matching managed Array element/result type.
acceptance_criteria: A focused ordinary-Haxe fixture is red for the reported conditional Array<Int> assignment; lowering emits a validator-approved managed Array set with exact Int element and assignment-result types; the array-runtime differential suite passes on Eval and native C; the Caxecraft runtime-level-loader proof passes without an application-shaped workaround.
notes: Implemented a generic control-flow fix in managed Array indexed assignment. The lowering now saves the evaluated receiver and index before a conditional right side creates branches, then reloads both at the join. Focused red: python3 test/differential/array-runtime/run.py --toolchain clang failed with HXC9000 at generated/Main.hx conditional Array<Int> assignment. Green: the same command passed the pinned Haxe Eval oracle, generated C, Clang, sanitizers, ownership, aliasing, allocation-failure, and deterministic-discovery checks. The Caxecraft runtime-level-loader vertical proof also passed without an application workaround.
close_reason: Conditional managed Array assignments now preserve evaluation order and pass differential native evidence.

title: Restore entity atlas rendering in desktop Caxecraft builds
description: A current default desktop adventure-journey build emits only three DrawBillboardRec call sites and fails play.py's reviewed four-borrow guard. The memory-software variant emits all four. In the failing desktop generation, CaxecraftAtlas.drawEntitySprite and its actor/enemy calls are removed even though the Haxe source still calls them, which may make NPCs and enemies disappear in the real desktop game. Diagnose whether this is incorrect haxe.c dead-code elimination or a compile-definition/input mismatch; retain focused compiler evidence if lowering is at fault and keep the desktop flagship guard honest. Discovered during Castle Courtyard content work; do not weaken the guard to unblock content.

The failing command was --build-only, whose contract is to validate/link the already published generated C project without invoking Haxe. That older project correctly contained the pre-4d10a6e drawWorldSprite path and failed the four-billboard structural guard instead of producing a misleading executable. A cold current-source desktop compile emitted four DrawBillboardRec sites and both current drawEntitySprite calls. A warm current-source compile emitted the same content-derived generation. Final real proof: python3 examples/caxecraft/play.py --no-build-cache --pilot adventure-journey --piloscript pilots/castle-courtyard.piloscript generated fd755f2d0845468f9431c795739d725f0ac8713b462e64056877aa71764d0e7b, built the desktop executable, and passed two identical semantic runs plus the 1280x720 framebuffer check. No guard or gameplay code changed.

title: Stage runtime levels from the package manifest
description: The native launcher stages runtime content from a fixed Python tuple that names Evergrove and Western Falls. A valid new campaign level such as Frostmere is therefore omitted even when caxecraft.package.json owns it with exact receipts. This makes package growth require launcher source edits and can produce a staged campaign that references a missing level.
design: Keep Python limited to host-side staging. Derive staged non-asset package files from the reviewed caxecraft.package.json entries, validate every relative path and duplicate fail closed, and add only the runtime Piloscript file as the one launcher-owned extra. Do not reimplement CAXEMAP, campaign, or package semantics in Python; Haxe remains the semantic validator.
acceptance_criteria: A focused red package with an additional level proves the old fixed tuple omits it; staging copies every manifest-owned non-asset entry including arbitrary admitted levels and removes stale formerly-owned files; asset staging remains separately owned; malformed JSON, missing entries, duplicate paths, path escape, symlinks, and missing source bytes fail clearly; build input hashes remain unchanged for content-only edits; governance tests and a real no-build Frostmere launch pass.
notes: Implemented and verified 2026-08-09. Correct red: the alternate-package staging test failed with FileNotFoundError for Frostmere because the launcher fixed tuple omitted it. Green: play.py now derives non-asset runtime paths from caxecraft.package.json, rejects malformed/duplicate/escaping/unknown entries, keeps assets separate, and lets --piloscript select exact repository content under the engine's generic active path. Governance: 19/19 build-state tests and check_pilot.py pass. Vertical proof: ordinary adventure-journey rebuild passed twice, then the identical Frostmere UI -> campaign -> level -> Nia journey passed through --content-feedback with 'reused the verified executable' and 'no build'. Frostmere map edits changed package receipts but did not enter the compile identity. Runtime content remains Haxe-validated; Python only validates bounded host copy paths.
close_reason: Manifest-owned staging and selectable no-build Piloscript journey are verified.

title: Preserve conditional String operands in concatenation
description: Caxecraft exposed invalid HxcIR for ordinary managed String concatenation when the right operand is a conditional expression: prefix + (condition ? value : fallback). Add the smallest focused red fixture, preserve the conditional result across its join, and retain the real Caxecraft rebuild as integrated proof.

Independent oracle: Haxe Eval exact output selected=chosen and selected=fallback. Green: the complete clang String output/runtime/cleanup lane and npm run test:hxc-ir pass. The original Caxecraft direct conditional concatenation is retained for the integrated rebuild.
close_reason: Closed

title: Preserve conditional-derived binary operands across joins
description: Caxecraft’s closed schema invariant compares two ordinary Bool expressions. The left expression lowers through an optional-scalar control-flow join; lowering the right expression opens another join, after which the outer binary instruction incorrectly reuses the left branch-local SSA value. HxcIR validation rejects the full app with HXC9000 value not available. The earlier haxe_c-af1 fix covered call, record, and enum-payload consumers but did not cover binary operands.
design: First add the smallest typed fixture with two conditional-derived primitive operands in one equality or inequality expression. Preserve Haxe left-to-right evaluation by staging an earlier operand before lowering a later operand that may change the current block. Reuse the established flow-local protocol rather than relaxing HxcIR validation or special-casing nullable integers. Keep the natural Caxecraft schema invariant as the vertical proof.
acceptance_criteria: The focused fixture is red with the recorded HXC9000 before the fix; Haxe Eval supplies the independent result oracle; generated HxcIR passes use-before-definition validation and shows a stable operand handoff; strict C11 O0/O2 output matches Eval; reversed and compiler-server-warm renders are deterministic; existing evaluation-order and HxcIR gates pass; the unchanged Caxecraft app compiles through haxe.c.
notes:
Current vertical red: npm run test:caxecraft-domain:full reaches playable snapshot compilation and rejects RuntimeContentPack.readStatefulObjects at the invariant (interaction == none) != (radius == 0). HXC9000 reports value.154 unavailable at instruction.228.binary.left in optional-scalar-join. The sanitizer-enabled runtime-level-loader lane had already passed, so the failure is generated HxcIR control flow, not schema behavior.
Focused red confirmed: python3 test/function_lowering/run.py --toolchain clang rejects mismatchedOptionalFacts at Main.hx:115 with HXC9000. The exact unavailable value is instruction.28.binary.left in block.3.optional-scalar-join. Eval owns the four-case truth table: absent/absent false, present/absent true, absent/zero true, present/zero false.
Green: python3 test/function_lowering/run.py --toolchain clang passed Eval, unity/split/package, repeated output, strict Clang, and zero-runtime checks. npm run test:hxc-ir passed. Vertical green: python3 examples/caxecraft/play.py --allow-network --pilot launch-smoke --raylib-configuration memory-software compiled the unchanged schema invariant, linked 128 native objects, and passed two identical 1280x720 semantic pilot runs. The fix teaches expressionCreatesFlow that non-null optional-scalar equality creates a hidden compare/join, so the existing generic binary staging saves the earlier operand.
close_reason: Optional-scalar equality now reports its hidden join to enclosing expression staging; focused strict/native and real Caxecraft graphical evidence pass.

title: Own managed enum local replacements
description: Caxecraft’s generic nearest-interaction selector naturally keeps a closed payload enum in a local variable and replaces that value while comparing candidates. Eval and Haxe typing accept this ordinary code, but haxe.c rejected the assignment because replacing a managed enum could leak the old payload or release a borrowed replacement too early. Implement the reusable ownership rule instead of forcing application code into numeric tags, duplicated branches, or out-parameters.
design: The focused ordinary-Haxe fixture replaces a managed enum local with fresh and borrowed payload variants, then consumes the result through exhaustive matching. Lowering must capture ownership of the replacement before it destroys the old value, which keeps self-assignment and borrowed payloads safe. The rule is generic HxcIR/CAST lowering and does not inspect Caxecraft names. The real Caxecraft selector remains the vertical proof.
acceptance_criteria: The focused fixture is red for the recorded managed-enum assignment HXC1001 before the fix; Eval provides the independent semantic oracle; generated C compiles under the primary strict compiler and runs with matching output; generated code acquires a borrowed replacement before releasing the old enum and has balanced cleanup; no raw-C or application workaround is added; Caxecraft’s natural AvailableInteractionTarget selector compiles and runs unchanged.
notes:
Red vertical command: python3 examples/caxecraft/play.py --allow-network --pilot launch-smoke. Exact compiler failure: CaxecraftApp.nearestAvailableInteraction is rejected with HXC1001 Unsupported typed Haxe node function-exit:unowned-fresh-managed-enum-value. The function returns a closed enum with EntityId or ScenarioId payloads and the caller exhaustively matches it. npm run test:all-sources passed first, so only generated-C ownership lowering is missing.
Focused red: python3 test/enum_lowering/run.py --bytes-payload-only --toolchain clang rejected replaceSelection with HXC1001 managed-Array-reassignment-not-admitted. Green: the same command passed Eval comparison, deterministic cold/warm generation, unity/split/package builds, strict Clang execution, and ownership cleanup. Generated C inspection shows borrowed string payload retention before old-enum destruction and replacement storage. Repository gates npm run test:all-sources (221 modules) and npm run test:hxc-ir passed. Vertical proof: python3 examples/caxecraft/play.py --allow-network --pilot launch-smoke --raylib-configuration memory-software compiled and linked the natural selector, then passed two identical semantic graphical pilot runs. The desktop GLFW launch was unavailable in this host session, so the software-memory backend supplied the native observer.
close_reason: Implemented and verified generic ownership-safe managed enum reassignment, with focused and Caxecraft vertical proof.

title: Make authored stateful interactables playable for the Tideweave vault
description: Western Falls now gives the player the exact four-mark code, but Tideweave is still reached through a mineable sand seam because runtime-loaded content rejects stateful-object definitions and the app can interact only with actors. Do not model glyphs as NPCs, hard-code Western Falls identities, add arbitrary scripting, or broaden this into a prefab/ECS framework.

title: Load the Caxecraft atlas-cell catalog from the content package
description: Adding a new sprite cell currently requires editing RuntimeAssetInventory.hx and rebuilding Caxecraft. Replace that reviewed static subset with a small typed runtime asset catalog inside the package, so creators can add atlas cells through data and use the existing content-feedback executable.

Lift that generic application-shell limit so authored levels can contain Moss, the Fallskeeper, and later NPCs without campaign IDs or prose entering engine Haxe.

title: Present authored journal clues in the playable HUD

The native playable currently ignores that event and exposes no readable journal, so content cannot keep an important clue recoverable after dialogue disappears. Connect the smallest generic presentation path, then use one Western Falls route note as a vertical content tracer without adding campaign facts to engine Haxe.

Resolve its validated localized title and body through the active RuntimeLevelPresentation, and show it in the existing paused overlay so Escape remains the only new player action needed in this slice. A newly added entry may show short generic feedback, but pausing must always make the latest clue readable. Do not add a journal screen state, input key, save format, campaign literal, second NPC, or general quest-log browser yet. The active level can resolve a validated journal title and body by stable ScenarioId and locale, with missing IDs failing to empty presentation rather than stale text. 3. The app records a journal only after a diagnostic-free committed CaxeFlow tick and exposes the latest unlocked entry in the paused HUD; simulation stays paused and no mutable scenario state reaches drawing. 4. Western Falls uses CAXEMAP to add one bilingual Moss route note and unlock it during the existing interaction, with no campaign prose or IDs in generic Haxe or Python. 5. Runtime Piloscript reaches the note through the real title to Adventure path and observes the generic journal identity or visible paused journal at the lowest faithful boundary. 6. Focused Eval/generated-C/sanitizer checks, the native journey, package receipts, ZIP closure, and reuse-only content feedback pass. 7. title: Advance authored objectives from real item collection
description: Western Falls can collect and equip Tideweave and collect the grotto lantern through generic authored-item mechanics, but those committed facts never reach CaxeFlow. The active objective therefore remains Find Tideweave after the player already owns it, and content cannot express a truthful find, explore, reward, complete progression without an engine name or polling workaround. Add the smallest reusable typed event-source slice, then use it only in CAXEMAP and runtime Piloscript to complete the existing chapter loop.

The parent haxe_c-xge.19.10 still owns consolidating all event-source metadata into a shared editor-facing event registry; do not invent a one-event parallel registry in this bounded tracer. Western Falls content owns Tideweave and lantern rules and bilingual objective copy. Piloscript observes progression through the real title-to-Adventure route. The canonical CaxeFlow model, codec, validator, writer, deterministic matcher, and tests admit one typed item-collected event with no dynamic payload; haxe_c-xge.19.10 retains the broader event-registry/editor consolidation. 3. title: Refresh package receipts after base content edits
description: The Haxe content-refresh planner succeeds for map edits but rejects a valid base content-pack edit because the outer package receipt still points at the old content bytes. This blocks the intended reloadable creator loop for adding NPCs, items, or mechanics data. Update the complete package graph in memory so a valid changed content pack updates its runtime receipt and outer package receipt before production verification.
design: Keep the existing Haxe planner and atomic publisher. Add the current content-pack receipt to the package update set before writing the outer manifest. Add a focused in-memory source overlay that changes one valid content value and proves the plan updates runtime-content.json and caxecraft.package.json without changing or compiling the game. Do not add Python or a second hashing implementation.

description: Caxecraft resolves actor identities and validates their presentation cells, but the native renderer still draws fixed Nia and Mossling atlas cells. title: Refresh content package metadata with one authoring command
description: A canonical CAXEMAP edit currently requires manual updates to the level record in the campaign manifest, the runtime-content receipt, and the outer package manifest. During haxe_c-xge.20.4.2.7, one 341-byte map edit first failed runtime-content generation at assertion 8, then failed package loading at assertion 2 until all nested byte lengths and SHA-256 values were updated. play.py can compute a staged runtime receipt, but no checked-in authoring command updates the full nested metadata chain. Add one content-authoring operation that canonicalizes the map and refreshes all derived content records atomically. Keep semantic ownership in Haxe or the existing editor/content model. Do not add another standalone Python script; a thin existing host command is acceptable only as an adapter.
design: Treat derived hashes and byte lengths as content build metadata, not hand-authored gameplay. Reuse the validated CAXEMAP writer and existing SHA-256/package models. Compute the complete output graph in memory, then publish it atomically. Keep ZIP as transport only and apply the same metadata operation before directory or ZIP export.
acceptance_criteria: One documented command accepts the affected content package or level; canonicalizes authored CAXEMAP before hashing; updates campaign.json, runtime-content.json, and caxecraft.package.json in dependency order; supports a read-only check/diff mode; writes atomically or leaves every file unchanged; gives an actionable error for malformed content or an inconsistent package graph; editor save/export can call the same operation; map-only edits do not require a Caxecraft rebuild; package-manifest, runtime-content-generation, campaign-runtime, scenario round-trip, and Piloscript content smoke evidence pass; no new standalone Python script or duplicate hashing algorithm becomes the content authority.
notes:
Representative red state (2026-08-08): `npm run caxecraft:content:check` exited 1 because the script did not exist. This is the intended failure: the checkout has no supported authoring command that checks or refreshes the campaign → runtime receipt → outer package metadata chain after a CAXEMAP edit.
Implemented evidence (2026-08-08): added one Haxe-owned in-memory refresh planner, typed campaign/package/runtime receipt writers, an Eval command with package-wide and --level forms, read-only --check, rollback-capable publication, and a durable editor-style replacement probe. play.py no longer computes the runtime receipt; it copies the Haxe-refreshed checked-in file. `caxecraft:content` refreshes before reuse-only play, while `caxecraft:content:validate` checks before the shortest Piloscript smoke. Oracle/provenance: ScenarioWriter plus the real RuntimeContentRegistry canonicalize and validate maps; RuntimeContentDigest owns SHA-256; decoded typed manifests preserve authored IDs, graph, roles, kinds, and order; the fixed generation input is shared with runtime verification. Tracer: an in-memory title edit changed map -> campaign -> runtime receipt -> outer package, then the final overlaid package passed the production verifier. A CRLF temporary-directory edit produced check exit 1, refreshed four files, converged byte-identically on the canonical source map, and left no temporary files. A malformed map returned its exact UnexpectedRecord location and left the campaign, runtime receipt, and outer package hashes unchanged. Timings: the missing-command red failed in 0.2 s without doing useful work; the complete current package check measured 3.92 s cold and 3.96 s on a second process run. No game rebuild occurs for this command. Verification passed: content-refresh Eval probe; scenario codec round-trip; package-manifest Eval/native C with sanitizers; runtime-content-generation Eval/native C with sanitizers; campaign-runtime Eval/native C with sanitizers; all-sources; typed-boundaries; Haxe format; package check; rebuilt launch-smoke with two identical semantic runs; then reuse-only `caxecraft:content:validate` Piloscript. The first native draft exposed assertion 8 in the hexadecimal digest path; byte-level verification restored native behavior while sharing the exact generation input. Follow-up haxe_c-7pov owns the reduced compiler/runtime investigation. The focused refresh probe is included in test:toolchain. No retries or quarantines were used for the final semantic evidence.
close_reason: One Haxe-owned command now canonicalizes maps and refreshes campaign, runtime, and outer-package metadata without rebuilding Caxecraft. Read-only, malformed-input, native sanitizer, final-package, and reuse-only Piloscript evidence pass; haxe_c-7pov retains the separate native hex-path investigation.

title: Lower reducible loop exits without goto
description: Caxecraft's rule-admission loop contains a repeat-policy switch. The Once and Cooldown arms leave the enclosing loop, but haxe.c emitted two goto statements because a C break inside a switch exits only that switch. The generated-C policy correctly rejected the result. A separate managed Array<Class> fixture also exposed a loop-local early-return error. Lower both reducible shapes to structured C without changing natural Haxe source or weakening cleanup and evaluation order.
acceptance_criteria: A focused Array<Class> fixture is red for the intended matched-return failure and uses Haxe Eval as its behavior oracle; a synthetic loop/switch fixture proves the nested-break shape; haxe.c emits structured C with no goto for both reducible shapes; strict native execution matches Eval; Caxecraft compile-only passes without an application workaround.
notes: Red evidence: before the fix, the managed Array<Class> native fixture hung after a matching lookup followed the loop exit instead of returning the matched object; Haxe Eval supplied the expected found/missing behavior. The Caxecraft compile-only command independently rejected CaxeFlowRulePlanner.c at lines 1023 and 1042 because the Once and Cooldown switch arms emitted goto hxc_tmp_while_exit_n9. Oracle/provenance: pinned Haxe Eval for class lookup identity and manually reviewed Haxe loop/switch semantics for the enclosing-loop break. Green evidence so far: test:evaluation-order passed its strict native matrix; array-runtime passed with clang, Eval, GC, failure paths, and sanitizers; Caxecraft --compile-only passed its no-goto policy; the full-inventory-gift native pilot then launched and observed both flowRuleObserved=true and objectiveChangeObserved=true.
close_reason: Replaced reducible loop/switch gotos with a loop-owned Boolean handoff and fixed loop-local abrupt-tail planning. The focused Array<Class> Eval/native/sanitizer lane, synthetic strict-C control-flow matrix, HxcIR and typed-boundary checks, formatter, Caxecraft no-goto compile-only path, and native objective-change pilot pass. Irreducible CFG gotos remain separately typed and audited.

title: Propagate stack-borrow contracts through direct instance calls
description: Borrow-contract refinement currently preserves class-reference forwarding only through direct static functions. A final or otherwise devirtualized instance method that forwards a caller-owned stack object to another exact synchronous instance method is incorrectly treated as an escape, blocking the native CaxeFlow executor.
design: Extend the existing fixed-point borrow refinement to resolve exact direct instance targets with the same dispatch proof used by lowering. Account for the implicit self parameter separately from explicit arguments. Preserve fail-closed behavior for virtual, interface, indirect, constructor, storing, returning, throwing, or capturing uses. Do not special-case CaxeFlow.
acceptance_criteria: A focused ordinary-Haxe fixture passes a stack-constructed local through a final direct instance method into a second exact borrowing instance method under Eval and native C; generated HxcIR marks both parameters as borrows and generated C uses automatic storage without allocation; unknown virtual forwarding still fails closed while genuinely retained objects keep owning storage instead of borrowing caller stack; constructor-lowering, HxcIR, class dispatch, sanitizers, strict GCC/Clang, and the Caxecraft runtime-level tracer pass.
notes:
Oracle correction: a known direct retaining chain is not required to fail compilation. Whole-program escape analysis may safely select collector-owned storage. The negative invariant is that it must never retain caller stack; unknown virtual forwarding remains fail-closed, while retained objects require an owning representation.
Implemented exact direct-instance borrow forwarding by reusing CBodyDispatchCatalog direct-dispatch proof and mapping explicit arguments past the implicit self parameter. The focused fixture was red with stack-reference-escape at ForwardingSink.read, then passed with automatic storage through ForwardingSink.read -> readDirect. Unknown virtual dispatch remains fail-closed; genuinely retained object graphs continue to select owning collector storage. Verification: python3 test/constructor_lowering/run.py --direct-argument-only; npm run test:hxc-ir; npm run test:constructor-lowering; git diff --check. The repository-wide Haxe formatting guard currently reports only the separate in-progress GameSession CaxeFlow integration file.
close_reason: Propagated proven stack borrows through exact direct instance calls with focused and exhaustive Eval/C11/sanitizer/layout/server/HxcIR evidence; CaxeFlow advanced to the separately owned managed Array field-reassignment boundary.

Connect the validated scenario flow to the fixed-tick session through the architecture records typed event/action boundary. Keep Raylib and translated prose outside the rule engine. Expand action application only as real mechanics gain typed command owners.
acceptance_criteria: A runtime-loaded CAXEMAP rule fires in the native playable from a real semantic gameplay event; the same scenario and event produce matching Eval and generated-C results; malformed or unavailable references fail before publication; the application contains no content-name special case; a focused engine regression diagnoses the event-to-flow contract and a representative Piloscript journey proves the real boundary; authored map edits remain no-build content changes.

Native compilation then exposed two general compiler gaps, which haxe_c-08bv and its predecessor fixed without a Caxecraft workaround. The expanded session probe later aborted because its handwritten C harness called managed Haxe before the generated GC lifecycle; the harness now invokes generated main and reads exported scalar observations. A final content review also found stale nested package hashes after the map edit and a duplicate C byte-total oracle. The shipped campaign expectation remains in map.caxemap and the Piloscript journey, not in GameSession.
