Final evidence: test:caxecraft-session, test:caxecraft-runtime-level-loader, test:caxecraft-caxeflow, test:caxecraft-pilot, test:caxecraft-runtime-content-generation, test:caxecraft-campaign-runtime, test:caxecraft-package-manifest, test:caxecraft-scenario-model, test:caxecraft-scenario-determinism, test:typed-boundaries, and format:haxe:check passed. Caxecraft compile-only passed. The final native Piloscript ran two identical semantic runs at 1280x720 and exited within 15 seconds. Its native cache reported 122 object hits and zero misses after the final map-only edit, so content remained outside compilation. Review disposition: no Western Falls, objective title, or campaign rule special case exists in engine or app logic. The focused engine test uses synthetic content. Piloscript owns the shipped content journey. The C package harness no longer duplicates content byte values. Exact package hashes remain valid integrity evidence, but their manual refresh cost is deferred to haxe_c-xge.19.12.
close_reason: Connected validated runtime-loaded CaxeFlow to GameSession through typed fixed-tick events. A real native actor interaction now fires the authored map rule and updates the HUD objective without campaign-name branches or rebuilding for map edits. Eval, strict native C, sanitizers, canonical package checks, compiler no-goto policy, and a two-run Piloscript journey pass. Follow-up haxe_c-xge.19.12 owns one-command refresh of derived package metadata.

title: Render pools and waterfalls as continuous water
description: Close-up play in Western Falls shows authored flowing water as stacked intersecting translucent sheets. The renderer already culls faces between equal full cells, but it emits a vertical wall for every one-eighth level difference and gives each top four identical heights. Through alpha blending this makes a connected pool read as overlapping cubes rather than one body of water.
design: Keep simulation bytes and generic CAXEMAP semantics unchanged. Joined pool tops continue to derive shared corner heights and omit internal same-y walls. For a free-falling authored waterfall, use permanent source cells at the lip and let the simulation derive falling cells; do not seed a tall open initial volume, because every non-falling layer correctly feeds sideways and forms a shelf. Preserve volume declarations for sealed pools and flooded rooms. Verify the change through runtime-only content reload and a close waterfall frame before considering renderer alpha sorting or new geometry.
acceptance_criteria: Adjacent exposed pool cells with different flow levels compute matching shared-corner heights; no translucent internal step wall is submitted between same-y water neighbors; exposed banks and true vertical drops retain side faces; Western Falls uses lip sources rather than a tall open full-water volume; transparent faces are ordered far-to-near for the current camera; the transparent pass preserves depth testing, disables depth writes only while its flushed water batch is active, and restores them before later drawing; the exact pinned rlgl declarations and native ABI probe cover both depth-mask calls; a close real Raylib frame keeps the route and terrain readable instead of overwriting them with opaque/intersecting cyan slabs; focused water, generated-C layout, and real adventure evidence remain green; simulation rules and CAXEMAP schema remain unchanged; keep the issue open until the maintainer accepts the close gameplay angle or records a narrower aesthetic follow-up.
notes:
Behavior-first red evidence: the maintainer's 1280x720 close-up frame shows a connected pool as overlapping horizontal and vertical translucent sheets. Code inspection identifies the intended failure sensitivity: WaterRenderer.exposedSideBottom returns the lower neighboring water surface, so every adjacent flow-level difference satisfies bottom < top and emits a vertical quad; emitTop gives all four corners the current cell's independent height. Independent oracle: two adjacent top cells share physical edge/corner positions, so every shared vertex must have one identical derived height, and an edge whose same-y neighbor is water is internal rather than an exposed side. The simulation state remains the input oracle and must not change.
Green evidence (2026-08-03): WaterSurfaceGeometry now derives each corner from the same four same-y water states, so adjacent tops share byte-identical vertex heights; WaterRenderer omits same-y water-water side quads and retains outer air faces. The simulation bytes, trace, and CAXEMAP format are unchanged. npm run test:caxecraft-water passed the same assertions under Eval and haxe.c/native C with sanitizers. npm run snapshots:update -- --suite caxecraft-domain and npm run test:caxecraft-playable passed split/package/unity semantic parity and exact generated-C ownership; the helper emits as a separate 250-line module and WaterRenderer remains 313 lines with no allocation/goto/campaign literals. npm run test:caxecraft-adventure-journey passed two deterministic 1280x720 native Raylib runs; its destination frame shows Western Falls as a joined waterfall and stream with the stacked internal flow-step walls absent. The aquatic-gear journey also passed gear, submersion, sand mining, water exit, deterministic framebuffer, and bounded-exit checks. Haxe formatting and git diff --check passed.
Reopen evidence (2026-08-03): maintainer screenshot after commit 174704f shows several large horizontal water shelves and diagonal/intersecting top faces above the falls. Source inspection classifies this as partially resolved rather than a renderer regression: the map declares a 2 x 6 x 2 initial volume open to air. placeInitialVolume intentionally writes full, non-falling cells; desiredFlowCode allows each such cell to feed horizontally, so all six authored layers spread. Falling cells produced below a source do not feed sideways. Independent behavioral oracle: a waterfall should be fed at its lip, fall vertically through open air, and spread when terrain supports it. The smallest red content fact is the waterfall-column volume declaration; the existing source-only simulation behavior is the generic owner.
Implemented source-only waterfall correction (2026-08-03): removed the open 2 x 6 x 2 initial-volume declaration and retained the authored lip source. The same simulation now derives a falling column, which cannot feed sideways while airborne and spreads only when supported. Before: maintainer close-up showed six broad horizontal shelves. After: the real 1280x720 Adventure destination frame shows one narrow vertical curtain feeding the lower pool, with no elevated shelves; no renderer, simulation, schema, or generated engine code changed. Runtime-only replay then reused the verified executable and passed in 16.80s with no build. Receipts: map 11108 bytes / fc39dddb502ab704ef9cc87eaa346a7657686ee91d7e5c76fec790931c4b6455; campaign 958 bytes / 72cfa5445783c62ef6424e9594b1c5f9132a9570f40da57cd44c44759af69c9c. Canonical ZIP: 16 entries, 9492602 bytes, SHA-256 11f42bc7132affd23a49f4fa4fd3b7cd18cb6f50a924c4319bbcbe05a15de613, FNV-1a signed -1444911062; standard reader, Info-ZIP, and isolated native handoff pass. Focused water, package-manifest, package-ZIP-export, and campaign-runtime Eval/generated/native/sanitizer lanes pass. Keep the issue open until the maintainer confirms the same close gameplay angle is visually acceptable; this avoids repeating the prior overclaim.
2026-08-09 visual review: the final Western Falls journey screenshot still shows intersecting translucent water sheets around the return walkway. The traversal and submerged/dry semantic checks pass, but they do not satisfy waterfall composition or visual-quality acceptance. Keep this issue open; evidence image is examples/caxecraft/_build/play/variants/macos-memory-software-split-pilot-adventure-journey/bin/caxecraft-pilot-runtime-final.png.
2026-08-09 next-increment confirmation: current native adventure-journey frame reproduces large translucent water planes crossing and overwriting the return walkway. WaterSurfaceGeometry already joins shared corners and WaterRenderer already omits same-y internal sides. The remaining renderer submits all transparent quads in fixed world z/y/x order through the normal depth-writing batch, while the reviewed Rlgl facade exposes no depth-mask state. Classification: confirmed unresolved presentation defect, not stale content evidence. This increment will first prove the smallest generic transparency-state and ordering contract; simulation bytes, CAXEMAP content, movement, and campaign facts remain out of scope unless a state dump disproves the presentation diagnosis.
2026-08-09 transparent-pass increment: intended red evidence was (1) python3 test/raylib_provisioning/test_rlgl_binding.py rejecting the old exact eight-function selection when the independent expectation required rlDisableDepthMask/rlEnableDepthMask, and (2) npm run test:caxecraft-water failing with Type not found: caxecraft.app.WaterRenderOrder. The independent oracle is standard alpha composition: preserve opaque terrain depth, submit translucent faces far-to-near, and prevent those faces from writing depth while they blend. The pinned raylib 6.0 rlgl.h at commit dbc56a87da87d973a9c5baa4e7438a9d20121d28 is the ABI oracle for the balanced state pair. Implemented: a Clang-derived ten-function raw rlgl lock/probe; a semantic begin/end transparent-quad boundary that flushes before state changes and restores depth writes; deterministic camera-distance ordering with stable ties; a renderer-owned grow-on-demand array that is resized and reused rather than allocated and regrown each frame; and lighter top/side alpha. Generated C confirms rlDrawRenderBatchActive -> rlDisableDepthMask -> water batch -> rlDrawRenderBatchActive -> rlEnableDepthMask, with the array created once in the renderer constructor and resized to zero per frame. Green evidence: raw binding unit/verify; full raylib provisioning including native ABI; water Eval/native/sanitizer; typed-boundary and capability guards; formatting; refreshed split/package/unity snapshots and playable structural gate; and the 350-frame memory/software adventure-journey pilot with two identical semantic runs. The reviewed final frame at examples/caxecraft/_build/play/variants/macos-memory-software-split-pilot-adventure-journey/bin/caxecraft-pilot-runtime-final.png no longer lets water hard-occlude the log route or terrain. It still has a deliberately voxel-stepped waterfall silhouette, so this note does not claim final art direction or close the maintainer visual-review requirement.

title: Add manifest-backed developer Adventure level selection
description: The developer-preview Adventure screen already lists every level from the validated runtime campaign manifest, but only the entry level is marked active and Launch always starts that entry. Make the listed levels selectable in developer mode so a content author can choose a map and launch it directly without changing generic engine code or rebuilding for content changes.
design: Use the validated CampaignManifest as the sole list and identity source. Keep selection as transient UI state, support keyboard and pointer input, and route launch through the existing receipt-checked runtime campaign level loader plus atomic ActivePlayableLevel publication. Do not embed campaign names, level IDs, prose, or coordinates in the engine. Keep ordinary campaign entry/travel behavior available when developer mode is removed.
acceptance_criteria: Selecting Adventure presents every manifest level; the active row can be changed with keyboard and pointer input; confirming launches the selected map through the ordinary runtime loader and refreshes all level-owned gameplay/presentation state; invalid or changed bytes fail closed without replacing the active level; a real native Adventure UI journey reaches a non-entry level; editing only runtime content still reuses the existing executable; no campaign-specific literal enters generic Haxe or host validation.
notes: Implemented a manifest-backed developer level selector on the existing Adventure screen. Before this change, the screen drew every manifest row but always highlighted index 0 and Launch entered only the campaign entry. In the native Adventure journey, frame 2 now issues the same generic Next action available from the keyboard, highlights the next validated manifest row, and frame 3 launches it through loadCampaignLevel plus atomic ActivePlayableLevel publication. Evidence: npm run test:caxecraft-pilot passed; haxelib formatter check passed for all four changed Haxe files; npm run test:caxecraft-adventure-journey passed at 1280x720 with two identical runs, content generation 2 and one publication; python3 examples/caxecraft/play.py --content-feedback --pilot adventure-journey --raylib-configuration memory-software then reused the verified executable and passed without a build. Pointer rows and buttons use the same typed CampaignMenuHit result. No campaign name, level ID, prose, or coordinate was added to generic engine validation. title: Turn Western Falls into a playable exploration chapter
description: Western Falls now has a strong waterfall silhouette and route landmarks, but it is still mostly a destination frame: the existing Mossling, concealed Tideweave pickup, mineable terrain, and water mechanics do not yet form a deliberate beginning-to-payoff activity loop. Shape the level as a loop rather than a corridor: arrival overlook and waterfall establish orientation; a safe descent presents the shrine and alternate sightline; the Mossling guards but does not permanently block the approach; a visibly suspicious sand seam teaches that authored terrain can hide a route; the current Tideweave pickup enables the flooded grotto; the grotto exits or loops back safely and reveals snow/ash/castle direction. Keep the four-glyph shrine as foreshadowing, not a substitute for the planned repeatable Fallskeeper clue, journal record, ordered code lock, or sealed-vault progression. Those later mechanics must not be falsely claimed. Content-specific geometry, prose, rewards, and observations stay in reloadable content; compiled Haxe remains generic.

title: Make the Evergrove stream fully traversable and mineable
description: The first real village playtest exposed three connected product gaps: the authored stream is only one voxel deep so the player can never become submerged; gradual wading ascent plus a full-height bank makes leaving the water feel blocked; and Adventure mining rejects Sand because the bounded inventory has no sand item contract. design: First preserve the report as red product evidence. Author a genuinely deep stream using canonical CAXEMAP water and terrain records. Add SandBlock as a real typed inventory item/drop/placeable block with an honest hotbar presentation; use a reviewed atlas cell or add a purpose-built asset rather than displaying another material. Keep underwater-mining capability separate: ordinary sand at the bank is mineable while fully submerged mining still follows the active aquatic profile.
acceptance_criteria: A real entry-to-stream path can reach the Submerged state and shows the underwater camera/breath behavior; holding rise plus movement exits an ordinary one-block water bank without coordinate-specific logic or clipping; Adventure mining removes sand only after inventory capacity succeeds, adds exactly one SandBlock, schedules neighboring water, and can place/consume that sand again; full sand inventory rejects mining without changing terrain or water; ordinary players still cannot mine while fully submerged unless their aquatic profile grants it; focused Eval/generated-C regressions demonstrate the original shallow/exit/sand failures and the corrected behavior; canonical map/editor/package receipts and a real native water-facing pilot pass.

Red evidence:
- npm run test:caxecraft-inventory failed before implementation because ItemKind.SandBlock and InventoryState.sand did not exist.
- npm run test:caxecraft-pilot failed before input repair because GameInputFrames.make had no riseHeld carrier.
- The first real deep-stream native pilot reached Submerged but could not clear the one-block bank. A later pilot could exit but initially looked downstream, so the real mining action missed. These high-level discoveries were reduced into AquaticsProbe and GameSessionProbe focused regressions.

Independent oracles and provenance:
- Hand-authored CAXEMAP coordinates define a two-cell-deep stream, sand bed, bridge clearance, bank, and persistent source; RuntimeLevelLoaderProbe checks representative cells directly.
- AquaticsProbe uses a manually authored minimal shore fixture and requires collision-checked one-block exit only after held rise and horizontal obstruction.
- GameSessionProbe and InventoryProbe require exact lossless transitions: full sand stack leaves terrain and water untouched; capacity removes exactly one block, adds one SandBlock, schedules neighboring water, and placement consumes it.
- The native pilot reports simulation observations rather than deriving expected state from generated C: gear=true, submerged=true, sandMined=true, exited=true, removed=1, rejected=0, 150/150 frames, and a grounded dry final body across two identical semantic runs.
- The SandBlock atlas image is an ImageGen-assisted one-cell edit. Only row 4 column 3 was accepted; 35,427 pixels changed inside that cell, zero outside changed, and transparent corners were retained. The reviewed provenance and exact SHA-256 are in assets/manifest.json.

Green evidence:
npm run test:caxecraft-aquatics; test:caxecraft-inventory; test:caxecraft-session; test:caxecraft-gameplay; test:caxecraft-pilot; test:caxecraft-runtime-level-loader; test:caxecraft-assets; and real play.py --pilot aquatic-gear --raylib-configuration memory-software. Full playable snapshots and direct-C invariants passed after reviewed snapshot refresh.

Boundaries retained: underwater mining still requires the aquatic profile capability; dry land has no new automatic stepping; the swim step is one collision-checked block and activates only for wet held-rise movement blocked horizontally.

title: Export a reproducible complete Caxecraft package ZIP
description:
Why

The bounded ZIP reader can verify a hand-authored archive, but creators still cannot produce one complete shareable package from current authoring data. The existing fixture intentionally omits the PNG files named by its asset inventory.

What

Add the smallest Haxe-authored canonical stored-ZIP export path for one validated package closure. Include every direct package entry and every runtime asset selected by package data, then prove the exported bytes reopen as the same logical package on a clean handoff fixture.

How

Derive the export plan from validated manifests rather than source-tree enumeration, timestamps, compiled constants, or a Python generator. Sort portable logical paths, reject missing/unlisted/colliding/stale inputs before output escapes, normalize ZIP metadata, write the same bounded stored profile admitted by ContentPackageZipSource, and use independent ZIP tooling plus the existing reader as separate structural and semantic observers. Keep authoring directories runtime-loadable without recompilation. Do not add Deflate, discovery, dependency activation, editor UI, signing, marketplace, or platform/release claims.
design: The canonical writer is a transport adapter over a validated package closure, not a semantic package owner. Expected ZIP bytes must not be generated by the reader under test. Determinism requires byte-identical output across repeated exports and input enumeration order. The fixture must include the runtime-selected PNG assets named by validated package data; manually compiled asset lists are not an acceptable authoring authority.
acceptance_criteria: The intended red is recorded before the exporter exists; one Haxe API builds a complete stored ZIP from a validated first-adventure package closure without using Python as product logic; direct semantic entries and runtime-selected asset bytes are all present with independently checked names, lengths, CRC-32, and SHA-256 provenance; two exports from deliberately different input enumeration order and metadata time produce identical bytes; missing, stale, extra, duplicate/case-colliding, oversized, and invalid-path inputs fail before bytes escape; Info-ZIP or another independent standard tool validates the archive; ContentPackageZipSource reopens it and the shared manifest verifier reports the same package identity and direct receipts; an isolated copy of the already-built proof plus ZIP runs without Haxe, haxe.c, a C compiler, or a linker; focused Eval, strict native C, sanitizers, scorecards, selectors, docs, and backstop evidence pass; Deflate/general haxe.zip, arbitrary discovery, dependencies, activation, editor UI, signing, marketplace, portability, and release claims remain unchanged.
notes:
Independent oracles: PKWARE APPNOTE 6.3.10 for canonical record fields and CRC-32; independently authored expected path/receipt closure from validated package and asset manifests; Info-ZIP unzip/zipinfo for external structure and payload validation. Start with one complete first-adventure tracer before permutations.
Intended red (2026-08-02): cd examples/caxecraft && haxe package-zip-export.hxml exits 1. The first diagnostic is ContentPackageZipExportProbe.hx:3, Type not found: caxecraft.content.ContentPackageZipExport, followed by the expected unknown exportContentPackageZip identifier. The already-green manifest/directory/ZIP-reader baseline proves this is the missing exporter owner, not an archive fixture or compiler regression.

Behavior-first tracer: Given the validated first-adventure package manifest, its exact directory source, and the asset manifest packagedPrimaryAssets selection; when exportContentPackageZip builds the canonical stored transport; then every direct semantic file plus the eight selected PNGs appears exactly once in UTF-8 path order with normalized metadata, the output is byte-identical on repetition, independent unzip validates it, and ContentPackageZipSource plus the shared semantic verifier recover the same package identity and direct receipts. Missing/stale/colliding selected inputs reject before output. The existing executable/data split remains: editing package data does not compile code.
Completion evidence (2026-08-02)

Implemented: `ContentPackageZipExport` derives one canonical stored ZIP from the validated package manifest rather than directory enumeration. `ContentPackageAssetClosure` cross-checks the independent asset inventory selection against package transport receipts. The first-adventure package now declares seven semantic or inventory payloads plus eight selected PNGs. ZIP remains transport only; levels, campaigns, packs, localization, assets, and the `mod` role retain their semantic formats.

Representative red and TDD path: the pre-existing intended-red command `cd examples/caxecraft && haxe package-zip-export.hxml` failed first at `ContentPackageZipExportProbe.hx:3` with missing `ContentPackageZipExport`. The focused owner then went green before package-manifest, reader, native, sanitizer, flagship, and affected backstops were run. No code change was fabricated only to demonstrate TDD.

Canonical result: 16 archive entries, 9,483,471 direct payload bytes, 9,488,899 archive bytes, SHA-256 `e0d29cb2837ee8a3530579ef4dc9f2bfa1990ec70bbddeda9494beaf80378b4a`, and independently calculated ordered-byte fingerprint `393434124`. Names are canonical UTF-8 order; timestamps, Unix regular-file mode, comments, and extras are normalized; files are stored without compression.

Independent oracles and provenance: authored package and asset manifests provide manually reviewed paths, lengths, SHA-256 receipts, selection, and provenance; PKWARE APPNOTE defines ZIP records and CRC-32; Python standard `zipfile` checks exact names, payloads, CRC, metadata, and the reviewed whole-archive golden; Info-ZIP validates when available. The generated native archive must emit the same byte fingerprint as the standard-inspected Eval archive. Expected values are not generated by the exporter or reader under test.

Tracer and negative evidence: one real authoring-directory -> Haxe exporter -> generated strict C -> bounded ZIP reader -> semantic verifier -> isolated native observer path carries campaign, levels, packs, localization, asset inventory, and eight real PNGs. Missing and same-length stale selected assets reject exactly; an unselected package asset rejects the cross-manifest closure; a synthetic 16 MiB declared entry rejects from manifest facts before payload read/allocation/hash. Existing package-manifest negatives retain invalid, duplicate, case-colliding, and total-budget rejection; the frozen independent ZIP-reader fixture retains 36 malformed archive and path cases. Source enumeration is structurally absent from `ContentPackageSource`; changed source-only labels/read-attempt metadata still produces identical bytes.

Review findings and dispositions: (1) asset closure validation moved before large PNG reads; (2) the old small reader fixture was decoupled from the growing live package and remains a frozen independent oracle, while the exporter owns current directory/ZIP parity; (3) package-specific selector rules were added after explain mode initially omitted the C ABI/native surface; (4) native evidence gained an ordered-byte fingerprint after review found that size plus self-read was not sensitive enough; (5) archive-budget planning moved ahead of payload reads and gained an exact negative. No mocked boundary replaces the POSIX read, strict C consumer, standard ZIP reader, or isolated executable handoff.

Focused and backstop evidence: package-manifest Eval/native/sanitizers 38.30s; frozen package-zip-source Eval/native/sanitizers 29.30s; final package-zip-export full owner 172.51s; content-json 49.80s with its widened 24 KiB edge; runtime-schemas 43.53s; caxecraft-domain full split/package/unity O0/O2/ASan/UBSan 186.90s. Governance, typed boundaries, fixture policy, toolchain shards, formatter, all-sources, HxcIR, hello, snapshot catalog, diagnostics, GC runtime, primitive differential, native smoke, and Raylib provisioning pass. R4 full toolchain remains the hosted/main backstop and was not replayed locally.

Timing comparison: before implementation the focused exporter command had no successful timing because it was intentionally red. The early positive-only owner was 113.92s; adding independent standard readers, negative cases, isolated native handoff, and sanitizers produced 184.84s; the final reviewed owner is 172.51s. Two exports run in one process and match byte-for-byte. No compiler-server warm path or runtime content-edit topology changed; staged data still reuses the existing executable. The prior 684.4ms warm content staging observation therefore remains unchanged rather than being remeasured as an exporter claim.

Observed timing noise: `test:caxecraft-content-json` twice reached its former 20s native cap after the admitted JSON ceiling grew from 16 to 24 KiB; the explicit bound is now 40s and the full owner passes. `test:native` once reached its 30s cold GC wrapper cap after adjacent work; the standalone GC owner passed and an isolated native-smoke rerun passed in 54.36s. No automatic semantic retry or quarantine was added.

Claims: justified only for reproducible complete stored-ZIP export and isolated handoff of the admitted first-adventure package on the local primary Clang/POSIX profile. Semantic conformance, native ABI, memory, and downstream scorecards remain independent. Unchanged or deferred: Deflate, ZIP64, encryption, general `haxe.zip`, arbitrary package discovery, dependency resolution/activation, creator-facing export/install UI or CLI, signing, marketplace, Windows/WebAssembly adapters, platform qualification, full campaign playability, and release readiness.
close_reason: Complete canonical stored-ZIP export, independent oracles, isolated native handoff, selectors, scorecards, docs, and affected backstops all verified; deferred scope remains explicit.

title: Bound large snapshot diffs without losing review evidence
description:
Why

The owned Caxecraft snapshot updater compares an 8.5 MB, 279,028-line runtime-plan JSON with Python difflib. Its repeated structure drives SequenceMatcher into quadratic CPU behavior; the update spent roughly twenty minutes in find_longest_match until interrupted. This blocks semantic review and the full backstop.

What

Keep small human-readable unified diffs unchanged, but route large canonical snapshots through a bounded deterministic diff implementation that preserves expected/actual context and fails closed. Do not skip review or silently refresh artifacts.

How

Use Git's no-index histogram diff for payloads above a documented size threshold, normalize its labels, test exact small/large behavior and errors, then rerun the Caxecraft owned updater.
acceptance_criteria: A focused test reproduces a large repeated JSON change without quadratic Python SequenceMatcher work; small snapshots retain current unified output; large snapshots produce deterministic expected/actual semantic diff output through a bounded implementation; updater writes only after showing the diff; malformed/tool failure remains fail closed; Caxecraft snapshot update and validation complete; timing evidence is recorded.
notes: Red/performance evidence (2026-08-02): caxecraft-domain owns an 8,480,679-byte, 279,028-line runtime-plan JSON. The stock updater spent roughly 20 minutes at 100% CPU in difflib.SequenceMatcher.find_longest_match before manual interruption; no snapshot had been written. Green: snapshots above 1,000,000 combined canonical characters now use git diff --no-index --diff-algorithm=histogram with external diff/text conversion/config/pager disabled, a 30-second timeout, and fail-closed exit/stderr handling. Small diffs retain Python unified-diff output. The focused 30,000-entry repeated-JSON regression plus failure injection and existing policy tests pass in about 2.5 seconds. test:fixture-policy and snapshots:catalog pass. The owned Caxecraft updater rendered its large diff promptly, updated two reviewed artifacts, and its validation passed Eval, split/package/unity, O2 native, 32 seeded properties, zero hxrt/allocation symbols, and semantic parity.
close_reason: Large snapshot changes now produce bounded reviewable diffs and fail closed; focused policy and real Caxecraft update/validation evidence pass.

title: Read Caxecraft packages from a bounded stored ZIP
description:
Why

The logical package manifest now loads through a transport-neutral source, but only the unpacked directory implements that source. A copied ZIP still cannot reach the same verifier.

What

Add one read-only Haxe ZIP source for a deliberately bounded, standards-conforming stored-entry profile. Prove a manually authored archive exposes exactly the same package manifest and payload bytes as its directory fixture.

How

Parse the end-of-central-directory and central directory from owned Bytes, validate every matching local header, then build an immutable-by-API logical-path index. Accept only one non-spanned, non-ZIP64 archive using stored entries and UTF-8 names. Reject encryption, data descriptors, extras, comments, directories, links or special entries, unsupported flags or methods, malformed/truncated/overlapping regions, duplicate or ASCII-case-colliding paths, CRC or size mismatch, excessive counts or byte budgets, and trailing/prefixed records. Reuse ContentPackagePath and ContentPackageSource; do not branch semantic loading on transport.
acceptance_criteria: A checked-in ZIP produced independently of the reader contains a small package manifest and real payloads with reviewed byte lengths and CRC-32 values; the intended pre-implementation focused command is recorded red because the ZIP source is absent; Eval and generated strict native C open the ZIP, load and verify its semantic package through ContentPackageSource, and produce the same identity, roles, entry receipts, and bytes as the directory source; every admitted central record matches one local header and all archive regions are exact and non-overlapping; malformed signature, truncation, prefixed/trailing bytes, span/ZIP64 markers, unsupported version/flags/method, encryption, descriptor, extras/comments, directory or special entry, invalid/duplicate/case-colliding name, mismatched local metadata, CRC mismatch, size mismatch, count/budget overflow, and missing logical path fail before a usable ZIP source or partial read escapes; no general haxe.zip, Deflate, arbitrary archive, extraction, editor export, package discovery, dependency activation, signing, marketplace, portability, or release claim advances; focused ownership, affected selectors, scorecards, docs, and full backstop mapping remain exact.
notes:
Behavior oracle: PKWARE APPNOTE 6.3.10 sections 4.1 and 4.3-4.4 define stored entries, little-endian records, matching local/central headers, CRC-32 conditioning, flags, and end-of-central-directory structure. The fixture bytes and expected CRC/length values must be produced and inspected with an independent standard ZIP tool, not by the reader under test. Security posture: this is a canonical import profile, not broad ZIP compatibility; unsupported format features are explicit negative cases.
Intended red (2026-08-02): `cd examples/caxecraft && haxe package-zip-source.hxml` exited 1. The first diagnostic is ContentPackageZipSourceProbe.hx:3, Type not found: caxecraft.content.ContentPackageZipSource. This is the intended owner absence; the just-committed directory/package baseline remains green.

Independent fixture provenance: Info-ZIP 3.0 created `test/fixtures/package-zip/first-adventure-store.zip` with `zip -0 -X` from the checked-in package manifest and its seven direct entries. `unzip -t` independently reports all eight entries OK. `zipinfo -v` reports one disk, 8 entries, 621 central-directory bytes at offset 45,072, no archive/entry comments or extras, stored method, no encryption or descriptors, regular Unix files, and independently computed per-entry CRC-32 values. The exact archive is 45,715 bytes with SHA-256 e7386e6da3ad37b1ce2b31fb7697a699582393f2f89ceaff2866da09c8ee3946. Timestamps are fixture provenance only; deterministic editor export remains deferred.
Implementation and distinct security review (2026-08-02): ContentPackageZipSource now owns/copies one <=16 MiB archive and admits only the documented single-disk, non-ZIP64, stored regular-file profile. It validates the EOCD, exact central/local layout and agreement, signed ZIP64 sentinels, flags/method/version, UTF-8/EFS, portable paths and ASCII-case collisions, regular-file attributes, count/entry/payload budgets, and every CRC before a source escapes. Reads return independent Bytes through ContentPackageSource; ContentPackageManifest has no transport branch.

Review findings and dispositions: (1) trailing-slash names were initially parsed as a generic empty path component before the directory policy could own the rejection; the check now runs first and has a dedicated mutation. (2) truncation, central stored-size disagreement, zero entries, and the per-entry ceiling were promised but only indirectly covered; four direct cases were added. (3) offset arithmetic is safe within the copied 16 MiB ceiling and fits() subtracts only after proving offset <= limit. (4) CRC-32 intentionally uses signed Int bit patterns on both record and computed sides. (5) exact sequential local layout rejects preambles, gaps, overlaps, descriptors, and trailing records. (6) archive ownership and returned read ownership are independently challenged. No mocked semantic boundary, scorecard laundering, extraction, or generated expected values remain.

Oracle/provenance: PKWARE APPNOTE 6.3.10 remains the format oracle; Info-ZIP 3.0 independently produced the 45,715-byte fixture (SHA-256 e7386e6da3ad37b1ce2b31fb7697a699582393f2f89ceaff2866da09c8ee3946), and unzip -t independently verifies all 8 stored entries. The tracer compares the package manifest plus seven direct semantic payloads byte-for-byte and receipt-for-receipt with the directory source. The nested PNG assets are intentionally not in this fixture, so deterministic export and complete clean-machine handoff remain deferred.

Evidence: test:caxecraft-package-zip-source passes Eval, strict split C, native execution, ASan/UBSan, and an independent C observer with outputs 0 / 105070 / 42943 / 36. Neighboring package-store, package-manifest, campaign-runtime, all-sources, playable snapshots, snapshot catalog, typed-boundaries, fixture-policy, exact 73-command toolchain shards, and full governance (228 unit tests) pass. The focused command is about 24 seconds on this host; no feedback-ring topology changed. The existing R4 backstop remains npm run test:toolchain:parallel -- --with-native; the ZIP owner is now mapped into the exact aggregate and Caxecraft shard. The prior aggregate had already passed all owners except reconciled stale snapshot/constructor expectations; rerunning the failed owners plus playable/catalog/governance provides the scoped backstop without repeating the entire expensive aggregate.

Claim disposition: justified only for reading one bounded stored ZIP as the same direct semantic Caxecraft package through admitted haxe.c/runtime slices. ABI, compiler conformance, platform portability, Deflate/general haxe.zip, archive export, discovery, dependency activation, marketplace/signing, transitive asset handoff, and release claims are unchanged and deferred to the parent/future children.
close_reason: Implemented and independently reviewed the bounded stored-ZIP reader, transport-neutral semantic parity tracer, 36 malformed archive cases, exact selector ownership, scorecards, and durable claim limits.

title: Define the logical Caxecraft package manifest and directory tracer
description:
## Why

ZIP must remain a sharing transport, so Caxecraft first needs one transport-independent semantic manifest. Today the confined directory store can read known files, but no typed package identity, role graph, owned-entry inventory, or dependency contract connects levels, campaigns, content, localization, assets, and mods.

## What

Define the smallest versioned typed manifest that can express those composable roles without duplicating CaxeMap, campaign, content-pack, localization, or asset schemas. Load one manually authored first-adventure package manifest through ContentPackageStore and resolve its existing files as a real directory tracer bullet.

## How

Capture scenarios and independent expectations first. Parse untrusted JSON only through the existing validated JSON boundary, convert immediately to closed target-owned types, validate package ID/version, role-specific entry paths, exact owned paths, dependency bounds, duplicate/conflicting roles and paths, and stable ordering. Keep transport facts out of the semantic model. Do not implement ZIP parsing, extraction, dependency installation, editor export, scripting, signing, or marketplace behavior in this child.
acceptance_criteria: A checked-in manually authored manifest describes a compatible composed first-adventure package using closed roles for its existing campaign, levels, base content, UI localization, and assets; focused tests record the intended pre-implementation red and independently authored expectations; Eval and generated native C load the manifest and every declared entry through the confined directory source and produce the same package identity, role graph, owned-path receipts, dependency facts, and diagnostics; malformed JSON, unknown version/role, invalid IDs or paths, duplicate/case-colliding owned paths, role/entry mismatch, missing owned entries, duplicate dependencies, self-dependency, and incompatible bounds fail before a package candidate exists; no product behavior branches on directory versus future ZIP transport; docs state that ZIP and arbitrary dependency resolution remain on the parent; selector and product-surface scorecards map this focused owner without broadening mod, portability, security, or release claims.
notes:
Behavior-first record (2026-08-02)

Positive tracer: Given the manually authored first-adventure package manifest at packages/first-adventure/package.json and ContentPackageStore rooted at examples/caxecraft, load the manifest, then every declared campaign, level, content, localization, asset-manifest, and runtime asset path. The observable result is package ID caxecraft:first-adventure, version 1, the exact closed role set, zero dependencies, 15 verified entries, and byte-length/SHA-256 receipts matching independently reviewed repository bytes. Owning surface: Caxecraft package/content behavior. Protected claim: one directory-backed package can compose existing schemas without transport-specific branching.

Negative scenarios: malformed JSON; unsupported schema version; invalid package ID; unknown/duplicate/non-canonical roles; invalid, duplicate, ASCII-case-colliding, or non-canonical entry paths; unknown entry kind; entry kind whose required package role is absent; declared non-mod role with no matching entry; missing entry; stale byte length or SHA-256; duplicate/self/unsorted dependency; and minimum version greater than maximum. Each must return the first located closed diagnostic or exact package-store/receipt error, with no partial package escaping.

Independent oracle: expected IDs, roles, paths, byte lengths, and SHA-256 values are manually authored from reviewed checked-in files using wc -c and shasum -a 256, not generated by the decoder or loader under test. Existing schema files remain authoritative for their own contents. ZIP is intentionally deferred: a later adapter must expose these identical logical paths and bytes through the same store-facing semantic model.
Red evidence (2026-08-02): `cd examples/caxecraft && haxe package-manifest.hxml` exited non-zero. The first diagnostic is ContentPackageManifestProbe.hx:3, Type not found: caxecraft.content.ContentPackageManifest. This is the intended failure because the focused behavior owner does not exist yet; the pre-change package-store baseline remained green via `npm run test:caxecraft-package-store`.
Tracer refinement: the conventional semantic manifest is `examples/caxecraft/caxecraft.package.json`. Its seven directly declared entries are the campaign, two levels, base content, runtime-content index, UI catalog, and asset manifest. The asset manifest remains the independent inventory/receipt owner for selected PNG bytes, avoiding a duplicated list and duplicate multi-megabyte hashing in the package layer. The verified direct-entry total is 42,943 bytes; the package roles remain assets, campaign, content, levels, and localization.
Distinct review findings and dispositions: (1) The first verifier signature accepted the concrete directory store, which would have forced ZIP to duplicate semantics. Fixed by introducing the read-only ContentPackageSource interface; ContentPackageStore is the first implementation. (2) Re-listing selected PNGs duplicated assets/manifest.json and made the package layer own another inventory. Removed those duplicate entries; the existing asset schema remains authoritative. (3) Per-file limits alone allowed a manifest to demand up to 8 GiB of sequential verification. Added a 256 MiB aggregate declared-byte budget and a generated-C negative. (4) The case-collision check initially allocated folded strings and produced divergent generated-C behavior. Replaced it with allocation-free ASCII code-point comparison; Eval/native now agree. (5) Scorecards explicitly deny ZIP, mod activation, dependency resolution, portability, public ABI, and release claims; the portability scorecard was not advanced.

title: Transition the running Caxecraft app between campaign levels
description:
## Why

The first campaign manifest and headless native tracer can load Western Falls and publish it as generation 2, but the graphical application still borrows its startup GameSession and level-local presentation data for the entire process. Players therefore cannot yet see a campaign transition, and simply publishing a new generation would leave the frame loop reading stale actors, items, spawn data, water presentation, and terrain state.

## What

Add the smallest live application owner that prepares all level-local bindings from one validated runtime candidate, publishes the candidate through ActiveContent at a frame boundary, and then makes the matching bindings visible to subsequent simulation and rendering. Add one deterministic Raylib pilot that triggers the typed first-adventure exit and visibly proves Western Falls is active.

## How

Load campaign data from the staged content directory at runtime. Keep the base pack and UI catalog stable, prepare the destination privately through CampaignRuntime, and mutate no active level on a rejected source, receipt, or runtime candidate. On success reset discontinuous presentation state and reacquire the new session on later operations. Keep one-level play independent of a campaign wrapper, add no content-specific Haxe or Python-generated campaign semantics, and retain the headless campaign tracer as the lower contract.
acceptance_criteria: A focused application-state test records the pre-fix failure and proves rejected transition candidates leave the original generation and bindings active. The app optionally loads the staged campaign at runtime without making campaign data mandatory for a one-level map. One real typed transition selects Western Falls, loads it through CampaignRuntime, publishes generation 2 through ActiveContent, and atomically exposes matching session, actor, item, spawn, fluid, terrain, and level-identity views at a frame boundary. The transition requires no recompilation after map or campaign file edits. A deterministic native Raylib pilot visibly and through telemetry proves the Western Falls generation; existing focused, headless campaign, playable snapshot, selector/backstop, typed-boundary, and agent-instruction checks remain green. Failure diagnostics are actionable and no public claim extends beyond this admitted two-level slice.
notes:
Behavior scenario: Given generation 1 is active, prepare generation 2 from the independently reviewed Western Falls receipt; when the app publishes it, subsequent session, actor, item, spawn, fluid, path, and generation reads must all describe generation 2. Given an older or rejected candidate, the current view and publication count remain unchanged. Oracle: manually authored map paths and placements (Evergrove player/item x=16500/4500; Western Falls x=12500/6500), manifest SHA/length receipts, nominal actor roles, and ActiveContent ordering—not values generated by haxe.c. Red command: npm run test:caxecraft-campaign-runtime. Expected failure observed 2026-08-02: Haxe reports Type not found caxecraft.app.ActivePlayableLevel at CampaignRuntimeProbe.hx:3 and at the create call; this is the intended missing ownership boundary, before implementation.
Implemented 2026-08-02. ActivePlayableLevel now prepares one immutable app view from each RuntimeLevelCandidate and delegates generation ordering to ActiveContent; rejected app preflight or stale candidates retain the prior session, actor IDs, items, spawn, fluid cell, path, generation, and publication count. CaxecraftApp optionally reads the staged first-adventure manifest, keeps standalone maps valid when it is absent, and maps N plus the target-neutral CampaignTravel pilot action to the sole outgoing typed edge. A successful Evergrove to Western Falls transition reacquires all level-local state, resets discontinuous presentation state, invalidates terrain chunks, exposes western-falls in the HUD, and reports generation 2/publication 1. Oracle provenance remains the manually authored manifest receipts, actor roles, and reviewed map placements: Evergrove player/item x=16500/4500; Western Falls x=12500/6500. Pre-fix red was npm run test:caxecraft-campaign-runtime, failing only because caxecraft.app.ActivePlayableLevel did not exist. Final focused evidence: campaign-runtime Eval/native/sanitizers green; runtime-content-generation Eval/native/sanitizers green. Vertical/system evidence: caxecraft-domain snapshot refresh native differential green; test:caxecraft-playable green; real Raylib campaign pilot passed twice byte-identically at 1280x720 with player x=12500, world hash 782472fe, generation 2, one publication, and a reviewed western-falls frame. Cold graphical sample: 79.44 s with 116 object misses and link miss. Warm sample: 18.53 s overall after 684.4 ms validation, 116 object hits, link hit; final rerun validation was 889.0 ms with the same cache result. No retries or quarantine were used and no flakes were observed. Selector explain mode maps this change to campaign-runtime plus the flagship owner and keeps the R4 full/native backstop available without laundering claims across scorecards. Formatting, Python syntax, snapshot catalog, scorecard policy, typed boundaries, all-sources, pilot scripts, governance, and git diff checks are green. Claims are limited to the closed two-level forward transition and staged runtime files; branching, return travel, save persistence, campaign editor UI, ZIP/mod discovery, portability, release readiness, and hot reload remain deferred.
close_reason: The live app now performs and visibly proves the admitted Evergrove-to-Western-Falls runtime transition while preserving the old level on rejected candidates.

title: Lower prefix and postfix updates on ordinary Haxe Array elements
description: Caxecraft campaign required-cycle validation uses the natural Haxe expression incoming[index]++. Eval succeeds, but generated C fails HXC1001 because update lowering routes indexed Array elements through the fixed-array place path even though indexed compound assignment already has a managed Array owner. Add a focused Array<Int> regression for postfix and prefix update result semantics, lower each as one checked read, wrapping typed arithmetic, and one checked write without reevaluating receiver/index, then retain the campaign tracer as the real product-boundary proof.
acceptance_criteria: The focused array-runtime owner is red for the exact collection-local-outside-admitted-slice reason before the change; prefix and postfix Array<Int> element updates agree with Eval including returned old/new values and mutations; HxcIR records checked get, typed arithmetic, checked set, and required runtime features; strict C, optimizations, sanitizers, and existing array ownership evidence pass; the unchanged Caxecraft campaign expression compiles and runs through its native vertical tracer.
notes:
Red evidence (2026-08-02): python3 test/differential/array-runtime/run.py exited 1 at generated/Main.hx postfix values[0]++ with HXC1001 TArray(collection-local-outside-admitted-slice:values). Eval semantics require postfix to return 41 while storing 42; the neighboring prefix ++values[1] must return and store 2. The manually authored combined oracle is 87.
Green evidence (2026-08-02): array-runtime passed the pinned Eval oracle, HxcIR sensitivity checks, strict Clang C, O0/O2, sanitizers, ownership/rollback, and selective-symbol evidence. body-lowering passed exact diagnostics, source mapping, runtime-none, and strict Clang behavior. The unchanged campaign-runtime vertical tracer also passed Eval/native C and sanitizers with the natural incoming[index]++ expression. Review disposition: added prefix/postfix increment and decrement plus side-effecting index sensitivity; bounded the new capability to Array<Int>; no Float or managed-element claim. Optional GCC was unavailable because the gcc command identifies as Clang.
close_reason: Array<Int> indexed prefix/postfix updates now preserve Eval result, mutation, ordering, checked access, and runtime failure semantics; focused and campaign double-lock evidence is green.

title: Load the first campaign manifest and second level headlessly
description: Establish the first real campaign path before modifying the Raylib application shell. Add one manually authored closed JSON manifest and one second independently valid CAXEMAP. Parse and validate campaign identity/version, entry-level selection, level paths, and typed exit-to-default-entrance edges in ordinary Haxe; load both levels through ContentPackageStore and RuntimeLevelLoader; publish the second level through ActiveContent; and prove a malformed/missing/cyclic-required manifest or failed destination load leaves the current generation active. This is the tracer bullet for haxe_c-xge.39, not ZIP transport, save persistence, editor UI, or the final graphical transition.

notes:

This is the intended lowest-faithful owner: the focused Haxe probe names the campaign schema boundary before implementation. Completion evidence (2026-08-02): manually authored campaigns/first-adventure/campaign.json names Evergrove and Western Falls with independent wc/shasum-derived byteLength/SHA-256 receipts. Western Falls is a separate 32x16x32 CAXEMAP and both entry/destination traverse ContentPackageStore plus RuntimeLevelLoader. CampaignRuntimeProbe is the durable scenario table and reviewed golden: campaign envelope 251221, generation 2, world -1715484850, scenario -1399453551, authored -1139403351. It rejects unknown fields, duplicate IDs/paths, missing entry/source/destination, unsafe paths, required cycles, stale length, stale hash, and missing destination with located closed errors; ActiveContent remains generation 1 until the valid generation-2 candidate publishes. test:caxecraft-campaign-runtime passed Eval, strict split C, the independent C harness, and ASan/UBSan in about 59-63 seconds on a loaded host; focused Eval was about 0.27 seconds. test:caxecraft-runtime-content-generation remained green, proving its three-file startup receipt was unchanged. Governance, all-sources, typed boundaries, semantic selector/backstop policy, and alternate runtime staging passed. Review found and closed compiler child haxe_c-xge.39.1.1 for natural Array<Int> indexed updates. No graphical transition, saves, editor campaign UI, ZIP transport, arbitrary campaign compatibility, or latency improvement is claimed.
close_reason: The first manually authored two-level campaign now has a closed typed manifest, independent receipts, focused negative schema/receipt coverage, real package-to-RuntimeLevelLoader execution, and atomic ActiveContent publication on Eval/native C. Broader graphical and transport claims remain on parent/follow-up work.

description:

title: Define container-neutral Caxecraft packages with ZIP transport
description:
Why

Players and creators need one logical package contract that can represent and combine mods, standalone levels, campaigns, content packs, localization, and the assets they reference. The on-disk container must not define those semantics. People also need a single ordinary file they can hand off and share easily.

What

Define a versioned container-neutral package manifest and typed entry graph. Keep an unpacked directory as the fast authoring transport and add actual ZIP bytes as the portable sharing transport. Both forms must feed the same parser, validator, dependency resolver, receipt builder, and atomic publication boundary.

How

Start from the existing confined package-store and runtime-generation contracts. The manifest declares stable package identity, version, package roles, owned logical paths, dependencies and compatibility bounds, entry levels or campaign graphs where applicable, and content/localization/asset references. Package roles are typed capabilities, not mutually exclusive filename conventions. ZIP handling is a bounded transport adapter and must not become a second semantic loader or imply broad Haxe ZIP support.
design: Use one logical PackageSource interface over validated logical paths. DirectorySource keeps edit/reload latency low; ZipSource reads standard ZIP archives without relying on extraction as authority. Normalize and validate entry names before lookup; reject absolute or parent paths, backslashes where ambiguous, duplicate normalized names, case-colliding names, symlinks/devices, unsupported compression, encrypted entries, unsafe ratios, oversized tables or files, and changed/corrupt bytes. Canonical export sorts paths, normalizes metadata, and produces reproducible bytes. A package manifest may declare level, campaign, mod, content, localization, or asset roles in a closed schema and may compose compatible roles. ZIP remains replaceable transport; no product rule may branch on ZIP versus directory.
acceptance_criteria: One versioned logical manifest can describe a standalone level, a multi-level campaign, a content pack, a mod that depends on another package, and one compatible composed package without duplicating semantic schemas; directory and ZIP transports produce identical validated package identity, receipts, dependency graph, runtime generation, and diagnostics from the same bytes; the editor can export one reproducible ZIP and import or open it without changing its logical meaning; a shared ZIP can be copied to a clean installation and loaded without Haxe, haxe.c, a C compiler, or a linker; path traversal, absolute paths, normalized duplicates, case collisions, links/devices, encryption, unsupported methods, corrupt headers/data, CRC/hash mismatch, archive bombs, excessive entry counts/sizes, missing dependencies, dependency cycles, incompatible versions, conflicting stable IDs, and partial publication all fail before replacing active content; an unpacked directory remains the fast authoring form and one content edit can validate/reload without rebuilding code; Eval and generated native C compare directory/ZIP parity and rejection traces, with strict compiler, sanitizer, fault-injection, and real handoff evidence; ZIP transport does not broaden general standard-library, platform, mod-scripting, marketplace, signing, or untrusted-code claims.
notes: Work confirmation after ca9984b (2026-08-02): classification is partially resolved. Children .1 and .2 now prove one transport-neutral logical manifest plus directory/stored-ZIP read parity. Current source has no canonical ZIP exporter, no data-derived transitive asset closure, and no clean-install handoff path; the authoritative docs explicitly keep those claims deferred. The next scoped child is .3. Dependency resolution, discovery/activation, and editor/application selection remain separate later children rather than being silently folded into export.

title: Admit definitely assigned primitive locals
description:
## Why
The pinned haxe.crypto.Sha256 implementation declares primitive work variables without initial values, assigns every one from the current hash state before entering the compression rounds, and reads them only afterward. Haxe Eval executes this code, but haxe.c currently rejects the declaration itself as TVar(a:uninitialized). The existing compiler-generated flow-carrier exception does not cover authored locals and must not be stretched without proof.

## What
Add bounded definite-assignment analysis for authored primitive locals. A definitely assigned local means every path that reaches a read has first written the same typed storage. Emit uninitialized HxcIR storage only after that proof, preserve Haxe evaluation/control-flow order, and reject any possibly uninitialized read before C emission.
design: Build this as a typed control-flow/dataflow capability, not a Sha256 source-position exception and not a blanket zero initialization. Start with one straight-line declaration followed by unconditional assignments before a bounded loop; then add branch/loop negatives that prove reads cannot precede writes. Reuse HxcIR declare-uninitialized only when analysis proves all reads dominated by assignment.
acceptance_criteria: A minimal target-neutral fixture is red at TVar(a:uninitialized) for the intended reason; the compiler admits only primitive locals whose every reachable read is dominated by an assignment; Eval/HxcIR/strict C/native/sanitizer behavior agree; branch, loop, early-return, and partial-assignment neighbors fail closed; pinned haxe.crypto.Sha256.make passes known vectors and independent hashlib differential expectations; no source-position or stdlib-name special case is introduced.

title: Separate test claims by product surface and evidence provenance
description:
## Why

The July 31 consolidated-testing delta adds behavior scenarios, independent oracle provenance, six feedback rings, and product-surface scorecards. haxe.c already separates many evidence lanes, but those conclusions are not yet one explicit, independently checkable contract. Without that contract, a green native or semantic lane could be read too broadly.

## What

Audit the post-July-30 test strategy and add only missing governance: scorecards for five claim-bearing surfaces, behavior/red/oracle/tracer guidance, executable example tiers, six named feedback rings, semantic-owner/product-surface selector output, and a separate high-risk review record. Preserve the capability manifest as authority and do not alter active compiler/runtime behavior.

## How

Use the existing String ownership regression as a documented representative workflow, extend the fixture/example policy and planner with fail-closed validation, classify current examples, record before/after timing and selection evidence, and retain unsupported public ABI/platform/release boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: Five independently validated surface scorecards exist and reference—not replace—the capability manifest. Current examples declare an honest tier, execution assumptions, claim surfaces, and independent oracle provenance. The planner explains R0 through R5 and reports semantic/product-surface ownership with conservative backstops. A real red-state workflow records its expected failure, oracle, tracer path, and unaffected claims without changing the active P0 fix. Focused governance and example/vertical checks pass, with full or deferred evidence reported honestly.
notes:
Implemented the incremental July 31 v3 delta without changing compiler/runtime behavior: exact five-surface scorecards reference bootstrap capability IDs; examples now declare tier, scenario, execution assumptions, and oracle provenance; test:plan emits R0-R5 with product-surface ownership, R3 observation-only, R4 fallback, and R5 unimplemented; policy docs record TDD red evidence, tracer-first, double lock, portfolio review, and a distinct high-risk review. Caxecraft full ran 200.49s and reached checked-in snapshots after oracle/layout/determinism passed, then failed on playable/hxc.manifest.json drift from active overlapping content work; no snapshot refresh. Independent gpt-5.6-sol xhigh review initially rejected the change: script-name surface inference contradicted scorecards, the manual guard admitted schema-invalid authority/command records, and unknown std/c ownership did not explicitly require R4. All findings accepted and repaired. The planner now loads owner surfaces and concrete R3 package commands directly from scorecards; policy-only owners map to no surface; test:string-runtime maps to compiler+runtime; unknown std/c/NewSurface marks R4 required with a reason. The guard now enforces strict root/nested fields, archetype/status, uniqueness, stable Beads owners from beads-plan, capability IDs, package scripts, evidence/selector/observed shapes, canonical full backstop, and valid release commands. Verification after repair: 7 adversarial scorecard/example tests, 50 selector tests, and fixture-policy pass. Same reviewer re-review pending.
Second gpt-5.6-sol xhigh review accepted R3/R4 repair but rejected remaining case-schema and owner-authority bypasses. Final repairs: complete case runner/expected/stream/artifact/path/type/range validation including bool-vs-integer; explicit policyOnlyOwners in scorecard authority and rejection from product surfaces; example.owner required and productSurfaces must exactly match scorecard ownership; affectedExtendedOwners now map direct changes too. Existing contains stdout and inline zero-runtime-plan assertions were added to the schema so current cases are honestly represented. Verification: 10 scorecard/case adversarial tests, 50 selector tests, fixture-policy, JSON parse, Python compile, plan explanations, and diff check pass. Final independent re-review pending.
Third review found one remaining medium bypass: policy-only scripts could enter systemOwners, which the selector consumes. title: Borrow proven call-bounded interface parameters
description: A direct static function that only reads an interface parameter for the duration of the call should accept a stack-constructed implementing class. haxe.c already performs an escape/use proof for concrete class parameters, but previously applied that result only to class mappings. Keep owning behavior whenever the value is returned, stored, thrown, captured, constructor-passed, or otherwise escapes. Do not weaken interface layout, dispatch, or null checks. Prove the behavior in the canonical interface-dispatch fixture with a separate static reader function receiving an interface and a stack-constructed concrete caller value.

notes: Extended the existing typed escape proof to interface parameters. title: Lower switch-result locals whose abrupt arm continues a loop
description: A natural Haxe switch expression inside a loop may use continue in one arm and return a value from every arm that reaches the following statement. Haxe 5 emits this as TVar(candidate, null), a TSwitch that assigns candidate in the value arms, and TContinue in the skipped arm. haxe.c currently rejects the declaration as an unsupported uninitialized local before its existing flow-carrier validation can prove the abrupt arm does not reach the read.
design: Extend the existing compiler-generated flow-carrier recognition, not general source-level uninitialized locals. Treat a typed break/continue as an abrupt arm only while lowering an active loop. Preserve the IRIODeclareUninitialized plus path-sensitive HxcIR validation boundary; add a focused real TypedExpr fixture with normal switch arms, continue, and a later read. Do not default-initialize the value, rewrite the source, or weaken arbitrary uninitialized-local rejection.
acceptance_criteria: A focused Haxe fixture using final selected = switch (...) { value arms; default: continue; } compiles through haxe.c, preserves source evaluation and loop behavior in strict native C, emits structured loop/switch control flow, and contains no defensive observable default. The HxcIR validator proves that every path reaching the local read assigned it. Break/continue are admitted only in a typed active-loop context. Existing negative uninitialized-carrier diagnostics, evaluation-order snapshots/runtime, body/function lowering, strict GCC/Clang, and Caxecraft actor-composition reproducer pass.
notes:
The focused Caxecraft reproducer refined the gap after active-loop continue recognition was added: its selected value is a managed closed record, not a direct scalar. haxe.c already generates exact record retain/destroy helpers with rollback and abort-on-retain-failure behavior, but the managed join-carrier recognizer and HxcIR lifecycle validator currently admit only String, reference-counted Array, and tagged enum. This issue therefore also owns the smallest general extension that admits a nonrecursive managed closed record through the same one-owner carrier protocol. It must reuse the record lifecycle helper, recognize fresh IRIOConstructAggregate results, register exactly one post-join cleanup owner, and retain existing fail-closed type/lifecycle matching.
Implemented active-loop break/continue flow-carrier admission, managed closed-record carrier lifecycle planning/validation, loop-reentry state reset, materialized-owner field reads, and a next-iteration-only normal-join proof. Focused direct-record and managed-record fixtures now cover the source and IR boundaries. Verified test:hxc-ir, test:body-lowering, test:function-lowering, test:evaluation-order, test:caxecraft-actor-composition, formatter, typed-boundaries, strict native C, sanitizers, and registered hxc-ir snapshots.
