title: Resolve validated actor placements into typed spawn plans
description:
## Why

Caxecraft can now store several characters and derive stable runtime IDs, but validated CaxeMap placements and content-pack actor profiles still stop before runtime construction. Building Nia or Mossling directly in application Haxe would couple reusable engine mechanics to shipped story content and would make later runtime loading/editor test-play use a second path.

## What

Add one target-neutral, all-or-nothing planning boundary that turns already validated character-like ScenarioObject placements plus typed content-pack facts into immutable CharacterSpawnPlan values. The plan names stable identity, transform, reusable mechanics, and a closed controller/profile intent; it does not mutate GameSession, run AI, render an actor, or execute CaxeFlow.

## How

Introduce a small ActorContentResolver contract separate from ScenarioContentRegistry validation. Extend the generated base-pack adapter and schema so every character-like NPC/enemy owns the mechanics facts needed for construction, including explicit health rather than a code default. Resolve Npc and character-like Entity placements without content-name branches in the planner, derive every EntityId through ActorIdentityPlanner in one preflight, preserve authored order, and return either the complete spawn list or one exact rejection. Keep dialogue as an NPC-specific typed payload and controller selection as a closed enum; avoid Dynamic, reflection, nullable field clouds, raw C, runtime string dispatch, publication, or expansion of the temporary FirstPlayableLevel adapter.
design: The scenario model remains authoring truth, ActorContentResolver converts validated ContentId values into closed mechanics profiles, ActorCompositionPlanner joins placement + profile + stable identity, and a later child owns transactional Character construction/publication. Use composition rather than subclasses: role/profile data selects reusable systems and future controllers. Keep world transforms in integer milliblocks until one documented conversion at CharacterBody construction. Do not add Nia/Mossling/Ivvy/Browser branches to the planner; base-pack-specific name matching stays in the generated resolver. A plan is an immutable value and has no live-session authority.
acceptance_criteria: content.json and its validator require every character-like NPC/enemy profile to contain all construction mechanics facts; BaseContentPack.hx is regenerated and its registry implements the new typed resolver without hand edits; ActorCompositionPlanner accepts validated ScenarioObject values, ignores non-character placements, preserves character placement order, produces stable positive IDs independent of reordering/unrelated insertions, carries exact transform/health/aquatic/controller/dialogue facts, and rejects duplicate IDs, storage collisions, wrong-kind or unknown profiles, invalid construction facts, and over-capacity candidates before GameSession mutation; no content-specific ID/name appears in the generic planner; focused Haxe tests cover empty, mixed placements, Npc, Entity/enemy, reorder/insertion stability, every rejection family, and all-or-nothing behavior; Eval and haxe.c-generated strict C agree with sanitizers; generated split C keeps resolver/planner modules recognizable and goto-free; content-pack, scenario, editor, session, typed-boundary, all-source, and registered snapshot owners pass; documentation states this slice plans construction but does not publish actors and names the next transactional publication owner.
notes: Implemented a data-only actor composition boundary. The generic planner filters validated Npc/Entity placements, plans stable IDs for the complete candidate set, resolves typed health/aquatics/controller profiles through the generated content registry, and returns immutable ordered spawn plans without mutating GameSession. Added fail-closed coverage for duplicate IDs, FNV storage collisions, capacity, unknown content, wrong content kinds, invalid mechanics, reorder/insertion stability, and non-character filtering. Added focused Eval/generated-C/native/sanitizer evidence and registered it in the exact toolchain shard. Documentation names haxe_c-xge.20.4.2.4.4 as the transactional publication owner. Verification: content-pack generator check; test:caxecraft-content-pack; test:caxecraft-actor-composition; session/scenario-model/editor/pilot owners; format:haxe:check; test:typed-boundaries; test:governance; test:all-sources; caxecraft-domain registered snapshot update; test:caxecraft-playable; snapshot catalog; git diff --check.
close_reason: Validated placements now resolve to complete, stable, typed spawn plans with fail-closed Eval/native/sanitizer and integrated snapshot evidence; live GameSession publication remains explicitly owned by haxe_c-xge.20.4.2.4.4.

title: Transfer managed Array results through generated flow carriers
description:
## Why

Caxecraft's natural exhaustive match on ActorIdentityPlanResult returns the successful Array<ActorIdentityBinding> payload or returns from the rejecting arm. Haxe types the selected Array through a compiler-generated local carrier. haxe.c recognizes the structural carrier but rejects its managed Array result as result-type-without-direct-default, even though every rejoining path assigns it and the other path terminates.

## What

Extend the existing managed compiler-generated flow-carrier protocol to admitted Array specializations. A selected borrowed Array arm must retain into the carrier; a fresh arm must move its owner; a terminating arm must not fabricate or acquire a value. The later read transfers or borrows according to the surrounding consumer exactly once.

## How

Reuse schema-20 HxcIR managed ownership, Array retain/release callbacks, structural carrier proof, and definite-assignment validation. Do not create an empty default Array, special-case Caxecraft, relax genuine uninitialized locals, or reinterpret Array.copy/payload ownership. Keep recursive/fallible cases fail-closed unless the existing cleanup and failure contracts prove them.
design: Generalize the existing carrier classification by managed value family only after the Array specialization has a complete retain/release plan. Preserve arm evaluation order and terminating returns. Add the smallest ordinary-Haxe fixture around a private enum carrying Array<closed record>; cover borrowed and fresh selected values plus a terminating reject arm. HxcIR remains the semantic owner and CAST only projects validated acquire/move/release instructions.
acceptance_criteria: An ordinary-Haxe fixture assigns Array<closed record> from exhaustive enum/if flow into local, argument, return, and nested consumption positions; borrowed and fresh arms match Eval under strict GCC/Clang C11 O0/O2 and ASan/UBSan with no leak, use-after-free, or double release; terminating arms do not acquire or default the carrier; HxcIR proves exactly one managed owner at each reachable join and rejects malformed read-before-acquire, duplicate-acquire, already-moved, and unsupported fallible deep-retain shapes; generated C contains no fabricated empty Array/default owner and retains readable branch structure; split/package/unity outputs are deterministic; the unmodified Caxecraft session probe advances beyond GameSessionProbe.checkActorIdentityPlanning without an application workaround.
close_reason: E3 managed ownership gap closed: reference-counted Array results now use the existing HxcIR managed-carrier family with exact fresh move, borrowed retain, statement-boundary owner transfer, and cleanup across later early returns; collector-backed Arrays remain fail-closed on precise-root ownership. Evidence: npm run test:array-runtime (Eval plus generated split/package/unity ownership, strict Clang C11 O0/O2, ASan/UBSan), npm run test:hxc-ir and python3 scripts/test/snapshots.py --check --suite hxc-ir (valid Array lifecycle plus wrong-lifecycle and collector-backed diagnostics in test/hxc_ir/expected/diagnostics.json), npm run test:all-sources, npm run test:typed-boundaries, npm run test:fixture-policy, and npm run test:caxecraft-session (GameSessionProbe actor identity planning advances under Eval/generated native C with sanitizers). Documentation updated in docs/hxc-ir.md, docs/architecture.md, docs/array-runtime.md, docs/testing.md, and the fixture taxonomy.

title: Plan stable runtime identities for authored actors
description:
## Why

A validated CaxeMap identifies actors with stable text IDs, while GameSession and EntityStore use compact positive EntityId values. The runtime composition path needs one deterministic, checked conversion before it can construct NPCs or enemies. Using actor array positions would silently rename existing actors when content is reordered or extended.

## What

Add the smallest typed Haxe identity-planning boundary for authored character-like actors. It accepts already validated ScenarioId values, derives stable nonzero storage codes, preserves input order, and returns either a complete immutable binding list or one exact rejection. It does not publish actors, execute CaxeFlow, or choose gameplay behavior.

## How

Use an explicitly documented deterministic hash over the CAXEMAP identifier grammar, then check the bounded candidate set for duplicate authored IDs, storage-code collisions, invalid results, and EntityStore capacity before returning any bindings. Keep the algorithm in ordinary target-neutral Haxe so the future generated adapter and runtime loader can share it. Avoid Dynamic, reflection, raw C, position-based numbering, hidden global registration, or partial GameSession mutation.
design: Place the planner at the content-to-runtime boundary, not inside EntityStore and not in the CaxeFlow registry. EntityStore continues to own live Character values by EntityId; authored identity remains loading metadata until a later actor-composition slice stores the complete runtime actor descriptor. Return a closed result enum and immutable binding records. A quadratic collision check is acceptable and clearer for the fixed 64-character bound; record that bound and revisit only with measured larger populations.
acceptance_criteria: The planner produces the same positive EntityId for the same valid ScenarioId regardless of candidate order or unrelated inserted actors; preserves candidate order in its returned binding list; rejects duplicate authored IDs, two distinct IDs with the same derived storage code, and more than EntityStore.MAX_CHARACTERS before any GameSession mutation; exposes exact closed failure reasons with the relevant authored IDs/code; focused Haxe tests cover determinism, order independence, duplicate, collision, empty, and capacity boundaries; the same probe passes under Eval and haxe.c-generated strict native C with sanitizers; generated split C keeps the planner and binding ownership recognizable and introduces no raw C, Dynamic, reflection, runtime registry, or position-based identity; nearby architecture/domain documentation states that this slice plans identity only and names the later actor-construction owner.
close_reason: Caxecraft actor-identity planning is implemented in ordinary target-neutral Haxe. ActorIdentityPlanner derives positive FNV-1a EntityId values from validated ScenarioId text, preserves authored order, rejects duplicate IDs, a real distinct-ID integer collision, and the 64-character capacity before any GameSession mutation, and returns only a complete plan or closed rejection. title: Lower discarded one-element Array.splice with ownership parity
description: Caxecraft's natural multi-character EntityStore removes a known element with characters.splice(index, 1). haxe.c currently fails closed on Array.splice even though hxrt already owns checked element destruction and suffix shifting. Admit the smallest reusable Haxe semantic slice required by this real application: a discarded-result, one-element splice over ordinary typed Array values. Do not add a Caxecraft-specific helper or claim the returned-Array form is supported.
design: Lower the ordinary Haxe call through a typed HxcIR/runtime operation whose argument evaluation, index normalization, mutation, element destruction, and alias behavior are explicit. Match Haxe's negative and out-of-range position rules even when the removed Array result is unused. Reuse the selected managed Array representation and lifecycle callbacks; do not expose raw hxc_array storage in application Haxe. The compiler must reject an observed splice result until the separate returned-Array ownership contract is implemented. Keep runtime-none/metal programs free of hxrt.
acceptance_criteria: Focused ordinary-Haxe fixtures cover primitive and managed element arrays; first, middle, last, negative, out-of-range, and empty cases; deterministic suffix order; aliases; and exact managed destruction without leaks or double-destruction. Haxe Eval and generated strict C agree under GCC/Clang and ASan/UBSan. Using the returned Array remains an exact fail-closed HXC1001 with no plausible artifact. HxcIR construction, validation, runtime-feature selection, ABI documentation, split/package/unity determinism, and generated-C readability are updated at the owning layers. The Caxecraft aquatics/multi-character test then compiles without changing its natural Array API.
notes:
Closure audit immediately found the newly added Eval-oracle runner launched generated/oracle.hxml from the repository root even though it contains ; Haxe therefore could not resolve Main. Reopened before commit. Fix the runner working directory and rerun the full owner before closure.
The corrected runner launches generated/oracle.hxml from its own generated fixture directory so its relative class path resolves Main. The complete Array owner then passed again with this Eval check included.
close_reason: Implemented the bounded discarded-result Array.splice(pos, 1) semantic slice through typed HxcIR, structural C emission, and hxrt ABI 0.15.0. Negative, clamped, out-of-range, empty, alias, deterministic suffix-order, and managed String cases now agree on Haxe Eval and generated native C. Observing the returned Array remains exact HXC1001 with no output. After correcting and auditing the Eval runner path, the full Clang Array matrix passed again, alongside runtime-feature and stdlib snapshot owners, hosted/freestanding/C++/sanitizer runtime smoke, capabilities, typed boundaries, and all-sources.

title: Keep direct String-literal evidence distinct from runtime dependencies
description: The aggregate managed-optional fixture selects the string-literal runtime feature transitively through haxe.io.Bytes, but its reachable HxcIR contains no source or compiler-created String literal. CCompiler correctly omits the direct-utf8-string-literals decision because no string-literal requirement exists; CProjectEmitter incorrectly rebuilds that decision from the dependency-closed feature list and raises HXC9000. Validate direct literal evidence from root runtime reasons instead, preserving the distinction between a directly used feature and one selected only as another feature's dependency.
acceptance_criteria: The focused managed-optional aggregate fixture passes from both the current worktree and unchanged HEAD semantics; a focused regression proves a dependency-selected string-literal feature does not claim direct UTF-8 literal evidence, while a real direct String literal still does; compiler/runtime reports remain deterministic and existing runtime-feature validation passes.
notes: Confirmed the failure on unchanged HEAD in an isolated disposable worktree. CProjectEmitter was rebuilding direct literal evidence from the dependency-closed feature set, so Bytes' transitive string-literal artifact became a false source-semantics claim. Validation now checks root runtime reasons instead. Verified with the managed-optional aggregate matrix, runtime-feature graph, String-output direct-literal/native matrix, and diff/format guards.

title: Generalize EntityStore for shared non-player characters
description: Replace EntityStore’s temporary one-character carrier with the smallest deterministic multi-character owner. GameSession must keep one authoritative Character per stable EntityId and admit a non-player fixture through the same movement, aquatics, vitals, world-view, and commit rules already used by the local player. This is the reusable ownership foundation for later content-driven NPC/enemy/companion construction; it does not add Nia, Mossling, AI, presentation, or a general ECS.
design: Start with ordinary Haxe Array<Character> behind a final EntityStore class because variable live-entity count and value-snapshot semantics are natural Haxe collection behavior. Bound capacity explicitly, reject invalid/duplicate identities and over-capacity publication, preserve deterministic insertion/iteration/save order, and return copy-owned observations rather than exposing mutable storage. GameSession binds local control by ID and steps a non-player through the same Character.step system using a typed intent supplied by a focused controller/test boundary. Do not add role-name branches, Dynamic bags, reflection, subclasses, raw C, nullable slot clouds, or a parallel simulator. If Array<Character> exposes a haxe.c representation or ownership gap, reduce it to a compiler fixture and lift the general gap before changing the game design.
acceptance_criteria: EntityStore owns several Character values with unique stable IDs, bounded deterministic order, exact read/replace/remove behavior, and no mutable storage escape; local-player binding still names exactly one stored character without copying authority. A target-neutral Haxe fixture constructs a player and one generic non-player, advances both through shared Character movement/aquatics/vitals rules, proves independent state and deterministic iteration, and covers invalid ID, duplicate ID, missing replace/remove, and capacity failure. Eval and generated strict C agree under sanitizers; split/package/unity output remains deterministic and readable; runtime/allocation evidence states the exact Array representation and steady-state behavior. Caxecraft’s existing session, domain, pilot, and playable gates remain green. No character/content name, controller brand, renderer, CaxeFlow-only state, or ECS framework enters the store.
notes:
First generated-C attempt reached test/caxecraft/qa/AquaticsProbe.hx:227 and failed closed with TNew(stack-construction-requires-unconditional-entry-block). The second EntityStore is constructed only after validation/early returns, remains local, and never escapes. Moving it to function entry or a helper would be a compiler-shaped source workaround, so this product slice now depends on the existing exact compiler owner haxe_c-0zm.
Completed evidence: EntityStore now owns up to 64 immutable Character snapshots in one ordinary Haxe Array, rejects invalid/duplicate/missing/capacity cases, preserves insertion order, provides copy-owned observations, and removes through the general discarded Array.splice capability. GameSession binds the local player by ID and advances a generic non-player through the same Character movement, aquatics, vitals, world view, and commit path. Automatic runtime selection is exact: runtime-base, status, alloc, and array. Construction and growth may allocate; explicit snapshots allocate; steady-state read, replace, remove, and step do not. Generated split C is source-shaped and goto-free; optional package and unity runs also passed strict C, Eval/native equality, and Address/Undefined sanitizers. Verified focused aquatics and session in split/package/unity, Haxe formatter, all-sources, typed-boundaries, snapshot catalog, the full Caxecraft domain split/package/unity native differential, pilot protocol, and playable snapshot/direct-C invariants. The snapshot refresh changed only the actor/session generated artifacts plus their manifest/runtime evidence. Content-driven construction, controllers/scheduling, inventory/equipment migration, rendering, and ECS remain outside this slice.

title: Bind Raylib gamepad input and drive editor focus
description:
## Why

Caxecraft promises controller-first usability, but the reviewed RaylibHx selection currently has no IsGamepadAvailable, button, or axis declarations. Keyboard focus work must not fake controller support with numeric raw calls.

## What

Select and generate the smallest Raylib 6.0 gamepad input ABI, add closed Haxe button/axis types and semantic input helpers, then map D-pad/stick navigation, confirm, and cancel into the editor focus model.

## How

Extend the pinned binding selection/lock/generator from the exact Raylib header; add independent C/C++ consumers and Haxe-to-C evidence; normalize dead zones/repeat at the Caxecraft input edge; keep EditorSession device-neutral.
design: RaylibHx owns ABI-faithful device queries; Caxecraft input owns controller policy; the editor focus model consumes only semantic navigation. This preserves reuse for gameplay, menus, and later split-screen controller assignment.
acceptance_criteria: Pinned raw ABI, typed facade, strict C11/C++17 consumers, Eval/native semantic input tests, hot-plug/disconnect handling, dead-zone/repeat behavior, visible editor focus, confirm/cancel parity, and a deterministic real-render pilot pass. No raw numeric gamepad calls in application code and no controller-specific editor commands.
notes:
Implemented the pinned Raylib 6.0 gamepad slice and device-neutral editor navigation. Raw ABI generation now owns GamepadAxis/GamepadButton plus availability, pressed/down, and axis queries; RaylibHx exposes closed typed facades. Caxecraft samples slot zero through a narrow adapter, while NavigationRepeater owns 35% dead-zone, immediate/350 ms/100 ms repeat, disconnect/reset, stalled-frame, and confirm/cancel policy. Keyboard, controller, and PilotScript all enter the same editor NavigationCommand route; the editor contains no device-specific command names or raw numeric Raylib identities.

Evidence: test:caxecraft-editor; real 1280x720 memory-software editor-shell pilot with two identical runs and bounded exit; Caxecraft Eval/split/package/unity/native-O2 snapshot owner; pinned Raylib raw+semantic snapshots; offline-source macOS desktop integration compiling/linking the strict C11 ABI probe and handwritten C++17 consumer; format, typed boundaries, all sources, capabilities, CI policy, fixture policy, and snapshot catalog all passed.
close_reason: Pinned typed gamepad input, shared navigation semantics, editor integration, and native/rendered evidence are complete.

title: Add semantic keyboard focus to the native editor
description:
## Why

The editor controls currently require pointer clicks. Keyboard users cannot see which control owns focus, move between controls, or activate the selected action, and the immediate-mode screen has no reusable semantic focus model.

## What

Add a closed renderer-neutral editor focus order and connect Tab/Shift-Tab plus Enter/Space to the existing native toolbar, tools, toggle, title field, and Back action. Draw one visible Caxecraft focus ring without teaching EditorSession about device input or widget geometry.

## How

Keep semantic focus identity/order in a target-neutral editor module. CaxecraftEditorScreen maps Raylib keys to next/previous/activate, keeps text editing exclusive while active, and reuses each existing typed action method. Presentation draws the ring around the current control. Controller input remains a separate child because the selected RaylibHx surface does not yet bind Gamepad APIs.
design: Editor focus is presentation-navigation state, not authored campaign data. A closed EditorFocusTarget value identifies each actionable control and a pure module function computes cyclic movement. The native screen owns the current target and geometry, maps device keys to semantic navigation, and activates existing methods. The focus ring is drawn by the app renderer so Raygui global state does not become a second focus owner.
acceptance_criteria: Target-neutral tests prove complete stable focus order, wraparound, next/previous symmetry, and activation routing identities. The generated-C native editor accepts Tab/Shift-Tab and Enter/Space without pointer input, preserves text-box editing isolation, shows a visible focus ring, and reuses the same EditorSession/action methods as mouse input. English/es-MX layout, Eval/native app-screen evidence, rendered editor pilot, formatting, typed boundaries, snapshots, and Raygui binding checks pass. No controller-support claim, raw C, hidden widget state, or EditorSession device dependency.
notes: Implemented a closed target-neutral focus order for all nine current controls, Tab/Shift-Tab navigation, Enter/Space activation through one exhaustive native handler, pointer-to-focus convergence, text-box input isolation, wrapped list selection, and a high-contrast focus ring. The deterministic editor pilot moves to Validate and invokes the same activation handler before proving the rendered ring. Caxecraft exposed a general overload-naming omission for non-inline c.CString parameters; fixed it in FunctionPreparer and retained a focused C-import/native regression. Verified editor protocol (19 focus checks), app-screen Eval/native/sanitizers, Raygui binding, localization, full generated-C editor pilot (two identical runs and 1280x720 framebuffer), c-import GCC/Clang/native, Caxecraft split/package/unity snapshot owner and native differentials, playable snapshot invariants, all-sources, typed boundaries, Haxe formatting, snapshot catalog, and diff checks. Gamepad polling remains explicitly owned by haxe_c-xge.19.6.1.6.
close_reason: Keyboard focus and activation are implemented and verified across target-neutral, generated-C, native-rendered, and compiler-regression layers; controller input remains separately tracked.

title: Persist the editor world name through EditorSession
description:
## Why

The native editor already renders a safe Raygui text field, but it is presentation-only: typing does not change the canonical CAXEMAP title, cannot be undone, and disappears when the UI state is rebuilt. That is an honest intermediate proof, not an acceptable authoring path.

## What

Add one typed EditorCommand for changing the scenario title and connect the existing World Name field to it. The edit must use the same revision check, validation, history, changed-ID observation, canonical writer, and undo/redo path as every other editor mutation.

## How

Use ScenarioText as the command payload, add a document-metadata change identity, apply the change in the renderer-independent editor model, and synchronize the Raygui text owner from accepted session state. Commit on an explicit edit completion/confirmation rather than mutating the draft for each presentation frame. Keep native file save/load outside this child.
design: The scenario title is authored document metadata, so the command belongs in the shared EditorCommand family rather than CaxecraftEditorScreen. The immediate-mode text widget owns only temporary editing bytes and focus state. On confirmation, the screen creates validated ScenarioText, submits a revision-tagged mutation, and refreshes from the accepted editor observation. Undo/redo therefore restore both canonical content and the next rendered field value.
acceptance_criteria: Eval and generated-C/native tests prove accepted rename, canonical output, stable changed ID, stale-revision rejection, invalid-title rejection without mutation, undo, redo, and copy-owned observations. The native editor field initializes from the scenario title and one explicit user confirmation commits through EditorSession; UI reconstruction reads the accepted title rather than a hidden second model. English/es-MX layout, Raygui binding evidence, formatting, typed-boundary checks, editor tests, and one rendered pilot pass. No raw C, Dynamic, direct draft mutation, filesystem persistence claim, or game-content special case.
close_reason: The native World Name field now confirms a literal title through revision-checked EditorSession.SetTitle rather than retaining presentation-only state. Accepted titles enter canonical CAXEMAP bytes, stable ChangedTitle observations, history, undo, and redo; empty or stale edits leave draft/history unchanged and resynchronize the field. The memory-software editor pilot exercises the production confirmation path with zero rejected edits. Verified by test:caxecraft-editor (23 command round trips and 50 protocol checks), Eval/native app-screen sanitizers, Raygui binding, localization, full split/package/unity Caxecraft domain regeneration/native differential, playable snapshots, graphical editor-shell pilot, all-sources, typed-boundaries, Haxe formatting, snapshot catalog, and diff checks. Native file persistence and message-backed title editing remain explicitly separate.

title: Reconcile Bytes dependency closure with direct runtime decisions
description: The existing Bytes-payload enum fixture fails before native execution with HXC9000: runtime feature closure selects string-literal as a Bytes dependency, so CProjectEmitter expects direct-utf8-string-literals, while CCompiler.directRuntimePlan correctly sees no source or HxcIR string-literal requirement and omits that decision. This reproduces unchanged with and without the fresh-enum Array-literal fix from haxe_c-7d0.14, so it is an independent pre-existing runtime-plan reconciliation defect.
acceptance_criteria: The Bytes-payload enum fixture compiles in unity/split/package and cold/server modes without inventing source string-literal evidence; compiler-owned direct decisions and dependency-closed selected features use one explicit semantic rule; a focused regression distinguishes direct source/runtime intent from transitive feature dependencies; npm run test:enum-lowering:bytes and the full enum-lowering owner pass with native sanitizer evidence.

title: Transfer fresh managed enum variants into returned Array literals
description: The natural editor helper changesFor(command):Array<EditorChangeId> returns a fresh Array literal from an exhaustive switch. EditorChangeId is a managed payload enum because some variants carry nominal String-backed IDs, even when the selected variant is fieldless. haxe.c admits managed enum arrays and array returns separately, but the combined direct switch-return shape reaches function-exit:unowned-fresh-managed-enum-value: the fresh enum element is not transferred into the Array slot before the containing Array owner returns. This is a general ordinary-Haxe collection/lifetime gap, not an editor-specific rule.
design: First reduce the exact shape into the enum/Array fixture: an exhaustive command-like switch returns one- and multi-element Array literals containing fieldless and payload variants of one managed enum, including duplicate values and a returned Array consumed after source locals end. Reuse the existing typed Array element copy/retain plan so each slot acquires an independent owner before the temporary enum owner is released, and then move the Array owner to the caller through the existing return contract. Preserve evaluation order, partial-copy rollback, borrowed inputs, and reverse cleanup. Do not change the editor API to caller-filled storage, classify the enum as unmanaged, leak temporary owners, or special-case its names.
acceptance_criteria: Focused ordinary-Haxe fixtures cover direct and switch-selected returned Array literals with fieldless and managed-payload variants, mixed variants, borrowed payload inputs, duplicate elements, and failure cleanup. HxcIR proves each fresh enum value has one bounded owner until the typed Array slot acquires its independent copy, the returned Array moves exactly once to its caller, and unrelated temporaries clean up in reverse order. Eval and generated C agree under split/package/unity, cold/reversed/warm-server determinism, GCC/Clang strict C11 and C++17 O0/O2, ASan/UBSan, and allocation-failure rollback. Existing fail-closed ownership diagnostics remain for unsupported escapes. The unmodified EditorObservationPlan.changesFor function compiles past the former function-exit diagnostic and the Caxecraft snapshot owner either passes or identifies one separately tracked later compiler boundary.
close_reason: Implemented the general managed-enum Array-literal ownership transfer. lowerManagedArrayLiteral now stabilizes each fresh managed enum exactly like Array.push: a bounded temporary owns the constructor result while the typed runtime copy gives the Array slot its independent owner, then normal/failure cleanup releases the temporary. Added a returned Array<RuleEnvelope> fixture with fresh payload, borrowed, and fieldless variants; HxcIR asserts construct -> owner -> create-literal -> reverse cleanup, and updated owned C/HxcIR/symbol snapshots. Evidence: focused render/validate passed; python3 test/enum_lowering/run.py --native-only passed its strict native matrix; the registered enum owner advanced through its core cold/reverse/metal, production layouts, server, String, class, and native work before an independently reproduced pre-existing Bytes dependency-closure mismatch now owned by haxe_c-8al.3; npm run snapshots:update -- --suite caxecraft-domain passed Eval plus split/package/unity generated-C/native differential and proved the unchanged EditorObservationPlan compiles beyond the former diagnostic; format, typed-boundary, and diff checks passed. No editor workaround or special case was added.

title: Expose stable editor tree observations and changed IDs
description:
## Why

The shared editor boundary can reject stale writes and return whole-draft copies, but a visual property panel or automation client still has to rescan the entire Scenario to discover authored content, and mutation results do not say which stable semantic IDs changed. Encoding JSONL now would only freeze this incomplete service and is blocked by the planned haxe.Json and hosted I/O capabilities.

## What

Add compact copy-owned campaign-tree and selection/property observations over the existing typed EditorSession model. Report deterministic changed semantic IDs from single and batched mutations, including deletion and replacement, without introducing transport, renderer, filesystem, Dynamic, or raw-C types.

## How

Derive closed observation records from canonical Scenario order and existing nominal IDs. Keep summaries small and typed: authored kind, stable ID, optional display/reference facts, validation state, and current selection/property facts. Compute changed IDs from the accepted command family and canonical before/after state, deduplicate in stable order, and attach them to applied mutation results. Queries and results remain revision-tagged and copy-owned. JSONL/MCP later serialize this exact service once their general compiler/runtime dependencies land.
acceptance_criteria: A closed query returns a deterministic campaign/level tree and selected-object/property observations tagged with the current revision; callers cannot mutate live editor state through returned values. Applied single commands and atomic batches report exact stable changed IDs in deterministic deduplicated order, including create/update/delete and recovery cases; unchanged and rejected work report no committed changed IDs. Undo and redo identify the restored transaction or object set without rescanning in transport code. Eval and generated-C/native tests cover ordering, replacement, deletion, multi-command deduplication, selection, validation diagnostics, rollback, undo/redo, and copy ownership. The native editor may consume the same observation for an implemented UI slice, but JSONL, MCP, haxe.Json, stdin, files, sockets, arbitrary code, and unrestricted host access remain outside this child and are named as blocked/deferred dependencies rather than emulated locally.
close_reason: Implemented revision-tagged, copy-owned editor tree/node/validation observations and deterministic changed semantic IDs across single edits, atomic batches, undo/redo, and recovery. Verified by test:caxecraft-editor (42 protocol checks), test:caxecraft-app-screen (Eval/native C plus sanitizers), the full caxecraft-domain snapshot updater, all-sources, typed-boundaries, Haxe formatting, snapshot catalog ownership, and diff checks. JSONL/MCP transport remains correctly deferred to haxe_c-0bx and haxe_c-fwg.

title: Add revisioned atomic editor commands and observations
description:
## Why

The 3D editor and renderer-independent EditorSession already share a closed command vocabulary, but callers cannot detect stale state, group related edits atomically, or inspect one immutable state envelope. Adding JSONL or MCP first would duplicate these semantics in transport code and could expose partially applied campaign edits.

## What

Add a renderer- and transport-independent editor service boundary with monotonic draft revisions, revision-checked single commands, bounded all-or-nothing command batches, and closed read-only observations. Route the current visual editor mutation path through this boundary while retaining the natural local convenience API for focused tests.

## How

Stage a batch against a private deep scenario image and selection, validate every command through the existing reducer, then commit one canonical before/after history entry only if the complete batch succeeds. A stale revision, oversized/empty batch, or rejected command leaves draft, selection, history, and revision unchanged. Queries return copied typed state rather than EditorSession internals. JSONL, file access, MCP, screenshots, and gameplay driving remain later adapters over this service.
acceptance_criteria:
A monotonic non-negative revision changes exactly once for every applied single command, applied batch, undo, or redo and does not change for rejected or semantically unchanged work. Revision-checked commands reject stale callers with expected/actual values before mutation. A bounded batch of related commands commits as one undoable history entry; any command failure rolls back the whole batch and preserves draft bytes, selection, history depths, and revision exactly. Empty and oversized batches fail closed.

A closed query API returns immutable/copy-owned session state, selection, canonical draft bytes, and deep draft snapshots tagged with one revision. Mutating returned arrays, bytes, or scenarios cannot affect the editor. The native editor submits edits through the revision-aware boundary. Target-neutral Haxe tests cover success, conflict, rollback, bounds, one-step undo/redo, copied observations, and deterministic results; Eval/generated C/native parity, editor, app-screen, typed-boundary, formatting, documentation, and relevant flagship checks pass. No JSON, Dynamic, filesystem, socket, raw C, or Raylib type enters the service.
close_reason: Implemented the renderer- and transport-independent editor service boundary: monotonic revision checks, bounded all-or-nothing batches, one-entry transaction undo/redo, and copy-owned typed/canonical observations. The native 3D editor now mutates through this boundary. Eval/generated-C/native editor checks, app-screen sanitizer/runtime-free checks, the deterministic graphical pilot, playable snapshots, the snapshot catalog, formatting, typed boundaries, all-sources, fixture/governance/CI policy, and the full split/package/unity snapshot owner passed. The selected runtime feature set remains unchanged; verbose runtime-reason ordinal churn remains owned by haxe_c-5sd.5.16. JSONL/MCP/file/process adapters remain intentionally open under parent haxe_c-xge.19.6.3.

title: Render, navigate, and select the first real 3D editor viewport
description:
## Why

Caxecraft currently presents its canonical draft through a top-down pixel grid. That proved the editor command/session boundary, but it does not let an author understand or work inside the voxel world they are building.

## What

Make the native editor canvas a perspective 3D view of the current draft. Add a focused fly camera and pointer selection for the existing select/paint/erase/fill tools. Keep all mutations routed through EditorSession and keep camera/hover state presentation-only.

## How

Add renderer-independent camera-step and ray-to-draft projection facts that Eval can test, then adapt Raylib input and drawing at CaxecraftEditorScreen. Use an exact pinned Raylib scissor boundary so the 3D view cannot draw over the toolbar or sidebar. Cache decoded draft cells only after accepted commands. Start with the currently admitted finite draft and current editable layer while making the representation volume-shaped so later layer, object, trigger, and cutscene tools extend the same boundary.
design:
The CAXEMAP draft remains the sole editable world. A cached volume projection is read-only presentation data. A closed camera input produces a new camera snapshot; mouse/keyboard handling translates native input into that target-neutral value. Pointer picking first chooses the nearest visible solid voxel, then the editable floor cell when the ray reaches empty space. The selected tool still becomes an EditorCommand and commits only through EditorSession.apply.

This slice owns perspective viewport, clipping, fly/look/zoom/focus controls, voxel hover/selection, and one deterministic graphical proof. It does not claim object gizmos, multiple editor modes, full multi-layer authoring, top-down view switching, persistence, CLI/JSONL, MCP, or campaign authoring; those remain on haxe_c-xge.19.6.3 and its linked tasks.
acceptance_criteria:
The native editor canvas is a clipped perspective 3D view rather than the old 2D-only grid; empty cells remain spatially legible, placed blocks have volume and depth, hover and selected cells have distinct outlines, and toolbar/sidebar/status remain unobscured. Keyboard/mouse controls provide bounded forward/back/strafe/vertical movement, pointer-look, wheel movement, and focus reset with localized instructions. Left-click select/paint/erase/fill resolves a visible draft coordinate and sends the existing typed command through EditorSession, history, validation, and projection refresh; UI code never writes cached cells.

Target-neutral Haxe tests cover camera focus/step/clamps, volume projection, included/excluded ray hits, nearest solid selection, empty-floor selection, and tool translation; generated C and strict native evidence cover Ray fields, scissor calls, cleanup, and no raw-C workaround. The editor-shell memory-software pilot applies a deterministic camera change, paints and selects one voxel through production methods, captures a nonblank perspective frame with visible depth/selection evidence, repeats byte/semantic checks, and exits within its bound. English and Mexican-Spanish labels, typed-boundary, localization, app-screen, Raylib binding, snapshot ownership, and Caxecraft playable gates pass. Any compiler gap is reduced and fixed generally before the editor is weakened.
notes: Implemented 2026-07-29: the native editor now renders the complete finite draft as a clipped perspective volume, supports bounded WASD/QE fly, right-button look, wheel travel, F focus, Raylib ray picking, typed Select/Paint/Erase/Fill submission through EditorSession, and read-only projection refresh only after accepted state changes. The renderer-neutral module owns volume projection, camera math, and nearest-solid/empty-floor picking; RaylibHx gained exact generated BeginScissorMode/EndScissorMode ABI calls plus read-only by-value Ray components. English and es-MX instructions and newcomer docs describe the current controls and bounded limitations. The editor-shell pilot moves the real camera, paints/selects one voxel, requires sky/ground/solid/selection framebuffer evidence, repeats deterministically, and exits bounded. Generated C contains structured loops, no goto, no allocator call in the new spatial module, and direct scissor/ray/session calls. Discovered haxe_c-5sd.5.16 owns encounter-order runtime-reason snapshot churn; haxe_c-7ge.1 owns readable Haxe for-loop control names. Full layers, object gizmos/modes, persistence, controller support, compact vast-world editing, and agent CLI/MCP remain on the parent.
close_reason: Shipped the first truthful 3D editor viewport through natural Haxe and exact RaylibHx bindings: complete finite-volume projection, bounded fly/focus camera, nearest-solid and empty-floor picking, clipped perspective rendering, typed EditorSession mutations, localized controls, and deterministic graphical evidence. Verified by test:caxecraft-editor, test:caxecraft-localization, test:caxecraft-app-screen, test:raylib-provisioning via its registered updater, the memory-software editor-shell pilot, caxecraft-domain registered snapshot update with Eval/split/package/unity native/O2 parity, test:caxecraft-playable, test:all-sources, typed-boundaries, CI/capability/governance/fixture policy, snapshot catalog, Haxe formatting, generated-C review, and diff checks. Deferred parent scope remains explicit; report churn and loop-name readability have separate discovered owners.

title: Make the 3D editor text-native and agent-driveable
description:
## Why

The current checked editor is a useful 2D shell, but the intended product is an in-world 3D authoring tool. A creator should be able to fly through the same world players see, select terrain and authored objects directly, and inspect or change their behavior. An AI agent should be able to create the same campaign without clicking pixels or maintaining a second private format.

## What

Make the primary editor viewport a rendered 3D world with fly, walk, orbit, and cinematic navigation. Keep a top-down view as an optional planning view or minimap, not as the only editor. Build modes cover terrain, entities and prefabs, logic volumes and connections, cameras and cutscenes, audio and lighting, and immediate Test Play.

Keep canonical campaign, level, region, object, rule, localization, cutscene, and test data in the public versioned Caxe formats. A human may edit that model visually or through an exact text view; an agent may edit it through files or a typed local automation service. All routes load, validate, mutate, undo, save, and test the same EditorSession model.

## How

Expose a renderer-independent typed editor command/query protocol above EditorSession. Commands name stable semantic IDs, carry expected draft revisions, execute as bounded transactions, return structured diagnostics and changed IDs, and participate in the same undo/redo history as visible edits. Queries inspect the current campaign tree, selection, properties, references, validation results, viewport/camera, and test state. The Raygui 3D editor, a local CLI/JSONL adapter, CaxeTest/Pilot tooling, and a later thin MCP adapter reuse that service. MCP is optional development integration: it must not become an engine dependency, a second data model, or an arbitrary code/filesystem/network escape.

Large voxel terrain remains compact: generators, regions, palettes, bounded chunk runs, stamps, and sparse authored overrides describe the world instead of requiring an agent to emit one record per block. The visual editor renders and edits that same representation. Cutscene cameras, paths, trigger volumes, audio zones, lights, entities, and logic links are first-class selectable authored objects.
design:
One canonical typed document model has multiple views. The text files are the durable source of truth and must stay deterministic, human-diffable, agent-writable, and independently valid without launching the editor. The 3D editor is a projection plus command producer over that model; it does not serialize hidden widget state into campaign content. The optional top-down view helps large-scale terrain planning.

Use a closed EditorCommand family and read-only EditorQuery/EditorObservation values rather than exposing EditorSession internals. Every mutation carries a base revision and is atomic: it either commits one validated change set with inverse data for undo, or leaves the draft unchanged with source/object-linked diagnostics. Batch transactions let an agent create a coherent region, encounter, or cutscene without exposing partially linked state. Stable IDs, typed references, deterministic canonical writing, and explicit rename/delete repair protect text, visual, test, and agent workflows together.

The local command-line adapter comes first because it is simple to script, test, and recover. Use bounded JSON Lines requests and responses only at this process boundary; validate immediately into closed Haxe types. A later MCP server is a thin translation layer over the same service, offering discoverable resources and tools for editor state, edits, validation, Test Play, screenshots, and traces. Neither adapter can execute arbitrary Haxe/C, shell commands, unrestricted host paths, or remote network requests.

Reuse haxe_c-xge.19.8 for real-engine driving and observations, haxe_c-xge.19.8.1 for the explicitly enabled local game/agent bridge, haxe_c-xge.19.9 for typed action vocabulary, haxe_c-xge.19.10 for event sources and visual trigger authoring, and haxe_c-xge.19.6.2 for reversible in-process Test Play. This issue owns editor-authoring automation, not a duplicate gameplay driver.
acceptance_criteria:
The primary native editor shows the authored level in 3D and supports mouse/keyboard/controller fly, walk, orbit, focus-selection, and cinematic-camera navigation; the same object may be selected in 3D, the optional top-down view, the campaign tree, or a diagnostic and resolves to one stable ID. Terrain/chunk/stamp tools and typed placement tools can create, move, rotate where applicable, resize, duplicate, connect, and delete entities, prefabs, spawns, checkpoints, items, trigger volumes, paths, cameras, lights, audio zones, exits/entrances, and other admitted objects. Logic and cutscene modes inspect and edit the same CaxeFlow/action/camera/timeline data used at runtime, including preview and reversible Test Play.

Canonical text can create the same campaign without the GUI, and visual edit -> canonical save -> text load -> visual save is byte- and semantic-stable. Large terrain uses bounded compact descriptions plus sparse overrides rather than per-voxel text. The Haxirio/Ivvy village-to-underwater/bridge-to-castle/Browser reference campaign is authored through these public files and editor/automation surfaces; required terrain, placement, cameras, dialogue, objectives, encounters, and progression are not hidden in Haxe source.

A documented closed editor command/query protocol supports campaign/tree/state inspection; typed create/update/delete/rename/connect operations; validated batch transactions; revision conflict detection; undo/redo; validation; save/load; Edit/Test Play transitions; semantic input; fixed-tick waits; screenshots; traces; and bounded quit. The visible editor, CLI/JSONL adapter, and later MCP adapter reach the same EditorSession operations and produce deterministic audit traces. An agent can create or modify a small multi-object level and cutscene, validate it, run a CaxeTest case through the real engine, inspect failure state, capture a screenshot, repair the content, save it, and reopen it in the 3D editor without human clicks.

Malformed JSONL/MCP input, stale revisions, duplicate IDs, invalid references, partial batch failure, oversized requests, unavailable commands, unsafe paths, arbitrary code, shell access, remote bind, and unbounded work fail closed. Eval tests own command/model semantics; generated C owns native parity and cleanup; selected memory-software pilots own rendered 3D selection and agent-driven screenshot evidence. Documentation includes a five-minute child-friendly visual path, an advanced text path, and a concise agent/CLI/MCP contract, while distinguishing implemented adapters from planned ones.

title: Return Bytes-decoded managed Strings safely
description: Why: GuiTextBoxState.text() naturally returns storage.getString(0, length), but haxe.c maps the function signature to a static String view before it notices that Bytes.getString creates an owned runtime String. The body then fails with result-requires-managed-String even though managed String return/call/root machinery already exists. What: make whole-program String representation planning account for fresh String producers that cross function returns, without changing the natural Haxe API or weakening lifetime checks. How: reduce the shape to a focused Bytes decode helper returning String; select the managed function result before body lowering; preserve borrowed literal/String identity paths; prove transfer, cleanup, roots, deterministic output, and strict native behavior; then resume the unchanged Raygui state API.
design: Treat Bytes.getString as a fresh managed producer. Function result and every caller must agree on the managed String ABI before HxcIR construction. Reuse the existing managed String return ownership protocol; do not special-case Raygui or generate a static view for runtime-owned bytes.
acceptance_criteria: A focused ordinary-Haxe helper returns Bytes.getString through String and agrees under Eval/generated C for ASCII and multibyte UTF-8; HxcIR records managed result ownership and caller transfer; invalid ranges/UTF-8 retain existing behavior; strict C11 O0/O2, sanitizer, deterministic layout/server, Bytes/String/body/function/HxcIR gates pass; GuiTextBoxState.text() compiles unchanged and its semantic fixture reaches Raygui lowering.
notes:
Implemented the general compiler fix without changing Raygui or Caxecraft's natural API. Whole-program String representation discovery now recognizes exact haxe.io.Bytes.getString/toString calls before function signatures are prepared, so helpers and callers agree on the managed String return ABI. The helper transfers the fresh immutable owner; caller cleanup releases it after use. Runtime-plan direct-decision derivation now distinguishes compiler-owned literal bytes from runtime-created Strings and reports exact expected/actual decision lists on internal drift.

Added a focused ordinary-Haxe regression whose Bytes-decoding helpers return ASCII/multibyte snapshots and whose caller mutates the source afterward. The lane proves Eval/native behavior, managed HxcIR return/caller cleanup, deterministic reversed discovery, exact runtime closure, strict C11 O0/O2, C++ headers, and Clang sanitizers. Registered the fixture in CI/capability ownership and documented the cross-function lifetime.

Verified: test:bytes-runtime -- --toolchain clang; test:body-lowering; test:function-lowering; test:hxc-ir; test:raygui-binding; test:capabilities; check_ci_policy.py; py_compile; git diff --check.

title: Admit validated factory class construction
description: Why: the natural GuiTextBoxState.create factory validates capacity before constructing its state object, but haxe.c rejects the ordinary TNew merely because it occurs after a guard instead of unconditionally in the entry block. That forces public APIs toward invalid objects or compiler-shaped workarounds. What: generalize class construction so a non-escaping or correctly managed instance can be created after ordinary structured guards while preserving initialization, ownership, cleanup, and generated-C readability. How: reduce the Raygui factory to a focused class-construction fixture, make storage/lifetime selection depend on real escape and control-flow facts rather than entry-block position, retain fail-closed unsupported cases, then resume the unchanged natural Haxe factory.
design: Keep the source-language class contract. A guard changes control flow, not object identity. Use the existing managed/escaping class representation when the result escapes through return; do not force stack storage merely because the constructor appears syntactically local, and do not weaken cleanup validation.
acceptance_criteria: A focused positive fixture constructs a class after a validation guard and returns it through Null without raw C or source restructuring; Eval and generated C agree for accepted and rejected inputs; HxcIR represents initialization and ownership on every reachable path; strict C11 O0/O2, sanitizer, deterministic output, class-layout/constructor/function/body/HxcIR gates pass; the Raygui semantic fixture compiles unchanged.

A concrete class crossing a reachable return now uses stable collector storage across its inheritance family, enabling validated Null<Class> factories, class pass-through, and traced children returned from temporary parents without dangling C pointers. Replaced four obsolete rejection fixtures with one positive Eval/native/GC stress fixture; updated class-layout snapshots, capability claims, and beginner-facing architecture docs. Verified focused factory Eval/split/package/unity/reversed/warm-server/C11 O0+O2/C++17/sanitizer matrix; remaining constructor negatives; HxcIR, class-layout, function-lowering, body-lowering, class-layout snapshot, capabilities, and governance gates.

title: Admit ordinary Bytes UTF-8 string snapshots

title: Admit call-scoped mutable Bytes buffers at C imports
description: Why: C APIs such as raygui GuiTextBox accept a caller-owned char pointer plus capacity, but haxe.c currently admits only scalar c.Ref borrows and static c.CString literals. Application code must not use raw C, pointer casts, or duplicate shadow state to bridge that gap. What: add a narrow typed c.* capability that lends an owned haxe.io.Bytes buffer to one direct imported-C call as mutable char storage, while preserving the Bytes owner and preventing return, storage, retention, or indirect-call escape. How: encode the borrow in HxcIR, validate its producer/consumer/lifetime independently, project an exact char pointer through a validated hxrt helper, and retain the direct-import boundary as its sole consumer.
design: Use a dedicated call-scoped mutable C-string-buffer reference rather than widening c.Ref or exposing a general pointer. The source owner is ordinary haxe.io.Bytes; the borrowed pointer is a distinct HxcIR type and may originate only from the recognized c.* intrinsic, be consumed only by one matching direct C import argument, and never escape. The selected imported declaration records its capacity partner and call lifetime. hxrt validates the Bytes owner and non-empty storage before publishing a char pointer; the semantic library owner remains responsible for a NUL within capacity and for passing the exact capacity. Add no Caxecraft or Raygui path/name special case.
acceptance_criteria: A positive ordinary-Haxe fixture owns Bytes, initializes a NUL-terminated UTF-8 buffer, lends it to an independent C function for one call, observes native mutation, and releases storage deterministically under strict C11, C++17, ASan, and UBSan. HxcIR contains an explicit mutable-buffer borrow and validator-approved single native consumer. Negative fixtures reject temporary owners, return/storage/indirect escape, wrong carrier, missing intrinsic, retained-pointer declarations, zero-capacity buffers at runtime, and mismatched imported parameter kind. Generated C uses the exact char pointer ABI without raw source injection or an application special case. Runtime feature manifests, ABI, docs, typed boundaries, snapshots, and focused compiler gates pass.
notes: Implemented c.CStringBufferRef.to(bytes) as a narrow one-call mutable text borrow. Schema-21 HxcIR gives the pointer its own non-storable type and independently requires one same-block direct native consumer; hxrt validates a live non-empty Bytes allocation and an in-bounds NUL before publishing char *. The ordinary Bytes value remains the owner, while typed bindings retain responsibility for exact capacity and post-call UTF-8/NUL validation. Added an independent handwritten-C mutation fixture, strict C11 O0/O2, C++17 header, ASan/UBSan, deterministic split/unity, runtime-policy, and source/HxcIR negative evidence for temporary/wrong owners, wrong parameter kind, missing intrinsic, retained return, storage, control-flow/return, indirect, and double use. Updated runtime manifests, capability inventory, schema snapshots, and Caxecraft's selected-Bytes manifest. Verified test:bytes-runtime (clang), test:hxc-ir, test:c-import (clang), test:runtime-features, test:typed-c, test:typed-boundaries, test:capabilities, test:all-sources, selective affected snapshot check plus registered Caxecraft/HxcIR updates, snapshot catalog, and test:governance. Local gcc identifies as clang, so the real GCC lane remains CI-owned.
close_reason: Call-scoped managed Bytes-to-char-pointer interop is implemented, independently validated, native/sanitizer verified, documented, and integrated into the exact runtime/schema manifests.

description: Why: the pinned RayguiHx surface can render buttons, toggles, and lists, but it cannot yet safely pass raygui's mutable char* text buffer. description: The real Caxecraft editor compile now advances beyond Array.shift and reaches EditorCommandReducer.removeMessage, where a comprehension and closed-record construction produce legitimate retain requirements at the same source position. Add a shared-reference wrapper, advance the internal same-major runtime ABI for the additive entry point, represent the nullable result and explicit failure edge in HxcIR, validate the exact Array/element/result contract independently, and keep CAST as a structural call projection. acceptance_criteria: Ordinary Haxe primitive and managed-record Arrays exercise present, repeated, and empty shift; results and alias-visible lengths/order match Haxe Eval; managed payload ownership transfers exactly once without callback/allocation churn and is released correctly; direct runtime tests cover empty, alias rejection, invalid inputs, suffix relocation, and lifecycle counters; HxcIR records an explicit shift operation with exact nullable result and failure edge; malformed result shapes fail validation; generated C structurally calls the typed shift-move wrapper without raw C; strict Clang/GCC O0/O2 and eligible sanitizers pass; portable/metal/reversed/server output is deterministic; runtime=none fails closed; stdlib ledger/docs/ABI manifests are exact; Caxecraft advances beyond EditorHistory.record to either success or one separately owned blocker.

Direct native tests cover invalid receivers, live-slot output alias rejection, empty/present/repeated primitive shifts, alias-visible suffix order, and managed relocation with frozen lifecycle/allocation counters. Full Array Eval/generated-C/Clang/sanitizer/server/profile matrix, native smoke, runtime-feature graph, HxcIR, stdlib ledger, string output, and Haxe formatting pass. title: Lower Array.resize(0) as ownership-aware clear
description: Context: The real Caxecraft editor history clears its redo branch with ordinary Haxe redoEntries.resize(0). Making visual paint/history reachable now stops at Array.resize:not-yet-admitted. Rewriting history around this compiler limit would weaken the flagship source design. Scope: Admit the exact resize(0) clear form for every already-supported Array element specialization. Preserve shared Array identity, reverse typed destruction of all removed elements, source evaluation order, failure/cleanup attribution, collector-backed containers, runtime selection, and strict structural C. Non-scope: Growing resize, nonzero or dynamic lengths, default-element construction, other Array methods, or a new public runtime ABI entry point. Compatibility: Portable and metal use the same existing hxrt array storage contract; runtime=none remains fail-closed; no public application ABI is added.
design: Recognize only an exact nonnegative integer-zero argument after normal typed-call classification. Lower it to an explicit validated HxcIR Array resize-zero operation after a semantic null check. CAST calls the already-versioned hxc_array_resize on the reference container's embedded storage with length zero and no default element; zero can only shrink or no-op, so it never needs Haxe target-default synthesis. The runtime destroys removed elements in reverse order through the specialization's existing typed lifecycle callbacks. Keep every nonzero or dynamic resize as an exact negative until general growth/default construction is separately owned.
acceptance_criteria: A focused ordinary-Haxe fixture clears aliased Array<Int> and managed-record Arrays with resize(0), matches Eval, observes zero length through aliases, and proves every removed managed field is released exactly once in reverse order; HxcIR contains the explicit null check and resize-zero operation; generated C structurally calls existing hxc_array_resize without raw C or a new ABI symbol; strict Clang/GCC O0/O2 and eligible sanitizers pass; portable/metal/reversed/server output is deterministic; runtime=none rejects the Array requirement; nonzero and dynamic resize remain exact fail-closed negatives with no output; Caxecraft compile advances beyond EditorHistory.record without a source workaround; docs explain the bounded clear versus deferred growth contract.

Full Array Eval/native/Clang/sanitizer/determinism/server/profile lane passed; Caxecraft advanced past EditorHistory.resize(0) to the distinct Array.shift gap.
