title: Admit caller-owned fresh Array arguments for direct borrowed calls
description:
Context: Caxecraft naturally passes a fresh Array<BlockPaletteEntry> literal to a direct static helper whose Array parameter is borrowed for the call. The compiler already stabilizes the same fresh managed Array owner for constructors and selected Array operations, but ordinary direct static and instance calls reject it as ownerless. This is a general Haxe Array call-lifetime gap, not editor-specific behavior.

Scope: Extend direct static and direct instance call lowering so a fresh reference-counted Array argument receives one caller-owned automatic temporary, is borrowed by the callee for the call, and is released exactly once on normal and abrupt exits. Preserve source evaluation order, concrete Array specialization, runtime-feature provenance, and readable structural C. Generalize the existing stabilizer rather than adding an application special case.

Non-scope: Indirect/function-value calls, StringMap or other managed families, callee-consuming/ownership-transfer parameters, public ABI exports, or broad collection parity. These remain fail-closed unless separately owned and proven.

Requirements: HXC-COMP-002, HXC-COMP-003, HXC-SEM-004, HXC-SEM-007, HXC-RT-009, HXC-QA-001.

Compatibility: Ordinary Haxe portable semantics; portable and metal share the same call rule. The existing Array runtime slice remains selected only by the Array operation. runtime=none must still reject the resulting Array requirement. No public ABI change.
design: Reuse stabilizeFreshManagedArray after argument conversion in the direct static and direct instance call paths. HxcIR must show a named automatic owner initialized from the fresh Array, the call receiving a loaded borrow, and one runtime Array release registered in the enclosing cleanup region. Keep the independent indirect-call rejection so this change cannot silently broaden an unmodeled callable boundary.
acceptance_criteria: A focused ordinary-Haxe fixture passes a fresh Array literal to both direct static and direct instance borrowed parameters and matches Haxe Eval under generated strict C11; HxcIR proves one caller-owned automatic Array temporary, borrowed call use, and exactly-once release; GCC and Clang O0/O2 plus eligible sanitizer lanes pass; portable and metal output is deterministic; runtime=none reports the Array requirement; an indirect/function-value fresh-Array call remains an exact fail-closed negative; the Caxecraft editor compile passes its original natural createBlankEditorScenario call without a source workaround; nearby ownership documentation/HxDoc explains the call contract.
close_reason: Fresh Array literals now cross known direct static and instance borrowed-call boundaries with one explicit caller owner and exactly-once cleanup. Verified by npm run test:array-runtime (Eval, HxcIR owner/borrow/release assertions, portable and metal reversed-discovery determinism, warm-server parity, strict native C, Clang O0/sanitizers; true GCC unavailable locally and remains CI-owned), npm run test:typed-boundaries, npm run test:hxc-ir, npm run test:function-lowering, npm run test:all-sources, npm run format:haxe:check, and the Caxecraft compile advancing beyond its original call to the unrelated planned Array.slice boundary. runtime=none/metal-runtime-none and indirect-call negatives remain fail-closed.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: Implemented the general direct-call ownership rule with no Caxecraft special case. A fresh reference-counted Array passed to a known static function or instance method now moves into one caller-owned automatic HxcIR local, the call receives a loaded borrow, and the enclosing cleanup region performs one exactly-once runtime Array release. The independent function-value form still fails with TCall(indirect-managed-argument-needs-explicit-ownership:0). The original Caxecraft createBlankEditorScenario call now lowers successfully; compile-only advanced to the separate planned Array.slice boundary in EditorWorldGrid.hx:254.

title: Connect Raygui editor tools to a real voxel viewport
description: The native editor currently renders a blank panel and ignores the selected Raygui tool. Add the first truthful visual editing vertical: render one bounded top-down voxel layer from an immutable editor draft view, map pointer positions to typed voxel coordinates, and route Select, Paint, Erase, and Fill through the existing EditorSession commands. This is application/editor work over the existing pinned RayguiHx surface; it must not add raw C, a second editor model, or game-specific mutation shortcuts.
design: Keep editor semantics renderer-independent. Add a small typed viewport projection and coordinate mapper that can run on Eval and generated C; CaxecraftEditorScreen owns only presentation state and translates Raygui selection plus Raylib pointer input into the same closed EditorCommand values. Cache the projection after accepted edits instead of serializing the draft every frame. Construct the bounded built-in blank world through public EditorSession commands and base-pack content IDs at the Caxecraft composition edge. Use one pilot-only typed invocation of the same screen command path for deterministic native evidence; do not teach production code fixture coordinates or synthesize operating-system input.
acceptance_criteria: The native editor displays a non-blank bounded voxel grid and visible selection; Raygui list selection chooses Select, Paint, Erase, or Fill; pointer actions map deterministically to in-bounds VoxelPoint values and all changes enter through EditorSession.apply; undo/redo and New World refresh the same cached projection; invalid commands leave the draft and view unchanged with a visible notice; steady frames do not serialize or allocate a new draft projection; focused Eval/generated-C tests cover projection, coordinate mapping, each tool, and bounds; the editor graphical pilot applies one real paint through the same typed screen path, observes the committed edit, captures two byte-identical screenshots, and exits; formatting, typed-boundary, editor, pilot, full Caxecraft snapshot/native, maintainability, runtime/allocation, and governance gates pass.
notes: Implemented the first truthful native editor viewport. EditorViewport projects one validated horizontal CAXEMAP layer, shares one integer layout between drawing and pointer hit-testing, and translates Select/Paint/Erase/Fill into the existing closed EditorCommand language. CaxecraftEditorScreen caches that read-only projection and refreshes it only after New World, accepted edits, undo, or redo; all mutation remains owned by EditorSession. The application composition edge supplies base-pack Air/Grass IDs to a content-neutral blank-world factory. The editor-shell pilot submits one deterministic Paint through the production screen/session path, validates exactly one accepted edit, renders a nonblank grid, and produces two byte-identical screenshots. Localization copy now comes from locales/ui.json and regenerates UiCatalog.hx. Updated beginner-readable editor docs and registered generated-C snapshots. Verified npm run test:caxecraft-editor; npm run test:caxecraft-localization; memory-software editor-shell graphical pilot; registered caxecraft-domain snapshot update/catalog; npm run test:caxecraft-domain:full (split/package/unity, cold/reversed/locale/warm, O0/O2/ASan+UBSan); npm run format:haxe:check; npm run test:typed-boundaries; npm run test:governance; and git diff --check. The desktop pilot executable also compiled and linked, but this agent process had no accessible macOS monitor; the deterministic memory-software renderer supplied the authoritative graphical evidence.
close_reason: The Raygui editor now displays and edits a cached bounded voxel layer through typed EditorSession commands, with deterministic Eval/generated-C/native graphical, snapshot, maintainability, and sanitizer evidence.

title: Reuse unchanged functions' shared-semantic discovery
description: The representative five-run incremental report now meets the initial changed-source budget at 12.285s p95, but remains above the 10s destination. On the edited request, HxcIR representation planning is the largest exclusive owner at 1.257s median; function preparation and replay-key construction each cost about 1.0s even though 508 of 509 semantic functions are reused. The current safe replay must rediscover every function's Array/class/map/import/adapter/global contribution before it can prove the shared program revision. Reuse those immutable contributions for frontend-reused declarations while rebuilding the exact changed closure, without retaining Haxe compiler objects or trusting path/mtime hints.
design: Persist a bounded, schema-versioned per-function contribution record containing only target-owned immutable values and the exact prior function input/provenance identity. Build the current request's shared representation/import/adapter/global plan from prior contributions only for declarations Haxe explicitly reports as frontend-reused and whose source/module/configuration identity remains compatible; rediscover every rebuilt or uncertain declaration. Canonically merge contributions, settle the same complete function-free program revision, and compare it in full before any HxcIR function replay. A missing, removed, renamed, ambiguous, cross-worktree, cache-off, or incompatible record is a visible rediscovery miss. Do not retain Type, TypedExpr, Position, Context, mutable registries, or aggregate objects, and do not skip the independent HxcIR validator.
acceptance_criteria: A focused fixture proves unchanged, one-function implementation edit, class/public-type/layout/dispatch/generic/runtime/import/static-global change, removal/rename/shadow, define/classpath/macro dependency, failure-success, restart, cache-off, two-worktree, corruption, and bounded-soak behavior against fresh-process HxcIR and generated bytes. The full playable edit reuses 508/509 eligible contribution records, rebuilds the changed one, and preserves exact runtime/ABI/init/dispatch/symbol/specialization reports and native behavior. An unsaturated five-run report attributes the saved work and reaches changed-source p95 at or below 10 seconds, or closes the experiment with the next measured owner and no weakened validation.

title: Settle static globals before freezing function replay
description: The new semantic-function replay prepass froze its function-free HxcIR program before static initializer destinations and ordinary static-field references had registered their globals. A natural reachable static field therefore produced an initializer or load instruction that named a global absent from the program, and HxcIRValidator correctly stopped compilation with HXC9000. The dedicated static-initialization suite and the mixed incremental fixture both reproduce this regression. This is a replay-planning order bug, not an application restriction.
design: During the output-inert shared-body prepass, register the destination owned by every static-field initializer and register every referenced ordinary Haxe static field after first excluding typed C import constants. Only then take the canonical global set and freeze the function-free replay revision. Preserve the unknown-global validator invariant and use the ordinary BodyGlobalRegistry path so the prepass cannot invent a second global model.
acceptance_criteria: A reachable non-entry class with a mutable initialized static field lowers that field and its initializer into one internally consistent HxcIR program; the generated C initializes it exactly once before use; the static-initialization plan and project output include the same owner; Eval/native behavior agrees; the minimized mixed class/generic/import shape compiles; HxcIR still rejects a genuinely missing global; deterministic, reversed-order, strict-C, sanitizer, typed-AST, static-initialization, and incremental-cache gates pass.
notes:
Fixed in the shared-body semantic prepass: static-initializer destinations and referenced ordinary Haxe static fields now enter the canonical global registry before the replay revision freezes. Typed C import constants remain owned by the import plan. The full static-initialization suite passes exact-once initialization, dependency ordering, cycle diagnostics, JavaScript differential behavior, and strict native C; the mixed incremental catalog and fresh-process oracle also pass.
The exhaustive matrix additionally proved two fail-closed boundaries: constant primitive globals must be admitted without moving unsupported-field diagnostics, and bare extern classes must remain owned by the TNew diagnostic rather than typed-C import discovery. Local enum layouts are now also settled before replay; evaluation-order, constructor-lowering, and String runtime focused owners pass.
Closure evidence: the final five-lane resumable toolchain matrix passed contracts, lowering-objects, lowering-semantics, Caxecraft, and native with two bounded workers. The focused String runtime, generic-specialization, and full Caxecraft snapshot/native owners also passed without refreshing expected output.
close_reason: Static initializer destinations, admitted constant globals, and local enum storage now settle before replay without stealing unsupported native-layout diagnostics; focused and exhaustive semantic/native gates pass.

title: Prove incremental-backend invalidation, soak, and budgets
description: Semantic-function replay now removes unchanged typed-body construction, but the parent cannot close from one implementation edit. Prove that every whole-program semantic input named by the parent invalidates the exact safe closure, that repeated warm requests keep one bounded successful generation, and that cold/cache-off behavior remains authoritative. Measure staged cold, unchanged, and one-module-edit budgets only on a declared unsaturated host; if the destination budget remains unmet, attribute the largest exclusive owner and create the narrowest implementation child instead of weakening keys or validation.
design: Extend the existing ordered Haxe-server fixture with a table-driven mutation catalog covering public types, class hierarchy and dispatch, generic specializations, static initialization, runtime features, bindings or target metadata, defines and classpaths, removed, renamed and shadowing modules, and declared macro dependencies. Each case compares a warm request with a fresh-process oracle and requires exact normal artifacts, diagnostics, runtime and ABI plans, symbol and specialization reports, plus one explicit replay miss reason. Add a bounded request-order and memory or retained-size soak that proves one-generation replacement, failure rollback, server restart and two-worktree isolation. Reuse the existing compiler profile and incremental edit report for timing; reject saturated samples according to the documented host criteria.
acceptance_criteria: A fast table-driven fixture proves the complete parent invalidation categories against fresh-process bytes and diagnostics; success, failure, success, corruption, cache-off, server restart, request ordering and two-worktree cases fail closed; a bounded soak proves retained function count and exact-input or process memory do not grow with request count; no persistent Haxe Type, TypedExpr, Position, context, mutable registry, or unbounded generation is introduced; an unsaturated repeated report records median, MAD and p95 for cold, unchanged and one-module edit, meeting changed-source p95 at or below 20 seconds and cold p95 at or below 40 seconds; the report either meets the 10-second destination or names the next narrow measured owner without weakening semantic validation.
notes:
Completed the nine-case table-driven invalidation catalog: static initializer, class hierarchy/dispatch, generic specialization, reachable Array runtime feature, typed C binding metadata, define context, classpath shadow, removed/renamed module, and declared macro dependency. Every warm result matches a fresh-process HxcIR and complete generated tree; restart cases require an exact no-prior-generation result. The existing ordered server matrix retains success-failure-success, cache-off, restart, request ordering, and two-worktree evidence; the replay probe rejects corrupt position evidence and proves 48 requests retain exactly one two-function generation. Caxecraft's owned-server compatibility schema now includes the path-only Haxe module inventory, so body edits remain warm while add/remove/rename replaces the server. A representative five-run report measured cold-prime 33.822s median / 34.209s p95, unchanged 11.993s / 12.317s, and one-module edit 12.166s / 12.285s. Initial cold <=40s and edit <=20s budgets pass. The 10s destination remains open: HxcIR representation planning is the largest edited-request exclusive owner at 1.257s median, followed by roughly 1.0s each in function preparation and replay-key construction. Child haxe_c-5sd.8.4.7 owns immutable per-function shared-semantic contribution replay. A separate direct cold five-run report was contended and is documented only as diagnostic evidence.
A failed exhaustive run exposed three missing shared-prepass cases after the initial focused proof. The corrected prepass now settles valid constant globals and local enums while leaving bare extern/native-layout errors to authoritative source-order lowering. Focused evaluation-order, constructor, String runtime, bootstrap, body-lowering, and warm/fresh invalidation gates pass; exhaustive rerun remains the closure gate.
Closure evidence: after narrowing enum discovery to the local declaration storage boundary, focused String runtime, generic-specialization, and full Caxecraft snapshot/native checks passed unchanged. The final exhaustive five-lane matrix then passed contracts, lowering-objects, lowering-semantics, Caxecraft, and native. The 12.285-second changed-source p95 meets this task's 20-second acceptance budget; haxe_c-5sd.8.4.7 retains the separate 10-second destination.
close_reason: Complete invalidation, restart, bounded-soak, fresh-oracle, repeated-budget, Caxecraft, and exhaustive toolchain evidence passes; the tracked 12.285s edit p95 meets the initial budget and child .7 owns the 10s destination.

title: Make HxcIR function builds replayable
description: The schema-10 contribution inventory found that 490 of 509 full-playable function builds add no new representation, import, or adapter semantics, but 19 builds still enlarge shared program plans and builds register 17,446 shared symbol requests. A direct cache of HxcIRFunction would therefore omit required later-phase facts. Establish the smallest complete immutable function result and program revision that can make proven-unchanged body work replayable without retaining TypedExpr or mutable registries.
design: First reconcile each registered symbol request with the function-owned local, span-length, temporary, tail-argument, and label request maps or with one named shared owner. Move the 19 body-time import, optional, IntMap, and StringMap discoveries into a deterministic pre-build semantic plan where practical; otherwise encode them as one closed immutable contribution package with a single replay owner. Define an exact function input digest plus settled program-plan revision, schema, profile, build mode, compiler identity, and provenance key. Retain at most one preceding successful generation initially. A hit restores the complete function-owned HxcIR, runtime requirements, name requests, and admitted shared contributions before ordinary whole-program validation. Cache-off, explicit miss reasons, failed-request rollback, bounded memory, and cold/warm/edit byte and diagnostic parity remain mandatory.
acceptance_criteria: Focused tests reconcile every build-time symbol request with one closed owner and prove zero/nonzero semantic contribution replay; full Caxecraft reports an exact hit/miss inventory for unchanged and one-module-edit requests; cold, warm unchanged, and edited builds retain byte-identical normal artifacts, reports, diagnostics, runtime and ABI plans, and native behavior; public type, representation, import, adapter, runtime-feature, compiler/schema/profile/build-mode, removed/renamed module, corruption, and success/failure/success cases miss or fail closed; cache-off runs the complete ordinary path; retained state is bounded and contains no Haxe Type, TypedExpr, compilation context, or mutable registry; measured target work improves enough to justify the validation and key cost, otherwise close the experiment as rejected with evidence.
notes:
Implemented schema-1 semantic-function replay with one successful generation, an exact complete shared-program revision, exact canonical typed-function input plus source-range ledger, fresh request-owned restored arrays and positions, explicit miss reasons, cache-off, and transactional publication only after output ownership. The body prepass settles the previously observed import, optional, IntMap, and StringMap facts; a post-build inventory rejects any late shared layout/import/adapter contribution. Final Caxecraft profile under closed profiler schema 11: cold 0 hits/509 misses, warm unchanged 509/0, one Vitals edit 508/1 with one changed-input miss; the edit changed only Vitals.c and hxc.manifest.json. Retained state is bounded to 509 target-owned functions, 5,931,151 exact input string code units, and 931,570 shared-revision code units; no TypedExpr, Type, Position, compilation context, or mutable registry persists. Host load was 8.109 to 6.830 on 12 logical CPUs, so 35.251s/12.945s/12.300s wall values are contended diagnostics, not an uncontended benchmark claim. Verification: test:hxc-ir, test:typed-ast, test:body-lowering, complete Caxecraft domain Eval/split/package/unity/native-O2 differential, test:caxecraft-playable, schema-11 incremental edit profile, caxecraft timing unit tests, typed-boundaries, formatter, governance policy, Python syntax, and git diff check all passed. Registered Caxecraft snapshots were regenerated through their owner and returned exactly to HEAD, proving normal output shape did not drift.
The normal commit hook then caught one cross-suite regression before publication: the output-inert shared discovery pass tried to map a bare null whose inferred record contained an unsupported Map, preempting the all-sources fixture original source-anchored HXC1001. The fix treats a bare null as representation-free and leaves its surrounding declaration/use to own type mapping. The existing fast unsupported-body fixture now contains this nested null/Map reproducer. test:all-sources, test:body-lowering, playable snapshots, and a fresh three-request schema-11 replay profile all pass after the repair; final profile remains 0/509, 509/0, and 508/1, with only Vitals.c and hxc.manifest.json changed by the edit.
The affected commit hook also found that the discovery pass entered Haxe temporary Array syntax for a fixed CArray literal, incorrectly selecting the managed Array runtime. Discovery now applies the same contextual CArray boundary as authoritative managed-representation lowering: fixed primitive storage emits no managed Array or hxrt requirement. The existing span fixture is the focused owner. Its 72-request portable/metal, debug/release, strict-C, sanitizer, and lifetime matrix passed with zero-hxrt links; playable snapshots and a fresh replay profile also passed afterward with the same exact 509/509 and 508/509 decisions.
close_reason: Exact transactional HxcIR function replay is implemented and verified: unchanged warm builds replay 509/509 eligible functions, a one-function edit rebuilds exactly one, output and native behavior remain authoritative, failures roll back, and retained state is bounded.

title: Attribute HxcIR body-discovered program contributions
description: Typed-body lowering still owns about 4.27 seconds of a representative warm Caxecraft target request, but a BuiltBodyFunction is not currently a pure per-function result. During build it can add aggregate, enum, class, interface, Array, map, Bytes, import, adapter, runtime-requirement, and symbol facts needed by the final program. Before admitting cross-request HxcIR function reuse, measure those contributions per stable function ID and distinguish function-owned replayable output from shared program state.
design: Add profiler-only request-local inventories around each FunctionBuilder.build call. Count exact before/after changes in every mutable program registry and name-request surface that body construction can reach, while preserving normal compiler bytes and avoiding persistent Haxe Type/TypedExpr state. The structured report must remain bounded, source-path-free, and attributed by stable function ID. Aggregate tooling should explain which unchanged functions are side-effect-free, which introduce shared facts, and what each future cache hit would have to replay. Do not add an HxcIR reuse path in this issue.
acceptance_criteria: A focused fixture proves zero and non-zero contribution attribution for representative primitive, aggregate/collection, adapter/name, and runtime-requirement bodies; the full Caxecraft profiler validates a closed contribution field inventory and reports deterministic totals by family; profiler-off generated bytes remain exact; profiling identifies the minimum freeze/replay contract or demonstrates that the proposed per-function cache granularity is disproportionate; architecture/performance docs state the evidence and keep HxcIR reuse unauthorized until a later issue owns the complete boundary.
notes: Implemented structured profiler schema 10 with one stable-ID span per ordinary FunctionBuilder build. The closed payload accounts for function-owned HxcIR blocks, instructions, locals, cleanup regions, runtime requirements, and name requests plus before/after deltas for every reachable shared representation, import, adapter, and symbol registry. A fail-closed Python decoder, focused zero/nonzero schema fixture, aggregate report, architecture guide, and performance guide own the contract. One warm full-playable diagnostic accounted for all 509 builds: 490 added no representation/import/adapter semantics; 19 added semantic facts; 452 added symbol requests only; totals were 50 import functions, 7 import owners, 4 import types, 9 optionals, 1 IntMap, 1 StringMap, and 17,446 symbol requests. It built 5,734 blocks, 35,050 instructions, 139 cleanup regions, and 3,645 runtime requirements. Normal artifacts were byte-identical to the warm prime. The host was contended, so 13.862s wall and the 4.315s typed-body observation are diagnostic only. The inventory rejects direct HxcIRFunction-only reuse; child haxe_c-5sd.8.4.5 owns the complete freeze/replay boundary. Verification: body-lowering, symbol-registry, C-import, Haxe formatter, 183 governance tests, focused profile parser tests, and the real warm full-playable profile all passed.
close_reason: Closed: schema-10 attribution now accounts for every profiled function build, preserves normal bytes, documents the minimum replay boundary, and hands implementation to haxe_c-5sd.8.4.5.

title: Reuse exact finalized symbol tables across warm requests
description: A full Caxecraft build registers about 22,923 deterministic C-name requests. A representative changed-Haxe request usually recreates the same complete set, yet haxe.c spends about 1.35 seconds sorting those requests, constructing candidate names, resolving collisions, and materializing the same table. Reuse the prior successful finalized table only when the current request proves that every semantic naming input is exactly identical.
design: Add a bounded one-generation persistent cache around CSymbolRegistry finalization. Its lookup key is the complete canonical request sequence and every request naming fingerprint; the cached value contains only target-owned immutable strings/records needed to reconstruct current-request CIdentifier lookups and the exact symbol report. Keep registration, explicit-name validation, request deduplication, and canonical ordering on every request. A hit may skip draft construction, collision resolution, and table materialization only after exact full-sequence equality. Begin a fresh lookup per compilation, stage a replacement after normal finalization, publish only after Reflaxe output ownership succeeds, and abort on errors. Retain no TypedExpr, Type, Position, CompilationContext, registry instance, or partial output. Provide a cache-off differential define and visible hit/miss/retained counters.
acceptance_criteria: Focused lifecycle tests prove exact hits, reordered registration hits, added/removed/fingerprint-change misses, equal-key conflicting-fingerprint rejection, explicit-name validation, failure rollback, bounded one-generation replacement, and disabled/cold behavior; cold, warm, changed-Haxe, cache-off, reversed-input-order, success/failure/success, split/package/unity, symbol-report, diagnostics, and native behavior remain byte-identical; profiling shows the real full playable reuses the exact symbol table and materially reduces symbol-finalization CPU without a cold regression; docs explain why this cache is safe while HxcIR body reuse remains blocked on a semantic freeze/replay boundary.
notes: Implemented a one-generation finalized-symbol cache keyed by the complete canonical stable-key + naming-fingerprint sequence. Publication occurs only from onOutputComplete; failures/aborts retain the prior success; cache-off, reversed registration, added/removed/fingerprint changes, failure rollback, and bounded replacement have focused coverage. Integrated Caxecraft evidence: 22,923 requests; cold 0 hits/1 miss, warm unchanged 1/0, and a Vitals implementation-only edit 1/0 while exactly one HxcIR function and two generated artifacts changed. Contended diagnostic naming wall times were 1.562s cold, 0.316s warm unchanged, and 0.467s warm edit; these are attribution evidence, not p50/p95. A warm full-playable diagnostic retained the exact 229-artifact tree digest 8b9f8c206d1bcd719d86f011a76b2e0dfe2f5a9ea9c104efd0988392ae016015. Passed profiler/governance contracts, symbol-registry, typed-boundaries, all-sources, bootstrap/server, content-digest, HxcIR, body-lowering, and split/package/unity cold/reverse/locale/warm/cache-off/native parity. Typed-body lowering remains the parent issue's dominant safe-next target; no HxcIR body cache was admitted.
close_reason: Exact warm symbol-table reuse is implemented, documented, profiled, and parity-verified; the broader incremental-backend parent remains open.

title: Reuse exact validated control-flow plans across warm requests
description: The representative changed-Haxe Caxecraft request spends about 2.9 seconds rebuilding and validating structural C control-flow plans for HxcIR functions even though one Vitals edit changes exactly one of 531 functions. Add the smallest cross-request semantic reuse slice: retain only the previous successful request’s target-owned validated control-flow plans and exact canonical HxcIR function text, then reuse a plan only when the current validated function text matches byte-for-byte.
design: Use one schema-versioned, bounded, one-generation @:persistent cache. A candidate contains only a logical function ID, exact canonical HxcIR function text, and a validated CBodyControlFlowPlanningResult; it must contain no TypedExpr, Type, Position, CompilationContext, symbol/name/ABI object, host path, generated C, or output owner. Begin a fresh request in the adapter, permit lookup only after current HxcIR validation, publish replacement evidence only from onOutputComplete, and leave the last successful generation untouched after failure. Cache-off remains authoritative. A hit may skip planning because the cached result was independently validated against byte-identical semantic IR before its successful publication; any schema/key/function mismatch is a visible miss. Reuse HxcIRDumper’s exhaustive canonical traversal rather than adding a second semantic hash walker, and share one full dump across optional reports when enabled so instrumentation does not triple the traversal. Measure key construction and reject the slice if it does not materially reduce representative changed-Haxe CPU/wall time.
acceptance_criteria: Focused lifecycle and real compiler-server tests cover cold misses, unchanged warm hits, one-function implementation edit, public-type edit, success/failure/success, request order, cache-off, server restart, and second worktree; one-generation replacement bounds retained entries and wrong schema/function/text evidence misses rather than being used. Cold/cache-off and warm outputs preserve exact HxcIR, generated C, diagnostics, runtime/ABI/symbol/specialization reports, and native behavior. Profile counters report hits, misses, retained functions, and retained key size in explicitly named Haxe string code units without host paths. The Caxecraft one-module profile reports all unchanged functions reused and only the changed closure rebuilt, and demonstrates a material control-flow-planning reduction without a material cold regression; otherwise remove the optimization and record the rejected result.
notes: Implemented schema-8 one-generation warm reuse for validated per-function C control-flow plans. The exact key is HxcIR schema + logical function ID + complete canonical function text; current HxcIR is still rebuilt/validated, and CAST/C emission uses current names, representations, runtime, and project facts. Publication occurs only after output ownership completes. The cache retains no Haxe macro objects, compiler context, host path, generated C, or partial failed generation. Full and per-function HxcIR report text now share one exhaustive traversal. Focused macro tests cover schema/function/text mismatch, abort, replacement, and disabled behavior; the compiler-server matrix covers cold/warm/edit/public-edit/failure/restart/second-worktree parity. One contended full-playable profile preserved 229 artifact bytes and measured cold 0/531 versus warm 531/0 cache decisions, with owned control-flow planning falling from 2.481s to 6.6ms; retained exact keys total 11,423,746 Haxe string code units. The real Vitals edit recorded 530 hits and one miss for the one changed HxcIR function, with one changed C TU plus the manifest and no changed headers. Cold/warm wall samples were diagnostic only because host load was 6.95-8.17. Gates passed: all-sources, HxcIR, typed-AST server lifecycle, body lowering/native, content digest, GC runtime/native, project layout cold/warm/cache-off/native, hello native, governance, formatter, full-playable cold compile-only, native build, full playable profile, and incremental-edit profile.
close_reason: Shipped the narrow exact validated control-flow plan reuse slice with fail-closed lifecycle, byte/native parity, real 530/1 Caxecraft edit evidence, and a material 2.481s-to-6.6ms owned warm-planning reduction.

title: Stabilize named-record source provenance across Haxe server requests
description: A one-module Caxecraft edit proved that Haxe 5/Reflaxe warm requests can report the same named anonymous-record field at either its typedef declaration or an object-literal use site. The record layout and normal generated C remain byte-identical, but optional HxcIR provenance changes across cold and warm requests. This must be resolved before a semantic backend cache treats those programs as interchangeable.
design: Preserve exact current-source diagnostics and source maps. Do not coarsen a field to the whole typedef span, persist macro Type/Position objects across requests, or declare provenance irrelevant. Find the smallest immutable, content-keyed source-provenance plan or frontend adaptation. Semantic shape and diagnostic provenance may have separate digests only when both stay revision-bound and independently validated.
acceptance_criteria: Focused cold, unchanged-warm, implementation-edit, public-typedef-edit, request-order, server-restart, cache-off, and two-worktree evidence proves stable exact field provenance and correct source-content invalidation. Generated C, diagnostics, and source maps match fresh-process output. No host path, unbounded process state, or stale macro object enters a reusable key. Per-function backend reuse remains blocked until this contract is either implemented or an equally strict validated provenance model is accepted.
notes: Implemented an exact, content-invalidated named-record provenance plan. Direct typedef fields use declaration-relative byte offsets only when every field is inside the current typedef span; warm requests rebuild fresh Haxe Position values from the current source path. The bounded 2048-entry persistent FIFO is keyed by declaration identity, exact source bytes, and the complete define set, and retains no Type, Position, host filename, or application value. Missing or inconsistent evidence fails before HxcIR/output with a typed internal diagnostic. Focused tests now cover cold, unchanged warm, implementation edit, public typedef edit, unsupported warm/cold diagnostic parity, request order, restart, server-off, and a second worktree. npm run test:typed-ast, test:aggregate-lowering, test:all-sources, targeted formatter, governance (182 tests), py_compile, and diff checks passed. The integrated Caxecraft profile showed zero cold-to-warm HxcIR drift and one Vitals edit changed exactly applyAttack, Vitals.c, and the manifest. Standalone sidecar source-map emission remains correctly owned by E8.T08/haxe_c-06n; this task proves the exact source provenance that future mapping consumes rather than claiming that not-yet-shipped product surface.
close_reason: Exact named-record field provenance is stable across cold, warm, edited, restarted, server-off, unsupported, and cross-worktree requests; focused and integrated evidence passes without retaining stale macro objects or host paths.

title: Restore launch-smoke framebuffer capture in variant generations
description: A real `npm run caxecraft:play -- --smoke` build succeeds, publishes its immutable generated state, and exits the native program with status 0, but the expected `caxecraft-smoke.png` is absent from the selected variant executable directory. The runner then fails after compilation. Older non-variant output roots contain historical screenshots, so the current launch-smoke path is not producing or locating fresh framebuffer evidence.
design: Reproduce with the existing launch-smoke pilot and inspect the generated pilot define/name, fixed-tick frame condition, Raylib screenshot return/logs, process working directory, and immutable variant path. Keep screenshot capture in repository-owned Haxe and the runner as an independent verifier. Do not copy an old image, weaken the PNG/visual checks, or special-case macOS. Make the native program report a bounded capture outcome through the existing pilot evidence path so a missing screenshot is attributed at its real producer.
acceptance_criteria: Two consecutive launch-smoke runs on the supported desktop path each create a fresh screenshot in the selected immutable variant's executable directory, validate its structure and expected visual state, emit deterministic semantic evidence, and exit within the bound; stale screenshots are deleted before each run and cannot satisfy the check. Missing/failed capture produces an actionable native/runner diagnostic. The memory-software path and another existing pilot remain passing, and the ordinary interactive build/launch behavior is unchanged.
notes:
Implemented native screenshot-publication evidence instead of relying on host inference. The Clang-derived raylib core now admits FileExists as its 61st fixed-arity function; the semantic facade forwards it without allocation or retention. Each Haxe pilot deletes stale evidence through the runner, captures its review frame, immediately observes the path from native code, and carries that result in telemetry protocol 7. The runner decodes the final native state before opening the review PNG, so a missing publication names the native checkpoint, Raylib log, and directory permissions. A focused negative fixture rejects a structurally valid final report whose capture-observed bit is absent.

Verification: python3 scripts/raylib/core_binding.py render --check; pinned-source Clang verify; 13 core-binding adversarial tests; registered raylib-provisioning snapshot update (3 reviewed artifacts); npm run test:raylib-provisioning; npm run test:caxecraft-pilot; npm run format:haxe:check; npm run test:all-sources; npm run test:capabilities; npm run test:typed-boundaries; npm run test:fixture-policy; npm run snapshots:catalog; npm run caxecraft:play -- --compile-only. Exact-candidate npm run caxecraft:play -- --smoke produced two identical 1280x720 desktop captures and deterministic reports; the next unchanged-generation run hit after 627.2 ms validation and again passed twice. Memory-software launch-smoke and move-jump-edit each passed two identical native runs. Reports record nativeObservedReviewScreenshot=true. The original stale generation was invalidated by the complete request snapshot and was not copied or accepted as evidence.
close_reason: Fresh and unchanged immutable generations now prove native screenshot publication before independent PNG validation; desktop, memory-software, gameplay, and non-pilot paths pass.

title: Load the first Caxecraft level pack at runtime
description: Caxecraft currently validates typed content manifests but may still embed the first playable through generated Haxe adapters, so changing authored terrain, placements, dialogue, objectives, or UI text can invalidate the full Haxe-to-C build. Add one bounded runtime-loaded level/UI pack so ordinary editor and content changes validate, publish, and relaunch or reload without running Haxe, haxe.c, the C compiler, or the linker.
design: Keep CaxeMap, CaxeFlow, and the typed content manifest as the source formats already owned by the game plan. Introduce the smallest cross-target byte/text-loading adapter: Eval may use its standard file support and C may call a typed existing-library or admitted haxe.c filesystem boundary; repository-owned behavior remains Haxe rather than raw C. Parse untrusted bytes immediately into the closed typed models, validate schema/version/IDs/references and complete ownership before replacing the live content generation, and report source-oriented errors. Stage files into an immutable generation and switch it atomically only after complete validation. Do not bundle campaigns, save games, localization infrastructure, audio, networking, arbitrary scripting, or marketplace behavior into this first slice. Generated built-in adapters remain an explicit fallback until the runtime path passes, then remove duplication rather than maintaining two authorities.
acceptance_criteria: Editing one admitted level/UI content item performs no Haxe, haxe.c, native compile, or link work and reaches a validated relaunch/reload in p95 at or below 2 seconds on an unsaturated declared host; the command reports the exact content hit/miss and generation identity. Eval and generated-C/native runs load the same bytes into semantically identical typed content. Valid, malformed, truncated, duplicate, missing-reference, wrong-kind, path-escape, unknown-version, changed-during-read, and corrupt-generation cases fail before replacing the live session. Publication is atomic, stale files cannot survive the generation switch, and an explicit built-in/cold path remains. The editor saves the same canonical format it reloads, and one focused CaxeTest/PilotScript proves the loaded pack reaches gameplay without hardcoded first-playable values.
notes:
2026-07-29 GPT-5.6 Pro review accepted as the execution split: keep the shared Scenario/CAXEMAP model; prove it natively from embedded Bytes before declaring broad stdlib blockers; resolve validated source into a private non-serialized construction plan; build a complete inactive content generation and publish with one atomic owner swap; read package bytes through a typed confined store; load the map first against the compiled registry; remove the per-level generator under RTLEVEL-G1; then load the base pack/UI catalog and remove generated pack authority under RTPACK-G1. Multi-level campaigns are downstream. Exact compiler gaps become focused children only after executable probes fail. The issue children .1-.9 own those gates and the no-build performance proof.
2026-07-30 platform selection correction: the confined package reader is explicitly selected only for Linux/macOS with caxecraft_posix_hosted. Windows now generates the typed UnsupportedCapability branch and no POSIX source instead of allowing a compile-only lane to bless unbuildable openat/fstatat calls. A Windows-native Haxe adapter remains required for cross-platform runtime-pack completion; sys.io.File stays separately owned by haxe_c-fwg because its ordinary-file contract does not replace package-root confinement.

title: Make changed-Haxe haxe.c rebuilds safely incremental
description: A primed Haxe compilation server reduces frontend work, but changing one Haxe module still reruns nearly the complete haxe.c target backend: the current representative playable is about 26 seconds warm because roughly 19.8 seconds of request-local lowering, validation, naming, C projection, hashing, and artifact planning executes again. The sub-second unchanged-build path and depfile-backed native object cache do not help this case. Introduce the smallest fail-closed cross-request reuse boundary that can preserve exact Haxe and C semantics while skipping proven-unchanged target work.
design: Begin with a representative one-module edit and record which typed modules/functions, whole-program representation facts, HxcIR functions, names, runtime/ABI decisions, CAST units, generated files, C objects, and link inputs actually change. Define an immutable schema-versioned backend revision and complete cache key covering Haxe, haxe.c, Reflaxe, HxcIR/CAST schemas, effective HXML/defines/classpaths, typed source/dependency facts, profile/layout, bindings, runtime/ABI, reports, and every whole-program fact that can affect an otherwise unchanged function. Reuse the highest safe artifact rather than retaining mutable TypedExpr or hidden macro-module state; the completed server experiment proved target statics do not persist. Prefer per-function or per-module validated HxcIR/CAST/artifact reuse only after global representation, dispatch, specialization, static-initialization, naming, and runtime-plan digests match. A missing, corrupt, stale, foreign, or expensive-to-validate entry is a visible miss. Preserve an authoritative cold/no-backend-cache path, atomic publication, bounded storage, exact miss explanations, and byte/diagnostic differential tests. Measure key construction as part of the cost; reject a cache granularity whose hashing or validation costs approach recomputation.
acceptance_criteria: A documented representative one-Haxe-module edit reports exactly which backend functions/modules and generated C translation units were reused or rebuilt; cold and warm-cache builds produce byte-identical normal artifacts, diagnostics, runtime/ABI plans, symbol/specialization reports, and native behavior; edits to public types, class hierarchy/dispatch, generics/specializations, static initialization, runtime features, bindings, defines/classpaths, compiler/schema/toolchain, removed/renamed/shadowing modules, and macro dependencies invalidate the complete safe closure; success/failure/success, corruption, request-order, two-worktree, memory-growth, and server-restart tests fail closed; cache-off remains functional. Establish staged budgets on an unsaturated declared host: changed-Haxe source-to-ready p95 at or below 20 seconds initially and at or below 10 seconds as the destination, while cold full-playable p95 remains at or below 40 seconds. If no candidate can meet the initial budget without unsafe or disproportionate complexity, close the implementation experiment as rejected with profiles and a narrower next recommendation rather than shipping partial semantic reuse.
notes:
2026-07-27 measured the first complete changed-Haxe inventory. The opt-in frontend report distinguishes cold-complete from server-partial requests and conservatively carries non-class declarations. A full Vitals.hx constant edit rebuilt 14/135 Caxecraft class declarations, changed exactly 1/531 HxcIR functions, 2/229 normal artifacts (Vitals.c and hxc.manifest.json), 1/84 C translation units, and zero generated headers; ABI, dispatch, initialization, runtime, specialization, stdlib, and symbol reports retained exact bytes. The current verified run completed cold/warm/edit in 31.84s/19.45s/18.93s on a contended host, so these are structural diagnostics rather than an unsaturated budget. Native reuse remains explicitly unmeasured pending haxe_c-5sd.8.3 depfile proof. The same run exposed warm named-record field-position drift despite stable normal C; child haxe_c-5sd.8.4.1 now blocks backend reuse until exact revision-bound provenance is proven.
Child haxe_c-5sd.8.4.1 removed the warm named-record provenance blocker. The integrated Caxecraft profile now has exact cold/warm HxcIR parity; editing Vitals.applyAttack changes one semantic function, one source module, Vitals.c, and hxc.manifest.json. Resume the parent by making this measured function/module/TU delta reusable under the complete request and provenance contracts, with fresh-process byte/diagnostic parity and explicit miss reasons.
Child haxe_c-5sd.8.4.2 shipped the first safe semantic backend reuse slice. Exact validated per-function control-flow plans now reuse 531/531 functions on an unchanged full playable and 530/531 after the fixed Vitals implementation edit. Owned planning fell from 2.481s cold to 6.6ms on the exact warm request; byte/report/layout/native evidence stayed exact. The contended full-playable warm Haxe-to-generated-C sample is now 15.158s, below the parent initial 20s target but not an unsaturated p95. Keep the parent open: typed-body/HxcIR construction remains the dominant warm target owner, and the parent still owes the broader invalidation matrix, memory/soak proof, and unsaturated staged budgets before claiming general incremental backend completion.
Child haxe_c-5sd.8.4.4 closed the body-cache safety inventory. Schema 10 attributed all 509 full-playable FunctionBuilder builds: 490 add no representation/import/adapter semantics, while 19 introduce 50 import functions, 7 import owners, 4 import types, 9 optional layouts, 1 IntMap layout, and 1 StringMap layout. Builds also register 17,446 shared symbol requests. This rejects a bare HxcIRFunction cache but shows a narrow complete replay boundary is plausible. Child haxe_c-5sd.8.4.5 owns symbol-request reconciliation, preplanning or closed contribution replay, exact revision keys, bounded publication, invalidation, and parity evidence.

title: Reuse one typed parameter-use analysis per function
description: The full playable spends about 1.14 seconds preparing HxcIR functions. FunctionPreparer and ConstructorPreparer currently walk the same TypedExpr body separately for every eligible class, interface, or callback parameter to prove call-bounded borrowing, synchronous callback use, and constructor self-field retention. Build one immutable request-local typed parameter-use fact set per function body, then answer each parameter proof from that set without changing the natural Haxe API or any HxcIR lifetime contract.
design: Analyze all declared parameter compiler IDs in one exhaustive TypedExpr traversal. Preserve the exact direct-value rules for parentheses/meta/casts and value-producing if/block/switch forms; distinguish direct-call callee use, escaping storage/return/throw/new uses, nested-function capture, and exact this.field retention. Function and constructor preparation consume only facts tied to that exact body. Retain the old proof functions temporarily in differential tests and remove them only after every admitted and rejected fixture agrees. Do not cache TypedExpr or facts across compilation requests.
acceptance_criteria: Focused fixtures cover multiple class/interface/callback parameters in one body, safe direct receiver/call use, unsafe local/assignment/return/throw/new escape, nested capture, direct synchronous callback-only use, mixed safe/unsafe uses, and constructor this.field retention; new and legacy proofs compare exactly before legacy walks are removed; diagnostics, HxcIR, generated C, runtime/ABI plans, and Eval/native behavior remain byte-identical; profiling shows one body traversal rather than one per eligible parameter and a material full-playable function-preparation CPU/allocation reduction, otherwise the optimization is removed.
close_reason: Measured and removed. Reusing one typed parameter-use analysis per function regressed function preparation by about 50 ms and increased cumulative Eval allocation by about 245 MB on the full Caxecraft profile. Generated artifacts remained byte-identical and the full differential constructor-lowering suite passed; no compiler code was retained.

title: Reuse exact generated-file digests across warm requests
description: The full playable spends about 1.88 seconds of request CPU and 12.9 GB of cumulative Eval allocation constructing SHA-256-addressed generated files. An interactive Haxe-server request usually reproduces most translation units byte-for-byte, but hashes them all again. Retain only the prior complete request's immutable path/kind/text/digest records and reuse a digest after exact full-text equality; cold builds and changed files still execute the reviewed SHA-256 implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Reuse requires exact relative path, artifact kind, and full immutable contents; only one prior complete request is retained and request lifecycle is explicit; failures cannot publish a partial cache generation; cold and server artifacts, manifests, diagnostics, and native behavior remain byte-identical; focused lifecycle/mutation tests cover hit, changed contents, changed kind/path, failed request, and process-cold behavior; profiler counters and an uncontended warm playable differential show material generated-file construction savings without a cold regression.
notes:
2026-07-28 correction after inspecting the pinned Haxe 5 macro runtime and vendored Reflaxe: the rejected experiment proved only that ordinary target macro statics reset. Haxe explicitly preserves fields marked @:persistent across reused Eval macro contexts, and Reflaxe already uses one to detect cached rebuilds plus transient @:build metadata to identify rebuilt classes. Reopen this bounded digest slice as the lowest-risk proof of an explicit persistent, immutable, one-generation target cache. The cache must retain no TypedExpr, Type, Position, CompilationContext, output manager, or partial request state; cold/off parity and failure rollback remain authoritative.
2026-07-28 implementation checkpoint: added a one-generation @:persistent digest cache containing only final path, artifact kind, complete immutable text, UTF-8 length, and SHA-256. CReflaxeCompiler begins a fresh lookup per request and publishes it only from onOutputComplete, after Reflaxe output ownership finishes; output errors abort without replacing prior evidence. Profile schema 7 reports exact hits, misses, retained entries, and retained bytes. test:content-digest covers same-input hits, content/kind/path misses, independent SHA-256 and UTF-8 length, abort rollback, bounded replacement, and disabled behavior. test:project-layout proves cold/warm/cache-off byte parity through the real split/package/unity lifecycle; test:project-emitter, test:bootstrap, test:all-sources, typed-boundary, formatter, and profiler-governance checks pass. A contended full-playable differential produced identical 229-artifact, 5,820,648-byte trees (digest 8b9f8c206d1bcd719d86f011a76b2e0dfe2f5a9ea9c104efd0988392ae016015); generated-file construction fell from 1.778s CPU on 229 misses to 0.022s on 229 hits. Cold/warm walls were 28.689s/16.028s in the one-sample diagnostic. A later five-run attempt also preserved parity but became contended when unrelated Chrome/Firefox, Genes, and Go debug-symbol jobs started; therefore the required representative five-sample warm differential remains open and no new wall-time baseline is claimed.

title: Gate constructor-only assignment recognition once
description: Every typed assignment currently probes eleven recognizers that can only succeed inside a Haxe constructor. Ordinary functions therefore repeat eleven role checks before normal assignment lowering. Route assignment statements through one constructor-role gate, keep the specialized first-field-initialization rules unchanged, and send non-constructor assignments directly to ordinary value lowering.
acceptance_criteria: All constructor-only initializer recognizers are reachable only through one explicit constructor-role gate; ordinary assignment behavior and source-positioned failures are unchanged; focused class/body tests and full generated/runtime evidence remain identical; profiling or counters demonstrate that ordinary assignments no longer execute constructor-only probes, and the change does not regress uncontended full-playable typed-body time.
close_reason: Measured and removed: the single constructor-role gate saved only 4,678,848 bytes of full-playable allocation and did not produce trustworthy material CPU improvement. The existing explicit recognizers remain; optimization effort returns to measured dominant owners.

title: Reuse exact nominal value plans before generic classification
description: The current full-playable profile attributes about 1.29 seconds and substantial Eval allocation to repeated value-type classification inside HxcIR typed-body lowering. An existing request-local exact nominal cache already proves repeated non-generic class identities, but classification reached it only after String, Map, alias, function, and collection recognition. Move this proven fast path ahead of those unrelated families while preserving dedicated import, native-reference, primitive, Array, and Bytes handling and exact unsupported diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria: The earlier exact nominal cache is consulted before unrelated generic recognizers only for exact non-extern, non-generic nominal types; Array and Bytes remain owned by their dedicated carriers; unsupported classifications still fail at their exact source position; HxcIR dumps, generated C, reports, runtime/ABI plans, and focused/native behavior remain byte-identical; an uncontended full-playable differential proves a material classification allocation/time improvement or the optimization is removed.
notes: A broader exact Type-object cache was rejected during implementation: ObjectMap cannot key haxe.macro.Type, and EnumValueMap caused the Eval target to fail while loading haxe.macro.Ref. The retained change reuses the already-proven nominal identity cache instead of introducing a structurally keyed Type cache.
close_reason: Measured and removed under its acceptance rule. The exact nominal fast path reduced the representative full-playable request CPU by only about 0.12 seconds and cumulative Eval allocation by about 185 MB out of roughly 71 GB; the wall sample was additionally host-contended. That is not a material improvement to the approximately 30-second source compile, so the compiler code remains unchanged and work moves to the higher-leverage architectural feedback-loop owners.

title: Add deterministic graphical pilot for the native Caxecraft editor
description:
## Why

The editor shell now renders real raygui controls, but the existing launch smoke captures only the title screen. A regression could blank or skip the editor while all domain and ABI tests still pass.

## What

Add one bounded pilot that starts on the editor screen, captures the real presented framebuffer, records editor screen identity in telemetry, validates editor-specific visual regions, repeats deterministically, and exits. Keep the pilot focused on engine/UI integration rather than exhaustively replaying authored scenarios.

## How

Extend the closed PilotScript and runner registries, make editor/title/gameplay presentation states explicit in telemetry, update the protocol version if its meaning changes, and add a dedicated screenshot validator. Compile and run the real generated Haxe -> C application against pinned raygui/raylib.
acceptance_criteria: The pilot starts directly in the native editor without synthetic OS input; captures a nonblank editor framebuffer containing the window, canvas/sidebar, localized tool list, and status area; telemetry distinguishes editor from title and gameplay without weakening existing terrain assertions; two runs produce identical semantic reports and screenshots; the pilot exits within the existing bound; focused tests and the complete Caxecraft generated/native evidence pass.
close_reason: Verified generated-C native editor pilot, protocol-v6 screen identity, structural framebuffer evidence, deterministic two-run report/image parity, bounded exit, and full snapshot/native ownership.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: Implemented and verified the deterministic native editor-shell pilot. It enters through the real typed title-to-editor transition, renders the generated Haxe -> C raygui screen, captures toolbar/canvas/sidebar/tool-list/status evidence, records a distinct protocol-v6 editor bit, repeats twice with identical semantic report and screenshot, and exits within the 15s bound. Focused pilot, app-screen Eval/native/sanitizer, all-sources, typed-boundary, formatter, strict graphical macOS, and complete split/package/unity snapshot/native owner evidence passed. The reviewed framebuffer is 1280x720 and contains the actual localized SELECT/PAINT/ERASE list. Also extended the complete-key no-change path to graphical pilots: the repeated editor QA skips Haxe after about 0.8s validation and completes both native runs in about 9-10s; a changed runner correctly caused a visible miss and rebuild.

title: Route Caxecraft profiler schema changes to affected evidence
description: A staged compiler profiling change touched examples/caxecraft/profile_compiler.py and its focused parser test test/governance/test_caxecraft_timing.py. The profile source is a known affected path, but its exact governance test is classified as unknown cross-cutting, so the pre-commit hook escalates to all five cold toolchain lanes. Under current host load that selected one worker and began repeating unrelated semantic/native evidence after exact all-source, profiler, body, and flagship parity checks had already passed.
acceptance_criteria: The exact Caxecraft timing/profile parser test joins the known affected route; a focused selector regression proves the combined producer/consumer path selects the affected base owners without Caxecraft domain or exhaustive fallback; genuinely unknown governance/fixture/runner changes remain exhaustive; governance policy passes; docs explain that complete cold coverage remains CI/explicit-command authority.
notes: Reproduced on the staged profiler producer plus test/governance/test_caxecraft_timing.py: the hook selected parallel-exhaustive and queued five lanes with one worker. The run was interrupted before accepting evidence. The exact parser test is now an explicit known-affected input; the combined staged path set selects affected base owners plus body/span for the actual central lowerer. test_fixture_policy.py and unrecognized governance/CI inputs retain exhaustive fallback. Focused test_toolchain_shard suite passed 41 tests, and direct selector probes returned the expected affected route/owners.
close_reason: The exact profiler consumer and parser test now share the affected route with executable selector coverage; unknown cross-cutting inputs remain fail-closed exhaustive.

title: Attribute remaining typed-body specialization and coercion comparisons
description: After exact nominal reuse, full Caxecraft typed-body lowering still costs about 4.4 seconds CPU and 14.3GB cumulative allocation. Recorded type-family classification accounts for about 1.25 seconds and source-span conversion about 0.41 seconds, leaving roughly 2.7 seconds unattributed. The same profile records 28,907 specialization applications and 25,150 coercion requests, but currently reports only their counts.
acceptance_criteria: Opt-in function-scoped profiles report specialization-application CPU and coercion type-comparison CPU with closed non-negative fields; normal compilation performs no added clock reads; profiler malformed/unknown-field tests remain fail closed; one digest-verified full playable identifies whether either operation materially owns the remaining phase; retain only profiler code needed to select and prove a subsequent optimization, and document/reject speculative shortcuts whose owned cost is immaterial.
notes: Structured profile /tmp/haxe-c-playable-profile-typed-ops.json retained exact 227-artifact digest 64c1a39e1e8814fc8f0146bbef0acdccfd9a266ba71b2dde5cb91da296515bb1. Across 28,907 requests, specialization application used 11.987ms CPU; across 25,150 coercions, HxcIR type-key construction/comparison used 23.223ms. Type-family classification used 1.291s and source spans 402.726ms inside 4.382s typed-body CPU. These request counts are not hotspots. The opt-in fields remain to prevent future misattribution and perform no clock reads in normal compilation. Passed profiler parser tests, all-sources, Haxe formatting, typed-boundary policy, and full playable parity.
close_reason: Remaining typed-body work is now attributed enough to reject specialization/coercion-count shortcuts; profiling is fail-closed, normal builds have no added timing work, and flagship artifacts remain exact.

title: Avoid serializing identical coercion value plans
description: The digest-verified full-playable profile records 25,150 typed-body coercion requests inside 4.419 seconds of typed-body CPU and 14.293GB of cumulative typed-body allocation. Every request currently serializes the source and target HxcIR type trees through typeKey before deciding whether the carrier already matches, even when lowering propagated the exact same immutable CBodyValueType object as its contextual target.
acceptance_criteria: Add an allocation-free identity fast path only when source and target are the exact same immutable CBodyValueType object; retain the existing structural type-key comparison and all conversion/diagnostic behavior for different objects; opt-in profiling proves how many requests use the fast path; focused coercion/body/native tests and full Caxecraft artifact parity pass; the owned typed-body CPU/allocation decreases without weakening HxcIR validation.
notes: Rejected after measurement and removed from the working tree. The full playable produced exact artifact digest 64c1a39e1e8814fc8f0146bbef0acdccfd9a266ba71b2dde5cb91da296515bb1 and recorded 8,727 identity hits among 25,150 coercions, but typed-body cumulative allocation moved only from 14.293GB to 14.282GB (~11MB). The contended run's CPU/wall were slower and cannot attribute a regression, but the allocation reduction is too small to justify the compiler branch and profile-schema surface. Future coercion work should attribute the remaining structural comparisons or replace string serialization with a central allocation-free HxcIR type equality only if a focused profile proves that operation material.
close_reason: Measured experiment was safely removed because its attributable allocation win was immaterial; exact parity and the rejected-path evidence are retained.

title: Reuse exact non-generic nominal body value plans
description: The full Caxecraft profile records 5,470 nominal type classifications and about 0.94 seconds of nominal-classification CPU inside typed-body lowering. Exact non-generic, non-extern class and interface types already resolve to one request-local nominal layout, but each use still traverses import, native-reference, primitive, string, map, alias, function, collection, and primitive-mapper checks first.
acceptance_criteria: Add a fail-closed fast path only for exact TInst class/interface types whose declarations are non-extern and have no type arguments; imported, generic, enum, alias, optional, and unsupported types keep their existing classifier and diagnostics; cache/reuse counters prove repeated hits; focused class/interface/body tests and the full Caxecraft playable retain exact HxcIR, generated artifacts, runtime plan, diagnostics, and native behavior; structured profiles show reduced nominal classification work and request cost.
notes:
Baseline /tmp/haxe-c-playable-profile-utf8-all.json: 5,470 nominal classifications, 935.325ms attributed nominal CPU, 21,722 body-value-type requests, 4.498s typed-body CPU, 14.981GB typed-body cumulative allocation, 18.126s target CPU, and exact 227-artifact digest 64c1a39e1e8814fc8f0146bbef0acdccfd9a266ba71b2dde5cb91da296515bb1. Host was contended; work counts and exact artifact identity are the primary baseline.
Implemented a request-local exact nominal value-plan cache after imported/native/primitive/string/Map classification. It admits only non-extern, non-generic TInst classes/interfaces and leaves Array, extern/import, generic, enum, typedef, abstract, Null, and unsupported paths on the full classifier. Full playable profile /tmp/haxe-c-playable-profile-nominal-cache.json recorded 3,463 hits and 32 first plans, reduced nominal-classification CPU from 935.325ms to 747.232ms (~20%), and reduced complete-request cumulative Eval allocation from 68.339GB to 67.595GB (~745MB). Both contended samples produced the exact same 227-artifact digest 64c1a39e1e8814fc8f0146bbef0acdccfd9a266ba71b2dde5cb91da296515bb1. Broad CPU/wall were noisy and are explicitly not claimed as an end-to-end speedup. Passed test:all-sources, test:class-layout, test:virtual-dispatch, test:body-lowering, format:haxe:check, test:typed-boundaries, and full playable byte parity.
close_reason: Exact nominal reuse is implemented, measured at its owning phase, byte-identical on the flagship, documented, and covered by focused semantic/quality gates.

title: Centralize allocation-free UTF-8 ordering during Eval compilation
description: Many compiler phases sort deterministic string identities by repeatedly allocating UTF-8 byte buffers inside comparison callbacks. Haxe Eval amplifies this otherwise avoidable target-owned cost because a sort calls its comparator many times. Centralize the order contract and use Eval native string comparison where its Unicode scalar ordering is equivalent to UTF-8 byte order, while keeping a portable byte-wise fallback for other hosts.
acceptance_criteria: All compiler-owned deterministic UTF-8 string comparisons use one documented helper except deliberately byte-keyed registries; representative compiler, project, runtime, and naming suites pass; a full playable warm profile preserves the exact artifact digest and reports lower cumulative allocation and/or CPU than the recorded baseline; docs record the bounded host-specific optimization and measurement caveats.
notes:
Baseline full-playable warm profile: 20.186 s wall, 19.660 s CPU, 73.728 GB cumulative allocation under a contended host. First centralized high-value comparator group: 18.717 s wall, 18.006 s CPU, 69.587 GB cumulative allocation on a representative host; all 227 generated artifacts retained digest 64c1a39e1e8814fc8f0146bbef0acdccfd9a266ba71b2dde5cb91da296515bb1. Single samples are structural evidence, not a stable benchmark claim; final verification will rerun after the remaining comparator owners migrate.
Completed migration: all 41 compiler string comparator wrappers now delegate to the single CUtf8Order module function; CSymbolRegistry retains one separate cached-Bytes comparator because its inputs are already encoded. A focused Unicode differential covers 1/2/3/4-byte UTF-8 values. Final contended full-playable warm profile: 18.759 s wall, 18.126 s target CPU, 68.339 GB cumulative allocation, 1.437 GB maximum observed RSS, 227 artifacts, exact digest 64c1a39e1e8814fc8f0146bbef0acdccfd9a266ba71b2dde5cb91da296515bb1. Versus the recorded baseline, cumulative temporary allocation fell by about 5.39 GB; timing is diagnostic only because host conditions differ.
close_reason: Closed

title: Attribute and reuse typed-body source positions
description: The latest byte-verified full Caxecraft profile still spends about 4.7 seconds of CPU and allocates 15.5 GB while lowering typed Haxe bodies. Each generated HxcIR instruction asks Haxe to convert a compiler Position into the same stable source range, and one source expression can produce several instructions. Measure those requests per function, then reuse only exact same-position conversions inside that function when the evidence shows repetition. This is request-local diagnostic/source-map work, not a cross-request semantic cache.
design: Route FunctionBuilder source-position conversion through one typed resolver that normalizes the logical source path once, records bounded opt-in request/miss/CPU counters, and keys reuse by the exact compiler file/min/max position facts. Preserve the current PositionTools coordinates and HxcSourceSpan bytes. Do not infer lines from byte offsets, merge different positions, suppress source spans, weaken diagnostics, cache TypedExpr across requests, or special-case Caxecraft.

title: Replace allocation-heavy HxcIR dominator sets
description: The structured full-playable profile attributes about 4.76 seconds of exclusive wall time to null-check coalescing, and HxcIR validation recomputes the same control-flow family. Preserve instruction failure edges, unreachable-block behavior, UTF-8 answer order, and fail-closed malformed-graph handling. title: Split Caxecraft compiler, maintainability, and product evidence owners
description: A narrow generated-C maintainability drift currently asks the broad full-playable snapshot owner to regenerate compiler reports, three project layouts, and integrated product evidence. The canonical Caxecraft shard had already proved gameplay/native/determinism before finding one expected maintainability drift, yet the updater repeated the full playable and timed out under contention. Separate independent proof responsibilities while retaining a cold catalog that prevents stale or self-generated expected evidence.
design: Define three explicit owners: compiler semantic/project evidence for HxcIR, runtime/ABI, symbols, and representative structural C; generated-C maintainability evidence for compact split/package/unity metrics and curated readable files; integrated Caxecraft product evidence for domain/native/gameplay/PilotScript/CaxeFlow/editor/determinism plus a compact generation identity. A downstream owner may consume a canonical generation only after validating its exact producer key and must independently compute its assertions. Keep a cold/nightly/release catalog that regenerates from source, checks one owner per expected path, and rejects stale artifacts. Move exhaustive generated-C audits out of normal play once the compact manifest proves launch integrity.
acceptance_criteria: Every Caxecraft expected artifact and metric has exactly one declared owner; changing one maintainability expectation reruns only its independent producer/validator when all non-snapshot inputs match; compiler semantic failures and product behavior failures remain separately attributed; normal play does not reread and audit the entire generated C corpus; reused generation evidence validates complete source/toolchain/configuration/generator identity and never compares unchecked output with itself; a cold snapshot catalog rebuild catches stale/missing/foreign files; canonical serial release output matches the isolated owner aggregate.
notes:
2026-07-29 Raygui text-entry snapshot evidence: the registered Caxecraft snapshot owner took about nine minutes after the actual compiler child had already passed. Once Haxe generation finished, snapshots.py itself remained near one CPU core for more than five minutes; a process sample placed the hot Python thread in large Unicode joins while constructing or comparing the integrated snapshot diff. The resulting console diff was about 549k tokens and was dominated by deterministic runtime-plan reason-ID shifts: rootReasonCount changed from 4725 to 4764 (+39), while the selected runtime feature set, artifact count (26), and direct decisions stayed unchanged. This is evidence for this issue’s existing owner split: ordinary product work should consume a compact, content-addressed generated-project proof, while exhaustive runtime-plan and maintainability diffs remain a separate cold owner. The Raygui task did not weaken or bypass the snapshot gate; the registered update and post-update playable verification both passed.
