title: Reuse native objects and links with compiler depfiles
description: The split generated project has stable C translation-unit boundaries, but caxecraft:play currently removes the object directory and serially recompiles every generated source. Add a fail-closed native cache so one changed Haxe module recompiles only the C files whose source or header dependency closure changed, then relinks from a validated ordered object set.
design: Compile with the selected compiler's dependency-file mode and store immutable per-object entries keyed by object schema, direct C bytes, compiler identity, target/sysroot, ordered flags/environment whitelist, ordered include roots plus shadowing inventory, parsed dependency closure and content hashes, generated public/private headers, runtime sources/headers, layout/profile, and sanitizer/debug mode. Missing, malformed, stale, or inconsistent depfiles are misses. Write object and metadata atomically. Link keys retain ordered object digests, linker/toolchain, flags, Raylib/Raygui/library/framework/runtime identities. Use a bounded resource-aware pool with per-unit logs collated in canonical source order. Begin per-worktree; share immutable objects only after cross-worktree path-reproducibility evidence.
acceptance_criteria: No-change native work hits object and link records; direct source, private header, public header, new include shadow, compiler, sysroot, flags, runtime feature/source, Raylib/Raygui header/library, missing/malformed depfile, and corrupt object changes invalidate exactly the safe set; link-only changes preserve objects and relink; failed compile/link never publishes; GCC and Clang strict/debug/release/sanitizer lanes match clean builds; one representative Haxe module edit reports changed generated files and translation units and meets an initial p95 <= 20s edit-to-launch target on the declared host; --native-cache=off remains functional.
notes: Implemented the core depfile-native vertical. Every source uses -MD, ordered include-path inventory, logical generated dependency rebinding, exact external/system dependency hashes, compiler/target/flags/environment identity, immutable content-addressed object entries, hint-only atomic indexes, corrupt-entry quarantine, bounded parallel compilation, and a separately keyed link cache. Focused 8-test suite covers exact hits, source/private/public/shadow invalidation, flags versus link-only changes, malformed dependency records, object/link corruption, failed compile non-publication, and cache-off. Real split build: 82 misses + link miss 6.28s; repeated 82 hits + link hit 2.62s; earlier uncached authority 6.94s with byte-identical executable. Remaining issue gates: GCC/Clang/sanitizer hosted coverage and representative changed-Haxe end-to-launch evidence; the ~26s haxe.c backend means the <=20s whole edit target also depends on haxe_c-5sd.5.2 rather than native work alone.

title: Publish immutable generated projects and own the Haxe server
description: After the no-change state contract is trustworthy, changed Haxe builds need a crash-safe publication boundary and a safely owned Haxe compilation server. Haxe can reuse eligible parse/type/module/macro state, but every haxe.c request must still receive fresh request-local semantic state and run its required target phases.
design: Build into a unique same-filesystem transaction, validate the complete Reflaxe ownership inventory, then atomically rename it to an immutable generation and atomically replace a state-record pointer; do not use a current symlink. A per-worktree/per-variant lock and monotonic requested/publication revision prevent older builds from replacing newer ones. Add auto/off/explicit-attach server modes. Auto owns one loopback server keyed by canonical worktree, Haxe binary/stdlib/packages, haxe.c/Reflaxe bytes, target/HXML compatibility, and cookie schema; it records exact PID plus process-start identity, relocates on occupied ports, never kills unknown processes, and retries once with a fresh process after a visible server failure. It never persists TypedExpr, CompilationContext, HxcIR, or CAST.
acceptance_criteria: Crash injection before and after each generation/state rename selects only the old or new complete generation; incomplete transactions are ignored/quarantined; two watchers cannot publish out of revision order; worktrees and variants have isolated mutable state; cold/server sequences A-A, A-B-A, success-failure-success, runtime profile changes, and split/unity/package changes produce cold-equivalent bytes and diagnostics; target/Reflaxe/Haxe identity changes reject/restart a stale server; stale cookie, occupied port, Ctrl-C, timeout, RSS/file-descriptor soak, and exact process cleanup pass; --server=off remains authoritative.
notes:
Implemented and verified the immutable generated-project half: play builds into same-filesystem transactions, validates the real Reflaxe project, content-addresses complete generations, atomically publishes a JSON pointer, and serializes each variant with an OS lock. Focused tests cover pre/post-pointer crash states, abandoned transactions, monotonic sequences, duplicate generations, and corruption. A real split Caxecraft compile passed through the new path in 34.12s wall on the current host. Owned auto/off/attach Haxe-server lifecycle remains before this issue can close.
Implemented the owned server half. Caxecraft now has auto/off/attach modes and an exact stop operation. Auto state is scoped by canonical worktree/output state root and infrastructure bytes; the cookie verifies PID, OS start identity, live executable identity, endpoint, and compatibility before reuse or termination. Startup is double-forked on POSIX so one-shot play can retain the server without child leaks; interrupted startup kills only the exact observed process. Automatic transport failure retries once; compiler diagnostics do not. Focused tests cover same-process reuse, infrastructure restart/reap, external attachment, stale foreign identity, separate worktree roots, and exact cleanup. Existing typed-C/bootstrap server tests own negative-diagnostic isolation; the Caxecraft warm matrix was reordered to A-B-C-A without adding requests and retains cold byte parity. Real split samples selected generation e754f133...: first server 35.28s, repeated warm 26.05s, cold 34.21s (single observations, not an unsaturated benchmark).

title: Cache generated-output prefix validation within one transaction
description: ReflaxeOutputWriter correctly validates the complete prior and planned ownership sets before writing, including traversal, symlink, case, and canonical-root safety. Its current per-file prefix checks can repeat exists, fullPath, directory, and directory-inventory work for many artifacts sharing the same parents. Optimize that repeated filesystem work without weakening the safety boundary or reusing mutable filesystem facts across requests.
design: Add a request-local canonical-prefix cache or trie scoped to one held output transaction. Cache normalized prefix identity, existence/type, canonical path, directory inventory/case result, and any rejection. Validate each unique prefix once, preserve complete-set validation before the first save, and abort if the filesystem changes unexpectedly. Do not cache across output transactions or replace canonical checks with lexical normalization. Add filesystem-operation counters before changing behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Empty, identical populated, stale-file, missing-parent, case-collision, dangling-link, descendant-symlink, traversal, unowned-destination, and concurrent-mutation fixtures preserve their exact accept/reject behavior; each shared prefix is probed at most once per transaction under instrumented tests; profiler/syscall evidence shows the before/after operation and wall-time change; normal generated bytes, Reflaxe ownership metadata, changed-file avoidance, and stale deletion remain exact; a cache mismatch or unexpected filesystem mutation aborts before publication.

title: Reuse revision-bound semantic facts within one compile
description: Several compiler stages rebuild maps and rewalk the same settled HxcIR program for managed roots, value/local uses, control flow, direct calls, headers, runtime needs, layout, reports, and CAST projection. Keep HxcIR as the semantic authority, but make these derived facts immutable and reusable inside one CompilationContext before attempting any cross-request backend cache.
design: Introduce an immutable HxcIRProgramRevision with canonical module/type/instance/function/global indices and deterministic count/digest summaries. Add only profiler-justified revision-bound fact families, starting with the highest measured repeated work. Every fact names its producer phase and source revision; consumers reject a mismatched revision. Preserve independent semantic validation: the validator checks index/fact consistency against the HxcIR program rather than trusting producer output. Centralize exhaustive child enumeration before moving generic analyses so a new child-bearing HxcIR constructor cannot silently become a leaf. Runtime/ABI selection should consume finalized semantic facts before CAST/project construction when evidence confirms the boundary.
acceptance_criteria: A schema coverage test fails when a child-bearing HxcIR constructor lacks declared traversal; canonical indices and each admitted fact carry and validate one exact program revision; stale-revision consumption fails at the first consumer; old and new derivations compare equal in differential fixtures before legacy scans are removed; HxcIR dumps, diagnostics, generated C, runtime/ABI plans, full reports, and deterministic builds remain byte-identical unless an intentional reviewed format change is declared; profiler counters show fewer visits/allocations and an uncontended full-playable improvement.
notes: 2026-07-27 implementation conclusion: exact immutable value-plan reuse cut typed-body CPU from about 11.34s to 4.44s, and dense control-flow facts cut control-flow planning from about 6.38s to 2.46s while preserving independently validated HxcIR and byte-identical flagship artifacts. Subsequent nominal, assignment-gate, digest-cache, and parameter-use candidates were measured and removed because their gains were immaterial or negative. A five-run cold diagnostic is stable at 29.40s median and 29.82s p95 under moderate host contention. This issue remains mechanically open only because its profiler dependency still owns the strictly uncontended five-sample baseline; no further speculative request-local micro-optimization is justified by the current profile.

title: Make the Caxecraft edit-play loop incremental
description: The ordinary caxecraft:play command currently repeats the full Haxe-to-C pipeline and serially recompiles every generated C translation unit before each launch. A measured fresh compile-only journey took 97.48 seconds before native compilation, which makes normal game iteration impractical. Preserve the authoritative cold path, but add a fail-closed developer path that fingerprints all semantic, compiler, ABI, generated-project, content, binding, and native-toolchain inputs; reuses a validated executable when nothing changed; restages data without compiler work for content-only changes; reuses a valid generated project when Haxe output is unchanged; and recompiles only changed C objects before relinking. Normal play output must report per-phase time and whether each phase ran or was reused. Add a simple watch/dev command only after invalidation is proven.
acceptance_criteria: No-change play validates and launches the existing binary without Haxe or C compilation; content-only changes avoid Haxe/native rebuild when their runtime packaging contract permits; generated-project reuse rejects stale or incomplete ownership; native object keys cover source bytes, generated/public headers, compiler identity and flags, platform, Raylib/Raygui identities, runtime sources, and ABI inputs; changed translation units compile in bounded parallel workers with deterministic logs; cold and explicit-clean paths remain; normal output reports phase timings and reuse decisions; tests cover hits plus representative invalidation misses; an uncontended before/after establishes a documented edit-loop budget.
notes: 2026-07-27 Oracle review accepted the layered edit-loop direction. The first user-visible milestone is a complete-key no-change validation and launch, not a vague incremental compiler. Later layers publish immutable generated generations, own a compatible per-worktree Haxe server, reuse depfile-proven native objects and ordered links, and eventually stage truly runtime-loaded content. Each layer has a schema-versioned key, output inventory/digests, exact miss reason, atomic publication, corruption recovery, and an explicit cold/off path. Children haxe_c-5sd.8.1-.3 own those stages.

title: Admit receiver-tied read-only fixed-array borrow returns
description: GameSession must lend its inline world storage to presentation for one bounded read-only scope without @:allow, copying 16 KiB per frame, or exposing mutable storage. Extend the direct class-call lifetime model so an exact non-generic instance method may return ConstSpan<T> only when the returned borrow is proven to originate from a fixed CArray field owned by that receiver. At each direct call, bind the result lifetime to the already-live receiver and reject every store, field/aggregate payload, unknown call, callback, owner-destroying reassignment, second return, or other escape. This is a scoped returned borrow, not the retained-span-field model owned by haxe_c-53k.7.
design: Infer the return provenance from typed/HxcIR facts rather than trusting application text or raw C. Give the semantic function and call result one closed receiver-borrow contract, validate the callee origin and caller lifetime/uses before CAST, and emit the existing const pointer plus length representation. Keep mutable Span returns rejected in this slice. Preserve ordinary direct-call evaluation order, source anchors, and runtime-free output. Caxecraft consumes the capability through a nominal read-only world view; mutation remains behind GameSession commands.
acceptance_criteria: A Caxecraft-independent positive fixture returns a ConstSpan borrowed from an exact receiver-owned CArray field, uses it through direct renderer/helper calls while the receiver lives, and emits readable runtime-free C under strict GCC/Clang plus sanitizers. Negative fixtures reject mutable returns, local-owner dangling returns, storing the result in fields/records/enums/arrays, returning it again from an uncontracted function, passing it to unknown/callback/exported/native calls, and using it after receiver invalidation. HxcIR validation owns the provenance and escape proof. GameSession can publish its read-only world without @:allow or a copy, and focused span/class/Caxecraft tests and docs pass.
notes: Implemented and verified in the current worktree: HxcIR schema 20 admits only an exact final non-generic instance method returning ConstSpan from its receiver-owned immediate CArray field. The result lowers to const pointer plus hidden size_t length, is runtime-free, and may be consumed only as one direct call argument while the receiver lives. Source-positioned HXC1001 negatives cover mutable/static/local-owner/retained returns; the established span negatives cover stored fields/globals, indirect callbacks, exported/native calls, and other escape shapes. The full span native/sanitizer suite passed, Caxecraft GameSession now publishes worldView without a copy or friendship, and playable/session/domain evidence passed.
close_reason: Receiver-owned read-only fixed-array return is implemented, validated before CAST, documented, and exercised by the standalone span suite plus Caxecraft.

title: Schedule isolation-approved toolchain commands independently
description: Large shards still run their internal package commands serially, so a cold high-fanout gate is bounded by the sum of long suites and a non-snapshot failure repeats the whole shard. Audit command-level output roots, compiler servers, ports, caches, and mutation order, then schedule only independently safe units through the existing resource-aware pool.
design: Introduce explicit command groups rather than assuming every package script is independent. Keep warm-server requests, shared-output stale-deletion tests, fixed ports, and ordered mutations inside one serial unit. Give every unit isolated temp/output roots and deterministic canonical log collation. Preserve cold CI, exact canonical coverage, bounded timeouts, and fail-closed evidence; compare representative unsaturated timings before increasing default concurrency.
acceptance_criteria: Every canonical command belongs to exactly one reviewed isolation group; the pool never exceeds the selected worker count; serial-sensitive tests stay grouped; cold output and failure attribution match the canonical toolchain; timing reports show unit-level progress; an unsaturated before/after demonstrates whether scheduling lowers wall time; governance and hosted cold CI pass.
notes:
2026-07-26 evidence from the schema-20 migration: one registered updater invocation for 11 independent snapshot owners was still running after 18m50s and had completed only body, function, aggregate, and class-layout owners; constructor-lowering was active. The host was saturated by separate haxe.ocaml workers, so this is contention evidence, not an unsaturated benchmark. It does demonstrate that the updater exposes only a serial owner loop even when output roots are isolated. Preserve the full commands, but treat independently proven owner invocations as candidate pool units and collate logs in catalog order.\n\nA later cold pre-commit run of the five exact toolchain lanes took about 50 minutes under the same contended host before reporting all shards. The two-worker pool remained active and isolated, but the largest serial commands dominated: constructor-lowering took 1,379,456 ms, project-emitter 582,831 ms, aggregate-lowering 349,109 ms, array-runtime 299,529 ms, and function-lowering 292,696 ms. The run correctly retained successful lowering-objects, lowering-semantics, and native evidence despite narrow hello-schema and Caxecraft-aquatics integration failures. This is valuable failure-attribution/cache evidence, not an unsaturated speed claim; command-level isolation groups and progress reporting remain the next optimization.
2026-07-27 Oracle review confirmed that scheduling and evidence ownership are separate optimizations. Child haxe_c-5sd.7.1 splits Caxecraft compiler semantics, generated-C maintainability, and integrated product proof before broader command parallelism. Reuse is allowed only with exact producer identity and independent assertions; cold catalog/release proof remains.
2026-07-27 source-position checkpoint evidence: the exhaustive pre-commit matrix passed and cached all four compiler/Caxecraft shards, but the auxiliary native lane failed only because runtime_smoke.py imposes a fixed 30-second child timeout. The exact Clang GC owner then passed all collector, sanitizer, C++17, cycle, root, pin, and pressure checks in 32.41 seconds while one-minute host load was 18.95 and several sibling-repository Haxe builds were active. Treat this as saturated contention evidence, not a semantic regression. The resource-aware lane design must account for per-command timeout budgets or defer launch until safe headroom exists; it must not merely raise every timeout, weaken native proof, or replay the four already-passing shards.
2026-07-27 invalidation-inventory commit-hook evidence: the bounded two-worker exhaustive run took about 41 minutes for its long pole even though contracts failed immediately on a stale vendored-Reflaxe digest and the other lanes continued. lowering-objects passed 8/8 in 2,450,034 ms. Its serial package costs were body 78,356 ms, function 234,098 ms, aggregate 228,071 ms, class 99,954 ms, constructor 1,164,998 ms, virtual dispatch 84,567 ms, enum 329,590 ms, and generic specialization 230,398 ms. Once other shards freed workers, they could not help this opaque serial bundle. Host contention included a sibling haxe.rust compile, so this is not an unsaturated budget; it is exact scheduling evidence for command-level isolation groups. The runner correctly preserved all passing shard/native evidence despite the 283 ms contracts failure.
2026-07-29 actor-composition CI-catalog evidence: commit fac2b25 changed the canonical command set from 63 to 64, so the pre-commit hook correctly invalidated all five exact lanes and ran test:toolchain:parallel --resume --with-native with two workers. All lanes passed, but the run started at 11:23 local time and completed about 49 minutes later, exceeding the documented 45-minute hard ceiling. The contracts shard was the long pole at 2,400,271 ms (40.0 minutes); project-emitter alone took 460,430 ms, array-runtime 279,199 ms, bytes-runtime 207,135 ms, c-import 159,717 ms, and string-map 151,684 ms. The first shard did not report completion until roughly 39 minutes, while active processes continuously rotated through fixtures, so this was serial command aggregation rather than a hang. Host load was moderate, roughly 5.6-8.0 with two haxe.c Haxe 5 workers plus some sibling-repository activity, so retain it as representative contention evidence rather than an unsaturated benchmark. The task-specific actor lane itself passed in about 12 seconds; command-level isolation/progress remains the necessary fix.
Correction to the immediately preceding timing shorthand: the Git commit records 11:23:14 and the post-hook clock was 12:16:51 local, so end-to-end commit latency was approximately 53 minutes 37 seconds, not 49 minutes. The 2,400,271 ms contracts-shard duration remains the exact runner measurement.

title: Reuse exact shard evidence across narrow snapshot corrections
description: A registered snapshot update changed one expected artifact after an otherwise green exhaustive run. The old resume key invalidated every large shard and forced all 61 commands to rerun. Preserve the common staged/worktree identity separately from catalog-owned expected bytes so unrelated shards remain reusable, and allow the affected shard to rerun only the exact focused snapshot owner when every non-snapshot input is unchanged.

Keep expected path, mode, inventory, catalog, compiler, fixture, toolchain, environment, hook, and runner state in fail-closed shared inputs; scope only conventional expected-file content bytes to their owner. A prior receipt must validate against its own key and lifetime before a focused rerun is admitted. Re-seal the full shard only after the changed owners pass and inputs remain stable. Keep native uncached and schedule broader command parallelism separately after isolation review.
acceptance_criteria: A cold run writes exact shard evidence; an unchanged retry reuses it; changing only an existing generic-specialization expected byte reruns test:generic-specialization and reuses unrelated commands/shards; changing compiler/fixture/catalog content or adding, deleting, renaming, re-moding, or symlinking an expected path forces the appropriate full shard; corrupt, stale, foreign-toolchain, incomplete-input, or failed evidence is rejected; timing schema identifies snapshot-only reruns; governance, partition, schema, and CI-policy tests pass.

A validated prior receipt can rerun only changed snapshot owners and records a closed snapshot-refresh basis with the prior evidence key. Expected path/mode/inventory changes and every non-snapshot input still force a full shard. Broader command-group parallel scheduling remains separately owned by haxe_c-5sd.7 after isolation benchmarking in haxe_c-5sd.2. Verification: 139 governance tests; 32 focused shard tests; 9 timing-schema tests; exact 61-command partition; real catalog ownership probe; Python compile; CI policy; JSON specs; git diff check.

Governance (139), shard/timing unit tests, exact partition, real catalog probe, schema/policy checks, Python compile, and diff checks pass. Broader command parallelism remains haxe_c-5sd.7.

title: Preserve borrowed interface aliases in HxcIR
description: A local Haxe interface alias copies the object-pointer and dispatch-table pair but does not acquire ownership of the concrete object. The lowering previously marked the alias as a borrowed class local, so HxcIR rejected its interface carrier shape during the virtual-dispatch gate.
acceptance_criteria: Compiler-produced HxcIR distinguishes borrowed class-pointer locals from borrowed interface-pair locals; validation permits one local initialization and reload while rejecting reassignment, ownership operations, unchecked forwarding, persistent storage, and escape; focused HxcIR and virtual-dispatch snapshots pass.
close_reason: Implemented separate borrowed-interface local ownership in HxcIR, preserved borrow propagation through local reloads, rejected escapes, and verified focused HxcIR plus full virtual-dispatch suites.

title: Reduce Caxecraft whole-program planning and report cost
description: The 2026-07-26 Caxecraft compile exposed target-pipeline costs that dominate developer feedback: semantic lowering about 54s, runtime planning about 26s, artifact planning about 46s, output ownership about 38s, and a 30.4MB full symbol ledger with 22,801 records. Cached symbol identities, lazy collision hashing, reason-set deduplication, immutable-output hash reuse, and an explicit summary symbol report reduced the interactive compile enough to finish under the 120s bound, but the fresh compile still took 97.48s on this Mac. Treat the summary report as a reviewed developer mode, retain full evidence in audit lanes, and optimize the underlying full plan rather than normalizing the delay.
design: Retain TypedExpr -> validated HxcIR -> structural CAST. The performance goal is to execute that architecture with fewer repeated projections, not to collapse the semantic boundary. First add non-overlapping request-scoped profiling. Then create immutable revision-bound canonical indices and only profiler-justified semantic facts within one CompilationContext, move canonical runtime/ABI planning between semantic finalization and CAST projection where the evidence supports it, and cache output-prefix facts only inside one locked transaction. Defer cross-request HxcIR/TypedExpr/backend caching and any compiler port until request-local duplication is removed and an overcomplete invalidation key plus cold differential proves a material remaining win.
acceptance_criteria: Record uncontended phase timings and host/toolchain identity; profile the remaining semantic/runtime/artifact/output phases; remove redundant traversal, sorting, copying, hashing, or serialization without changing full report bytes; retain full and summary report regression evidence; define a documented Caxecraft edit-loop budget; prove cold/server determinism, focused compiler fixtures, full audit reports, and the flagship compile/native build.
notes:
2026-07-26: the registered caxecraft-domain snapshot updater exceeded play.py's 120s full-playable Haxe-to-C timeout twice consecutively under host load 23.34 on 12 logical CPUs. The same generation completed earlier in the canonical shard before reporting maintainability-package snapshot drift, so this is currently classified as a reproducible saturated-host feedback-loop blocker, not a semantic failure and not an unsaturated regression claim. Do not raise the timeout or hand-edit snapshots; seek validated artifact reuse or retry under representative load.

It independently recommends retaining durable target-earned HxcIR, making CAST consume settled semantic facts, keeping the printer formatting-only, profiling nested spans with exclusive cost/counters, removing request-local repeated maps/traversals/report serialization, and optimizing ReflaxeOutputWriter prefix checks without weakening ownership. Children haxe_c-5sd.5.1-.3 own the first executable stages. Cross-request backend caching, a daemon, native host promotion, and universal IR remain deferred.
2026-07-27 after Oracle reconciliation: a third registered caxecraft-domain snapshot update timed out at the unchanged play.py 120-second full-playable Haxe-to-C boundary. Starting host load was 7.35/7.61/9.37 on 12 logical CPUs with active sibling genes-ts, haxe.ocaml, and haxe.ruby Haxe processes. The same canonical shard previously completed generation and reached only maintainability-package drift, so this remains contention/broad-owner feedback-loop evidence rather than a semantic regression or unsaturated baseline. Do not retry blindly, raise the timeout, or hand-edit expected files; haxe_c-5sd.8.1 and haxe_c-5sd.7.1 own the first reusable-generation and ownership corrections.

Independent Sys.time spans: typed capture 1.890s; whole-program analysis 3.455s; HxcIR construction 62.251s; validation 14.187s; semantic analysis/naming 22.329s; CAST bodies 18.513s; enclosing semantic lowering 118.102s; runtime planning 59.386s; C printing 11.103s; artifact planning 24.959s; target pipeline 217.414s; output ownership 0.130s. Parent/child spans overlap and must not be summed. This proves the repeated 120s updater failures reflect a real current cold target-pipeline regression under this host state, not a hang; output prefix caching is not the first fix for this workload. Pinned-Haxe --times showed the known unconverted Mach timer scale and is not the wall authority. Temporary generation is diagnostic only and must not update snapshots outside the registered owner.

title: Give optional primitive switch bodies one structural owner
description: A natural switch over Null<Int> routes both an absent value and an unmatched present payload to the same Haxe default arm. Direct graph edges made that default an internal shared node, forcing structured C either to duplicate the body or use a goto. Normalize the choice through a typed arm ordinal: inspect the payload only on the present path, select one ordinal, then enter each source case or default body exactly once.
acceptance_criteria: The existing ordinary-Haxe optional statement-switch fixture covers absent, matching, and unmatched present values; strict generated-C layouts and native execution pass; inactive optional payloads are never read; Caxecraft advances past ScenarioLexer.readQuoted; and lowering introduces neither duplicated source bodies nor a new goto authority.
close_reason: Nullable primitive switches now select a typed arm ordinal before entering each source body once. The complete function-lowering lane passed strict generated-C layouts and native execution, and Caxecraft advanced past ScenarioLexer.readQuoted to CaxeFlowActionRegistry.schemaMatchesId.

title: Give comma-separated String switch arms one structural owner
description: Caxecraft natural case all, any parser arm exposed a structural control-flow graph in which multiple ordered String comparisons jumped directly to one shared body. The semantic IR was correct, but a readable structured C tree could only duplicate that body or introduce a goto. Group consecutive patterns belonging to the same Haxe arm, reduce their comparisons through a typed Boolean flow carrier, and branch into the shared body once. Preserve source-order text/null comparisons, single subject evaluation, statement/value switch semantics, managed String ownership, deterministic C, and fail-closed validation.
acceptance_criteria: Focused ordinary-Haxe tests cover comma-separated String patterns in statement and value switches, both spellings reach the same arm, fallback remains correct, native/Eval parity and sanitizer-backed generated projects pass, Caxecraft advances past CaxeFlowValueReader.predicate, and no target-specific/game-name special case or new goto is introduced.
close_reason: Grouped String switch patterns now join through one typed Boolean arm decision. The focused String runtime lane passed Eval/native parity, split/package/unity generated projects, C11/C++17, and sanitizers; Caxecraft advanced past CaxeFlowValueReader.predicate to ScenarioLexer.readQuoted.

title: Keep normal-join ranking inside the current loop iteration
description: Caxecraft exposed an outer loop branch containing a nested loop and early returns. Structural control-flow ranking walked through the outer continue/header into a future iteration, selected the nested-loop exit instead of the current iteration's shared cleanup tail, and then tried to emit that tail twice. Stop distance searches at active break/continue targets, preserve the existing proof rules, and add a synthetic nested-loop regression plus the flagship compile.
close_reason: Stopped loop join-distance searches at the active iteration boundary, admitted dominated acyclic early-return regions, and retained abrupt sibling proofs without crossing competing continue prefixes. Added synthetic regressions for nested loops and branched early returns. Verified with the complete clang evaluation-order structural/Eval/native zero-runtime lane (91.48s), a fresh Caxecraft compile-only journey (97.48s), validated generated project reuse, native C build (6.94s), and a focused bounded launch attempt; the latter reached Raylib initialization but this tool session had no desktop monitor authority.

title: Omit unreachable defaults from exhaustive enum switches
description: Caxecraft's paired enum-pattern match becomes a typed outer enum switch that explicitly covers every source tag while retaining the source wildcard as an unreachable default. HxcIR correctly forbids a default edge on an exhaustive tag switch. Make enum statement/value lowering recognize that the typed cases already cover the closed enum, omit the unreachable default without changing nested mismatch behavior, and retain focused enum plus Caxecraft evidence.
close_reason: Enum lowering now omits source defaults proven unreachable after complete typed tag coverage while preserving nested mismatch behavior. Verified by focused enum lowering and Caxecraft generated/native evidence.

title: Carry Array receivers across nested argument and index flow
description: Caxecraft exposed ordinary Haxe indexing where the Array expression is evaluated before a conditional index. The index creates HxcIR branches, so the earlier block-local receiver cannot be named at their join. Stage the borrowed receiver without retaining it, reload it after the join, preserve Haxe evaluation order, and add focused generated-C/native evidence plus the Caxecraft integrated proof.
notes: The next Caxecraft boundary showed the same rule in Array.push: the receiver is evaluated before a conditional managed-String argument. Apply one staged-receiver contract across admitted Array methods, not an index-only special case.
close_reason: Array receivers are staged and safely reloaded across conditional index and argument control flow without retaining a borrowed receiver or changing Haxe evaluation order. Verified by evaluation-order generated/native checks and Caxecraft integrated evidence.

title: Validate managed join carriers across loop iterations
description: Caxecraft exposed a valid managed String conditional inside a loop. HxcIR acquires and moves one owner per iteration, but validateManagedCarrierFlow follows the CFG back to the declaration and mistakes the next iteration for reuse of the prior owner. Model re-entry as a new empty protocol only after the previous iteration reached moved, retain fail-closed rejection for empty/owned redeclaration, add focused semantic/native evidence, and keep Caxecraft as the integrated proof.
close_reason: Managed join validation now treats loop re-entry as a new per-iteration ownership protocol after the prior owner is moved, while malformed reuse remains rejected. Verified by focused HxcIR validation and the Caxecraft integrated render/native path.

title: Preserve instance receivers across argument-created control-flow joins
description: Caxecraft's CaxeFlowReader.readSequence evaluates an instance receiver, then passes an enum argument whose construction contains conditional control flow. Instance-call lowering keeps the receiver as a block-local HxcIR value while argument lowering moves to a join block, so HxcIRValidator correctly rejects the later call with HXC9000. Static and indirect calls already stage earlier values across later argument flow; instance calls need the same general rule.
design: Preserve Haxe's receiver-before-arguments order and evaluate the receiver exactly once. Perform the existing receiver null check at the same point, save the checked receiver in a typed automatic local only when a later argument may create control flow, preserve whether a direct receiver is a non-owning class borrow, reload it in the final block, and rebuild direct, virtual, or interface dispatch with that available value. Stage earlier explicit arguments across later argument joins by the same shared mechanism. Do not re-evaluate the receiver, relax HxcIR validation, or patch Caxecraft.
acceptance_criteria: A focused ordinary-Haxe fixture calls an instance method with a side-effecting receiver and at least one conditional/enum-producing argument; Eval and strict native C agree on receiver/argument order and result; HxcIR validation passes with no cross-block value use; direct, virtual, interface, nullable, and borrowed-receiver behavior remains covered as applicable; Caxecraft advances past CaxeFlowReader.readSequence.
close_reason: Fixed instance-call lowering to stage checked receivers and earlier arguments across argument-created HxcIR joins, preserve direct-class borrow identity, and rebuild direct/virtual/interface dispatch with values available in the final block. HxcIR validation now carries a non-null proof through a staging local without emitting a redundant second check and recognizes addresses of direct class storage as borrows. Evidence: focused direct-receiver Haxe Eval plus split Clang O0/O2 native corpus passed; npm run test:hxc-ir passed; Caxecraft compile-only, native build-only, and three-frame Raylib smoke passed.

title: Promote retained class-reference graphs to precise collector storage
description: Ordinary Haxe composition may construct one class that retains another class reference, as CaxeFlowRulePlanner does with CaxeFlowState. haxe.c currently recognizes final new-valued fields as inline owned children before later bodies reveal this persistent alias, then rejects the safe program. Conservatively promote every reachable class with a retained concrete-class field, its referenced targets, inheritance chain, and affected new-valued fields to the existing precise nonmoving GC representation. Add constructor-only first-field initialization for managed class references, preserve exact tracing/root/failure behavior, emit readable typed pointer fields, and add positive/negative/native sanitizer evidence. Keep direct inline storage for graphs with no persistent class reference. A later measured escape-analysis optimization may recover same-parent containment, but it must not block natural Haxe or require a new semantic IR family without evidence.
close_reason: Retained concrete-class graphs now promote to the precise nonmoving collector with typed pointer fields, constructor-first self references, exact tracing/rooting, managed inheritance validation, and direct storage preserved for non-retained graphs. Verified by HxcIR, class-layout native C/C++ and sanitizer coverage, constructor split/package/unity native coverage, and Caxecraft snapshot plus native layout gates.

title: Embed final class fields assigned by constructors
description: CaxecraftApp declares final editorScreen:CaxecraftEditorScreen and initializes it exactly once in its constructor. haxe.c currently recognizes inline owned child construction only when Haxe moved a declaration-site initializer into the constructor; an equivalent explicit constructor assignment is left as a generic class reference and rejected as stack-construction-requires-direct-local.
design: Use Haxe ClassField.isFinal plus the already type-checked direct this.field assignment to recognize a single exact constructor initializer. Reserve the child as an inline owned class field and reuse owned-field address/constructor lowering at the assignment's real source position. Multiple/conditional shapes that cannot prove one initialization remain fail-closed; do not heap-allocate solely to bypass the layout proof.
acceptance_criteria: Focused ordinary-Haxe fixtures cover a final child initialized at its declaration and an equivalent final child assigned once in the constructor; both preserve stable identity, mutation, Eval/native behavior, direct readable struct embedding, zero heap/runtime for the direct case, deterministic output, strict C11/C++/sanitizer gates, and final-field safety. Caxecraft advances past CaxecraftApp.editorScreen construction without an application rewrite.

title: Transfer owned managed Array element copies across returns
description: The real Caxecraft compile reaches ScenarioRecordCursor.lastRecord, which returns a managed ScenarioLexRecord copied by checked Array indexing. The Array runtime already produces an independently owned element copy and lowering gives it a stable cleanup local, but the return boundary rejects that borrowed view instead of moving the existing owner to the caller.
design: Track the exact cleanup action behind each borrowed managed Array element. At a matching return, return the loaded value and exclude that one cleanup action, transferring the already-created owner without a redundant retain/deep copy. Keep all other escape contexts explicit and fail-closed.
acceptance_criteria: An ordinary-Haxe fixture returns a managed record Array element after its source Array and source locals leave scope; Eval/native results agree; HxcIR return cleanup omits exactly the transferred element destructor while preserving every unrelated cleanup; deterministic output, strict C11 O0/O2 and ASan/UBSan pass; the former planned negative is removed or promoted to positive; Caxecraft advances past ScenarioRecordCursor.lastRecord.

title: Compare nullable fieldless enums with concrete enum values
description: The real Caxecraft compile now reaches variableKindInScope(...):Null<FlowValueKind> != kind:FlowValueKind. haxe.c's tagged optional equality supports primitive payloads and separate non-null fieldless-enum equality, but the composition rejects the fieldless direct-enum payload as non-primitive.
design: Reuse the existing direct optional presence branch and exact enum-tag equality contract. When present, unwrap the optional and compare two matching payload-free native enum values with haxe.enum-tag.equal/not-equal. Keep payload enums, unrelated enum identities, managed values, and unsupported structural equality fail-closed.
acceptance_criteria: Focused ordinary-Haxe tests cover present equal, present unequal, and absent Null<FieldlessEnum> versus FieldlessEnum for == and !=, with Eval/native agreement, explicit optional presence branching, exact enum-tag comparison, deterministic output, strict C11/sanitizer evidence, and Caxecraft advancement.

title: Admit compiler-hoisted flow carriers across value-producing preludes
description: After the private-set property fix, the real Caxecraft compile reaches a second general TypedExpr shape in CaxeFlowReader.readVariable. Haxe lowers a final local initialized from a nullable switch into an uninitialized carrier, one or more independent initialized prelude locals (including a value-producing conditional), and then exhaustive control flow that assigns the carrier. haxe.c already proves carriers across non-flow preludes but rejects this safe value-producing prelude as TVar(scope:uninitialized).
design: Extend the existing structural carrier proof, not general uninitialized source locals. Permit an initialized prelude even when its initializer creates control flow only after proving it does not reference the carrier and that the later exhaustive if/switch assigns or terminates on every normal path. Keep HxcIR's path-sensitive definite-assignment validation authoritative; do not default an enum to a forged tag or relax arbitrary reads.
acceptance_criteria: A focused ordinary-Haxe fixture reproduces the hoisted carrier plus conditional prelude and matches Eval/native C; HxcIR proves no read before assignment on every reachable path and malformed genuine uninitialized locals remain rejected; deterministic split/package/unity, strict C11 O0/O2, sanitizer where applicable, and Caxecraft advancement pass.
notes: Caxecraft's authored-controller oracle exposed the remaining guarded-result form: Haxe emits an empty carrier followed by an if whose successful path assigns and whose fallback returns. The structural recognizer now uses the existing assigns-or-terminates proof for if arms; FlowCarrierFixture owns the guarded-return Eval/native shape.
close_reason: Admitted compiler-generated guarded carriers only when every continuing path assigns and every other arm terminates; the full evaluation-order matrix preserves genuine uninitialized-local rejection.

title: Preserve legal writes to private-set Haxe class properties
description: Caxecraft exposes a general class-lowering bug: an inline method declared by a class legally increments public var position(default, null), but haxe.c derives generated-storage mutability from the public write accessor and rejects the already-type-checked TUnop as immutable. Separate source access control from physical storage mutability. True final fields must remain immutable after construction.
acceptance_criteria: A focused ordinary-Haxe fixture mutates a (default, null) instance field through its declaring inline method and matches Eval/native behavior; generated HxcIR/C marks the storage mutable while final fields remain immutable; Caxecraft compiles past ScenarioRecordCursor.advance without weakening source access checks; focused native and sanitizer gates pass.

title: Destroy ignored managed optional call results
description: Ordinary Haxe may call a function for its side effects and ignore its return value. Caxecraft EditorSession.redo ignores history.takeUndo() while rolling back a failed redo. That call returns a fresh Null<EditorHistoryEntry>; the present record owns Bytes. haxe.c currently detects the fresh owner but rejects it as discarded instead of running the optional lifecycle destroy operation.
design: At the statement-call boundary, recognize only a fresh managed tagged optional result. Move it into one typed automatic place and immediately emit its existing program-local destroy operation, consuming the fresh-owner marker exactly once. Do not retain first, delay cleanup to function exit, silently discard other unproved managed families, or special-case EditorHistory. Existing optional lifecycle generation remains the single owner of present/absent destruction.
acceptance_criteria: The managed optional ordinary-Haxe fixture ignores a function result whose present payload owns Bytes and also covers absent behavior; Eval and generated C agree, HxcIR contains an immediate typed optional release, generated C calls the optional destroy helper, and strict C11 O0/O2 plus ASan/UBSan pass without leaks or double release. Other unproved discarded managed families remain fail-closed. The real Caxecraft compile advances past EditorSession.redo without source changes.

title: Retain fresh managed class instances in nullable class fields
description: Caxecraft EditorSession.enterTestPlay naturally assigns a fresh EditorTestPlay instance to a nullable field and later reads, replaces, and clears that field. The child therefore outlives the creating method. Current lowering rejects every field assignment whose right side is TNew before it consults the already-selected collector representation. Implement the general collector-owned object-graph case instead of moving construction, leaking a stack address, or changing the application API.
design: When the parent class has a precise collector-managed representation, recursively classify class references contained by its optional and aggregate field shapes. Permit a fresh class construction on the right side of a field assignment only when that child is also collector-managed. Emit the existing managed allocation, exact temporary root, constructor call, and typed store; the parent exact trace keeps the child reachable afterward, replacement removes the prior edge, and null clears it. Preserve the existing fail-closed stack-construction diagnostic for direct or unproven class representations. Add no Caxecraft special case, reference counting, raw C, or stack escape.
acceptance_criteria: An ordinary-Haxe focused fixture stores a fresh managed child through a nullable field, survives forced collection pressure, reads it, replaces it, clears it, and agrees with Eval. HxcIR records managed allocation/root/store; the parent trace visits the exact child field; generated split/package/unity C is deterministic, warning-clean, sanitizer-clean, and uses no reference-count calls for the collector graph. Direct/unproven field-new assignment remains fail-closed. The real Caxecraft compile advances past EditorSession.enterTestPlay without application changes, and architecture documentation explains the lifetime rule in plain language.

The unmodified Caxecraft compile advances past the former stack-construction rejection at EditorSession.hx:152 and now fails at the same expression with TNew(managed-fallible-constructor-not-yet-admitted:constructor.caxecraft.editor.EditorTestPlay). title: Lower Array.pop with nullable managed-element ownership
description: The real Caxecraft compile now reaches EditorHistory.takeRedo and fails closed on ordinary Haxe Array.pop(). This is a general core-collection parity gap: pop mutates shared Array identity and returns Null<T>, including for elements such as records that own Bytes and nullable aggregate fields. The compiler must preserve Haxe empty-array behavior and transfer or copy the removed element into an independently owned nullable result without leaks, double release, use-after-free, or an application workaround.
design: Add the smallest typed HxcIR/runtime operation that implements Haxe Array.pop for every already-admitted Array element representation. The operation must distinguish an empty array from a present element, preserve shared Array identity, and give a managed returned element exactly one owner before the slot is removed. Extend validator, structural C emitter, runtime feature manifest/API, and focused ordinary-Haxe/native tests. Do not compose get_copy plus remove_at unless the combined failure and ownership contract is explicitly failure-atomic; do not special-case EditorHistory or inject raw C.
acceptance_criteria: An ordinary-Haxe differential fixture covers empty and non-empty pop for trivial and managed elements, alias-visible mutation, repeated pops, and a managed record matching Caxecraft's ownership pressure. Eval and generated C agree. HxcIR validates the exact Array specialization and nullable result. GCC and Clang O0/O2 plus ASan/UBSan show no leak, double release, or use-after-free. Malformed IR fails closed. The native hxrt fixture covers invalid inputs and empty/present transfer behavior. npm run caxecraft:play -- --compile-only advances past EditorHistory.takeUndo/takeRedo without application changes.

title: Release fresh managed enum switch subjects after matching
description: After haxe_c-djl.13 admits Caxecraft's compiler-generated flow carriers, the real compile reaches CaxecraftEditorScreen.redo and fails with HXC1001 function-exit:unowned-fresh-managed-enum-value. session.redo() returns a fresh managed EditorHistoryResult that is consumed as a statement-switch subject. The tag/payload match succeeds, but the lowering leaves the fresh result in its ownership inventory instead of giving the switch region an exact cleanup owner. This is a general managed-enum switch-subject lifetime gap, not editor-specific application behavior.
design: Model the switch subject's lifetime explicitly in HxcIR. A fresh managed enum call result must remain alive through tag testing and every borrowed payload projection, then be released exactly once on each completion path after the arm no longer needs it. Preserve source evaluation order and early return/throw cleanup. Do not hide the compiler gap by assigning the result to Caxecraft storage, weakening the ownership audit, or injecting C.
acceptance_criteria: A focused ordinary-Haxe fixture switches directly on a fresh managed enum call result with payload-free and managed-payload arms. Eval and generated C agree; GCC/Clang O0/O2 plus ASan/UBSan prove no leak, double release, or use-after-free. HxcIR shows one bounded subject owner and exact cleanup on normal and admitted abrupt exits; malformed ownership fails closed. npm run caxecraft:play -- --compile-only advances past CaxecraftEditorScreen.undo/redo without an application workaround.
close_reason: Fresh managed enum switch subjects now receive one explicit bounded owner that survives tag and payload reads, releases exactly once on normal and abrupt paths, and cannot be fabricated by malformed HxcIR. Verified with npm run test:enum-lowering and npm run test:hxc-ir; the real Caxecraft compile advanced past CaxecraftEditorScreen undo/redo into the later Array.pop boundary.

title: Release fresh managed String inputs after Bytes.ofString copies them
description: Caxecraft now reaches ScenarioWriter.write and fails at Bytes.ofString(lines.join("\n") + "\n"). The joined String is a fresh managed value with one owner. Bytes.ofString immediately copies its length-delimited UTF-8 bytes into independent mutable Bytes storage, but the current intrinsic lowering borrows the value without first assigning that owner to a cleanup-capable compiler local. The function-exit audit correctly rejects the unowned fresh String. This is a reusable ordinary-Haxe lifetime rule, not a Caxecraft serialization workaround.
design: At the Bytes.ofString intrinsic boundary, evaluate the source exactly once, stabilize only a fresh managed String into the existing typed String temporary-owner protocol, null-check and copy from that stable borrow, then release the String owner exactly once on every normal or admitted failure exit. Existing borrowed parameters, aliases, and static strings must not gain redundant retains or owners. The returned Bytes owns only its independent byte copy; it must never retain or point into the source String. Reuse typed HxcIR cleanup and runtime planning rather than adding a Bytes-specific opaque escape.
acceptance_criteria: Ordinary-Haxe fixtures cover literals, borrowed runtime parameters, fresh concatenation, Array<String>.join, nested evaluation order, empty/non-ASCII/embedded-NUL data, and Bytes independence after the source dies. Focused HxcIR and generated-C checks prove a fresh String gets one temporary owner and one release, while borrowed/static inputs add no redundant lifecycle work. Forced Bytes allocation failure and normal success release every String and Bytes owner exactly once; strict C11 O0/O2 plus ASan/UBSan agree with Eval and leave no plausible artifacts on rejected cases. Runtime feature selection remains exact, documentation explains copy-versus-lifetime ownership, and unmodified Caxecraft compiles beyond the ScenarioWriter function-exit diagnostic to either success or one newly recorded later boundary.
close_reason: Implemented fresh managed String ownership for Bytes.ofString copy inputs. The focused Bytes fixture now proves exact evaluation, reverse cleanup, borrowed/static no-retain behavior, Unicode/NUL byte parity, allocation rollback, sanitizer safety, and selective runtime planning; the full five-lane toolchain gate passed. Unmodified Caxecraft advanced to the separately owned managed flow-carrier boundary haxe_c-djl.13.

Literal and borrowed inputs remain retain/release-free in HxcIR. title: Lower nonescaping capturing callbacks with stack environments
description: Caxecraft ScenarioValidationContext passes ordinary capturing predicates to a synchronous higher-order helper. Implement the smallest reusable positive closure slice: prove the callback parameter cannot escape, represent its typed callable and captured environment explicitly, keep the environment on the caller stack, and preserve capture reads, writes, evaluation order, diagnostics, and generated-C readability. This child must advance the real Caxecraft path; it must not close the parent work for escaping, recursive, or managed closures.
design: Use source-level whole-program facts to distinguish direct function pointers from capturing callable values. Admit stack storage only when the receiving parameter's uses prove synchronous non-escape. Carry an exact typed invoke signature plus explicit environment identity through HxcIR; do not use globals, raw C, application-specific callbacks, or pretend that stack environments support escaping closures.
acceptance_criteria: Focused positive Haxe fixtures cover immutable and mutable local captures, repeated callback calls, callback arguments/results, and nested control flow. A focused negative proves an attempted escape remains fail-closed without output. Eval and generated strict C agree under sanitizers; generated C contains a typed stack environment with no heap/runtime closure feature. Caxecraft compiles beyond ScenarioValidationContext.hx:242 and its snapshot updater advances without source workarounds. The parent haxe_c-ckk.3 remains open for escaping, recursive, cyclic, and managed closure lifetimes.
close_reason: Implemented and verified typed caller-stack environments for exact, nonescaping captured callbacks. Eval, strict native C, ASan/UBSan, structural snapshots, escape diagnostics, determinism, and the Caxecraft integrated boundary all pass. The broader closure parent remains open for lifetimes that can escape or cannot be proven synchronous.

Evidence: npm run test:function-lowering; npm run test:enum-lowering; npm run test:hxc-ir; npm run test:array-runtime; npm run format:haxe:check; npm run test:typed-boundaries; npm run test:agent-instructions; git diff --check. General escaping, nested, recursive, self-capturing, virtual, generic, and managed closure lifetimes remain on parent haxe_c-ckk.3.

title: Migrate stateless Caxecraft editor wrappers to module functions
description:
## Why

The completed module-field capability task proved that haxe.c can lower ordinary Haxe module-level functions with readable split C, but the editor still contains audited static-only wrapper classes such as EditorWorldGrid. Those wrappers add a fake nominal namespace even though all state is supplied by callers.

## What

Strengthen the durable Haxe style rule so work in a subsystem also checks neighboring static-only wrappers, then migrate the clear stateless editor helpers whose public contracts do not require class identity. Start with EditorWorldGrid and inspect EditorCommandReducer, EditorPolicy, EditorScenarioFactory, and EditorScenarioSnapshot. Keep any class that has a real nominal/API reason and document that reason.

## How

Convert one coherent editor ownership slice to direct module functions, import operations explicitly or under readable aliases, preserve enum/result ownership in the same modules, and retain Haxe's hidden module-field identity only inside compiler semantics. Verify Eval behavior, generated C readability and source-module ownership, native/editor/scenario tests, and no runtime/allocation regression. Do not perform an unreviewed repository-wide textual rewrite.
design: Use ordinary public/private module-level functions for stateless editor transformations. Keep enums and typedefs in their owning modules. Update callers with explicit aliased imports where names would otherwise be ambiguous. Add an opportunistic but bounded instruction: when changing a Haxe subsystem, inspect its neighboring static-only wrappers and migrate clear cases in the same verified ownership slice; create a follow-up for material unrelated work instead of growing scope silently.
acceptance_criteria: AGENTS rules clearly require module functions for stateless operations and a bounded neighboring-wrapper audit when a subsystem is changed; EditorWorldGrid no longer uses a static-only class; the remaining named editor wrappers are either migrated or retain a documented concrete nominal/API reason; Eval/editor/domain/scenario behavior is unchanged; generated split C retains readable source-module ownership; focused function-lowering and native checks pass; no new runtime feature or allocation is introduced.
notes: Implemented the source-architecture phase: strengthened root and Caxecraft rules so a changed Haxe subsystem audits neighboring static-only wrappers; migrated EditorWorldGrid, EditorCommandReducer, EditorPolicy, EditorScenarioFactory, and EditorScenarioSnapshot to module functions with explicit aliased imports; retained EditorSession, EditorHistory, and EditorTestPlay as real state/lifetime owners; expanded @:noCompletion explanations; and updated the audited documentation. title: Remove CaxecraftApp friend access to mutable GameSession state
description: CaxecraftApp currently relies on class-level @:allow friendship to borrow GameSession's mutable world and authored-item buffers and to call WaterSimulation directly. This crosses the application/presentation-to-simulation ownership boundary. It is statically safer than a cast, but it lets the outer shell bypass GameSession invariants and couples rendering and input orchestration to storage representation. Replace this explicit migration debt without making raw mutable storage public or copying the world each frame.
design: Move mutations behind typed GameSession commands or fixed-tick intents: mining, placement, terrain invalidation, authored-item pickup, recovery, combat, and related committed events must have one simulation owner. Give rendering the smallest read-only WorldView/capability needed for bounded traversal; its lifetime must be tied to the session and it must not permit writes or escape into persistent application state. Keep GameSession Raylib-free and keep CaxecraftApp responsible for platform resources, input, screens, frame accumulation, and presentation only. Prefer an ordinary public typed boundary over friendship. If haxe.c cannot safely lower the natural session-tied read-only borrow, reduce that compiler limitation to a focused fixture and fix or separately track the general borrow/lifetime capability rather than retaining @:allow as product architecture. Do not replace class-level friendship with field-level friendship and call the ownership problem solved; field-level narrowing is only an interim risk reduction.
acceptance_criteria: CaxecraftApp has no @:allow access to GameSession and no direct access to worldStorage, authoredItemStorage, WaterSimulation, or other mutable session internals. All simulation mutations enter through typed commands/intents and preserve deterministic fixed-tick ownership; renderers receive a bounded read-only view with no copy, heap allocation, raw C, or Raylib dependency in GameSession. The compiler rejects storing or returning the borrowed view beyond its valid owner lifetime. Focused Eval/generated-C tests cover accepted reads, rejected writes/escapes, mining/placement/item behavior, and failure atomicity. Full Caxecraft domain, PilotScript, strict C/C++ headers, sanitizers, generated-C readability, zero-unplanned-runtime/allocation, snapshots, typed-boundary, and governance gates pass. Documentation removes the migration warning only when the @:allow seam is gone.
notes:
The storage-ownership slice is implemented and verified: CaxecraftApp no longer has @:allow access or touches worldStorage, authoredItemStorage, or WaterSimulation; rendering receives a zero-copy WorldView and terrain/item edits use GameSession methods. Eval now wraps its Array in a read-only abstract as well. The issue remains open because CaxecraftApp still constructs recovery/combat character snapshots and commits them through broad replaceLocalPlayer(...); closing requires semantic commands/intents so GameSession owns those mutations rather than merely owning their final storage write. That remaining work should align with the typed actor-composition path haxe_c-xge.20.4.2.4.
Completed the remaining semantic-command slice. GameSession now owns local-player revival, hostile damage, recovery, and authored aquatic-equipment collection as typed read-calculate-commit operations; CaxecraftApp no longer imports those mutation helpers or publishes a whole Character snapshot. This fixes a real multi-tick ordering bug where a later fixed tick could overwrite damage or equipment held only in the frame-local variable. Recovery commits health before returning a consumed immutable inventory value, and equipment commits the profile before clearing its authored-item flag. The focused session probe covers unbound failure atomicity, normal no-ops, immediate persistence across a following fixed tick, recovery consumption, equipment idempotence, and revival. That probe also exposed and fixed Vitals.recover exceeding MAX_HEALTH. Generated/source guards reject reintroduction of replaceLocalPlayer, generic deactivateAuthoredItem, and direct app mutation helpers. The registered snapshot owner refreshed six artifacts and passed. Verification: format:haxe:check; Python py_compile; test:typed-boundaries; test:all-sources; snapshots:catalog; test:caxecraft-session; test:caxecraft-gameplay; test:caxecraft-pilot; caxecraft compile-only; graphical combat-drop, recovery-use, and aquatic-gear pilots (each two deterministic framebuffer runs); test:caxecraft-domain:full with split/package/unity, reversed/locale/warm determinism, standalone strict headers, O0/O2, ASan+UBSan, zero hxrt/allocation symbols, and maintainability checks; test:governance. The broad test:native wrapper reached its unrelated GC subtest and timed out at its fixed 30-second child bound while host load was about 11 on 12 logical CPUs with sibling haxe.ocaml jobs; the exact GC command then passed all precise-GC, C++17, and sanitizer checks in 32.6 seconds. No timeout was raised or semantic gate weakened. Actor inventory/equipment ownership remains truthfully assigned to haxe_c-xge.20.4.2.4.

General retained span fields remain rejected; this task does not weaken lifetime safety.

Extend the tagged optional plan so the presence flag is the sole authority for payload lifetime: present construction captures or retains one owner, copies retain only when present, assignment retains the replacement before releasing the old present payload, destruction releases only when present, and unwrap remains a checked borrow unless ownership is explicitly transferred. Reuse the managed aggregate lifecycle plan and explicit HxcIR retain/release operations. Preserve failure rollback, branch cleanup, runtime feature provenance, and split/package/unity ordering. Keep pointer-nullable classes and unmanaged tagged optionals unchanged; reject cycle-capable graphs at the existing collector boundary.
acceptance_criteria: A minimized managed Null<Record> and the Caxecraft ScenarioMessages editor-draft path compile without application-specific code; absent and present construction, copy, assignment where admitted, branch joins, checked unwrap/projection, call/return transfer, failure rollback, and cleanup match Eval; no inactive payload bytes are retained or released; runtime-none rejects managed optionals while automatic/minimal select only dependency-closed features; normal/reversed/server split/package/unity output is deterministic; strict GCC/Clang C11, C++ header consumers, ASan/UBSan, aggregate, enum, Array, HxcIR, runtime-plan, all-sources, typed-boundary, reduced CaxeFlow, and real Caxecraft split gates pass.

Presence-gated optional helpers delegate to the record lifecycle; present construction moves or retains one owner; copies retain only when present; alias-safe assignment captures the replacement before releasing the old target; branch joins transfer one owner; checked unwrap remains explicit; call/return and loop-local cleanup use schema-14 retain/release. The focused managed-optional lane now covers Eval, present/absent, generic alias assignment, conditional join, checked projection, call/return, normal/reversed discovery, cold/first/warm server, unity/split/package native execution, strict C++17 header consumers at O0/O2, ASan/UBSan, selective runtime features, and runtime-none rejection. Extend aggregate lifecycle classification so records with managed fields have a typed copy/retain/destroy plan, and make locals, calls, returns, Array<Record> elements, optionals where sound, and failure rollback use that one plan. The enum tag remains the authority for active payload access. Reuse the selected Array/enum lifecycle helpers and HxcIR cleanup validation; reject cycles that require the tracing collector until that collector is selected. Preserve dependency-first split/package/unity definitions and runtime feature provenance.

title: Lower core haxe.io.Bytes values into a selective binary-storage slice
description: Implement the smallest reusable generated-Haxe Bytes slice needed by Caxecraft editor snapshots while preserving Bytes as mutable binary storage, not text or Array<Int>. title: Add seamless in-process Edit ↔ Test Play switching
description:
## Why

Content authors need to see and feel a change immediately. The current visual shell can validate an EditorSession and toggle its disposable CaxeFlow test object, but it does not yet render or control the authored world through the normal game engine. Calling that state playable would be misleading.

## What

Make Edit -> Test Play -> Edit a first-class in-process loop. Test Play uses the current validated in-memory draft, the ordinary fixed-step GameSession/gameplay/render/input path, and a disposable runtime state. Stop Test returns to the exact editor draft, viewport camera, selection, active tool, panels, and undo/redo history.

## How

Define one explicit application-mode transition and an editor workspace snapshot. Instantiate the same engine path used by a loaded level from the validated Scenario without serializing to disk. Keep editor state alive while a separate disposable GameSession runs. Stop, failure, or game-over discards runtime mutations unless a future explicit import command is chosen. Preserve loaded render assets and the Raylib window across the transition.
design: This is not a second simulator and not the lightweight CaxeFlow-only EditorTestPlay object presented as the game. Reuse normal semantic input, fixed ticks, systems, renderer, localization, audio, and console/driver seams. Test Play must be unavailable for invalid drafts with source/object-linked diagnostics. Saving is orthogonal: neither entering nor leaving test play requires filesystem access.
acceptance_criteria: From the native editor, one mouse/controller/keyboard action starts the current valid draft in the ordinary rendered game within the existing window and process; another action or Escape returns to the exact draft/camera/selection/tool/panel/history state; no Haxe compile, C compile, process restart, save, or reload occurs; invalid drafts stay in edit mode with actionable diagnostics; runtime edits, inventory, entity state, rule variables, and world mutations are discarded on return; repeated cycles do not leak resources or grow steady-state allocations; a target-neutral state test plus generated-C engine test and one real Raylib pilot prove the transition and state restoration.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: The fast loop is explicitly in-memory and in-process: no Haxe compile, C compile, executable restart, save, or reload. The current UI's status-only CaxeFlow test toggle is not accepted as playable. Completion requires the normal authored-level GameSession/input/fixed-tick/render path plus exact restoration of the editor workspace and disposal of test mutations.

title: Lower reachable typed Haxe Array values into the selected runtime slice
description:
## Why

Caxecraft's runtime CaxeMap editor reaches ordinary Haxe parser code that uses resizable Array<T> values. The checked-in hxrt array implementation proves the native data structure, but haxe.c still rejects generated Haxe array construction, access, mutation, calls, ownership, and cleanup. Keeping the parser Eval-only would make native edit-to-test-play impossible.

## What

Add the first generated-Haxe Array<T> lowering slice over the existing dependency-closed hxrt array feature. Cover closed admitted element representations, literals and empty construction, length, checked indexing, push, copy/alias behavior, iteration needed by the parser/editor, and explicit lifetime/root planning. Keep c.CArray/Span runtime-free and reject unsupported element or escape shapes before artifacts.

## How

Introduce an explicit HxcIR managed-array representation and operations, a request-local element representation plan, structural CAST emission, and runtime feature selection with exact source reasons. Reuse hxrt array callbacks and allocator contracts. Do not box all elements, map Array to fixed storage, special-case Caxecraft, erase element types, or emit raw C.
design: Start with the minimized Array surface exercised by ScenarioLexer and EditorScenarioSnapshot, but design identities and operations as a closed typed family. The first slice must preserve Haxe evaluation order, bounds/failure semantics, aliasing across growth, and cleanup. Add operations only with focused Eval/native parity evidence; unsupported methods remain exact source diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria: A focused ordinary-Haxe fixture constructs empty and nonempty closed Array<T> values, reads length and checked elements, pushes through growth, observes aliases, iterates in source order, and exits with sanitizer-clean ownership; generated HxcIR and C are structural, deterministic, readable, and select only the dependency-closed array/allocator runtime features with source reasons; primitive and one admitted reference/aggregate element plan are covered or explicitly split with a dependency; unsupported element, escape, allocation-policy, and metal/runtime-none conflicts fail before artifacts; c.CArray/Span runtime-none evidence remains unchanged; repeated/reversed/server builds are byte-identical; the reduced Caxecraft lexer proceeds beyond Array construction and method lowering without any application workaround.

The hxrt array seed is implemented, but generated TypedExpr -> HxcIR -> CAST lowering and runtime selection are not. This must land before generic Array specialization and enum-payload integration can honestly unblock the editor.

title: Support nested Array types in reachable generic specialization
description:
## Why

The first native Caxecraft editor shell reaches the ordinary generic ScenarioLexer.fail<T>() helper with T = Array<ScenarioLexRecord>. haxe.c rejects the closed class type argument during reachable-function graph discovery with HXC1001, preventing normal editor/parser code from compiling. The flagship rule forbids an editor-only workaround.

## What

Teach deterministic generic specialization identity/substitution and reachable graph discovery to admit closed nested Array element types wherever the existing array representation is supported. Preserve fail-closed rejection for open, dynamic, unsupported, recursive, or budget-exceeding types.

## How

Reduce the ScenarioLexer call to a focused generic-specialization fixture, extend the one typed canonicalization owner rather than string-special-casing Array or Caxecraft, and retain exact report/symbol/determinism/native evidence. Then re-run the real Caxecraft playable compile containing CaxecraftEditorScreen.
design: Extend the current target-owned specialization type model/canonical key. Do not add an Array-name exception, erase element types, lower through Dynamic, or copy ScenarioLexer behavior. Reuse the existing array representation and specialization bounds; add only the missing closed structural-type case and its recursive validation.
acceptance_criteria: A minimal ordinary-Haxe fixture with a generic result/error helper specialized at Array<Record> compiles to deterministic direct C and runs under the native harness; nested supported class/array type arguments have stable structural identities and substitution through reachable discovery; existing dynamic/open/unsupported and specialization-budget diagnostics remain exact and fail before artifacts; reversed discovery and repeated builds are byte-identical; the Caxecraft playable compile reaches its editor parser without this HXC1001; focused generic-specialization, array, all-sources, typed-boundary, generated-C, and relevant flagship gates pass.
