title: Run the real Caxecraft headless pilot under GCC and Clang sanitizers
description: The deterministic memory/software pilot now proves the real game and renderer, but the real generated application is not yet compiled and executed under AddressSanitizer (invalid memory access) and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer (invalid C operations). Add an explicit play.py sanitizer profile, preserve strict warnings, instrument every generated C translation unit and final link, record the profile in semantic evidence, and run the pinned Raylib memory/software pilot under both Linux GCC and Clang. The verified prebuilt Raylib library may remain the same locked binary; this child owns generated-program instrumentation and an actual real-Raylib run, not a claim that every upstream Raylib source line is instrumented.
design: Extend the existing typed/argument-array native adapter; do not inject raw C or build a second game. Reuse the checksum-verified memory/software Raylib build per toolchain. State accurately that generated C is instrumented while the locked upstream static library is executed under the sanitizer runtime but not rebuilt with instrumentation in this slice. If evidence shows upstream-library instrumentation is required, record a separate lock/provisioning design instead of adding unreviewed CMake flags.
acceptance_criteria: --sanitizers is explicit, fail closed on unsupported hosts/toolchains, and adds address+undefined sanitizers plus no-recovery/frame-pointer flags to both compile and link. The move-jump-edit pilot passes twice with selection/removal/placement evidence under Linux GCC and Clang, leak detection enabled where supported, and artifacts identify compiler and sanitizer profile. CI remains bounded and parallel per isolated toolchain; policy tests fail if either sanitizer lane, explicit flag, or artifact disappears. Ordinary desktop/pilot builds remain unchanged.
notes: Implemented an explicit Linux-only --sanitizers profile in examples/caxecraft/play.py. It recognizes GCC/Clang fail closed, adds -fsanitize=address,undefined, -fno-sanitize-recover=all, and -fno-omit-frame-pointer to every generated C compile and the final link, isolates sanitized output paths, and records address/undefined in the portable pilot report. Governance CI now runs isolated linux-gcc and linux-clang memory/software move-jump-edit jobs with leak detection and fail-fast ASan/UBSan settings, reusing the checksum-verified per-toolchain Raylib library; artifacts identify compiler and sanitizer profile. Policy checks lock the matrix, environment, explicit switch, and artifact paths. Documentation states plainly that generated game C is instrumented while the verified Raylib archive is executed but not source-instrumented. Local evidence: check_pilot.py PASS; py_compile PASS; check_ci_policy.py PASS; governance YAML parse PASS; git diff --check PASS; macOS unsupported-host and sanitizer+compile-only paths fail clearly before build; ordinary macOS memory/software move-jump-edit still compiles, runs twice identically, captures 1280x720, and records native.sanitizers=[] in about 28 seconds. Actual Linux GCC/Clang sanitizer executions remain pending remote CI because the current host is macOS and no commit/push authority has been given; do not close until both jobs pass.

title: Preserve class receivers across lazy Boolean control flow
description: Caxecraft's ordinary Haxe session assertion exposed HXC9000 before C emission: a lazy || chain that calls more than one method on the same local class instance injects a class-field/null check in a short-circuit RHS block, but that check refers to an IR receiver value unavailable in that block. Reduce the pattern to a focused compiler fixture, make receiver stabilization obey block dominance and Haxe evaluation order, and retain the Caxecraft session/headless path as integrated evidence.
design: Fix the owning HxcIR/body-lowering rule rather than splitting or weakening the Caxecraft expression. Reuse the existing stable-flow/spill machinery when possible. The focused fixture must include a class instance, lazy Boolean control flow, intervening record fields, and a later instance call; validation must remain fail closed.
acceptance_criteria: The minimized fixture validates and emits strict C with no goto/heap/runtime workaround, native behavior matches Haxe Eval, the Caxecraft session test passes unchanged in expression shape, and relevant HxcIR/body/evaluation/class tests remain green.
close_reason: Fixed in HxcIR schema 12: borrowed class-field receivers now use validated automatic pointer locals that remain valid across lazy Boolean blocks; focused Eval/native/strict-C tests and the Caxecraft session probe pass without goto, heap, or runtime workarounds.

title: Run Caxecraft through pinned Raylib memory/software rendering
description: The required Raylib memory/software lane currently executes only the small binding smoke, while Caxecraft's graphical pilot runs only through a Linux Xvfb desktop. Add the smallest configuration-aware Caxecraft build/run path that compiles the production custom-target output against the checksum-pinned PLATFORM=Memory/software library, executes a representative deterministic gameplay pilot with 3D terrain, HUD, picking/edit state and clean shutdown, validates its semantic report, and preserves a renderer-scoped reference image without treating GPU screenshots as portable byte goldens.
design: Reuse play.py, PilotScript, the typed raylib binding, the existing prebuilt-provision report contract, and the centrally locked build/link facts. Keep desktop and memory/software configurations explicit and fail closed; do not add raw C game behavior or a second simulator. Any exact pixel golden is authoritative only for the pinned Linux memory/software configuration.
acceptance_criteria: A focused local/CI command can build Caxecraft with raylib_configuration_memory_software and a verified matching prebuilt Raylib report; the move-jump-edit pilot runs twice identically, covers 3D/HUD/picking/edit/quit via semantic telemetry, and produces a validated review image. CI provisions the locked library from a clean cache, runs the focused command, uploads normalized report/image evidence, and policy tests fail if the lane or configuration match is removed. Desktop behavior and ordinary snapshots remain unchanged.

title: Render the authored sand, forest, snow, and ash material set
description: Promote the already-reviewed base/adventure terrain cells into one typed content-driven renderer path. Add finite storage identities for sand, wood, leaves, snow, and ash; keep water on its existing typed fluid path; load the second atlas with explicit ownership; submit each atlas in one coherent batch; and author representative first-playable terrain through CAXEMAP rather than application conditionals. Preserve gameplay/editor/save identities independently of atlas coordinates and retain bounded draw calls, deterministic probes, readable generated C, and real-pilot evidence where the desktop is available.
acceptance_criteria: The base content manifest and generated adapter validate unique stable block IDs/codes for sand, wood, leaves, snow, and ash; World/Water storage treats them as exact solids without confusing fluid ranges; TerrainAtlas selects reviewed base/adventure cells and face roles for grass, dirt, stone, bedrock, sand, wood, leaves, snow, and ash; the first-playable CAXEMAP—not Main or renderer code—contains representative authored placements; Caxecraft loads/unloads both terrain atlases and submits no more than one opaque batch per ready atlas plus the existing water batch; focused Eval/native, map/pack, playable, strict/sanitizer, runtime/allocation, generated-C readability, and graphical pilot evidence pass or unavailable desktop evidence remains explicitly unclaimed.
close_reason: Stable authored materials, two-atlas rendering, authoritative map placements, and non-graphical evidence are complete; desktop visual evidence remains explicitly unclaimed as permitted by acceptance.

title: Admit consecutive compiler-generated Boolean flow carriers
description: Caxecraft's natural interpolation assertions use three inlined range checks in one lazy Boolean guard. Pinned Haxe emits consecutive uninitialized compiler temporaries, then exhaustive branches that assign both. haxe.c recognizes one such flow carrier but rejects the first when another proven carrier appears before its assigning branch.
design: Extend the existing structural proof, not general uninitialized-local support: an uninitialized prelude temporary may be skipped only when that second exact variable is itself independently proven to be exhaustively assigned later in the same sequence. Retain fail-closed authored-local behavior and explicit defensive initialization.
acceptance_criteria: A minimal FlowCarrierFixture reproduces nested inlined range checks; Eval and native strict C at O0/O2 agree; generated C is structured, runtime-free, heap-free, and goto-free; existing uninitialized-local negatives remain exact; the natural Caxecraft presentation test compiles without source reshaping.
notes: Fixed the general typed-tree shape. The sequence proof now admits a later uninitialized carrier only after independently proving its exact exhaustive assignment, and it recognizes that nested carrier's assigning branch as a prelude before the outer carrier. Added a natural three-inline-range FlowCarrierFixture and structured-C check. Verified test:evaluation-order, test:body-lowering (including exact fail-closed diagnostics), and the new Caxecraft presentation Eval/native strict-C sanitizer lane. No runtime, heap, raw C workaround, or goto was introduced.
close_reason: Closed

title: Preserve owned-child borrows through inlined instance methods
description: A final embedded child can receive a direct method call, but an inline method on that same child introduces Haxe local _this and haxe.c rejects it as owned-class-borrow-escape. CaxecraftApp exposes this when its final GameSession child calls the inline replaceLocalPlayer method from run.
design: Treat this from an admitted instance method as a borrow valid for that call, just as constructor this already is. Permit only the same-function automatic alias created by inlining; retain the existing borrow marker so return, storage, throw, constructor capture, and unproven forwarding still fail closed. Add a minimal constructor-lowering fixture that forces the pinned Haxe front end to create the inline _this alias.
acceptance_criteria: A final owned child may call an inline instance method from its parent instance method; HxcIR retains the child address and bounded alias without copying or heap ownership; existing owned-borrow escape negatives still fail at their exact boundaries; focused Eval/native/strict C/sanitizer constructor evidence passes; CaxecraftApp compiles with a final GameSession child and selects no goto, heap, or hxrt machinery.
notes: Reduced with an explicit inline OwnedCounter.addInline fixture that makes pinned Haxe introduce the same child receiver alias as Caxecraft GameSession.replaceLocalPlayer. The lowerer now recognizes current-this only at direct owned-child alias formation and binds the compiler alias directly to the existing borrowed value ID; it does not create a second addressable HxcIR local or ownership slot. Existing return/store/throw/forward escape checks remain active, and the owned_return negative retains its exact owned-class-borrow diagnostic. Documented the rule in constructor-lowering.md. Verified registered constructor snapshots, Eval oracle, strict C11 O0/O2 native execution, C++17 public-header consumer, deterministic reports, all existing negative fixtures, and Caxecraft compile-only with final embedded GameSession. Generated C selects no goto, heap, or hxrt.
close_reason: Closed

title: Introduce CaxecraftApp as the outer application owner
description: Main still owns the complete Raylib lifecycle and frame loop even though the accepted architecture gives that responsibility to CaxecraftApp. Establish the real application object without changing gameplay, drawing, pilot, or resource behavior.
design: Move the existing validated Raylib run scope and its private presentation helpers into one CaxecraftApp instance. Keep Main as the executable boundary that constructs the app and calls run. This is an ownership move, not a license to keep a permanent monolith: document the remaining input, rendering, and gameplay migrations, and retain the existing deterministic evidence before extracting those slices.
acceptance_criteria: Main only constructs CaxecraftApp and calls run; CaxecraftApp owns current Raylib startup/shutdown, texture lifetime, screen state, input polling, accumulator, drawing, and pilot presentation; no implementation is duplicated; Eval/native pilot and canonical playable evidence preserve behavior; generated split C has distinct readable Main and CaxecraftApp modules with no new goto, heap, or hxrt machinery; documentation distinguishes this shipped owner from still-pending presentation/input/interpolation extraction.
notes: Implemented the real outer owner. Main.hx now only constructs one CaxecraftApp and calls run. CaxecraftApp owns a final embedded GameSession, Raylib startup/shutdown, texture lifetime, input, screen state, accumulator, drawing, and pilot presentation; no loop or helper was duplicated. Source guards keep Main free of Raylib/session/loop authority and keep localization/HUD checks pointed at the new owner. The playable verifier requires a <=30-line split Main.c, distinct CaxecraftApp.c, and a by-value GameSession field. The natural final-child design exposed compiler child haxe_c-xge.20.4.2.3.4.1; that general inline-owned-borrow fix is closed with full constructor evidence. Verified: constructor-lowering; Caxecraft compile-only; caxecraft pilot/source contract; localization; canonical caxecraft-domain updater and validation across Eval/split/package/unity/native O2/maintainability; real macOS Raylib build-only link; all-sources; capabilities; typed-boundaries; git diff --check; governance 125 tests. Generated Main.c shrank from 2,220 lines to 16; CaxecraftApp directly embeds GameSession; no new goto, heap, or hxrt. Remaining external check: this tool process has no GUI desktop session, so the actual screenshot-producing Raylib pilot was not rerun. The existing open sibling haxe_c-xge.20.4.2.3.2 already owns that exact desktop recapture proof; do not claim it passed here.
close_reason: CaxecraftApp now owns the application lifecycle with thin Main, distinct generated modules, preserved domain/playable/native evidence, and no new goto, heap, or hxrt; the separate screen-state task retains desktop recapture evidence.

title: Allow imported by-value C structs inside closed Haxe records
description: Caxecraft's typed HudResources record exposes a compiler inconsistency: haxe.c admits a semantic abstract over raylib Texture2D as a direct parameter, return, local, and call argument, but closed-record shape discovery unwraps the abstract/import alias and then misclassifies the same header-owned struct as a Haxe reference.
design: Teach CBodyAggregate structural identity to recognize imported direct value types through CImportRegistry before primitive fallback. Key the closed-record field by its validated semantic HxcIR representation, keep the authoritative C header as layout owner, and reuse normal imported-type planning/emission. Reduce this to the c-import fixture with a record containing a header-owned struct and a readiness scalar. Retain fail-closed behavior for non-imported references, pointers, open records, and unsupported ABI types.
acceptance_criteria: An ordinary immutable Haxe record may contain an already-admitted header-owned by-value struct or transparent typedef/semantic abstract over it; its shape is deterministic across module order and aliases; HxcIR and generated C retain the exact imported struct field; strict C/C++ native consumers, sanitizers, runtime-free checks, and snapshots pass; unsupported Haxe reference fields remain HXC1001; Caxecraft HudResources compiles without raw C, metadata, or positional-parameter fallback.
notes: Fixed closed-record structural identity to consult the existing typed C-import registry before primitive/reference fallback. The authoritative header continues to own foreign layout; the private record hashes the validated semantic imported instance. Evidence: c-import fixture PointResources contains pointlib_point plus Bool; cold/repeated/reverse-order renders, exact source/header checks, strict -O0/-O2 native matrix, runtime absence and fail-closed edges pass; Caxecraft HudResources now compiles to named structs with direct Texture fields, empty hxrt plan, no goto/allocation/raw C, and the target-neutral pilot boundary passes.
close_reason: Closed

title: Replace Caxecraft HUD scalar arguments with immutable views
description: Main currently calls drawHud with a long positional list that mixes committed gameplay observations, short-lived presentation feedback, locale, counters, and Raylib textures. This makes call-site mistakes easy and hides the intended read-only presentation boundary.
design: Introduce a target-neutral immutable HudView made only from values that drawing may observe, plus a separate presentation-owned HudResources record for Raylib textures and readiness. Main constructs the snapshot after simulation commits; HUD drawing receives the snapshot and resources but no GameSession or mutable storage. Preserve current pixels and localization behavior. Keep content migration status explicit rather than claiming that authored Nia/Mossling prompts are already data-driven.
acceptance_criteria: drawHud no longer has a long scalar parameter list; HudView contains no Raylib type, GameSession, mutable span, or storage authority; texture ownership stays in an explicit resources value; current playable snapshots and pilot contracts do not drift unintentionally; source guards prevent reintroducing the scalar list; generated split C remains readable, warning-clean, and free of new goto/hxrt/heap machinery for the view.
notes: Implemented HudView as a target-neutral immutable post-simulation observation snapshot and HudResources as a separate C-only borrowed Raylib resource bundle. Main now constructs one named view after simulation commits and calls drawHud(view, resources); source guards reject the old scalar signature and storage/session authority. Caxecraft exposed a general compiler gap for imported by-value structs inside closed records; child haxe_c-xge.20.4.2.3.3.1 fixed that through the typed import plan and closed with focused c-import evidence. Verified: npm run test:c-import; python3 examples/caxecraft/play.py --compile-only; npm run test:caxecraft-pilot; canonical caxecraft-domain snapshot update/validation across Eval, split/package/unity, native O2, maintainability, runtime/allocation absence; npm run test:capabilities; npm run test:typed-boundaries; git diff --check; npm run test:governance (125 tests). Generated Main_drawHud takes exactly two named structs and the relevant generated C contains no goto, hxrt, or heap calls.
close_reason: Closed

title: Lower equality for payload-free Haxe enum values
description: Caxecraft's closed AppScreen state exposed that haxe.c can construct and switch on a payload-free Haxe enum, but rejects ordinary == and != between two values of that enum as closed-record-not-admitted-in-primitive-operation. Haxe permits this comparison and a C programmer would expect a direct tag comparison.
design: Reduce the failure into the enum-lowering compiler corpus. Admit equality and inequality only when both operands are the same payload-free enum representation and compare their deterministic C tags directly. Preserve Haxe evaluation order, reject mismatched or payload-carrying enum comparisons unless their complete semantics are separately implemented, and add positive, negative, generated-C, Eval/native, runtime-free, and sanitizer evidence.
acceptance_criteria: The minimal enum fixture compiles == and != for the same payload-free enum; generated C compares enum tags without allocation, hxrt, goto, or raw C; Eval and strict native C agree; mismatched or unsupported enum shapes still fail closed with source-positioned diagnostics; Caxecraft AppScreenProbe passes without rewriting its natural equality assertions.
notes: Implemented target-earned HxcIR operations haxe.enum-tag.equal/not-equal for matching payload-free direct enums. CBodyLowering preserves left-to-right evaluation, HxcIRValidator rejects mismatched and payload-carrying enum operands, and CAST emission uses ordinary C ==/!=. Evidence: npm run test:enum-lowering; hxc-ir snapshot updater/validator; python3 examples/caxecraft/run_haxe_c_test.py app-screen; generated modeEquality C contains no goto, allocation, or hxrt; npm run test:caxecraft-pilot; npm run test:caxecraft-playable.
close_reason: Closed

title: Replace loose Caxecraft screen booleans with a closed state
description: Main currently represents title, play, pause, and cursor capture with three mutable booleans whose valid combinations are implicit. Introduce one target-neutral closed AppScreen state and small transition/query functions, then derive pause and capture behavior from that state so invalid combinations cannot be represented.
design: Use a Haxe enum with Title, Playing, and Paused variants. Keep Raylib cursor effects in Main; the state module owns only deterministic transitions and queries. Start launch/resize pilots on Title and other pilots on Playing. Preserve title start, focus-loss pause, pause toggle, explicit recapture, fixed-tick gating, HUD, and pilot telemetry. Add focused target-neutral tests and retain native pilot evidence.
acceptance_criteria: One AppScreen value replaces onTitle/paused/captured mutable state in Main; queries and transitions are documented and exhaustively matched; title, focus-loss, pause, resume, and capture transitions have focused Haxe assertions; no Raylib dependency enters AppScreen; PauseRecapture and playable snapshot/native structure gates pass; generated C remains readable and does not gain goto/hxrt/heap machinery for this state.
notes: Implemented target-neutral AppScreen (Title/Playing/Paused), replaced Main's loose onTitle/paused/captured mutable booleans with one closed state, kept Raylib cursor side effects at the application edge, documented the shipped state architecture, and added Eval/native-C assertions as test:caxecraft-app-screen in the exact CI shard. Evidence passes: app-screen Eval/native/sanitizers/runtime-free; enum-lowering; hxc-ir validator; caxecraft pilot contract; playable snapshots/direct-C invariants; capabilities; full governance (125 tests). The earlier desktop attachment limitation is now resolved by the pinned Raylib 6.0 memory/software lane: pause-recapture compiled the real game, presented a validated 1280x720 frame, completed 7 frames/5 fixed ticks twice with identical reports, ended Playing (paused=false) with cursorCaptured=true, submitted exactly three terrain batches, and exited cleanly within the bound.
close_reason: One closed AppScreen now owns title/playing/paused state; focused target-neutral/native gates and the real deterministic Raylib pause/recapture pilot all pass without hxrt, heap, or control-flow workarounds.

title: Publish the first immutable GameView snapshot
description: Introduce the first renderer-neutral read model from GameSession. Presentation, telemetry, and later application extraction need one immutable snapshot of the committed local character and deterministic clock instead of separate mutable-session reads.
design: Define a small target-neutral GameView record containing validity, the committed local Character snapshot, and completed tick count. GameSession.view constructs it without exposing EntityStore, storage spans, WaterSimulation, or mutation methods. Main reads the view at frame boundaries; the existing replaceLocalPlayer migration seam remains only for gameplay work not yet moved into tick. Keep world rendering on its separately tracked friend-view seam until a bounded world-view design is earned.
acceptance_criteria: GameSession.view returns an immutable renderer-neutral snapshot whose validity follows the local-player binding and whose completedTicks matches the session clock. Main uses GameView rather than calling readLocalPlayer or completedTickCount directly. Focused Eval/native tests cover unbound and committed views; generated Main calls GameSession_view and retains no direct session-clock read; snapshots, playable/direct-C checks, strict C, sanitizers, runtime/allocation checks, all-sources, and governance pass.
notes: Added immutable renderer-neutral GameView with explicit validity, committed local Character, and completed-tick count. GameSession.view is the sole producer; Main consumes initial/committed frame snapshots and no longer calls readLocalPlayer or completedTickCount directly. The generated app calls GameSession_view and contains no EntityStore_read; structural checks retain that boundary and forbid a duplicate update counter. The first mid-loop break shape was reviewed and replaced with a fail-closed quit flag to keep generated Main.c flat and readable. Focused Eval/native sanitizer evidence, registered split/package/unity differential and snapshots, playable direct-C checks, zero hxrt/allocation, all-sources (563 Haxe files), governance, Python syntax, and git diff checks pass. Repeated proven receiver null guards remain separately owned by haxe_c-xge.20.4.2.1.1.
close_reason: GameSession now publishes a tested immutable GameView and presentation no longer reads EntityStore directly.

title: Make GameSession own the deterministic tick clock
description: Move the authoritative completed-tick count out of Main and into GameSession. Real frame time and the accumulator remain platform/application concerns, while the session records only successfully committed fixed simulation steps.
design: Add a private completed-tick counter to GameSession, expose a narrow read method, and return the committed tick index/count in GameTickResult. A rejected tick must leave the clock and all previously guarded simulation state unchanged. Main uses the session-owned clock for actor scheduling, HUD, and pilot telemetry without gaining a second counter. Do not move Raylib frame time, pause state, or content-specific actor behavior into this slice.
acceptance_criteria: GameSession starts at tick zero, increments exactly once after each successful commit, and does not increment on a missing/mismatched local-player rejection. Main has no mutable updateCount or equivalent authoritative tick counter. Focused Eval/native session evidence covers clock behavior; registered domain/playable snapshots, strict C, sanitizers, runtime/allocation and generated-C readability checks, all-sources, and governance pass.
notes: GameSession now embeds completedTicks, returns a zero-based tickIndex only for committed steps, and exposes a read-only completedTickCount. Main has no updateCount and uses the session clock for Mossling scheduling, HUD, and pilot telemetry while retaining only the real-time accumulator. The focused probe proves missing-player rejection stays at tick zero and successive commits report indices 0/1 with counts 1/2. The registered Caxecraft updater passed Eval, split/package/unity differential, strict native/O2, zero hxrt/allocation and maintainability checks; playable snapshots/direct-C invariants, all-sources, governance, sanitizers, Python syntax, and git diff checks pass. Generated GameSession C uses one direct int32 field with no goto, heap calls, or hxrt, and structural checks forbid a second app-level update counter.
close_reason: GameSession now owns deterministic fixed-tick time and the focused/native/playable/governance evidence passes.

title: Admit nonescaping local aliases of stack-backed class values
description: Caxecraft reads a freshly constructed GameSession through ordinary inline methods. Haxe 5 introduces a local _this alias, and constructor escape analysis rejects the original TNew as stack-reference-escape:local-alias even though the alias is used only for field and method reads inside the same function.
design: Reduce the typed shape in the constructor-lowering fixtures. Track local aliases of stack-backed class references through the same bounded nonescape proof used by direct borrows. Admit only same-function field/method uses and forwarding whose lifetime is already proven; retain rejection for returns, field storage, aggregate capture, unknown calls, and other escapes. Do not special-case Haxe generated names or Caxecraft.
acceptance_criteria: A minimal local-alias fixture lowers to direct stack storage and executes under strict C/C++ and sanitizers; a bounded automatic alias that is later stored, returned, thrown, captured, or forwarded remains rejected; HxcIR and generated-C snapshots are deterministic and runtime/allocation free; the natural Caxecraft session test compiles unchanged.
notes:
The exact Haxe 5 reduction aliases an inline owned child field (session.entities) through generated local _this. The implemented rule admits direct local and embedded-child aliases only, carries stack provenance to the alias compiler ID, and leaves borrowed function-parameter local aliases outside this slice.
Implemented direct same-function aliases for stack-backed class references and embedded owned-child addresses. The alias compiler ID retains stack provenance; escape_alias now proves a later static-field store is rejected as a real assignment escape. The registered constructor snapshot shows one ordinary pointer local. test:constructor-lowering and the natural Caxecraft session test passed with strict native and sanitizer evidence.
close_reason: Bounded class aliases now preserve stack lifetime and reject later escapes, with constructor and Caxecraft regressions passing.

title: Make GameSession own the local-player binding
description: Remove the duplicate local PlayerAgent value from Main. GameSession must bind the one admitted local character atomically, use that binding for fixed ticks, and expose narrow read/replace operations until the remaining gameplay mutations move inside the session.
design: Store the small immutable PlayerAgent value inside GameSession. Replace the public ID-shaped tick request with controller-neutral one-tick intent plus policy and water budget; resolve the bound character internally. Keep EntityStore as the one character owner and preserve its stable ID checks. Do not add Nia, Mossling, Raylib, inventory, or content-specific state to GameSession in this slice.
acceptance_criteria: Main creates and binds the local character through GameSession and holds no PlayerAgent or local-character ID after construction. GameSession.tick resolves and commits the bound character internally; missing or mismatched bindings fail closed. The aquatics/session Eval-native tests, strict C, sanitizers, playable snapshots, generated-C readability/runtime-free checks, all-sources, and governance pass.
notes: GameSession now owns PlayerAgent, binds it only after EntityStore accepts the character, and resolves the stable ID internally for tick/read/temporary replace. Main carries neither PlayerAgent nor local-character ID. A missing binding rejects before water work, and the session test proves the pending queue is unchanged. Aquatics/session Eval-native sanitizer lanes, combined domain snapshots, playable structural checks, all-sources, governance, zero-goto/allocation/runtime inspection, and git diff checks passed.
close_reason: GameSession now owns and resolves the local-player binding, with fail-closed tick semantics and integrated evidence passing.

title: Lower checked indexing of owned CArray fields
description: A nonescaping class can own an inline CArray field, but array access lowered only when the collection was a local variable. Natural field[index] reads and writes failed even though the field layout and short-lived span borrow were already supported.
design: Resolve an indexed collection to a typed HxcIR place. Admit fixed-array instance fields, emit the same static or checked bounds policy as local CArray access, and key validator proofs by the exact stable field place and index. Keep whole-array assignment and escaping values rejected.
acceptance_criteria: The span fixture and Caxecraft session use direct checked field indexing; HxcIR validates the exact field-place bounds proof; snapshots, strict C/C++ consumers, sanitizer runs, negative bounds cases, and runtime-free evidence pass.
notes: Generalized checked indexing to exact HxcIR places for class-owned CArray fields and extended validator proof keys to field places. Direct field writes are covered by span snapshots, strict native consumers, sanitizer checks, and the Caxecraft session probe. test:span-lowering passed in 74.510 seconds.
close_reason: Owned fixed-array field indexing and exact-place bounds proofs implemented and verified.

title: Keep loop-local normal joins within the current iteration
description: A conditional inside a natural loop can have one arm that returns and other arms that meet before continuing. Normal-join analysis walked through the loop header into future iterations, so a later iteration made the current abrupt arm look reachable from the join and the structural planner tried to emit the join twice.
design: Treat active break and continue targets as reachability boundaries while proving the current branch normal join. Retain the existing disjoint-prefix and explicit-terminal proof; do not add a goto fallback.
acceptance_criteria: A focused evaluation-order fixture with assignment, nested returning else-if, join, and loop continuation emits structured C once per block; existing control-flow planning tests, generated output, strict native builds, and Caxecraft session assembly pass.
notes: Bound normal-join reachability at active loop break and continue targets. The exact loop-local return/join reproducer now emits structured C without replay or goto fallback. test:evaluation-order and test:caxecraft-session passed.
close_reason: Loop-local join ownership fixed and verified with structured generated C.

title: Lower compiler-generated temporaries in short-circuit validation expressions
description: Caxecraft natural level validation expression combines several pure typed calls with &&/||. Haxe 5 types that expression with a compiler-generated uninitialized temporary (TVar tmp:uninitialized), and haxe.c rejects it with HXC1001 before short-circuit lowering. Implement the general typed-expression rule instead of splitting the application expression as a workaround.
design: Add the smallest source fixture reproducing the typed shape, inspect the Haxe TypedExpr, and lower only semantically valid compiler-generated temporaries through HxcIR. Preserve left-to-right short-circuit evaluation, definite assignment, source spans, and fail-closed rejection for genuinely uninitialized reads. Do not special-case Caxecraft names or weaken general local initialization safety.
acceptance_criteria: A focused positive fixture using chained call-based validation lowers and runs with exact Eval/native parity; a genuine uninitialized-local negative remains source-positioned and rejected; HxcIR validation/dump, generated C, strict native compilers, sanitizers, and the Caxecraft session test pass without rewriting the natural validation expression.
notes: Implemented sequenceFlowInitializesLocal in CBodyLowering. The focused FlowCarrier evaluation-order fixture proves compiler-generated prelude temporaries are initialized before exhaustive flow assignment, while genuine uninitialized reads remain rejected. test:evaluation-order and test:caxecraft-session passed.
close_reason: General compiler rule implemented and verified by evaluation-order and Caxecraft session regressions.

title: Move validated built-in level assembly behind GameSession
description: Remove Main's direct mutation of GameSession world, pending-water, and authored-item buffers during startup. The temporary generated first-playable adapter may remain the data carrier until runtime CAXEMAP loading, but one typed assembly boundary must validate and populate an unpublished session before the application uses it.
design: Add narrow GameSession loading operations that create their own short-lived buffer views. Add a content-bridge loader that consumes the generated adapter without moving campaign-specific facts into the engine session. Keep the new session unpublished until all terrain, fluid, item, spawn, and presentation facts validate. Do not expose or retain spans, add raw C, or imply runtime CAXEMAP support.
acceptance_criteria: Main constructs a candidate GameSession through one typed first-playable assembly call and does not directly reset/populate its world, pending-water, or authored-item storage. Invalid generated facts fail before Raylib startup and before the candidate is treated as live. Eval/native behavior, generated-C ownership/readability, runtime-free/allocation evidence, level-adapter freshness, and focused Caxecraft snapshots pass.
notes: Main now constructs a fresh candidate through FirstPlayableSessionLoader before Raylib starts. GameSession owns terrain, water, and item assembly operations; the generated adapter remains explicitly temporary until runtime CAXEMAP loading. Eval/native session parity, runtime-free sanitizers, adapter freshness, combined domain snapshots, playable structural checks, all-sources, toolchain policy, and governance passed. The generated session loader contains zero gotos.
close_reason: Validated first-playable assembly now belongs behind GameSession, with focused and integrated evidence passing.

title: Admit nonescaping borrowed class parameters in direct calls
description: GameSession storage integration requires ordinary Haxe loaders and focused helpers to receive a nonescaping session for the duration of one direct call. The compiler currently rejects every constructed class argument as an escape, even when the callee only calls methods or reads/writes fields and cannot retain the reference. Add a bounded borrowed class-parameter contract for reached direct non-generic calls so a stack-owned object remains owned by its caller and the callee receives only a temporary view.
design: Represent the parameter's non-owning lifetime explicitly in the typed lowering/HxcIR contract. Admit only compiler-known direct calls whose complete callee body is validated not to return, store, alias, capture, forward to an unproven target, construct into, or otherwise retain the parameter. Preserve nullability, exact class identity/upcasts, evaluation order, and existing owned-child rules. Calls from unknown/native/virtual/interface/closure/exported boundaries remain fail-closed. Emit an ordinary private C pointer parameter with no allocation or runtime feature.
acceptance_criteria: A positive caller-owned GameSession-like fixture passes a constructed parent to a direct helper that performs field and method operations, preserving identity and mutation. Returning, storing, local aliasing, unsafe forwarding, constructor capture, and unsupported dispatch fail at exact source positions. HxcIR validation/dumps make the borrow inspectable; strict GCC/Clang C11 and C++ consumers at O0/O2, sanitizers, deterministic snapshots, no allocation/hxrt, and the real Caxecraft GameSession loader/test path pass.
notes: Implemented schema-11 borrowed class-parameter ownership for proven direct calls. Positive constructor coverage preserves mutation and identity through an ordinary private C pointer; source negatives cover return, local alias, constructor capture, and unsafe forwarding, while HxcIR negatives reject return and storage escapes. AquaticsProbe now passes a real stack-owned GameSession through prepareSession/placeSessionLayer helpers, then advances the same session. Constructor, HxcIR, class-layout, Caxecraft Eval/native sanitizer, zero-runtime/allocation, deterministic snapshot, all-source, typed-boundary, capability, and governance gates passed.
close_reason: Implemented and verified bounded nonescaping borrowed class parameters in direct calls, including the real Caxecraft GameSession test path.

title: Admit region-safe composition of nonescaping Haxe class instances
description: GameSession must compose the existing EntityStore and other cohesive stateful owners without flattening them into duplicate fields or allocating them through a general heap. Today a constructed class reference cannot be passed to a constructor, assigned into a field, or otherwise escape its direct local. Add a bounded ownership representation in which one nonescaping parent stack object owns a directly constructed nonescaping child for the same lexical lifetime.
design: Use explicit HxcIR ownership and lifetime facts, not pointer-pattern rewriting. Admit only concrete non-generic classes with one clear parent owner, deterministic construction order, embedded or otherwise equivalently safe strict-C storage, stable identity, non-null child access, and reverse cleanup. Reject aliases, cycles, nullable replacement, child escape, parent escape, independent reassignment, polymorphic ownership ambiguity, and any lifetime the compiler cannot prove. Preserve ordinary Haxe source and do not invent target-only application annotations unless evidence proves one is necessary.
acceptance_criteria: A focused parent/child fixture proves construction order, identity, child method and field mutation, cleanup order, and no allocation/runtime features. Alias, cycle, returned child, passed child, parent escape, nullable/reassigned child, throwing construction, inheritance/virtual ambiguity, and unsupported generic cases fail closed or receive separately proven semantics. HxcIR validation, strict Clang/GCC C11 plus C++ consumers at O0/O2, sanitizers, deterministic output, readable generated C, and GameSession composing EntityStore pass.
notes: Implemented the general owned-child slice without application annotations: a proven nonescaping parent may embed an exact final child initialized by an infallible constructor. HxcIR represents the child by value, validates finite direct layout, tracks derived child references as nonescaping borrows, and structural C emits dependencies before parents, binds virtual tables before child construction, and uses stable field addresses. Added positive order/identity/mutation/C++ layout evidence plus fail-closed mutable, returned, passed, fallible, cycle, parent-escape, native, and generic cases. Caxecraft GameSession now owns EntityStore and WaterSimulation and its fixed tick passes Eval/native C with ASan/UBSan and no hxrt. Constructor, class-layout, virtual-dispatch, HxcIR, project-layout, playable snapshot, typed-boundary, capability, fixture, and CI policy gates passed. Repeated redundant nonnull checks are separately owned by haxe_c-xge.20.4.2.1.1.
close_reason: Region-safe nonescaping parent/child composition is implemented, documented, fail-closed outside the bounded model, native/sanitizer verified, and consumed by Caxecraft GameSession.

title: Admit inline fixed-array fields in nonescaping Haxe classes
description: GameSession must own world, pending-water, and authored-item buffers. Today c.CArray is admitted only as automatic local storage, and c.Span borrows may begin only from such locals. Add a bounded compiler-owned representation for positive compile-time-sized c.CArray fields in a concrete nonescaping class. A zero initializer establishes the field length and the enclosing stack object owns the bytes; a method or the enclosing function may create a scoped Span or ConstSpan from that field without returning or storing the borrow. Preserve exact Haxe lifetime, bounds, and initialization semantics without raw C, global storage, heap allocation, or a Caxecraft special case.
design: Extend HxcIR and structural C emission only as much as needed for an inline fixed-array member and a scoped borrow from an addressable class-field place. Keep fixed-array values non-copyable. Validate class-layout size and alignment, one complete zero initialization before use, receiver non-null proof, borrow origin/lifetime, element type, witness identity, length, and storage budget. The printer only renders the validated declarator.
acceptance_criteria: A focused positive class fixture owns and mutates zero-initialized UInt8 and Int fixed-array fields through scoped mutable and const spans; invalid dynamic/zero/oversized lengths, whole-array assignment/copy, returned or stored borrows, nullable unsafe access, unsupported elements, and escaping owner lifetimes fail at exact source positions. HxcIR and CAST validation, strict Clang/GCC C11 and C++ consumers at O0/O2, sanitizers, deterministic snapshots, no allocation/hxrt, and a Caxecraft GameSession consumer pass.
notes:
Implemented and documented the general inline-owned-array slice: concrete nonescaping classes may own zero-initialized CArray fields, methods may take scoped Span/ConstSpan borrows from those fields, HxcIR validation ties bounds proofs to the typed field place, and CAST emits direct C array members with no allocation or hxrt. Added exact negative diagnostics for missing/dynamic/zero/oversized/unsupported initialization and whole-array assignment, deterministic snapshots, strict C11 O0/O2/sanitizer execution, and a C++17 layout consumer. Full span suite passed (66 Haxe requests, 74.279 s); typed-boundary, HxcIR, class-layout, constructor-lowering, capability, and instruction gates passed. Keep open until GameSession is the real Caxecraft consumer required by acceptance.
Acceptance completed: GameSession is now the real consumer and directly owns UInt8 world/pending arrays of 16,384 cells plus 256 Int authored-item slots. The playable/domain split snapshot shows those arrays embedded in the GameSession C struct, tick derives scoped spans internally, and the runtime plan remains allocation- and hxrt-free. Caxecraft Eval/split/package/unity/native O2 differential and maintainability gates passed. The full 66-request span suite passed in 75.588 s, alongside HxcIR, class layout, constructors, aquatics sanitizers, all-sources, capabilities, typed boundaries, and governance.
close_reason: Implemented and verified general inline fixed-array class fields with scoped span borrows and the required real GameSession consumer.

title: Build the typed runtime actor composition path
description: Build one content-driven runtime path for NPCs, enemies, companions, and world objects inside GameSession. Character-like actors reuse the movement, aquatics, and vitals foundation, then generalize inventory, equipment, weapons, interaction, and effects through the same shared component pattern as real non-player consumers arrive. Roles differ through controllers, validated profiles, and authored capabilities. Replace character-specific application variables and classes without committing Caxecraft to a general ECS.
design: Use stable EntityId ownership, a typed EntityStore or ActorStore boundary, shared Character composition, and the smallest closed non-character roles needed by shipped content. Player, AI, companion, scripted, cutscene, and test controllers produce common typed intents. Content packs define mechanic and presentation profiles; CaxeMap places stable instances; CaxeFlow uses descriptor-backed typed actions; the visual and text editor discover the same schema. Behaviors execute only through ordinary GameSession systems. Favor composition and explicit dependencies. Avoid nullable field clouds, subclasses, macro-injected behavior, Dynamic bags, reflection queries, string dispatch, duplicated script simulators, or a full archetype scheduler. Keep storage private so later evidence can justify a different layout without changing content.
acceptance_criteria: Validated CaxeMap and content data construct all live NPC, enemy, companion, and world-object actors with stable IDs. Nia, Mossling, Ivvy, and Browser are authored compositions rather than source subclasses or Main variables. Every eligible actor reuses shared movement, water, life, inventory, equipment, weapon, interaction, and effect systems; role-specific behavior is limited to justified controllers, profiles, presentation, and authored policy. The same typed descriptors expose authorized operations to CaxeFlow, editor cards and text completion, cutscenes, console, and CaxeTest, and all execute through the normal GameSession path. Unknown IDs and capability mismatches fail before session publication; creation/removal is command-boundary work; iteration and save ordering are deterministic. Eval/native traces, content negatives, editor test-play, PilotScript, generated-C readability/layout, allocation/runtime plan, update budget, strict compilers, and sanitizers pass. ECS admission metrics are recorded without requiring a general ECS.
notes: Queued after the shared action-descriptor dependency haxe_c-xge.19.9. The application/presentation migration is complete, but runtime actors must consume the one registry rather than invent a parallel command surface.

title: Separate Caxecraft presentation and the outer application loop
description: Extract the Raylib frame loop, screen lifecycle, and presentation from Main after GameSession owns simulation. Rendering and audio should consume read-only views and committed events, while CaxecraftApp owns window/input/resource lifetime and closed screen transitions.
design: CaxecraftApp.run polls platform events and input once per frame, bounds elapsed time, invokes zero or more fixed GameSession ticks through the accumulator, renders once, and presents. Preserve prior/current authoritative transforms and use accumulator interpolation only for presentation. Replace loose title/pause/capture booleans with closed screen state. Produce GameView, PlayerView, and HudView shapes that prevent long scalar parameter lists and contain no mutable simulation access.
acceptance_criteria: Main only constructs CaxecraftApp and calls run; CaxecraftApp owns Raylib startup/shutdown, resource lifetime, input sampling, frame accumulator, screen changes, and presentation; GameSession remains Raylib-free; rendering, HUD, camera, audio, and telemetry consume read-only views/events; fixed-tick state is never changed by drawing; transform interpolation removes visible fixed-step motion without changing collision, traces, or saves; title/loading/playing/paused/editor/settings/exit transitions are closed and tested; resize/focus/input, PilotScript, screenshot evidence, draw/update budgets, resource cleanup, strict native/sanitizer, and generated-C readability pass.
notes: Completed as four behavior-preserving vertical slices. Main is now a 19-line entry boundary that constructs CaxecraftApp and calls run. CaxecraftApp owns Raylib startup/shutdown, native resources, input polling, the outer frame loop, fixed-step scheduling, closed AppScreen transitions, presentation, and telemetry. GameSession remains the simulation owner; GameView and HudView give presentation immutable snapshots instead of long mutable/scalar interfaces, and MotionInterpolation changes display sampling without changing authoritative ticks. Focused Eval/native/sanitizer/runtime-free gates, generated project/snapshot/maintainability checks, and the real pinned Raylib memory/software move-jump-edit and pause-recapture pilots pass twice with bounded exits. Further decomposition of the intentionally visible first-playable/content seams belongs to typed runtime actor composition haxe_c-xge.20.4.2.4, not this native-lifetime ownership slice.
close_reason: Main is startup-only; CaxecraftApp owns the complete native frame/resource lifetime, while GameSession and immutable views preserve simulation and presentation boundaries under focused and real-Raylib evidence.

title: Introduce GameSession and the fixed-tick simulation boundary
description: Establish the stateful foundation for one loaded simulation. GameSession owns the voxel world, pending water work, authored-item activity, EntityStore, local-player binding, WaterSimulation, and deterministic completed-tick clock. A validated built-in candidate is assembled behind this boundary, and one controller-neutral tick advances shared movement, aquatics, vitals, water, and commit order.
design: Preserve the existing outer-frame accumulator in the application layer. GameSession.tick always advances one exact duration, creates storage views only inside its methods, resolves the local player internally, runs bounded environment and character work in documented order, commits atomically at the entity boundary, and increments its clock only after success. Unsupported actor orchestration, CaxeFlow events/commands, read-only presentation views, screen extraction, and full content-driven loading remain explicitly owned by sibling tasks haxe_c-xge.20.4.2.4, haxe_c-xge.19.9, haxe_c-xge.20.4.2.3, and haxe_c-xge.39 rather than being smuggled into this foundation.
acceptance_criteria: GameSession directly owns world, pending-water and authored-item storage, EntityStore, WaterSimulation, the local-player binding, and completed-tick time with no process globals or heap/runtime dependency. The validated built-in loader assembles a candidate through typed session methods before publication. GameSession.tick receives controller-neutral intent, rejects a missing binding before mutation, advances bounded water plus shared movement/aquatics/vitals once, commits under the stable ID, and increments the clock only on success. Main no longer owns those values or performs those shared core steps, but actor/content interactions and presentation remain visibly tracked by their sibling tasks. Eval/native session and aquatics traces, split/package/unity snapshots, strict compilers, sanitizers, generated-C ownership/readability, runtime/allocation plan, all-sources, governance, and playable structural checks pass.
notes: Scope correction on 2026-07-22: the original acceptance also required non-player controllers, CaxeFlow events/commands, read-only views, load swapping, and removal of every gameplay update from Main. Those outcomes are retained on the architecture parent and the already-created actor, action-registry, presentation, and runtime-loader tasks. Keeping them here formed a dependency cycle because those tasks were blocked by this foundation. The shipped foundation now includes all six closed vertical children: fixed-array/class composition, borrowed calls, built-in assembly, local-player ownership, safe local aliases, and the deterministic session clock.
close_reason: The GameSession foundation now owns the loaded core simulation, local-player binding, fixed tick, and deterministic clock with full focused and flagship evidence; actor, action, loader, and presentation extraction remain on their explicit sibling tasks.

title: Define reusable character composition and bind the local player
description: Establish the shared character foundation before GameSession moves the loop. EntityStore owns one Character; PlayerAgent binds human control and player-specific camera or HUD policy to its stable ID; common controller intents, profiles, and focused component APIs establish how NPCs, companions, enemies, bosses, cutscenes, and tests reuse mechanics. Prove the design with the current movement, aquatics, and vitals path rather than waiting for every future system.
design: Use explicit ordinary Haxe: stable nominal IDs, a cohesive Character aggregate, focused serializable component state, closed controller intents and profiles, and deterministic module functions. Migrate the smallest current movement/aquatics/vitals vertical slice and give it a focused non-player consumer or fixture. Empty or disabled capabilities are validated states, not separate player/NPC implementations. Do not introduce inheritance, mixins, macro-injected behavior, a dynamic component bag, Raylib resources, content defaults, or a giant Character update method. Fix general haxe.c gaps rather than flattening back into scalar locals. Inventory, equipment, weapons, interaction, and effects follow the same established pattern under the content-driven actor slice as real consumers arrive.
acceptance_criteria: EntityStore owns each character once with stable typed identity; PlayerAgent refers to the local character by ID and owns only human-control or player-presentation policy. Common controller intent, profile, focused-system, and explicit dependency rules are executable. The current movement, aquatics, and vitals slice has one shared implementation and a focused non-player consumer or fixture. Authored starting values and profiles come from validated content or explicit fixtures. Main/session callers no longer carry the migrated state as unrelated top-level variables. Eval and generated-C traces match; the playable pilot passes; class and enum construction, fields, mutation, identity, representation, allocation/runtime plan, split-C readability, GCC/Clang, optimization, and sanitizers are verified. Remaining mechanics are explicitly owned by haxe_c-xge.20.4.2.4 and do not block introduction of GameSession.
notes: Implemented the first composition slice. Character now owns stable EntityId, CharacterBody, AquaticState and profile, and VitalsState. EntityStore owns one committed value through an intentionally narrow stack-local class; PlayerAgent contains only the local character ID. Main reads one snapshot, advances shared systems, and commits once per frame. The focused AquaticsProbe creates a second non-player character with a different ID, advances both through Character.step and shared damage, compares their results, and rejects cross-ID replacement. Role-neutral module names are CharacterPhysics, Aquatics, and Vitals; the old player-specific files were removed through the registered snapshot updater. Evidence: Eval/native aquatics parity and sanitizers; explicit Apple Clang and Homebrew GCC 16 runs; gameplay and PilotScript probes; linked Raylib build; playable direct-C snapshots; class-layout, constructor-lowering, enum-lowering; full split/package/unity O0/O2/ASan+UBSan differential, determinism, standalone headers, zero hxrt/allocation; all-sources, typed boundaries, formatter, fixture policy, CI policy, and snapshot catalog. The background macOS smoke cannot create a GLFW window, so no framebuffer claim is made; Main now checks IsWindowReady and exits cleanly instead of loading textures after platform initialization fails. Redundant per-field class receiver null guards are separately owned by haxe_c-xge.20.4.2.1.1.
close_reason: Shared character composition, local-player binding, non-player reuse proof, direct generated-C shape, native compiler matrices, and playable integration are implemented and verified. Broader actor/component migration remains owned by haxe_c-xge.20.4.2.4.

title: Establish Caxecraft composition-first runtime architecture
description: Main currently coordinates player motion, aquatics, vitals, inventory, equipment, combat, actors, content, input, fixed updates, rendering, and screens. Replace that coupling incrementally with one runtime architecture for the whole game. Shared character capabilities must serve player, NPC, companion, enemy, boss, cutscene, and test controllers; content and editor surfaces select those mechanics through typed descriptors instead of creating parallel implementations. This is a behavior-preserving compiler QA migration, not a framework rewrite or permission to import a general ECS.
design: Use a functional core with a stateful application/session shell. CaxecraftApp owns platform lifetime and screens; GameSession owns one loaded simulation; EntityStore owns each character once; PlayerAgent binds human input and player-only presentation policy to a character ID. Movement, aquatics, vitals, inventory, equipment, weapons, interaction, and effects are focused components and systems shared by every eligible role. Controllers produce common typed intents; profiles and closed modifiers provide data-driven variation; typed events and commands connect committed results. Validated content selects profiles and CaxeFlow actions through the one descriptor registry owned by haxe_c-xge.19.9, which also supplies editor, cutscene, console, and CaxeTest views with explicit authority. Prefer ordinary Haxe features. Admit a macro only for demonstrated mechanical registry/schema/editor glue; never for copied gameplay behavior, hidden update order, runtime reflection, or executable user content. Do not add a string bus, service locator, dynamic component bag, subclass-per-character tree, or full ECS without measured pressure.
acceptance_criteria: Publish and follow one current-versus-target architecture record covering ownership, dependency direction, fixed-tick order, shared character composition, controller/profile/modifier hooks, typed events and commands, content/editor/script integration, Haxe feature and macro admission, rendering, saves, ECS admission, file organization, rejected alternatives, migration order, and executable gates. Main becomes startup composition only. GameSession owns live level state; EntityStore owns one copy of each character; player and non-player roles reuse the same movement, aquatics, vitals, inventory, equipment, weapon, interaction, and effect rules wherever semantically eligible. A focused non-player fixture or runtime actor proves each generalized slice before it is claimed shared. Authored profiles and descriptor-backed actions expose the same mechanic to allowed CaxeFlow, editor, cutscene, console, and CaxeTest consumers without duplicate simulators. Presentation cannot mutate simulation; saves use stable semantic state. Eval, generated C, native PilotScript, strict compilers, sanitizers, generated-C structure, allocation/runtime plan, compile time, and frame/update budgets cover each vertical slice. No big-bang package move, general ECS, or macro framework is required.
notes: The 2026-07-21 audit confirmed that Main already contains the correct basic timing model: the outer loop is the while condition using WindowShouldClose, and the inner accumulator loop compares against FIXED_SECONDS. The migration extracts ownership rather than inventing another independent loop. Audit counts are a point-in-time complexity signal, not a line-count acceptance gate. Official Godot scene-organization guidance, Bevy ECS concepts, and Flecs entity/component documentation support composition, explicit ownership, focused systems, and a schedule; they do not justify importing a full ECS before actor-query or profiling pressure exists.

title: Load a multi-level campaign manifest and select levels at runtime
description:
## Why

The first native level/UI loader and multi-level campaign work currently
overlap in separate issues. Campaigns should build on one proven runtime
generation boundary rather than reopening the parser, package, or publication
architecture.

## What

After the first runtime level/UI pack is authoritative, add one minimal
campaign manifest that selects levels and connects typed exits to typed
entrances.

## How

Keep each `.caxemap` independently valid. The first vertical contains one entry
level, one second level, one visible transition, and failure recovery that
keeps the current level active. The manifest owns only campaign identity,
level-ID-to-logical-path selection, and the typed transition graph; it does not
absorb terrain, actors, local messages, CaxeFlow, engine storage, or a general
world/scene framework.
acceptance_criteria: The authoritative runtime map/pack/UI path is the prerequisite; formal content-loop percentile measurement remains independent in haxe_c-xge.20.4.3.9 and does not block game progress. One minimal campaign manifest declares a stable campaign ID/version, entry level, level-ID-to-logical-CAXEMAP paths, and typed exit-to-entrance edges; the first vertical loads one second level and performs one visible transition through the existing inactive-generation publication boundary; every level remains independently valid; missing/wrong/cyclic-required destinations fail with actionable diagnostics and leave the current level active; one-level Creative maps require no campaign wrapper; Eval/native/headless traces and one graphical transition pass without a new container, world/scene framework, content-specific Haxe, or Python-generated campaign semantics.
notes:
2026-07-22 runtime-loader audit: the shared CAXEMAP lexer/parser/validator/writer is implemented and strong on Eval, but production haxe.c does not yet admit its ordinary Haxe runtime needs. Native loading is explicitly blocked by String/StringBuf parity (haxe_c-c3s), typed dynamic collections (haxe_c-7d0), Bytes/core I/O (haxe_c-8al), and hosted file adapters (haxe_c-fwg). Keep FirstPlayableLevel as the deterministic temporary adapter; do not duplicate the parser with fixed C arrays, use Raylib as a hidden filesystem runtime, or add game-specific raw C. Resume this issue after those general capabilities have executable evidence.
2026-08-02 prerequisite revalidation: ce14148 completed the authoritative runtime map/pack/UI generation and removed generated product mirrors. Focused runtime/native/sanitizer, playable snapshot, no-build, and governance evidence pass. No campaign manifest or second product CaxeMap exists in the current checkout, so the feature remains genuinely unresolved. The prior blocking edge to aggregate haxe_c-xge.20.4.3 is stale because that aggregate remains open only for the deliberately deferred P3 percentile owner haxe_c-xge.20.4.3.9; the maintainer explicitly prioritized game progress over a strict load-time percentile. Removing that edge does not close or weaken .9 and does not add a speed claim.
Headless tracer haxe_c-xge.39.1 is complete: real manifest plus second map load and publish atomically through generated native C. Remaining parent work is the visible application-shell/Raylib transition and its representative system proof; ZIP transport, save persistence, and editor campaign UI remain separate scope.
Completed by children haxe_c-xge.39.1 and haxe_c-xge.39.2. The first-adventure manifest and Western Falls remain plain staged JSON/CaxeMap runtime data; each map validates independently, the headless owner proves manifest/hash/failure/publication semantics under Eval/native/sanitizers, and the real Raylib app visibly follows the sole Evergrove-to-Western-Falls edge without recompilation. Standalone one-level maps remain valid without a manifest. The parent is intentionally closed at this admitted first vertical only: the broader haxe_c-xge.20.2 still owns campaign expansion, while branching, return travel, saves, campaign authoring UI, ZIP transport/mod discovery, portability qualification, and release claims remain open or deferred and are not implied by this result.
close_reason: The bounded first two-level campaign now loads, transitions visibly at runtime, fails closed, and retains independent focused and graphical evidence.

title: Preserve collection bounds proof across assignment RHS control flow
description: Caxecraft exposed a general lowering defect: a mutable Span index on the left of an assignment is checked before the right-hand side, but a conditional right-hand side moves the eventual store into a join block. The HxcIR validator then cannot see the bounds policy and rejects valid ordinary Haxe. Fix the owning lowering/IR contract rather than restoring an inline or static-class workaround.
design: Keep Haxe left-to-right evaluation and fail-closed bounds behavior. Carry or re-establish a typed bounds proof for the exact collection and index at the post-flow access; do not weaken HxcIR validation. Cover module-level functions and the equivalent class/function shape with a small span-lowering fixture.
acceptance_criteria: A focused span fixture compiles a non-inline function that assigns span[index] = (condition ? a : b), generated C retains a checked access in valid order, strict native output is correct in both branches, existing negative bounds diagnostics remain unchanged, the full span-lowering suite passes, and the Caxecraft water differential/sanitizer lane passes without an application workaround.
notes: Implemented CFG dominance for exact fixed-array/span bounds proofs. A proof may cross into a later basic block only when its complete producer block dominates every path to the access; proof blocks with mid-block failure jumps remain local. Added a negative branch-only proof fixture and the ordinary Haxe span[index] = condition ? a : b positive/native case. Verified registered span snapshot update/full suite (54 requests; strict native and ASan/UBSan), npm run test:hxc-ir, and the Caxecraft Eval/native/sanitizer water lane.
close_reason: Closed

title: Clean stale content inside owned Caxecraft play variants
description: The content-layout migration left the formerly generated scenarios/first-playable/messages.json in an existing launcher-owned build variant. stage_content_catalogs rejected it as foreign even though the verified parent output marker proves the bounded variant belongs to the launcher, preventing normal game startup.
acceptance_criteria: Owned play variants remove exact stale staged files and now-empty directories before copying the current content set. Unmarked destinations still reject unexpected files without deleting them. The focused localization/package test reproduces both cases, and a real build-only launcher run succeeds from the previously affected variant.
close_reason: Closed

title: Admit transient borrowed spans on final-class instance methods
description: Caxecraft water exposed an over-broad haxe.c restriction: every instance method parameter whose type lowers to a borrowed span is rejected, even when the declaring class is final and the span is used only during that direct call. Admit this bounded direct-call case without allowing the span in constructors, fields, returns, virtual/overridable methods, generic specializations, or recursive escape paths. Preserve the existing virtual-span negative diagnostic.
acceptance_criteria: A focused positive fixture passes a mutable or const borrowed span through a method on a final class and runs warning-clean native C. Existing virtual-method, constructor, field, return, recursive, and generic span negatives remain fail-closed. The compiler change is generic and contains no Caxecraft special case.
close_reason: Closed

title: Integrate authored water with packs, maps, rendering, editor, and saves
description: Expose the proven water mechanics through the validated content pack, CaxeMap/CaxeFlow, editor, renderer/audio/HUD, and versioned world/save state. Author the Adventure water route and Tideweave placement as data only after the generic mechanics exist.
design: Extend only the smallest closed schemas earned by the implemented mechanics. The pack declares the water medium/render profile and aquatic equipment capability; CaxeMap owns sources and initial volumes; saves own mutable fluid queue/state plus per-character breath and equipment. Renderer reads simulation state and never advances it. Aquatic movement, buoyancy, breath, drowning, immunity, and Tideweave modifiers are shared character systems: human, AI, companion, enemy, scripted, and test controllers produce the same movement intents and profiles decide variation. Do not hardwire the water contract to PlayerAgent or create NPC-specific swimming.
acceptance_criteria: Built-in water and Tideweave definitions validate; editor authors sources and volumes; canonical map/save round trips preserve fluid and character aquatic state; the same aquatic and vitals rules pass for the local player and at least one focused non-player character fixture; above/below-surface visuals, audio, HUD, loading, and real-Raylib pilot pass; Adventure placement and equipment progression have no content-specific or player-only Haxe branches.
notes:
Checkpoint 2026-07-22: Tideweave is an authored content-pack item and CaxeMap placement consumed through generic storage-code, pickup, renderer, equipment-profile, HUD, and asset paths. Localization uses target-neutral typed lookup catalogs; haxe_c-zcj.2 and haxe_c-xge.38 closed after full Clang plus identity-verified GCC 16 C-import evidence. Aquatics passes Eval/native C with sanitizers and no hxrt. Registered snapshots passed Eval, split/package/unity generation, native O2 differentials, 32 seeded properties, runtime/allocation absence, generated-C maintainability, ownership, and fixture policy. The shared-character architecture still requires a focused non-player aquatic/vitals consumer.

The real graphical water/Tideweave gate now passes through pinned Raylib 6.0 memory/software rendering: AquaticGear completed 96 deterministic frames/ticks twice with identical reports, equipped the authored gear, displayed textured water and the equipment HUD, submitted exactly three terrain batches, captured a validated 1280x720 frame, and exited cleanly within the bound. This replaces the earlier unclaimed desktop attempt.

Still open: audio, full save composition under haxe_c-4my, native runtime content loading under haxe_c-xge.39, the focused non-player aquatics/vitals consumer, and removal of temporary content-specific CaxecraftApp wiring through haxe_c-xge.20.4.
2026-08-03 visual defect observed in the interactive Western Falls pool: translucent water presents as stacked/intersecting voxel sheets with poor depth readability (maintainer screenshot at 1280x720). WaterRenderer already omits faces between adjacent water cells, so investigation must distinguish authored flowing surface steps from unsorted alpha/depth submission. Fix at the generic renderer or simulation/content boundary; do not hide it with Western Falls-specific geometry or opaque water.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: Correction after focused audit: the shared non-player aquatic/vitals consumer is already implemented in AquaticsProbe.sharedCharacterCheck. Separate EntityStore instances contain a local-player-bound character and an NPC character with different stable IDs; both advance through the same Character.step, Aquatics, breath, movement, vitals, replacement, and attack functions, while cross-store identity writes are rejected. npm run test:caxecraft-aquatics passes Eval and native C, runtime-free, with sanitizers. This acceptance item is complete; remaining water scope is save composition, audio/editor/runtime-content integration, and removal of temporary application/content wiring.

title: Blend submersion, swimming, buoyancy, breath, and Tideweave
description: Build player-medium behavior on the deterministic water field. Sample feet/body/head immersion, derive a continuous submersion ratio and stable named movement state, then blend gravity, buoyancy, drag, acceleration, ascent/descent, floating, breaching, camera effects, oxygen, drowning, recovery, and the bounded Tideweave capability without waterline jitter.
design: Physics owns truth at the fixed simulation tick. Rendering interpolates positions and presentation only. Sample several documented heights across the player AABB, apply hysteresis around state labels, and derive forces from the measured fraction instead of one Boolean water flag. Keep suit effects as a typed capability/profile supplied by validated content, not a campaign-name branch.
acceptance_criteria: Focused deterministic traces cover dry entry, wading, surface floating, full submersion, ascent/descent, breach, exit, oxygen loss/recovery, drowning/retry, and equipped/unequipped Tideweave behavior with no waterline jitter. Eval/C parity and readable runtime-free C pass.
close_reason: Implemented fixed-tick continuous submersion, stable dry/wading/floating/submerged labels, shared land/water collision, swimming forces, buoyancy, drag, ascent/descent, breath recovery, drowning cadence, retry reset, and generic bounded equipment capabilities. The Haxe-owned AquaticsProbe passes Eval/native-C trace parity, strict runtime-free C, no-goto output checks, and available ASan/UBSan. Documentation explicitly defers Raylib presentation, content resolution, authored maps, editor, and persistence to haxe_c-xge.20.5.3.

title: Implement deterministic bounded voxel-water flow
description: Add the target-neutral Haxe simulation core for Minecraft-like water. A voxel has a typed empty/source/flowing state with bounded level and falling status; fixed-tick updates prefer downward flow, then deterministic horizontal neighbors, leak through openings, settle, recede, and reflow after solid edits. Keep a bounded work queue so a large release continues across ticks without stalling rendering. This slice owns domain storage, update scheduling, terrain invalidation hooks, stable hashing/traces, and focused Eval/generated-C tests; it does not yet own swimming, breath, rendering, persistence, or authored campaign placement.
design: Use the existing compact one-byte world carrier. Reserve explicit water codes that encode source versus flowing strength/falling state and keep all decoding behind typed Haxe functions; gameplay must never compare magic codes. Use a fixed neighbor order and duplicate-safe bounded queue. Compute a cell's next state from the previous committed neighborhood or another explicitly documented deterministic schedule, never renderer traversal order. World solid placement/removal schedules the changed cell plus bounded neighbors. Per-tick processed-cell budget is observable in tests.
acceptance_criteria: Focused tests prove source stability, downward fall, lateral weakening, one-cell leaks, obstacle routing, stable settling, receding after source removal, dam open/close/repair reflow, deterministic state/hash across enqueue orders and render-frame grouping, and bounded continuation across ticks. Invalid water levels/codes fail closed at the typed boundary. Eval and haxe.c produce the same trace; generated strict C is warning-clean, sanitizer-clean where available, runtime-free, and contains no content-name special cases or raw C.
notes: Implemented target-neutral typed bounded water, compact explicit storage codes, deterministic lowest-index pending work, terrain edit invalidation, bounded tick/settle behavior, and Haxe-owned executable assertions. The shared host runner now coordinates Eval, haxe.c, strict native C, runtime-plan inspection, and optional sanitizers without reimplementing water in Python. Verified test:caxecraft-water (Eval/native exact agreement, runtime-free, ASan/UBSan), typed boundaries, all owned Haxe sources, Haxe format, CI/toolchain policy, and snapshot catalog.
close_reason: Closed

title: Implement water, swimming, breath, and Tideweave underwater play
description: Deliver water as a real simulated voxel fluid used by Creative mode and the authored Adventure route. Water has typed source and flowing cell states, falls through open space, leaks through openings, spreads laterally with bounded strength, recedes or settles after neighboring blocks change, and schedules deterministic local updates when water or terrain is placed or removed. Player physics measures submersion continuously and transitions through wading, surface swimming, floating, fully underwater movement, and breaching: effective gravity, buoyancy, drag, acceleration, jump/swim controls, camera, breath, and audio/visual presentation respond to that measured state. Add breath depletion/recovery, drowning damage, respawn/checkpoint behavior, underwater mining policy, and the Tideweave Suit capability.
