title: [HXC-DISC] Ratify generated-output and runtime redistribution license treatment
description:
## Decision needed

Decide and document the licensing treatment for generated C sources and headers, selectively emitted hxrt source/binaries, compiler-provided templates, generated manifests, and user-authored inputs. Keep source publication separate from package/release claims and obtain owner/legal review before promising an exception or permissive runtime grant.

## Rationale

The repository GPL-3.0-only license governs repository-owned source but does not, by itself, settle whether every compiler output is a derivative work or what terms should accompany copied runtime/template material. Users need a deliberate, consistent answer before release packaging, and the answer affects emitted SPDX data, notices, templates, and runtime selection.

## Alternatives Considered

- Assume all generated artifacts inherit GPL-3.0-only. Rejected as an unsupported blanket inference that could unnecessarily constrain users.
- Promise permissive or exception-based treatment immediately. Rejected because the exact runtime/template boundaries and owner-approved terms have not been reviewed.
- Leave the question undocumented until release. Rejected because implementation could harden conflicting output and packaging behavior.
- Track an explicit pre-release decision with runtime-free and runtime-linked fixtures. Selected as the fail-closed path.
acceptance_criteria: An accepted decision names the license/SPDX treatment for generated C and headers, generated manifests, bundled hxrt source and binaries, templates, and copied third-party inputs; public docs explain user obligations without implying legal advice; release packaging emits the decided notices and SPDX/provenance metadata; representative runtime-free and runtime-linked package fixtures pass the license policy validator.

notes:
ADR 0004 is accepted and normative. Implement private immutable valid UTF-8 storage; every Haxe index is a Unicode-scalar index; no implicit normalization; malformed UTF-8 lossy decode replaces each maximal ill-formed subsequence with U+FFFD and checked decode returns an explicit result. Bytes stays binary. Safe CString conversion rejects embedded NUL and distinguishes source-lifetime borrow from allocator-owned conversion. String must remain independently linkable from object/GC/reflection. The E0 Eval probe observed astral length/code 1/128512, composed/decomposed lengths 1/2, and embedded-NUL length 3.
Terminology clarification: ADR 0004's exact lossy policy is one U+FFFD per maximal subpart of an ill-formed UTF-8 byte sequence, not one replacement for an arbitrarily long malformed run.
Production String work is blocked by target-carrier decision haxe_c-od2.6. Haxe 4.3.7 Cross selects target.utf16/utf16 before initialization macros and cannot be relabeled safely; do not implement scalar UTF-8 semantics behind a compiler configuration that types UTF-16 branches. Reuse the structural String/StringTools/UnicodeString snapshot from haxe_c-od2.4 once the carrier is resolved.
Carrier decision haxe_c-od2.6 is resolved: the exact Haxe 5.0.0-preview.1 CustomTarget(c) production snapshot selects scalar String/StringTools/UnicodeString branches with target.unicode and without target.utf16/utf16. Hosted/freestanding capabilities are target-owned; Eval remains only an independent oracle. String implementation may proceed when its planned dependencies are ready.
close_reason: Implemented E4.T03 as a bounded native UTF-8 scalar string contract: immutable valid UTF-8 values, scalar length/access/slice, checked decoding and deterministic maximal-subpart lossy decoding, direct literal/compare/hash paths, allocation-aware concat and mutable buffering, allocator identity, and explicit borrowed versus owned CString lifetimes with embedded-NUL rejection. Context: Represent structurally known records as named/deduplicated C structs with clear value/reference behavior.

Scope: Represent structurally known records as named/deduplicated C structs with clear value/reference behavior.

Non-scope: Work outside this outcome and its acceptance criteria. Create a linked discovered-from issue instead of silently widening scope.

Dependencies: E2.T11, E1.T03

Validation: Satisfy every acceptance item with executable evidence and the applicable PRD §40 definition-of-done gates; record exact commands and artifacts in the close reason.

Compatibility: Assess and document portable/metal, runtime-policy, environment, generated-C, and public-ABI impact where applicable. Do not harden an unresolved public contract without an accepted ADR.

Documentation: Update affected ADRs, documentation, diagnostics, capability data, and ledgers required by the acceptance criteria and PRD §40.
acceptance_criteria:
- Field order/layout policy is deterministic.
- Anonymous structural equality does not accidentally become C nominal incompatibility.
- By-value copies and address-taking are explicit.
- Metal @:c.layout(c.Layout.Struct) validation rejects unsupported layout combinations.
notes:
The M0 collector validates c.Layout ownership, pack/align literal shape, opaque-by-value use, and impossible by-value cycles only. E3.T01 owns actual struct/value representation, native layout evidence, address-taking/copy semantics, and capability-dependent rejection.
Implemented a bounded TypedExpr -> HxcIR -> structural C path for closed anonymous value records. Canonical UTF-8 structural shapes deduplicate aliases and nested records into dependency-first private C structs; construction retains source evaluation order, and copies, projections, field places, addresses, and dereferences remain explicit. Added structural offsetof/align/size assertions, strict C11 and independent C++17 layout consumers at O0/O2, runtime-free production evidence, exact HXC1001 negative boundaries, and metal packed-layout HXC5002 rejection. Compatibility: portable and metal emit the same private record C; auto/none/minimal runtime policies retain zero hxrt for this slice; the existing executable carrier remains hosted; no public ABI stability or general record/class/Dynamic/mutation/equality support is claimed. Evidence: docs/aggregate-lowering.md, test/aggregate_lowering/expected/, docs/specs/bootstrap-inventory.json. Verification: npm run test:aggregate-lowering; npm run format:haxe:check; npm test; git diff --check.
close_reason: E3.T01 acceptance complete: deterministic deduplicated field/layout policy, structural alias compatibility, explicit copy/address HxcIR, metal packed-layout rejection, runtime-free generated C, C/C++17 native layout evidence, documentation/capability updates, and full npm test pass.

title: Repair Browser finale route after solid NPC/relay collision
description: The Browser Chamber Piloscript still selects the correct level, but its pre-arena movement was authored before stationary NPCs and solid mechanisms gained physical separation. Current native play reaches frame 180 with both relays waiting and objective.prepare-arena still active. The old first leg now stops at Ceesh instead of reaching the west relay; the second leg can also pass east of its relay. This is a reloadable content-route regression, not a request to weaken generic collision.
acceptance_criteria: Update the single existing browser-chamber Piloscript to navigate the current Ceesh and solid relay layout through ordinary actions; native play selects Browser Chamber, activates both relays, opens the entry gate, defeats Browser through the existing telegraphed phase contract, reaches the victory dialogue/journal, and passes twice with identical semantics. Do not add another journey, move campaign facts into Haxe, or weaken NPC/mechanism collision.
notes: Red evidence: before this change, the native memory-software adventure journey failed at pilots/active.piloscript:35: expected objective.confront-browser but observed objective.prepare-arena. A live agent observation at frame 180 placed the player at x=30.699,z=29.5 with both relays waiting; current solid Ceesh collision had blocked the old route. During correction, the first compact route also failed because the streamed one-line briefing still owned movement input, and a later run showed Browser needed its sixth remaining health hit after the corrected approach.\n\nGreen evidence: python3 examples/caxecraft/play.py --pilot adventure-journey --piloscript pilots/browser-chamber.piloscript --raylib-configuration memory-software --output-root /tmp/haxec-bread-build.WzI5ya --allow-network passed. It reused the native haxe.c executable and reported 2 identical semantic runs in a bounded process. The journey now closes each one-line conversation deliberately, walks around Ceesh, activates west then east relay, opens the gate, defeats Browser, and reaches dialogue.victory plus journal.victory. Oracle/provenance: expected milestones are authored in the reloadable browser-chamber CAXEMAP; movement was derived from live world observations of the authored actor and relay positions. No Haxe campaign literals, collision changes, or extra journey were added.
close_reason: Repaired the existing reloadable finale journey and proved the complete native route twice with identical semantics.

title: Investigate deterministic runtime-level-loader stateful collision failure
description: The focused runtime-level-loader probe now deterministically returns result code 122 on Eval. Its presentation, localization, flow, and stateful-binding checks pass first; the later movement check expects a second eastward tick to stop at the active glyph-control collision, but the observed position does not satisfy that assertion. The failure repeated three times while localized speaker-name work was in progress and is independent of the speaker schema.
acceptance_criteria: Reproduce code 122 at the smallest faithful GameSession/stateful collision owner; identify whether movement, bounds, or the probe expectation changed; fix the owning engine behavior or update the expectation only with an independent movement/collision oracle; restore runtime-level-loader Eval and generated native C evidence without weakening other checks.
notes: Root cause and fix, 2026-08-12: commit 0b43f11 made stationary dialogue actors solid to prevent camera clipping. The synthetic runtime-presentation fixture still placed Nia and the solid glyph-control at the same point, directly east of the player. The gate probe therefore started inside Nia's personal-space collision and recovered upward before it could measure the gate. Independent oracle: the authored coordinates plus the character/NPC collision boxes show the overlap without using the movement result under test. Moved only synthetic Nia two units along Z; she remains within the authored 2.5-unit interaction radius, while the east path now intersects only the gate. The engine was correct and unchanged. Red: runtime-level-loader returned stable code 122 three times. Green: the complete runtime-level-loader command passed Eval, generated native C, and sanitizers.
close_reason: Separated the synthetic NPC from the gate path and restored the complete loader collision proof without changing engine behavior.

title: Add gamepad input to Caxecraft play and conversations
description: Caxecraft menus and the editor can observe a controller, but ordinary first-person play still samples only keyboard and mouse. Add one device-neutral gameplay mapping for movement, look, jump or swim, interact, use, attack, pause, hotbar navigation, and the conversation complete/advance/skip actions. Preserve the existing GameInputFrame boundary so gameplay and conversation logic do not know the device.
acceptance_criteria: A supported gamepad can play the representative Adventure path without keyboard or mouse; controls are documented and shown through device-appropriate prompts; conversation action first completes a revealing line and then advances while deliberate skip remains distinct; focus loss and pause are safe; a small input-mapping probe plus one representative real-device or deterministic adapter review provides evidence without duplicating campaign tests.

title: Add reloadable animation for voxel models
description: Extend Caxecraft's static .vox model presentation with an original, reloadable animation contract for props and future 3D actors. Support authored clips without requiring an engine rebuild, while preserving deterministic asset publication, bounded resource ownership, and useful silhouettes from all gameplay angles.
design: Start with one tracer bullet and choose the smallest representation that matches it: discrete .vox frame sequences for transforming voxel shapes, rigid named parts for mechanisms, or a documented skeleton only when smooth character motion requires it. Record clip names, frame timing, looping, bounds, and model paths in reloadable content. Keep simulation and collision authoritative and independent from decorative interpolation. Use classic voxel replacements only as technique inspiration; do not copy Duke Nukem 3D assets, identity, or source. Do not imply that one static MagicaVoxel file contains animation.
acceptance_criteria: One original animated voxel tracer loads from package-declared assets, selects a reloadable clip, advances deterministically, respects pause and content reload, and releases every native resource exactly once; missing frames or invalid timing fail clearly; a real gameplay review proves readable motion and no sprite slabs; documentation explains when to use frame animation, rigid parts, or a skeleton; broader 3D NPC/enemy conversion remains separate content work.

title: Show the water dive control in the HUD
description: The live input maps Left Shift to downward swimming, but the persistent control label omits it. Players cannot discover how to dive from the game. Add the concise control to the English and Spanish UI text without changing aquatic behavior.
acceptance_criteria: The English and Spanish control labels name Left Shift as the dive control. The localization catalog remains valid, and the existing device-input mapping still sends Left Shift as downward swim intent.
close_reason: The reloadable English and es-MX control hints now identify Space as jump/rise and Left Shift as dive. The longer footer was shortened to keep the new control readable until haxe_c-u7iw replaces the dense footer with the polished contextual HUD. README aquatic guidance documents both controls. Content refresh and content-check passed without rebuilding the game.

title: Repair Browser Chamber Piloscript catalog selection
description: The reloadable Browser Chamber journey still advances five entries from the campaign entry level. After Ashfall entered the sorted development catalog, that sequence selects Ashfall instead of Browser Chamber. Keep this as a content-owned menu journey; update only its selection steps and confirm the level expectation through the native Piloscript path.
acceptance_criteria: The Browser Chamber Piloscript reaches level browser-chamber from the title UI, retains its journey-shaped milestones, and does not add campaign facts to compiled engine code.
notes: Revalidated 2026-08-12. Classification: already resolved in commit 2488f84. That commit added the sixth menu-next action required to wrap from the manifest entry Evergrove to Browser Chamber after the catalog gained another preceding row. Direct current-native evidence: a one-step diagnostic selected Flooded Ruins, while the checked-in six-step script selected Browser Chamber before its later journey checkpoints. No source change is needed. A separate full-journey failure remains outside this Bead's catalog-selection acceptance and must not reopen a solved menu count.
close_reason: Already fixed by 2488f84; current source retains the six selection steps and native menu selection reaches Browser Chamber.

title: Render authored props from true voxel models
description: Caxecraft currently turns small stateful controls into a few generic cuboids and stretches a 2D atlas cell over every face. This gives depth but not a coherent object, and it cannot match the high-quality voxel replacements used by classic sprite-based games. Add one standard, reusable voxel-model asset path and use a polished relay as the first tracer bullet.
design: Prefer the established MagicaVoxel .vox format because pinned Raylib 6.0 already loads VOX models. Keep model selection and transform in reloadable package/content data. Extend the curated typed Raylib binding and explicit resource lifecycle only as far as one warning-clean model load/draw/unload tracer requires. Do not auto-extrude every sprite, emit one cube draw per pixel, invent a Caxecraft-only binary model format, or special-case campaign IDs. Preserve original art provenance and let the editor expose model placements later.
acceptance_criteria: A package-declared original .vox prop loads through a precise typed Haxe/Raylib boundary, renders with a readable silhouette and palette from multiple angles, respects authored yaw and bounds, and unloads exactly once; the gate relay uses that path without campaign-specific renderer logic; missing or invalid models fail clearly or use a reviewed bounded fallback; native memory-software and desktop review show no intersecting sprite slabs or debug cubes; generated C remains direct and warning-clean; broader NPC voxel conversion remains optional follow-up work.
notes:
Implemented the first real model path and expanded it to both recurring castle controls after visual review showed the neighboring fallback still looked inconsistent. Reloadable content now selects original 32-cubed MagicaVoxel relay and winch models; the generic catalog caches, scales, rotates, draws, and unloads them, while atlas cells remain bounded fallbacks. Asset/package checks pass for 15 exact assets. The full Caxecraft Haxe-to-C compile and desktop native build pass. Memory-software review shows the relay as a coherent charcoal/copper cabinet with a teal crystal instead of intersecting slabs. A close-up route to the winch exceeded the current 25-second pilot timeout, so keep this issue open until a desktop/free-play review confirms its crank/drum silhouette and model shutdown is observed on a clean exit.
2026-08-11 visual review found additional flat world props in the castle/archive content: scroll or field-note items still render as camera-facing billboards and expose the same flat-object problem as the former relay. Keep the atlas art for inventory/HUD icons, but represent placed scrolls/notes as small original textured voxel models selected through generic reloadable presentation data. Do not special-case scroll IDs in the renderer. The shared billboard depth-mask defect is tracked separately by haxe_c-rr69.
2026-08-11 incremental prop pass: the generic reloadable VOX path now also owns Ceesh field notes. The original 32-cubed field-note model uses parchment, teal binding, and copper-seal forms; the 2D cell remains HUD/fallback art. Reloadable content reduced its world bounds to 0.85 x 0.42 x 0.60 blocks after live memory-software review found the first 1-block version oversized. The real agent-session frame showed a volumetric silhouette and no dark billboard rectangle. Added deterministic npm refresh/check commands; check rebuilds all three models in memory and compares exact bytes. Asset validation reports 16 exact assets, and content receipts are current. Keep the issue open for the existing desktop/free-play winch review and broader model shutdown acceptance.

title: Keep campaign level rows clear of action buttons
description: Adding Forge Archive as the seventh runtime campaign level made the campaign list draw through the Adventure and Back buttons. The selected row remains technically usable, but its name and route order are obscured. The generic picker must keep its visible level window inside the panel at supported window sizes.
design: Calculate row capacity from the actual panel and screen height. Draw a bounded window that always includes the selected level, and use the same first visible index for mouse hit testing. Do not special-case Forge Archive or cap campaign data to the current level count.
acceptance_criteria: At 1280x720 all seven current campaign rows are readable above the action buttons; at smaller supported layouts, a bounded visible window includes the selected row; mouse row hit testing maps to the same visible indices; the real campaign screenshot shows Forge Archive without overlap; campaign identity does not enter Haxe layout logic.
notes:
Red evidence: the real 1280x720 memory-software campaign frame with seven levels draws the Forge Archive row through the Adventure and Back button band. The selected row remains forge-archive in the Haxe observation, so this is presentation geometry, not missing campaign data. Independent oracle: non-overlapping rectangles from the screen dimensions and the reviewed native frame.
Green evidence: CampaignMenu now derives panel height, visible row capacity, and first visible index from screen height and selected index; draw and mouse hit testing share the same layout. At 1280x720 the calculation gives seven visible rows, and the reviewed native memory-software frame shows all current levels plus Forge Archive above the buttons. At 960x540 the same calculation gives two visible rows and scrolls the window to include the selected index; row bottoms remain above buttonTop. npm run test:caxecraft-app-screen passed Eval, native C, runtime-none, and sanitizers. The rebuilt Adventure graphical pilot passed two identical semantic runs at 1280x720.
close_reason: Campaign rows now use a bounded selected-level window and no longer overlap action buttons.

title: Allow runtime levels without a combat enemy
description: A runtime-loaded level currently fails to launch unless ActivePlayableLevel resolves exactly one object tagged enemy. Live Frostmere review exposed this when removing an opaque optional Mossling made the selected level remain at the campaign screen. Puzzle, story, exploration, and peaceful creator content must not need a hidden or irrelevant hostile actor merely to satisfy application state.
design: Make the absence of an enemy an explicit valid runtime state. Keep combat and presentation generic, and do not add a dummy actor or campaign special case. This task is deferred while Frostmere keeps its optional Mossling at a separate supply-cache encounter.
acceptance_criteria: A small synthetic runtime level with no enemy launches and remains playable; enemy observation, rendering, fixed-tick updates, combat input, telemetry, and drops safely represent no active combat target; existing one-enemy levels behave unchanged; Eval and native C cover the reusable contract; one real combat-free content level proves the vertical boundary without campaign literals in engine code.

title: Collect authored no-use items such as bread
description: Authored world items currently enter the bounded hotbar by mapping their use profile to an ItemKind. Bread has the valid NoItemUse profile, so RuntimeInventoryBinding returns no inventory kind. A placed bread reward can therefore remain uncollectable even though bread already has a hotbar slot.
acceptance_criteria: A reloadable CAXEMAP can place caxecraft:bread; approaching it through ordinary gameplay collects the complete stack, removes the world item, preserves its collect-item CaxeFlow event, and increases the existing bread inventory slot. The reusable mapping uses validated item identity or another typed content-owned fact rather than inventing a campaign special case. Add the smallest focused engine regression and retain one real content-boundary proof.
notes:
Castle Underworks reproduced the gap through the real runtime package: the bread stack rendered at the authored cache position and remained in the world while the player stood inside pickup range; inventory bread stayed at 3 and no collect-item event fired. RuntimeInventoryBinding maps NoItemUse to no ItemKind. The content chapter uses supported berries for now; this issue remains the generic bread owner.
Implemented 2026-08-12. Red: before the mapping change, the real base-package probe called inventoryKindForRuntimeItem for caxecraft:bread and exited with code 20 because NoItemUse returned no ItemKind; Castle Underworks had also reproduced bread remaining in pickup range with its hotbar count unchanged. Green: RuntimeInventoryBinding now narrows validated base-pack item identity for no-use inventory items and maps caxecraft:bread to the existing Bread slot; unrelated no-use items remain absent. The runtime-level-loader fixture now authors a two-bread CAXEMAP stack and proves complete transfer, bread count 2, world removal, collect-item CaxeFlow dispatch, and full-inventory rejection. Independent oracle: validated content ID from the real base package, the pre-existing typed ItemKind.Bread and Inventory bread slot, manually authored quantity 2, and CAXEMAP collect-item semantics. Evidence: runtime-schemas and runtime-level-loader passed Haxe Eval, generated native C, and sanitizers; a clean flagship compile-only proof passed. Live native agent play selected Western Falls through the campaign UI and walked to item.rootway-ration: the observation changed bread 3 to 5 at x=26.3,z=26.1 and the collected item was absent from nearby state. No permanent content Piloscript was added.
close_reason: Bread now uses the existing typed inventory slot and passes focused, native, sanitizer, flagship compile, and live player evidence.

title: Refresh asset-manifest receipts with runtime content
description: The Haxe content refresh planner reads a changed assets/manifest.json and uses its new receipt inside runtime-content.json, but omits that receipt from the outer package update list. The final package overlay then rejects the normal content workflow with ContentPackageEntryLengthMismatch. Update both receipt owners atomically.
acceptance_criteria: A changed asset manifest, content pack, or level can be refreshed through ContentRefreshMain without manual hash edits. The resulting runtime receipt and outer package manifest both name the exact changed asset-manifest bytes, and the final package graph loads successfully. A focused Haxe planner regression proves the former mismatch.
notes: Added the missing asset-manifest receipt to the outer package update list. The Haxe refresh probe now mutates the asset manifest and requires both runtime-content.json and caxecraft.package.json to authenticate the new bytes. npm run caxecraft:content:refresh updated the real changed graph without manual hashes; the focused refresh lane passes.
close_reason: Asset-manifest edits now refresh both receipt owners atomically, with a focused Haxe regression and real package refresh proof.

title: Anchor the sun in the world and add basic daylight
description: Replace the current screen-space HUD-circle sun, which appears to follow mouse look, with a stable world-space sky object. Add the smallest basic daylight treatment that improves terrain depth without creating a general shader engine or changing game simulation. Preserve the deterministic software renderer and direct typed Raylib boundary.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Rotating the camera changes the sun's screen position and can move it outside the viewport; the sun remains fixed relative to the world. 2. Terrain and world objects have a basic coherent daylight/shading cue with readable face depth. 3. The normal renderer retains bounded cleanup and no campaign-specific behavior. 4. A representative real or software-rendered frame is visually reviewed; permanent automation protects the generic camera/world contract rather than brittle pixel layout.
notes: Removed the screen-space sun circles and draw a fixed world-space sphere inside BeginMode3D. Terrain and authored boxes now use directional face tints consistent with the north-east sun. Compile-only, launch-smoke, move-jump-edit, and Castle journey native memory-software runs pass. The broader campaign still needs a much larger visual and level-design pass; this issue claims only the camera/sun bug and basic face lighting.
close_reason: The sun now occupies a fixed 3D world position and basic directional face lighting matches it; bounded native pilots pass.

title: Let pack-defined actors use reloadable sprite atlases
description: Lift the generic actor renderer's fixed entities-atlas restriction so a validated NPC or enemy presentation can retain its authored atlas ID through resolution, generation publication, the playable view, and native drawing. Protect the engine with a small synthetic fixture. Use Ceesh from the existing adventure-characters atlas as the real castle tracer bullet; do not compile campaign names or atlas IDs into the engine.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Actor presentation resolution returns both validated asset ID and cell index. 2. Those facts survive resolved plan, generation bindings, and playable-level publication without path- or campaign-specific branches. 3. Native actor drawing uses legacy entities when selected and RuntimeTextureAtlasCatalog for supplemental sprite atlases, with a visible fallback only when neither owner can draw. 4. A focused synthetic engine test proves a non-entities actor atlas and would fail under the old restriction. 5. One castle content path renders Ceesh from reloadable pack data and passes the narrow runtime journey/visual proof.
notes: Implemented generic actor presentation as an authored asset ID plus cell index through pack decode, resolved plan, generation binding, playable view, and native drawing. The focused synthetic resolver uses a non-entities atlas, and the shipped registry now resolves Ceesh to adventure-characters/ceesh-front. The Castle Piloscript passed twice under Raylib memory-software, and the reviewed final frame shows Ceesh beside the inner gate. This proves reloadable actor art, not animation, 3D creatures, the castle interior, or Browser.
close_reason: Pack-defined actors now retain and draw supplemental atlas selections; Ceesh is the real Castle tracer and focused/native regressions pass.

title: Wire CAXEMAP trigger-zone events into live gameplay
description: CAXEMAP parsing and CaxeFlow validation admit enter-zone and leave-zone rules, but the live GameSession only queues interaction and item events. A player can stand inside a validated trigger zone without the rule firing. Add typed zone bindings, detect boundary crossings from committed player positions, queue each event once per crossing, and retain a focused deterministic engine regression. This was discovered while authoring the Castle Courtyard chapter; that content uses an interactive inner gate until the reusable engine capability lands.
notes: Implemented typed trigger-zone IDs, half-open integer bounds, and per-session inside state. RuntimeLevelLoader derives these bindings from validated CAXEMAP objects. GameSession observes the committed player body origin after movement and queues EnterZone or LeaveZone only when membership changes. Red: npm run test:caxecraft-runtime-level-loader returned 111 because the spawn-inside EnterZone rule did not fire. Green: that command passed Eval, generated native C, and sanitizers; the synthetic fixture proves one initial enter, no stationary duplicate, and exactly one leave after movement. The real Ashfall Piloscript reached journal.castle-road through zone.castle-road. A deliberate native rebuild passed two semantic runs, then --content-feedback reused the executable and passed without a build. Typed-boundary and formatter checks passed.
close_reason: Live runtime levels now emit authored trigger-zone entry and exit events once per observed boundary crossing.

title: Make CaxeFlow actor activation govern runtime actors
description: CaxeFlow object spawn/despawn currently changes generic stateful-object activity, but authored dialogue actors remain visible and eligible for nearest interaction after a content rule despawns their scenario object. This was observed while placing the Tideweave runic pedestal near the Fallskeeper: the guide continued to win interaction selection.
acceptance_criteria: A focused red proves that despawning an authored actor object removes its presentation and interaction without deleting unrelated controller state; spawning restores the actor according to the admitted lifecycle; generic runtime and real Caxecraft integration pass on Eval/native/sanitizers; documentation states any save-persistence boundary honestly.

title: Isolate native runtime generation hex-digest mismatch
description: The first content-refresh implementation made RuntimeContentGeneration compare runtimeGenerationSha256(...) with the expected lowercase digest. Eval accepted the checked-in runtime receipt, but the generated native runtime-content-generation probe returned assertion 8 and the rebuilt Caxecraft executable rejected byte-identical staged content before Raylib opened. Restoring the existing byte-level sha256Matches check while sharing runtimeGenerationInput fixed native sanitizer and Piloscript evidence. Isolate whether the divergence belongs to StringBuf hexadecimal construction, generated String equality, or another compiled-C String/Bytes edge. Do not change content receipts or weaken runtime verification.
acceptance_criteria: A minimal Eval/native fixture reproduces the exact divergence; the smallest compiler/runtime owner is identified; the natural hexadecimal digest path agrees on known vectors and the runtime-generation input; focused generated-C evidence passes with sanitizers; Caxecraft may use the natural path without losing the proven byte comparison or changing receipt bytes.

title: Drive the HUD from live content-logic objective state
description: The active level now publishes its first initially active objective with the matching runtime map, which fixes stale destination text. Longer campaigns need objectives to advance while a level remains loaded. Connect the generic HUD presentation owner to the live CaxeFlow objective state and its validated localized objective records, without embedding campaign IDs or prose in compiled Haxe.
design: Current main already applies ObjectiveChanged presentation events to one HUD ID. Complete the narrower missing contract: give the generic live CaxeFlow owner a deterministic active-objective projection in authored order; publish that projection with each successful fixed tick; make the HUD consume it atomically rather than reconstructing state from event order; retain validated RuntimeLevelPresentation only for localized text lookup. Completing or failing the selected objective must reveal another objective that is already active, while no active objective produces empty HUD text. Add a target-neutral focused projection regression before changing the shell. Then author one real Western Falls objective progression entirely in reloadable CAXEMAP and update its runtime Piloscript expectations; do not compile campaign IDs, prose, coordinates, or outcomes into Haxe/Python.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A focused target-neutral fixture proves initial selection, activation, completion/failure fallback to another already-active objective in authored order, unrelated presentation events, and no-active behavior. 2. Each successful GameSession fixed tick exposes the live active objective selected by the CaxeFlow state owner; failed or absent flow leaves explicit behavior and cannot publish a partial state. 3. The HUD uses that live ID with RuntimeLevelPresentation's validated locale/fallback lookup; it no longer reconstructs objective truth only from presentation-event order. 4. Western Falls CAXEMAP contains a small honest objective progression tied to existing admitted gameplay events, and English/es-MX text describes only implemented play. 5. The reloadable runtime Piloscript observes at least one real objective transition through the UI/game path without rebuilding Haxe or C, while the existing route journey remains intact. 6. No campaign name, objective ID, prose, coordinate, or expected route outcome is compiled into generic Haxe or Python owners; focused engine tests protect mechanics and Piloscript protects authored content.
notes:
2026-08-09 current-main audit: partially resolved by df5e974. CaxecraftApp consumes FlowPresentationEvent.ObjectiveChanged and mutates currentObjectiveId, so the old claim that HUD state never changes is stale. Remaining evidence: the shell stores only one ID and clears it when that objective becomes non-active; it cannot recover another objective that was already active because FlowTickResult exposes events but no complete active-objective projection. No focused HUD-state owner covers this behavior. Western Falls currently declares only objective.western-falls and no rules, while active.piloscript expects that same ID at launch and finish, so there is no real content transition proof. Existing npm run test:caxecraft-caxeflow passes executor semantics but does not distinguish the missing HUD projection. No open PR owns this work.
2026-08-09 focused red evidence: `npm run test:caxecraft-caxeflow` failed while compiling `CaxeFlowProbe.hx` at `result.activeObjective`; Haxe reported `FlowTickResult has no field activeObjective`. Expected failure: the portable fixed-tick result does not yet publish the authoritative live objective projection. The new scenario covers authored-order initial selection, completion fallback to another already-active objective, unrelated dialogue presentation, no-active state, and later activation.
2026-08-09 implementation and review: CaxeFlowState now selects the first Active objective in authored declaration order. FlowTickResult publishes that projection only when the tick has no diagnostic, and CaxecraftApp replaces its HUD objective from this complete value instead of replaying ObjectiveChanged event order. The focused manually authored scenario is the independent invariant oracle: second and third start active, completing second falls back to third despite an unrelated dialogue event, failing third yields no objective, and activating first publishes first. A budget-failure negative proves partial execution does not publish an objective. RuntimeLevelLoaderProbe independently proves the real GameSession path before and after an authored interaction using the manually authored runtime-presentation fixture. Western Falls now keeps objective IDs, English/es-MX text, and the Nia progression rule in CAXEMAP. Runtime Piloscript drives Title -> Adventure -> Western Falls, observes objective.meet-nia, interacts with Nia, observes objective.find-tideweave, and preserves the sand/Tideweave/two-lantern/submerged/dry route. The first route revision failed honestly with one lantern because interaction replaced one movement frame; shifting the existing route by one frame restored two lanterns without weakening expectations. Real graphical evidence passed twice with identical semantics, objectiveChangeObserved=true and flowRuleObserved=true. A warm run reused generated C, all 128 native objects, and the link; current runtime content restaging validation took 320.5 ms. Focused CaxeFlow, runtime loader Eval/native/sanitizer, runtime Piloscript, package manifest, deterministic ZIP export, campaign runtime, presentation, scenario model/determinism, typed boundaries, package/unity/split domain differential, O2 native, 32 seeded properties, and snapshot catalog passed. Snapshot review found only the new objective carrier/control flow, optional-record identity changes, and reason-ID shifts; selected runtime capabilities did not broaden. No campaign literal entered generic Haxe or Python. Distinct review challenged event-order sensitivity, multiple-active fallback, failed-tick publication, absent flow, localization provenance, mocked boundaries, selectors, and content coupling; all material findings were fixed or covered. Public compiler/platform claims remain unchanged.
close_reason: The HUD now consumes an authoritative authored-order live objective projection, failed ticks cannot publish partial objective state, Western Falls advances from meeting Nia to finding Tideweave entirely through reloadable content, and focused plus real UI/native evidence preserves the full journey without campaign-specific engine code.

title: Remove the compiled first-playable text catalog from game presentation
description: Most shipped scenario prose still reaches title, campaign, dialogue, combat, and failure presentation through FirstPlayableCatalog, a generated Haxe catalog compiled from the entry map. That means editing those CAXEMAP messages does not fully update the running game until it is rebuilt, and a later campaign level can inherit entry-level wording. Move all scenario-owned text lookup to the validated presentation published with the active map or campaign data. Keep only generic stable identities or schema rules in compiled Haxe.
acceptance_criteria: 1. No campaign title, dialogue, objective, encounter, or failure prose is embedded in repository-owned production Haxe. 2. Title/campaign/HUD presentation resolves scenario-owned text from runtime-loaded validated content, including locale fallback. 3. Editing those messages and rerunning the content loop reuses the existing executable and visibly changes the appropriate screen. 4. Generic Haxe tests use small synthetic catalogs to protect lookup, fallback, publication, and malformed input; content-specific expectations live in reloadable Piloscript content tests. 5. The legacy FirstPlayableCatalog and its generation/freshness path are removed when no consumer remains.
notes:
Behavior-first red evidence (2026-08-08): `npm run test:caxecraft-runtime-level-loader` failed during Eval compilation at RuntimeLevelLoaderProbe.hx:118 with `caxecraft.content.RuntimeLevelPresentation has no field message`. The new synthetic-fixture expectations request `objective.title` in English, Spanish, fallback French, and one missing key. Oracle/provenance: the manually authored runtime-presentation.caxemap fixture supplies English, Spanish, fallback, missing-key, and tagline expectations; shipped map catalogs supply content-specific wording. Tracer/system proof: test:caxecraft-adventure-journey passed title -> Adventure -> campaign -> level -> Western Falls with two identical native memory-software runs and framebuffer checks. No-build proof: changed the Western Falls tagline, ran content refresh (two receipt files, no build), then ran the Adventure journey through --content-feedback; it reused the verified executable and passed. SHA-256 stayed 96f9b6f35f1b578e9c92789550865a551def7a9c727a51c10daf85c95019a9db before and after. Restored the proof text and refreshed receipts. Other passing evidence: runtime-level-loader Eval/native C with sanitizers; runtime-schemas Eval/native C with sanitizers; caxecraft-domain snapshot update plus split/package/unity differential and O2 native checks; formatting; all-sources; toolchain-shards; content-refresh; package metadata check; governance build-state tests; git diff check.
close_reason: Scenario-owned presentation now comes from validated active runtime content, the legacy compiled catalog and Python freshness path are removed, and focused plus real UI/no-build evidence proves the content loop without broadening compiler claims.

title: Load Piloscript content tests as reloadable game content
description: Content creators can already reload CAXEMAP and campaign data without rebuilding the executable, but content-specific Piloscript inputs and expected journey facts still live in compiled Haxe or Python orchestration. Define a validated runtime-loadable form for Piloscript content tests so a map, campaign, dialogue, objective, cutscene, or mod edit can update its focused journey without recompiling Caxecraft. Keep the compiled Haxe side generic: it owns the loader, runner, semantic observations, bounded execution, and fail-closed diagnostics, not any named campaign or prose.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A documented runtime-loadable Piloscript content-test format expresses bounded input actions, checkpoints, and semantic expectations without campaign literals in the engine or generic runner. 2. The editor or text workflow can edit and rerun one content journey against an existing executable. 3. The Haxe engine validates the format and reports located fail-closed errors; Python may transport or collate evidence but does not define game semantics. 4. One real campaign journey migrates from compiled content-specific facts and proves UI-to-level launch plus a semantic objective/cutscene/content checkpoint. 5. Generic Haxe tests protect parser, runner, limits, publication, and malformed input with small synthetic fixtures; content changes do not require editing those engine tests.
notes:
Representative scenario: Given the staged first-adventure campaign and an existing verified pilot executable, a creator edits a runtime Piloscript and launches title -> campaign picker -> selected level. Haxe applies the authored frames, captures declared roles, and compares screen, mode, level, objective, generation, and publication facts. Invalid headers, actions, expectations, duplicate frame owners, unsafe captures, and bounds fail with a source line and no success artifact. Product surface: downstream Caxecraft content workflow. Oracle: manually authored actions plus stable runtime content IDs and typed application state. The implementation does not generate expected values.

Red evidence: npm run test:caxecraft-runtime-piloscript failed before implementation at RuntimePilotScriptProbe.hx:4 with Type not found : caxecraft.pilot.RuntimePilotScript. This was the intended missing typed parser and runner.

Implemented: PILOSCRIPT 1 typed parser and generic observer; bounded forced quit; four generic visual roles; staged pilots/active.piloscript; Adventure UI journey migrated from compiled PilotScript actions and checkpoints; runtime input hash reaches native telemetry; old Western-Falls-specific Python pixel and generation oracles removed. Compiled engine-regression pilots remain separate and allocation-free.

Independent malformed proof: a temporary unknown-action edit made the native executable report pilots/active.piloscript:6 unknown action unknown-action. The host received no Haxe semantic checkpoint. The valid source was restored.

Vertical evidence: npm run test:caxecraft-adventure-journey passed twice through generated C, Raylib memory-software, title, Adventure, campaign picker, Western Falls, objective objective.western-falls, generation 2, publication 1, generic framebuffer review, and bounded exit. Final screenshot shows the matching FIND TIDEWEAVE BENEATH THE FALLS objective.

No-build evidence: a harmless runtime action edit changed the Haxe input hash from e5388a56 to 8241c841. Content feedback passed while executable SHA-256 stayed edad1d1c81d5e70dd8862434a5af94746932fa024e2455fbcb6d0f5b60b6ac69. The restored canonical journey also passed with the same executable hash in 15.99 seconds. A verified rebuild and two-run journey took 64.69 seconds with all 126 native objects and link reused from cache.

Focused evidence: runtime-piloscript passed Eval, strict native C, and sanitizers. caxecraft-pilot, content-refresh check, typed-boundaries, agent-instructions, all-sources, and git diff check passed. The existing haxe_c-xge.20.6 task remains open for deriving host filename and identity metadata from one Haxe authority; it does not block runtime content editing.
close_reason: Runtime-loaded Piloscript now owns the real Adventure content journey. Haxe validates actions and semantic expectations, malformed files fail with located diagnostics, and content feedback proves edits run against an unchanged executable.

title: Make Haxe the authority for Caxecraft pilot metadata
description: Stop duplicating each Caxecraft pilot's stable name, numeric code, frame limit, compile define, and screenshot name across PilotScript.hx, play.py, and check_pilot.py. Keep game behavior and semantic assertions in Haxe. Retain Python only where it adds host-side value: invoking the compiler/linker/process, enforcing a wall-clock timeout, decoding files produced by the native program, and checking portable PNG/report evidence.
design: Choose one reviewed, typed Haxe-owned authority and derive or export the host metadata from it without executing the implementation under test to create expected gameplay values. A small generated manifest is acceptable if freshness is checked and generation does not require compiling the Caxecraft executable that the host runner is trying to build. Do not rewrite build/process orchestration in Haxe merely to remove Python; the goal is to remove duplicated policy and registries, not to move suitable host glue.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Adding a pilot requires declaring identity/frame/checkpoint metadata in one authored place. 2. Haxe remains the owner of semantic actions and behavior assertions. 3. The host runner consumes validated derived metadata and fails closed on stale or malformed data. 4. Expected gameplay state and framebuffer oracles remain independently authored; they are not generated by the implementation under test. 5. Existing pilots, deterministic repeated runs, timeout handling, and report validation remain green. 6. The resulting Python is materially smaller or more stable, with remaining responsibilities documented in plain language.
notes:
Discovered while adding haxe_c-xge.20.2.1. The adventure-journey feature needed small host mappings, but PilotScript identity/code/frame limits now appear in both Haxe and Python. This follow-up prevents that duplication from growing without distracting from the playable campaign task.
2026-08-09 residual runner finding from haxe_c-xge.20.2.3: when caxecraft-domain correctly reported snapshot drift, examples/caxecraft/run.py entered its exception tuple and raised NameError because LocalizationCheckFailure was not defined. The registered snapshot update and post-update domain validation passed, so this did not mask a semantic failure. Consolidating the remaining host runner should restore the missing exception authority and add a focused failing-path check.
2026-08-09 focused red evidence: npm run test:caxecraft-pilot failed with 'pilot metadata has no Haxe catalog authority at examples/caxecraft/src/caxecraft/pilot/PilotCatalog.hx'. Expected reason: pilot IDs, script codes, frame limits, compile defines, and screenshot names are still duplicated in play.py instead of coming from one typed Haxe owner and checked host manifest.
2026-08-09 implementation and review: PilotCatalog.hx now owns every host pilot command name, telemetry code, frame bound, compile define, screenshot basename, and compiled-versus-runtime kind. PilotCatalogMain exports 14 records to pilot-catalog.json without building Caxecraft. The manifest carries the SHA-256 of the Haxe authority; play.py validates that digest, the exact schema, closed execution kinds, safe names, numeric bounds, and uniqueness before compilation or launch. The old Python code/frame/define/screenshot registries and argparse choice list are removed. Adding another pilot no longer requires Python registry edits. Python remains responsible for process orchestration, timeouts, telemetry/PNG decoding, and portable artifact checks. A focused malformed/stale-manifest check fails closed. The unrelated domain-runner NameError was reproduced through its controlled pre-compile exception path and fixed by removing the obsolete LocalizationCheckFailure tuple entry. Independent oracle/provenance: the typed Haxe PilotScript behavior and checkpoints remain the semantic owner; the committed manifest is derived metadata, not expected gameplay state; the existing manually authored Piloscript remains the Adventure oracle. Evidence: catalog refresh/check, target-neutral pilot probe in C and es_MX.UTF-8 locales, py_compile, all-sources, typed boundaries, runtime Piloscript Eval/native/sanitizers, launch-smoke real memory/software Raylib at 1280x720 with two identical runs, Adventure journey real memory/software Raylib with two identical 351-frame semantic runs, full Eval/split/package/unity Caxecraft differential with 32 seeded properties and native O2, and all 233 governance tests passed. Snapshot review found no PilotCatalog module, generated header, C, runtime-plan, or capability change in the ordinary playable; only the symbol-table digest changed. No public compiler, runtime, platform, or campaign claim broadened.
close_reason: Haxe now owns pilot metadata through one typed catalog and checked derived manifest; Python consumes it fail-closed without duplicate registries, compiled and runtime native journeys pass, and the stale domain-runner failure path is repaired.

title: Admit constrained generic helpers over class subtypes
description: The Caxecraft runtime-schema tracer used an ordinary private helper validateOrder with a type parameter constrained to RuntimeLocatedId and an Array of that parameter. Eval accepted it, but haxe.c failed closed with HXC1001 during reachable generic-specialization discovery when the parameter was a class subtype. The application can keep an equivalent non-generic private comparison today, but the admitted generic specialization slice should either lower this bounded constrained method or diagnose a deliberately documented unsupported boundary with a focused fixture.
design: Reduce the pattern outside Caxecraft: one base class with immutable scalar fields, one subclass array, and one constrained generic function that reads only base fields. Preserve typed specialization and array invariance; do not admit unchecked casts or Dynamic. Add Eval, HxcIR, strict generated C, native behavior, negative/runaway, and generated-shape evidence before broadening the capability manifest.
acceptance_criteria: A focused minimal fixture is red with the current HXC1001 for the intended node; the reusable compiler implementation admits bounded constrained class-subtype specialization without unchecked casts; Eval/native results agree under strict C and sanitizers where applicable; recursion/count safeguards and unsupported neighboring generic shapes remain fail closed; Caxecraft may remove its duplicated per-definition order wrappers only after the focused capability is admitted.

title: Map incremental and span lowering semantic owners
description: The scorecard-derived planner conservatively marks R4 required when test:incremental-backend or test:span-lowering is selected because those package owners do not yet map to a semantic product surface. The fallback is safe, but explain mode cannot name the affected surface or R3 owners.
design: Review each owner against the five checked product-surface scorecards. Add only evidence-backed semantic mappings, keep policy-only and unknown ownership distinct, and retain R4 fallback for any ambiguous path. Do not move evidence out of hosted R2.
acceptance_criteria: Planner explain and JSON modes map test:incremental-backend and test:span-lowering to reviewed product surfaces and affected R3 owners; governance tests cover the mapping and unknown-owner R4 fallback; no public claim is broadened and R2/R4 backstops remain intact.

title: Calibrate generic-specialization runaway cost model
description: The current bounded specialization slice uses canonical instance discovery plus 64-function, 64-type, and 524,288 generated-C-source-byte limits. The layered fail-closed design is sound, but the fixed global text-byte threshold was not benchmark-derived and text size can change with formatting. Compare it with stable structural work measures such as specialized HxcIR instructions, blocks, types, payload units, per-instance cost, and total/program-relative work. Use official GCC, Clang, Rust, and GHC limit designs as precedent, not as numbers to copy. This is nonblocking research plus the smallest evidence-backed implementation; do not weaken or remove the current guard before a replacement proves equivalent termination and diagnostics.
design: Measure first. Record per-specialization structural cost, emitted C bytes, compiler time, peak memory where available, and native C compile/size effects across focused recursion/large-body fixtures and representative programs including Caxecraft. Evaluate a layered model with canonical visited-set termination, recursion/count bounds, per-instance and total structural budgets, and emitted bytes retained as report evidence. Prefer formatting-independent costs and actionable diagnostics naming the largest contributors. If evidence favors retaining the current byte guard, document that result rather than forcing a schema change.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible unsaturated benchmark relates current text bytes and candidate structural units to compiler work for focused normal/runaway cases and Caxecraft. The selected policy explains every threshold and whether it is fixed, program-relative, or configurable; no value is claimed as universal without evidence. Genuine recursive, count, single-large-instance, and total-growth cases fail deterministically with source-positioned actionable diagnostics and no output, while legitimate corpus builds remain accepted. Cold/server, reversed-order, schema/report, strict native, snapshot, and full Caxecraft evidence pass. Documentation cites comparable official GCC/Clang/Rust/GHC safeguards and distinguishes shared practice from haxe.c policy.

title: Admit safe reassignment of managed Array fields
description: Ordinary Haxe permits assigning a new Array value to a mutable Array field, but haxe.c currently rejects the expression as managed-Array-reassignment-not-admitted. Caxecraft actor publication exposed the gap while considering whole-store reference replacement. Its definitive store design instead keeps a private Array identity and commits in place after preflight, so this compiler capability does not block that task; other natural Haxe APIs still need the general rule.
design: Lower mutable managed Array field assignment with capture-before-release ownership. Evaluate receiver and replacement exactly once, retain or move the replacement as its provenance permits, release the previous field owner only after replacement capture succeeds, handle self-assignment safely, and commit without leaking or double-releasing. Keep constructor initialization distinct from replacement and preserve exact exception/allocation cleanup order.
acceptance_criteria: Direct mutable Array fields admit local/parameter/field/call-result replacements with self-assignment, aliases, empty/non-empty values, primitive and managed elements, early returns, and allocation failure; old storage releases exactly once and replacement aliases remain live; invalid immutable/final targets and unsafe provenance fail closed; HxcIR validation, Eval/native differential, split/package/unity, strict C11, sanitizers, deterministic output, runtime feature selection, and focused negative diagnostics pass.
notes:
2026-08-08 red evidence: the ordinary-Haxe Eval oracle accepts ArrayFieldOwner alias/self, borrowed-parameter, fresh-empty, managed-String-element, and Array.copy() result replacements. The same fixture through haxe.c fails at ArrayFieldOwner.assignToSelf with exact HXC1001 TBinop(OpAssign:managed-Array-reassignment-not-admitted). Pre-fix command: HAXE_NO_SERVER=1 node_modules/.bin/haxe -cp test/differential/array-runtime/generated -lib reflaxe.c -main Main -D hxc_project_layout=split --custom-target c=<temporary-output>.
Implemented the narrow mutable instance-field rule. Reference-counted Arrays now acquire the replacement before releasing the previous field owner, then store it; collector-traced Array<Class> fields use a direct traced store without reference-count operations. Constructor initialization remains separate, and local/static/indirect whole-Array reassignment remains fail closed. Independent oracle: ordinary Haxe Eval. Focused evidence: test:array-runtime passed with alias/self, borrowed parameter, fresh empty literal, Array.copy result, conditional join, String elements, traced class elements, allocation-failure ordering, strict C11, Clang, sanitizers, split/package/unity, warm determinism, live GC pressure, and cycle reclamation. Vertical evidence: test:caxecraft-runtime-level-loader passed Eval/native C and sanitizers with CaxeFlow resetTickOutput presentation replacement. Supporting gates: test:hxc-ir and test:all-sources passed. Review disposition: no mocked boundary, selector omission, scorecard borrowing, or public claim broadening; broader non-field reassignment is intentionally unchanged.
close_reason: Admitted and verified safe mutable Array instance-field replacement with acquire-before-release ownership, traced Array<Class> handling, and the real Caxecraft CaxeFlow boundary.

title: Lower fresh class construction used as a call argument
description: Natural Haxe may pass a fresh nonescaping object directly to a synchronous function, for example validate(value, new Resolver()). haxe.c currently requires every stack construction to initialize a named source local and rejects the direct argument as TNew(stack-construction-requires-direct-local). Caxecraft's actor-composition probe exposed the missing general expression form while passing a test resolver through a proven call-bounded interface parameter. A named local is equally natural for the active probe and keeps that task moving, but the language form remains a real compiler capability gap.
design: Extend the existing compiler-owned automatic construction path used by direct fresh method receivers. Materialize the fresh argument in a compiler-owned local, preserve left-to-right argument evaluation, constructor failure and partial cleanup, convert the borrowed object to the exact class/interface parameter representation, and destroy it after the synchronous direct call. Keep storage, return, asynchronous/unknown forwarding, and other escapes fail-closed. Do not heap-allocate or require application raw C.
acceptance_criteria: Focused ordinary-Haxe fixtures pass new FinalClass(args) directly to proven call-bounded class and interface parameters, including neighboring managed arguments and a fallible constructor. Eval/native behavior, exact construction/destruction order, HxcIR borrow validation, strict GCC/Clang C11 O0/O2, sanitizers, split/package/unity, server/order determinism, and generated-C readability pass. Escaping, retained, virtual/unknown, and asynchronous shapes remain source-positioned negatives. The temporary Caxecraft probe local may be collapsed without changing behavior once this issue closes.
notes: Implemented the natural direct-argument form for proven synchronous direct calls. Fresh unmanaged classes now use compiler-owned automatic storage, preserve left-to-right argument evaluation, convert to exact class/interface parameters, clean partial construction on failure, and end temporary owners immediately after the call. Virtual, indirect, retaining, and unproved calls remain fail-closed. Focused evidence passed: npm run test:constructor-direct-argument; npm run test:constructor-direct-receiver; npm run test:caxecraft-session; manual exact negative diagnostic for direct_argument_escape; Python syntax, Haxe formatting, generated adapter, and diff checks. The duplicate exhaustive constructor matrix was intentionally stopped under concurrent identical pre-commit load after all earlier families passed; the dedicated acceptance matrices cover the changed rule.
close_reason: Implemented and focused acceptance evidence passed; direct fresh class arguments now lower through exact call-bounded lifetime semantics without application workarounds.

title: Recover readable for-loop control names in generated C
description: Caxecraft's new target-neutral 3D viewport lowers cleanly without goto or allocation calls, but ordinary Haxe for-loops still emit compiler-created control locals such as hxc_g_hb6d1f8fcece2 and hxc_g1_hd771ab8a203e. The user-authored x/y/z locals are readable; the loop counter and upper-bound scaffolding are not. This makes otherwise structured C look more machine-generated than necessary.
design: Preserve Haxe evaluation, overflow, and loop-bound semantics while carrying a typed role for compiler-created induction and bound values into the existing deterministic name planner. Prefer compact context-derived names such as cell_index or z_end only when collision and shadow analysis proves them safe; otherwise retain a deterministic bounded fallback. Do not special-case Caxecraft, rewrite printer text, or infer semantics from emitted spellings.
acceptance_criteria: Focused nested/range-loop fixtures retain exact Eval/native/sanitizer behavior, deterministic output, scope safety, and collision handling while generated C uses bounded role-aware names for admitted induction and loop-bound temporaries. Caxecraft EditorWorldViewport.c no longer exposes hash-first hxc_g/hxc_g1 loop controls for its x/y/z scans. Snapshot and maintainability evidence distinguish user locals, compiler temporaries, and necessary collision suffixes, with no change to HxcIR/CAST semantics or public ABI.

title: Give runtime-plan reasons stable provenance IDs
description: Adding the first Caxecraft 3D editor module changed no selected runtime feature family, but its alphabetical position shifted traversal ordinals and rewrote about 14,700 lines of the canonical hxc.runtime-plan.json. The report remains semantically valid, yet unrelated source additions create noisy snapshot reviews, large diffs, and extra storage/verification work.
design: Replace encounter-order-only reason identities with deterministic provenance keys derived from the semantic owner: stable module/type/function identity, operation family, and an intra-owner identity that is itself invariant under unrelated modules. Preserve useful source attribution, exact reason deduplication, deterministic ordering, and the same selected runtime closure. Do not weaken or summarize away the full audit report.
acceptance_criteria: Adding an unrelated module before existing modules in canonical order does not renumber existing runtime reason IDs. Focused fixtures prove identical selected runtime features and reason coverage before/after insertion, deterministic cold/server output, no collisions, and actionable provenance. The Caxecraft runtime-plan snapshot changes only for genuinely new editor requirements rather than repository-wide ordinal churn, and full audit/summary modes still agree on their semantic feature closure.

title: Propagate fallible inline-child construction with recursive cleanup
description: A final child can share its parent's C storage even when the child constructor may throw. haxe.c currently rejects that shape. Make the child call carry the parent's failure convention, ensure the caller-owned partial parent recursively releases managed fields inside inline children exactly once, preserve argument evaluation and root lifetimes, and promote the existing owned_fallible negative into native positive evidence. Discovered in Caxecraft EditorTestPlay.executor while validating haxe_c-53k.2.7.

title: Replace mutable managed record fields without leaking aliases
description: Ordinary Haxe permits reassignment of a mutable field whose closed-record value owns Arrays, Bytes, strings, enums, or optionals. haxe.c can retain/destroy that record family but ordinary assignment currently overwrites its C struct bits without first acquiring the replacement and releasing the prior owner. Add self-assignment-safe capture-before-release lowering, make the first constructor store establish the field owner without releasing zero storage, and preserve exact failure/cleanup order. Discovered in Caxecraft EditorSession.draft while validating haxe_c-53k.2.7.

title: Initialize final direct-record fields from constructor values
description: Haxe permits a constructor to assign a final field exactly once. haxe.c has specialized constructor initialization owners for strings, enums, Arrays, maps, retained interfaces, and inline children, but an unmanaged closed record currently falls through to ordinary assignment and is rejected as immutable. Add a constructor-only first-store rule for exact unmanaged closed records, preserve by-value source evaluation and nominal type identity, and keep later writes fail-closed. Discovered in Caxecraft EditorHistory.settings while validating haxe_c-53k.2.7.

title: Trace and finalize inline owned children inside managed classes
description: A collector-managed Haxe class can directly embed a final, fixed-lifetime child class. The C layout is correct and avoids a second allocation, but descriptor generation currently rejects the shape because it cannot yet walk managed references or owned runtime values inside that child. Add cycle-safe recursive trace/finalizer emission for by-value owned-class fields, retain fail-closed behavior for pointer-like class references, and prove reclamation and exact cleanup with a focused generated-Haxe native fixture. Discovered while compiling Caxecraft EditorSession.history after haxe_c-53k.2.6.

title: Admit function-valued Array element storage
description: Array.sort now accepts exact typed comparators, but an Array whose element type is itself a function remains fail-closed because the collection planner has no function-element layout or lifetime contract. This is a general collection representation gap, not an Array.sort special case.
design: Start with exact non-capturing function values represented as typed C function pointers and prove whether trivial relocation is sufficient. Keep callable signature identity in specialization keys and generated C; do not erase distinct signatures to void pointers. Broaden to capturing closures only after haxe_c-ckk.3 supplies a typed environment representation and ownership plan. Preserve Array copy, growth, assignment, destruction, sorting, aliasing, and failure behavior without a universal callable box.
acceptance_criteria: Focused ordinary-Haxe fixtures cover construction, indexing, mutation, copy, growth, iteration, and sorting for at least two exact function signatures; Eval and strict generated C agree; signature mismatches and unsupported capturing values fail before artifacts; allocation/lifetime behavior, runtime selection, split output, determinism, GCC/Clang C11, and sanitizers pass; stdlib and architecture claims advance only the admitted slice.

title: Lower managed compiler-generated flow carriers
description: A focused managed-enum conditional test with block-expression arms is typed by Haxe/Reflaxe as an initially empty compiler-generated TVar followed by arm assignments. haxe.c currently tries to fabricate a default value for that flow carrier and rejects the managed enum as result-type-without-direct-default. This is distinct from direct TIf lowering: the compiler must recognize and validate the already-desugared assignment graph without inventing a zero owner.
design: Generalize the schema-19 managed carrier ownership protocol to proven compiler-generated flow carriers. Preserve source order and exactly-once arm evaluation; distinguish fresh moves from borrowed retains; reject reads before acquisition, duplicate ownership, unsupported failure edges, and ambiguous Reflaxe shapes. Do not special-case block expressions or weaken ordinary uninitialized-local rules.
acceptance_criteria: Ordinary Haxe block-valued if expressions producing a managed tagged enum compile in local, argument, return, and nested positions. Eval plus GCC/Clang O0/O2 and ASan/UBSan prove selected-arm order, no leak, no use-after-free, and no double release. HxcIR snapshots show exact acquire/move ownership, malformed generated-flow shapes fail closed, and no fabricated zero enum appears in C.
notes: Implemented the compiler-generated carrier protocol for managed String/nonrecursive tagged enums and complete unmanaged direct values. Managed arms now move fresh owners or retain borrowed owners; the later read moves once. Direct records/enums/imported structs use validator-proven uninitialized storage instead of a fabricated zero. Recursive managed enum carriers fail closed because deep retain can allocate and the carrier is infallible. Added exact branch/switch HxcIR negatives, block-valued local/argument/return/nested/switch ordinary-Haxe coverage, an Int switch regression for non-enum classification, generated-C no-default inspection, and beginner-facing architecture documentation. Verification: Eval oracle; npm run test:enum-lowering:bytes (cold/repeat/reverse/warm server, unity/split/package, GCC/Clang native and ASan/UBSan); npm run test:hxc-ir; npm run test:all-sources; npm run test:typed-boundaries; formatter 1.18; fixture policy; snapshot catalog. The original Caxecraft FlowActionFamily carrier now lowers. The next compile stops later and cleanly at fresh managed enum switch-subject cleanup in CaxecraftEditorScreen.redo; that distinct P1 gap is owned by haxe_c-djl.18, discovered from this task, with no application workaround.
close_reason: Managed and direct compiler-generated flow carriers now lower with exact ownership/assignment validation, focused native/sanitizer evidence, and no fabricated enum default; the later switch-subject lifetime gap is separately owned by haxe_c-djl.18.

title: Explain Reflaxe and haxe.c architecture boundary
description: Document the verified relationship between Reflaxe's GenericCompiler/BaseCompiler lifecycle and haxe.c's target-owned TypedExpr, HxcIR, CAST, runtime-planning, printing, and project-emission pipeline. The guide should be readable by a newcomer and exact enough for a Reflaxe target developer.
design: Keep the overview in docs/architecture.md and the deeper IR contract in docs/hxc-ir.md. Base every present-tense claim on the current CReflaxeCompiler, CompilerInit, vendored Reflaxe lifecycle, and ReflaxeOutputWriter implementations.
acceptance_criteria: docs/architecture.md states the real inheritance and registration path, explains why per-type GenericCompiler callbacks return null, shows what Reflaxe provides versus what haxe.c owns, includes the syntactically-close/semantically-distant C rationale, links the deeper HxcIR contract, and passes repository documentation/policy checks.
notes: Verified against CReflaxeCompiler, CompilerInit, CompilerBootstrap, ReflaxeOutputWriter, and vendored Reflaxe GenericCompiler/BaseCompiler/ReflectCompiler. Added the real inheritance and lifecycle, whole-program callback rationale, Reflaxe-versus-target ownership table, exact vendored 4.0.0-beta revision/provenance model, and the C-is-syntactically-close-but-semantically-distant HxcIR rationale. Focused local-link, toolchain-lock, governance-policy, and diff checks pass.
close_reason: Architecture guide now explains the verified Reflaxe integration and C-specific semantic pipeline for newcomers and Reflaxe target developers.

title: Index exact collector payload lookup for bounded pause scaling
description: The portable collector currently validates and resolves each exact managed pointer by scanning the allocation list. This is safe and sufficient for the initial correctness contract, but marking can become too expensive as the managed heap grows. Add a request-local exact-base index that never dereferences unknown memory, preserves deterministic behavior and the custom/freestanding allocator contract, and keeps the collector free of process-global state. Measure representative graph shapes before and after; do not claim a pause improvement without reproducible evidence.
design: Prefer the smallest target-owned index compatible with non-moving allocations and explicit collection state. Keep lookup/index maintenance request-local and deterministic. Treat hash/table allocation failure explicitly and preserve collector correctness; do not introduce conservative scanning or hidden host allocation.
acceptance_criteria: Exact managed-base lookup no longer performs a full allocation-list scan for every traced reference; unknown, interior, freed, and foreign pointers still fail or follow the documented policy without unsafe dereference; hosted and freestanding/custom-allocator tests remain warning-clean and sanitizer-clean; reproducible stress evidence reports pause scaling, memory overhead, and fragmentation tradeoffs; docs and capability claims state the measured boundary.
notes: 2026-07-26 architecture review: the exact-root/descriptor/non-moving/intrusive-worklist foundation is sound and matches established compiler/GC integration patterns, but current per-root/per-edge exact-base lookup is O((R+E)*N) because it scans the allocation list. docs/gc-runtime.md now states this complexity, per-object allocator cost, stop-the-world limitations, comparison references, and the evidence gate before any high-performance claim.

title: Integrate cyclic managed collection graphs with the selected collector
description: Managed Arrays, records, and enum payloads now compose through typed retain/release callbacks for acyclic graphs. Because Arrays are mutable, ordinary Haxe can also construct a reference cycle such as an Array whose enum element reaches the same Array. Local reference counting preserves live aliases but cannot reclaim an unreachable cycle. Integrate these collection graphs with the selected precise collector before claiming general cyclic Haxe collection semantics.
design: Reuse ADR 0005 and haxe_c-3ye rather than inventing cycle detection inside each Array callback. Representation planning must distinguish proven acyclic/local ownership from collector-managed graphs, emit exact roots and field tracing for active enum arms and nested records, and keep runtime-free/direct specializations when whole-program evidence proves they do not need collection. Do not make every Array unconditional GC storage or add application-specific no-cycle assumptions.
acceptance_criteria: Eval and generated C agree for self-cycles, mutual Array/record/enum cycles, alias mutation, cycle breakup, and unreachable reclamation under allocation pressure; active enum tags govern exact tracing and inactive union storage is never scanned; roots, ownership transitions, collector/runtime selection, and cleanup are explicit in HxcIR/plans; direct proven-acyclic programs retain the smaller selective path; strict GCC/Clang O0/O2, sanitizers, stress/deep-graph gates, deterministic layouts, and code-size/allocation evidence pass; public ABI remains separately owned.

title: Lower proven integral Std.int division to readable C integer division
description: Caxecraft's chunk layout uses ordinary Haxe expressions such as Std.int(coord.x / 8). haxe.c currently emits a floating conversion, hxc_f64_divide_zero_safe, and hxc_f64_to_i32_saturating even when both operands are integers, the divisor is a positive nonzero constant, and range analysis proves the quotient is exactly representable. Preserve Haxe semantics while selecting direct C integer division only for a proven safe subset; keep all other Float division/conversion behavior unchanged.
design: Add a typed lowering/analysis rule before CAST. Do not special-case Caxecraft names, rewrite generated text in the printer, or change Haxe's general / operator type. The proof must account for truncation direction, zero, precision, and C signed-division undefined behavior.
