acceptance_criteria: Positive fixtures prove direct readable C integer division for nonnegative Int operands and positive nonzero constant divisors; negative, zero-divisor, overflow/precision, Dynamic, and general Float cases retain their existing semantics or fail closed; HxcIR records the semantic choice rather than the printer recognizing text; Eval/native differential and UB sanitizers cover boundary values; generated Caxecraft chunk-layout output no longer uses the floating division helpers for admitted coordinate calculations.
notes: Discovered during haxe_c-xge.8 generated-C review. Current TerrainChunkLayout.c uses guarded f64 division for x/8, z/8, chunk/4, and packed/6; the first three have simple nonnegative-range proofs, while packed/6 needs its own bounded proof.

title: Provide a monotonic clock in raylib's macOS Memory platform
description: The pinned raylib 6.0 Memory platform implements GetTime() only for Windows, Linux/BSD, and Emscripten; on macOS it always returns 0. Caxecraft's deterministic headless renderer benchmark exposed this when its benchmark-only Haxe timer produced twelve measured frames but zero elapsed microseconds. Add or adopt a reviewed upstream fix without mutating the verified source cache, retain provenance, and test a strictly positive monotonic delta on macOS Memory builds.
design: Prefer an upstreamed/pinned raylib fix or an explicit content-addressed provisioning patch over editing cached third-party source. Keep timing in the typed raylib boundary; do not add example-only raw C.
acceptance_criteria: A macOS memory-software native probe observes a nondecreasing GetTime() value and a positive delta around bounded CPU work; Linux and Windows Memory timer behavior remains covered; provisioning preserves verified upstream identity and records any reviewed patch as a separate deterministic input; Caxecraft's headless benchmark either uses the repaired clock or fails with an actionable unsupported-clock diagnostic.
notes: Discovered by haxe_c-xge.8 on macOS: telemetry v5 words 36/38/39 were zero while word 37 proved all 12 post-warmup frames executed. In pinned rcore_memory.c GetTime and InitTimer exclude __APPLE__.
close_reason: Verified deterministic provisioning patch, native monotonic-clock probe, macOS Caxecraft benchmark, and cross-platform CI coverage

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: Implemented a content-addressed macOS/Memory patch without mutating the verified Raylib tree. The lock now pins the recipe hash; exact-text application verifies source and result hashes in a private build copy; reports retain pristine/effective tree identities and patch/file provenance; Caxecraft cache and prebuilt checks include the patch identity. A strict native probe requires nondecreasing GetTime() with a positive interval after bounded CPU work. Real macOS pinned-source integration passed and the full 7-sample Caxecraft renderer comparison now runs headlessly on macOS with semantic and byte-exact screenshot parity. Linux's existing headless matrix now runs the same clock probe; macOS and Windows Memory probe/run lanes are registered alongside the desktop matrix. Network-free provisioning tests (35 adversarial tests plus Haxe/snapshots), Caxecraft pilot tests, CI/toolchain policy, verify-lock, and whitespace checks pass. Documentation explains why the patch exists, automatic application, provenance, cache invalidation, testing, and eventual upstream replacement.

title: Admit path-dominated local class construction
description: Natural Haxe can validate inputs or take an early return before constructing a nonescaping local class. The current bounded stack-construction lowering rejects any TNew after the entry block, even when every path reaching the construction initializes the object and every later exit is dominated by that construction. Caxecraft's terrain-chunk oracle exposed this with a cache created after constant checks. Preserve the active renderer work by creating its test owner at entry, but lift the general language restriction in this dedicated compiler slice rather than teaching product code to depend on it.
design: Extend the lifetime model only with an executable path proof. Construction storage, initialization state, constructor failure, reverse cleanup, normal returns, and abrupt exits must be correct for paths before and after construction. Prefer HxcIR control-flow/dominance and explicit phase legality; do not initialize/clean an object on a route where construction never ran, hoist observable constructor work, or fall back to heap allocation.
acceptance_criteria: Positive fixtures cover early-return guards followed by construction, construction in a branch whose uses and exits remain inside that branch, and multiple path-dominated objects with reverse cleanup. Negative fixtures retain escaping references and any conditional shape whose lifetime cannot be proven. HxcIR validates per-path initialization and cleanup; strict C11 GCC/Clang O0/O2, C++ consumer where relevant, sanitizer, throwing-constructor, deterministic snapshot, and Eval/native behavior gates pass. Documentation replaces the unconditional-entry limitation with the exact admitted path rule.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: 2026-07-25 flagship advancement: after haxe_c-7d0.8 admits nullable ownership-transferring Array.pop, the real command npm run caxecraft:play -- --compile-only reaches examples/caxecraft/src/caxecraft/editor/EditorSession.hx:152 and fails exactly at activeTestPlay = new EditorTestPlay(snapshot) with TNew(stack-construction-requires-direct-local). The instance is created on the validated enter-test-play path and stored in EditorSession state, so this is fresh executable pressure for the existing path-dominated/owned construction work. Do not move construction earlier or weaken the natural class API in Caxecraft.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: Correction to the 2026-07-25 flagship note: EditorSession.activeTestPlay = new EditorTestPlay(snapshot) is not path-dominated local stack construction. The field retains the child after enterTestPlay returns, so automatic-storage lowering would create a dangling pointer. The bounded collector-owned parent/child case is tracked by haxe_c-53k.2.4; haxe_c-71g remains scoped to genuinely nonescaping local instances whose lifetime is proven by control flow.

title: Drive Caxecraft interpolation through a variable-cadence native pilot
description: MotionInterpolation has focused Eval/native proof, but every current graphical pilot forces exactly one 50 ms fixed tick per rendered frame and therefore cannot observe a between-tick camera sample. Add one bounded SmoothMotion pilot with deterministic representative render intervals, normal movement input, and a closed telemetry observation that becomes true only when the real rendered position lies strictly between adjacent committed simulation positions.
design: Extend PilotScript with integer frame-duration milliseconds so the input hash covers timing. Keep the accumulator and MotionInterpolation production code unchanged. Add one pilot-only Boolean observation and one protocol flag; do not feed visual positions into simulation, infer smoothness from a screenshot, raise the fixed-tick rate, or add a second game loop.
acceptance_criteria: A target-neutral pilot supplies a documented deterministic 8/17/25 ms cadence while gameplay retains exact 50 ms ticks; the real Caxecraft application observes at least one render position strictly between adjacent committed positions, reports that fact through the bounded versioned pilot protocol, captures a valid scene, runs twice identically, and exits within the existing bound; focused PilotScript tests lock name/code/cadence/hash/checkpoint; authoritative player/world traces and existing pilots remain unchanged; Eval/native interpolation, playable snapshots, formatting, generated-C no-goto/no-heap/no-hxrt, and real memory/software evidence pass; human feel remains an explicit manual check.
notes: Implemented the bounded smooth-motion pilot in ordinary Caxecraft Haxe. It drives the real outer loop with a deterministic 8/17/25 ms cadence while simulation stays at exact 50 ms ticks; cadence participates in the input hash. The script walks and queues a jump at the second tick boundary. Pilot protocol v3 exposes one closed interpolation-observed bit, set only when the real presentation sample lies strictly between different committed positions. Native validation also requires an airborne final state, so requested input alone cannot pass. Memory/software Raylib evidence passed twice identically at 1280x720 in 15.36 s: 12 frames, 3 ticks, interpolation=true, y=5.604 m, vertical speed=+5.6 m/s, grounded=false, 3 terrain batches, 2,446 visible blocks, bounded exit, and a visually valid textured scene. Focused PilotScript, Eval/native presentation with ASan/UBSan, Haxe formatting, Python syntax, playable snapshots, and generated-C no-goto/no-heap/no-hxrt checks pass. Human judgment of control feel remains the documented interactive smoke, not an automated claim.
close_reason: Implemented and verified presentation-only fixed-step interpolation through focused Eval/native tests and a deterministic real Raylib move-and-jump pilot; generated C stays structured, allocation-free, runtime-free, and human feel remains a documented manual review.

title: Make the Linux desktop graphical gate prove live resize
description: The pinned Raylib memory platform cannot resize by design, while the Linux desktop CI job currently spends its one graphical O2 run on launch-smoke. Replace that one desktop run with resize-layout: it starts on the same title screen, performs a real GLFW SetWindowSize transition under Xvfb, validates the resized title framebuffer, and exits deterministically. Reuse the existing O2 build/run slot rather than adding a duplicate compile.
design: Replace, do not duplicate, the existing Linux O2 graphical command. ResizeLayout already starts on Title and uses the same screenshot validator, so it retains the useful title/presentation proof. Do not weaken expected dimensions or add memory-backend game branches.
acceptance_criteria: Linux desktop CI invokes --pilot resize-layout under Xvfb, uploads its semantic report and 960x540 screenshot, and policy fails if the pilot or artifacts disappear; no second O2/game compile is added; the ordinary local --smoke command remains available; docs state that desktop/Xvfb owns live resize and memory/software owns the game/render/sanitizer path; YAML and policy checks pass; remote Linux job must pass before closure.
notes: Replaced the Linux desktop lane's single O2 --smoke run with --pilot resize-layout under the same Xvfb invocation. ResizeLayout starts on Title, performs the real Raylib/GLFW SetWindowSize transition, validates the 960x540 title framebuffer, runs twice deterministically, and retains launch/presentation coverage. Artifact paths now preserve the resize semantic report and caxecraft-pilot-resize.png. CI policy locks the pilot and exact paths. The local --smoke command remains unchanged; no second O2 Haxe/game compile was added. Local evidence: check_ci_policy.py PASS; governance YAML parse PASS; check_pilot.py PASS; git diff --check PASS. Actual Linux desktop/Xvfb execution is pending commit/push and remote CI, so leave open.

title: Reject live-resize pilots on Raylib's fixed memory platform before compilation
description: Raylib 6.0 PLATFORM=Memory deliberately implements SetWindowSize as unavailable. The resize-layout Caxecraft pilot currently spends a full Haxe/native build before its exact 960x540 screenshot assertion discovers the unchanged 1280x720 framebuffer. Add an early, configuration-specific diagnostic, focused policy coverage, and plain-language documentation. Keep live resize desktop-only; do not weaken the screenshot assertion or pretend an alternate initial size proves dynamic resize.
design: Treat backend capability as runner policy. Do not patch pinned Raylib, silently accept the unchanged framebuffer, add a game conditional, or replace the live-resize pilot with an initial-size test.
acceptance_criteria: play.py rejects --raylib-configuration memory-software --pilot resize-layout before preparing an output root or invoking Haxe; the diagnostic names the pinned backend limitation and directs the user to desktop/Xvfb; focused tests lock the failure; docs distinguish deterministic memory/software rendering from desktop live-resize evidence; ordinary memory pilots and desktop resize behavior are unchanged.
notes: Pinned Raylib source at src/platforms/rcore_memory.c confirms SetWindowSize logs 'not available on target platform'. Added validate_renderer_pilot before sanitizer/tool/output/Haxe work, with an exact desktop/Xvfb diagnostic for memory-software + resize-layout. Focused pilot policy admits desktop resize and ordinary memory pilots while rejecting only that pair. The game-pilot guide, Caxecraft README, and Raylib provisioning guide distinguish fixed software framebuffer evidence from live desktop resize. Evidence: check_pilot.py PASS; py_compile PASS; git diff --check PASS; direct CLI rejection completed in 0.016 seconds, returned exit 1, and did not create the requested output root. The prior full compile correctly failed at 1280x720 versus 960x540 and is retained as discovery evidence, not normalized away.
close_reason: The runner now rejects the one impossible memory/software live-resize combination before compilation, with focused tests and documentation preserving desktop resize as the real authority.

title: Coalesce proven class-receiver null guards in generated C
description: Caxecraft stack-local EntityStore lowers to a direct C struct with no allocation, but every field read or write repeats an identical self-equals-NULL abort guard. The checks preserve Haxe null behavior, yet the receiver is unchanged inside each direct instance function and a single dominating guard should be enough. Reduce this to a focused class fixture, prove the safe dominance rule in HxcIR and CAST, and emit readable C without weakening nullable-reference semantics.
design: Keep null behavior explicit and fail closed. Establish one named owner for receiver validation, then remove only guards whose receiver identity is unchanged and whose earlier guard dominates the dereference on every control-flow path. Do not pattern-delete C statements in the printer or special-case EntityStore/Caxecraft. Preserve one guard when a receiver can be null, retain guards after reassignment or at uncertain joins, and compare optimized versus unoptimized runtime behavior.
acceptance_criteria: A focused positive and nullable negative fixture prove constructor/method/field behavior; generated C for a method with several accesses contains one necessary receiver guard rather than one per access; reassignment and branch joins retain required guards; Clang and GCC strict C11 O0/O2 plus sanitizers pass; snapshots, HxcIR/CAST validation, determinism, and runtime-plan/allocation evidence remain unchanged except for the intentional structural improvement.
notes: Implemented a named HxcIR receiver-null-check coalescing pass backed by a shared control-flow dominator analysis. The pass removes only identical value+policy checks when an earlier check runs on every path; branch-local checks do not escape joins, instruction-level failure jumps stay conservative, and reassigned/reloaded receivers retain fresh value identities and checks. HxcIR validation independently accepts only same-block or dominating proofs and now has a non-dominating-null negative. Focused class fixtures prove one guard across entry/branch/join, four guards at an uncertain two-receiver join, one guard per immutable receiver load after local reassignment, generated-C guard counts, SIGABRT on NULL, strict Clang/GCC C11 O0/O2, C++17 layout, and address/undefined sanitizers. Caxecraft Eval/split/package/unity/native differential passed; playable HxcIR fell from 11126 to 11057 instructions, and EntityStore now emits one receiver guard per method (3 total). Also refreshed the intentional class, constructor, span, HxcIR diagnostic, and Caxecraft snapshots. Passed test:class-layout, test:hxc-ir, test:constructor-lowering via updater, test:virtual-dispatch, test:span-lowering via updater, test:evaluation-order, test:project-layout, test:caxecraft-domain via updater, test:caxecraft-playable, test:all-sources, test:typed-boundaries, format:haxe:check, snapshots:catalog, py_compile, and git diff --check.
close_reason: Closed

title: Decouple Caxecraft localization lookup from Raylib drawing
description: Replace the transitional generated catalog methods that call Raylib.DrawText directly with a target-neutral typed lookup API. Validated JSON/CaxeMap catalogs remain the source of truth; built-in C builds use allocation-free static text with explicit lifetime, while future runtime-loaded mod catalogs can implement the same interface.
design: Generate closed message IDs and a catalog lookup layer. Keep rendering in app/UI adapters. On C, return only a typed representation whose static lifetime has been proven; do not weaken CString borrowing or introduce raw C. Retain generated C snapshots as QA evidence, not source data. Runtime-loaded catalogs are a later provider behind the same API, not a reason to require hxrt for built-ins.
acceptance_criteria: Application and generated catalog code contain no catalog-owned Raylib draw calls; locale plus message ID selects text through one typed API; built-in C output is deterministic, allocation-free, runtime-free, and has proven static lifetime; Eval/native localization tests cover English, Spanish, invalid IDs/locales, and catalog completeness; generated C snapshots remain registered; docs distinguish built-in static catalogs from future runtime-loaded content.
close_reason: Replaced renderer-coupled generated localization methods with typed text lookup catalogs. Eval uses String, C uses proven static c.CString literals, and Main/TitleMenu own Raylib drawing. English/Spanish lookup, raw-code validation, malformed catalogs, packaged bytes, runtime/allocation absence, registered playable snapshots, split/package/unity native differentials, and documentation passed.

title: Allow stack-backed class construction after validated early exits
description: Caxecraft's ordinary startup validation exposed HXC1001 TNew(stack-construction-requires-unconditional-entry-block): a local WaterSimulation constructed after a fail-closed map-load return cannot lower even though the instance stays stack-local and borrows no storage. Add a focused class-lowering fixture that validates a guard, returns on failure, constructs a non-escaping class on the surviving path, uses it, and emits readable lifetime-safe C. Preserve the existing escape/lifetime analysis and fail closed when construction is truly conditional in a way C cleanup cannot represent. Caxecraft currently constructs the scheduler in the unconditional entry block, which is semantically equivalent but should not remain a general source-shaping requirement.
notes: Implemented function-outer-sequence stack construction after earlier validated exits. HxcIR proves the early return has no object cleanup and later exits carry initialized cleanup; branch/loop/switch-local construction remains fail-closed. Verified with npm run test:constructor-early-exit, npm run test:fixture-policy, npm run test:typed-boundaries, npm run format:haxe:check, npm run test:all-sources, strict GCC/Clang C11 O0/O2, Eval parity, reversed-input determinism, and Clang ASan/UBSan.
close_reason: Closed

title: Lower enum switches with early-return arms without duplicate HxcIR exits
description: Caxecraft water snapshot validation exposed HXC9000 while lowering an ordinary enum switch inside a loop. The switch had one InvalidStorage payload arm that returned false and grouped valid arms that continued; CBodyControlFlow reported that the structural sequence would emit the generated enum-switch-exit block more than once. A second occurrence appeared in WaterSimulation.placeInitialVolume with grouped valid arms and one early-return invalid arm. Replacing those byte-validation switches with centralized primitive WaterCellCodec predicates is the clearer application design, but the source shape is valid ordinary Haxe and the compiler must not reach invalid HxcIR.
design: Reduce the original loop-plus-switch shape into the smallest ordinary enum fixture, including a payload arm, grouped arms, an early return, and loop continuation. Inspect enum statement-switch block ownership in CBodyLowering/CBodyControlFlow and ensure each generated exit block is emitted exactly once. Keep the application using the primitive codec predicates; this issue owns the general compiler correction rather than a water-specific branch.
acceptance_criteria: A focused fixture reproduces the original HXC9000 on the parent revision; the fixed compiler lowers ordinary enum switches with grouped continuing arms and early-return payload arms inside a loop into valid deterministic HxcIR and warning-clean strict C; Eval/native results agree; neighboring expression/statement enum switches, fallthrough policy, nested loops, and malformed enum carriers retain explicit behavior; exact HxcIR/CAST snapshots, strict GCC/Clang O0/O2, sanitizers, formatter, and all-sources gates pass.

title: Consolidate Caxecraft Haxe probe orchestration
description: Caxecraft has accumulated one Python wrapper per mechanic. Most behavior assertions already belong in Haxe probes, but repeated process/locale/output plumbing makes that ownership hard to see and invites future game logic in Python. Introduce one small shared runner and migrate the existing inventory, gameplay, terrain-atlas, CaxeFlow, scenario, and similar probe wrappers in bounded groups.
design: Haxe test modules own gameplay, engine, parser, and DSL assertions. A shared independent host runner may own pinned compiler launch, isolated roots, timeouts, locales, Eval/haxe.c/native differential execution, sanitizers, filesystem bytes, graphical capture, and concise reporting. Keep case configuration closed and reviewable. Do not force graphical pilots or build-time content generators through the same abstraction when their OS duties differ.
acceptance_criteria: No migrated mechanic has Python reimplementing its rules; repeated Haxe process/locale/exact-output code is removed; focused npm command names remain stable; failures still name the selected mechanic; focused timings do not regress materially; malformed fixtures, alternate locales, native C, sanitizer, and graphical evidence remain in their appropriate lanes; AGENTS/testing docs state the boundary.
notes:
Implemented incremental consolidation:\n- deleted six per-feature Python launchers (caxeflow, inventory, gameplay, editor, scenario model, scenario determinism); npm command names now select data-driven cases in run_haxe_c_test.py;\n- retained Haxe probes and exact result envelopes, locale checks, warm-server determinism, source-boundary scans, canonical fixture byte checks, and nominal-ID negative diagnostic;\n- routed profile:caxecraft-content-loop through existing profile_incremental_edit.py; the observer is now internal dev_content_loop_profile.py and remains excluded from product build inputs;\n- kept assets, content-pack, localization, Pilot, play, native/sanitizer, compiler profile, and aggregate runners separate where the host/system boundary is the faithful observer.\nCounts: 23 -> 17 Python files; executable Python files 23 -> 16; unique Python files behind npm Caxecraft commands 17 -> 10; total Python lines 18,729 -> 18,414.\nEvidence: intended red was check_toolchain.py naming exactly six stale package mappings. Green: all six focused npm commands; water Eval/native strict C + ASan/UBSan; assets/content-pack/localization; content-loop 6 tests; build-state 16; incremental profile 7; formatting 799 Haxe; typed boundaries 799; toolchain and CI policies; toolchain shard map; full governance 231 tests. all-sources reached its fixed 30s timeout while load was 29.58 on 12 CPUs with unrelated target builds; no semantic failure, representative retry pending.\nTiming: baseline six commands 11.30s. Contended after sample 14.29s at load 15.82/12 CPUs; process counts unchanged, so no speed/regression claim until representative retry.
Independent review disposition: removed the migrated Python CaxeMap object-order/run-total/canonical-byte validator because ScenarioCodecProbe.hx already parses the real fixture, rejects malformed input, and requires byte-identical canonical round trips. Python now retains only process, locale/server, source dependency, result-envelope, and Haxe diagnostic checks. Updated final Python line count: 18,383.
Timing-review fix: the first shared scenario-determinism path repeated Haxe --version and HXML resolution per sample. It now verifies the pin once per focused command and resolves each probe/locale argument set once, restoring the old cold/locale/warm process topology. All six cases passed after the refactor. Current total Python line count is 18,404; representative timing remains pending because host load stayed 12-14 on 12 CPUs.
Corrected-topology diagnostic timing: six commands 14.76s while load remained about 14 on 12 CPUs. All outputs passed; sample is not representative and does not close the timing criterion.
Startup review: scenario-model now retains its former ordinary checkout HaxeShim route instead of adding pin/version/HXML-resolution subprocesses. It measured 1.44s under load 18 versus the 1.42s baseline and remained green. Native water also remained green through strict C and ASan/UBSan. Current total Python line count is 18,470.
Quiet-host audit 21:00-21:05: 60 checks at 5s intervals never reached the <=6.0 representative threshold. Load fell from 10.71 to a minimum 6.73, then an unrelated job raised it to 12.58; final load was 9.16. No haxe.c timing or all-source command was launched during the monitor. Timing/all-source acceptance remains externally blocked without weakening the threshold.
Final verification: npm run test:all-sources passed its full 220-module macro/non-macro and exact HXC1001 no-output boundary after a bounded, user-authorized pause of exact sibling compiler/test process trees; the trap resumed every captured PID. Two bounded quiet-host waits still never reached the declared <=6.0 load threshold, including one after those sibling trees were paused, so no absolute before/after speed claim is made. A same-host paired audit instead ran each deleted launcher from HEAD directly before its replacement: all six old/new paths passed under load 19.35-23.20 on 12 CPUs. Old paths totaled 14.90s wall and 11.38s user+system CPU; shared paths totaled 13.71s wall and 10.95s CPU. This closes the no-material-regression criterion while remaining explicit that contention makes the sample unsuitable as an absolute speedup benchmark. Every paused process was resumed; surviving roots were in runnable/sleeping, not stopped, state.
Commit-scope correction: the completed consolidation alone changes 22 -> 16 tracked Caxecraft Python files, 16 -> 10 distinct Python files behind npm Caxecraft commands, and 17,606 -> 17,347 tracked Python lines. Earlier larger counts included the separate in-progress content-loop observer from haxe_c-xge.20.4.3.9 and are not attributed to this task. Exact staged-tree verification used a temporary detached worktree and passed py_compile, toolchain policy, CI policy, all six migrated npm commands, and test:caxecraft-water through Eval, generated native strict C, AddressSanitizer, and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer. The temporary worktree was removed.
close_reason: Six redundant Python mechanic launchers are consolidated into the shared Haxe probe runner with stable npm selectors, preserved boundary evidence, isolated staged-tree verification, and paired no-regression timing.

title: Handle exhaustive enum-abstract switch exits without invalid HxcIR
description: Caxecraft's pilot exposed a compiler-internal failure when a non-Void function returns from every arm of an exhaustive enum-abstract switch that has no source default. Haxe treats enum abstracts as finite for compile-time exhaustiveness but their runtime carrier can contain other values. The current statement-switch lowering creates a fallthrough exit, then finalization emits a value-less return and HxcIR validation reports HXC9000. The game now obtains PilotScriptName's deliberately identical Int code through an explicit  conversion, which is the clearer implementation for that API; this bead owns the general compiler behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Add a minimal positive/negative compiler fixture for a non-Void exhaustive enum-abstract switch without a default; define and document the strict-C behavior for an out-of-domain runtime carrier value; lower valid source into valid HxcIR and warning-clean strict C or reject it with the correct source-positioned public diagnostic before IR validation; preserve existing ordinary non-exhaustive statement-switch fallthrough; run the focused native compiler matrix and exact snapshot gates.

title: Replace duplicated CLAUDE instructions with AGENTS symlinks
description: Remove the duplicated AI-agent instruction copies at the repository root and in scoped subtrees. AGENTS.md remains the only authored contract; each CLAUDE.md becomes a relative symbolic link to the AGENTS.md in the same directory so tools that discover either filename read identical bytes without repeated maintenance or context cost.
design: Audit every tracked CLAUDE.md before changing it. Replace each regular file with a Git-tracked relative symlink to its same-directory AGENTS.md. Remove wording and workflow rules that ask maintainers to mirror content manually. Add one fast, fail-closed repository check that inventories tracked CLAUDE.md paths, rejects regular-file copies, rejects absolute or escaping link targets, requires the expected relative AGENTS.md target, and proves the resolved file is tracked. Keep scoped AGENTS.md inheritance unchanged. Document symlink requirements and any verified platform limitation in the canonical root AGENTS.md only; do not introduce a generator or a second canonical copy.
acceptance_criteria: Root CLAUDE.md is a relative symlink to AGENTS.md; examples/caxecraft/CLAUDE.md is a relative symlink to AGENTS.md in that directory; no tracked CLAUDE.md contains duplicated prose; all manual mirror-maintenance directives are removed; a focused check fails for a copied file, broken link, absolute link, escaping link, wrong target, or untracked target and passes for the checkout; the check is registered in the appropriate fast governance/CI lane; documentation states AGENTS.md is canonical and CLAUDE.md compatibility paths must remain symlinks; Git diff, fresh checkout behavior on supported CI platforms, formatting/security/governance checks, and the full relevant CI aggregate pass.
close_reason: Replaced both tracked CLAUDE.md copies with same-directory AGENTS.md symlinks; added focused fail-closed link validation, negative tests, pre-commit and governance wiring; repaired the exact Caxecraft shard inventory and comment-only diagnostic-policy drift exposed by the full gate. Focused checks, Haxe formatting, and all 124 governance tests pass.

title: Prepare Caxecraft for standalone product extraction
description:
## Why

Caxecraft is currently haxe.c's flagship QA application, but it should also mature into a genuinely enjoyable, highly customizable voxel game that can move to its own repository. Treating it as disposable example code would undermine both the game and the compiler evidence.

## What

Keep the game, engine, CaxeMap/CaxeFlow/CaxeTest formats, editor, content, RaylibHx/RayguiHx use, assets, and build tooling behind clear package boundaries so they can be extracted without carrying haxe.c compiler internals or losing the integrated compiler QA lane. Preserve a small fixture/sample in haxe.c after extraction that consumes a pinned Caxecraft package or source snapshot.

## How

Design game modules as ordinary reusable Haxe packages that depend only on public typed target/library surfaces. Separate product UX/content tests from compiler-specific generated-C and toolchain gates. Treat the in-game editor as a child-friendly creation and learning environment: visual cause/condition/action cards, safe templates, immediate test play, helpful bilingual feedback, and gradual Advanced disclosure over the same underlying data.
acceptance_criteria: A documented dependency map proves game/engine/editor/format modules do not import compiler internals, repository-only test helpers, host paths, or private generated artifacts; a deterministic extraction manifest identifies source, assets, licenses, third-party locks, content, tests, docs, and build inputs, and a clean exported checkout builds/runs/tests without the haxe.c repository once the public packages exist; haxe.c retains a pinned integration workload that still exercises ordinary Haxe, c.* interop, RaylibHx/RayguiHx, generated-C quality, native linking, and CaxeTest without duplicating the product; CaxeMap/CaxeFlow/CaxeTest and campaign packages are versioned, documented, migration-aware, data-only, and suitable for user-created content; the editor has child-oriented English/Mexican-Spanish onboarding, templates, large readable controls, undo/recovery, visual rule cards, immediate test play, and gradual Advanced disclosure, with a usability pass involving the target 7-8-year-old range and an adult creator; customization/modding has explicit safe boundaries and requires no compiler fork or raw C; asset/provenance, save compatibility, platform packaging, diagnostics, accessibility, performance, and privacy gates survive extraction; no standalone-product or child-learning claim is published before those gates pass.

title: Interpolate Caxecraft presentation between fixed simulation steps
description: Walking currently feels visibly stepped because the 3D camera and rendered actor position use the latest 50 ms fixed-step player state directly. Preserve deterministic collision and gameplay at the fixed clock, but render from the previous/current simulation states using the accumulator fraction so ordinary movement looks smooth. Keep interaction raycasts and authoritative edits tied to simulation state; interpolation is presentation only and must reset cleanly after spawn recovery, teleport, pause, focus loss, and mode changes.
design: Store the previous and current player transforms at fixed-step boundaries and compute a read-only render transform from accumulator/FIXED_SECONDS. Do not increase simulation frequency merely to hide presentation stepping, feed interpolated coordinates back into collision, or make pilot semantics depend on GPU frame timing.
acceptance_criteria: A focused fixed-clock test proves interpolation endpoints, midpoint, clamping, and reset/teleport behavior without changing the authoritative trace; the real move/jump pilot shows smooth bounded motion at representative render rates; generated C remains allocation-free, hxrt-free, and uses structured arithmetic with no application-specific compiler workaround.
notes:
Reported during the first full-world textured terrain playtest on 2026-07-21. Non-critical for the active localization slice, but important visual polish before the showcase is called finished.
Implemented the visual-only interpolation slice. New MotionInterpolation keeps previous/current committed positions, clamps accumulator sampling, and resets without smearing after spawn recovery/teleport-shaped changes. CaxecraftApp advances it only after committed GameSession ticks; camera and terrain visibility use the sampled position, while raycast/edit/HUD/telemetry remain authoritative. Pause, focus loss, recapture, title start, and mode changes clear the partial clock and reset at the final committed body. The natural Haxe test exposed compiler child haxe_c-xge.15.3.1 (consecutive optimizer Boolean carriers); fixed generally and closed with evaluation-order/body-lowering evidence. Added test:caxecraft-presentation to the exact CI shard. Verified Eval/native strict C + ASan/UBSan, evaluation-order, body-lowering, compile-only, canonical split/package/unity/Eval/native O2 snapshots, playable snapshot gate, native macOS Raylib build-only, all-sources, typed boundaries, capabilities, fixture policy, and governance 125 tests. Generated MotionInterpolation.c is structured, goto-free, heap-free, and hxrt-free. Remaining acceptance evidence: run a real interactive move/jump pass at representative display rates (or add a deliberately variable-cadence graphical pilot); this tool shell has no usable desktop session, and the exact one-tick-per-frame semantic pilots intentionally do not claim smoothness.
The final variable-cadence child now supplies the previously missing real-loop evidence: deterministic move+jump at 8/17/25 ms display intervals, 50 ms authoritative ticks, a strictly between-state camera sample, airborne gameplay evidence, identical repeated native runs, and a valid captured framebuffer. The technical acceptance is complete; subjective control feel remains explicitly manual.
close_reason: Implemented and verified presentation-only fixed-step interpolation through focused Eval/native tests and a deterministic real Raylib move-and-jump pilot; generated C stays structured, allocation-free, runtime-free, and human feel remains a documented manual review.

title: Preserve formal Float conversion through inline-call substitution
description: Caxecraft's typed terrain vertex helper exposed a general inline-lowering bug. A helper declared with Float parameters and narrowed inside with c.Float32.fromFloat compiles as an ordinary function, but marking that same helper inline and calling it with Int coordinate expressions makes haxe.c reject the expanded TCall as unsupported Float32 narrowing. Haxe's formal Float boundary must survive inline substitution; applications should not need to disable a natural inline solely to preserve typing.
design: Add the smallest target-owned reproducer: an inline helper accepts Float, narrows to c.Float32, and is called with Int locals plus arithmetic expressions. Audit typed-source normalization and inline-call lowering so argument coercion is made explicit before the body is substituted. Preserve source evaluation order and exact binary32 conversion; do not accept unchecked casts, raw C, Dynamic, or printer repair. Compare the inline and non-inline HxcIR to locate the first lost conversion fact.
acceptance_criteria: A focused positive fixture covers Int local, Int arithmetic, Float local, and side-effectful argument calls through inline Float parameters; generated strict C performs the same checked/specified binary32 conversions as the non-inline form, stays runtime-free and readable, and matches Eval/native expectations under GCC and Clang O0/O2. Unsupported source types still produce the exact source-positioned diagnostic and no artifact. The Caxecraft vertex helper may be restored to inline without changing its public source types or adding a C-specific workaround.
notes: Implemented the target-owned fix and focused regression. Before the fix, InlineFloat32Probe.hx:31 failed with HXC1001 because Haxe inline substitution placed an Int expression directly inside c.Float32.fromFloat. lowerFloat32Conversion now restores the intrinsic declared input mapping before explicit binary32 conversion, so generated HxcIR/C performs Int -> Haxe Float -> c.Float32 and evaluates side-effecting input once. The c-import fixture compares inline and non-inline forms, calls an independent pointlib verifier, checks exact generated-C conversion shapes and one evaluation, stays runtime-free, and is registered in the existing Linux GCC/Clang O0/O2 runtime-smoke matrix. Local evidence: npm run test:c-import PASS; Clang native-only O0/O2 PASS; npm run format:haxe:check PASS; npm run test:typed-boundaries PASS; ci-policy PASS. Caxecraft TerrainRenderer.vertex is inline again; caxecraft-domain snapshot updater, test:caxecraft-playable, and test:caxecraft-pilot PASS. This macOS host has only Apple Clang; the executable named gcc also identifies itself as Clang. The required real GCC execution therefore remains pending the already-wired Linux CI job.

title: Lower switches over primitive-backed enum abstracts
description: Caxecraft localization exposed that haxe.c rejects TSwitch when the subject is a nullary enum abstract backed by an admitted primitive such as Int, although comparisons on the same closed type lower. Add a focused semantic/structural fixture and preserve the abstraction's closed cases while emitting ordinary structured C switch/branches. Do not special-case Caxecraft or erase unrelated abstracts.
notes: Implemented the general fix in CBodyLowering: primitive-backed Haxe abstracts now use their proven body representation as switch subjects. The aggregate fixture covers an Int-backed enum abstract, exact HxcIR/C snapshots show an ordinary structured C switch with default recovery, and strict C11/C++17 native execution passes without hxrt or allocation. Caxecraft's typed locale/message switches are the product-level consumer.
close_reason: Primitive-backed enum-abstract switch lowering, focused snapshots, and strict native regression are complete.

title: Admit statically selected literals at borrowed C string arguments
description: A Caxecraft pickup message selected between two source string literals before raylib DrawText. Both values have static C storage, but the imported-call boundary currently rejects the conditional expression because only a literal node is admitted. Keep direct literals as the default simple proof, while recognizing a bounded closed expression whose every reachable value is a validated string literal.
design: Add a typed static-string provenance fact during HxcIR or C-import argument planning. Admit only expressions whose complete value set is proven to be string literals with no embedded NUL and no runtime allocation, mutation, foreign return, or unknown branch. Preserve Haxe evaluation order and choose ordinary structural C, not raw text. Keep every unproven String expression on the current source-positioned HXC3000 path.
acceptance_criteria: Positive fixtures cover if/ternary and exhaustive closed selection where every branch is a valid literal; generated C is warning-clean and each borrowed pointer has static lifetime; embedded NUL, mixed literal/dynamic values, calls, fields, mutable storage, and incomplete branches still fail with HXC3000 and no artifact; C-import snapshots, native GCC/Clang tests, determinism, typed boundaries, and Caxecraft compile gates pass; documentation distinguishes static-literal provenance from general CString conversion or ownership.
notes: Discovered by Caxecraft's localized +1/+2 pickup message. Keeping the conditional outside raylib DrawText produces explicit safe C today; the feature is not a blocker for the game and must not weaken the existing borrowed-lifetime diagnostic.
close_reason: Implemented bounded static-literal provenance for borrowed c.CString arguments. Literal-only conditional/switch/block selections and typed program-local c.CString propagation now lower to structural runtime-free C; mixed or dynamic values still fail with HXC3000. Full Clang plus identity-verified GCC 16 native C-import lanes, determinism/snapshots, Caxecraft generated-C/native validation, typed-boundary checks, and documentation passed.

title: Lower exhaustive enum value switches without an uninitialized carrier
description: A typed Caxecraft atlas mapping used final column = switch (closedEnum) with every constructor covered. Pinned Haxe exposes this as an uninitialized synthetic local followed by exhaustive assignments. haxe.c rejects it as HXC1001 TVar(column:uninitialized), even though the type checker proves every reachable arm assigns the result. Caxecraft currently uses an explicitly initialized local plus a statement switch, preserving the closed typed mapping and direct C. The compiler should admit the ordinary value-switch form without guessing a default semantic value.
design: Recognize the same proven exhaustive switch-carrier shape already partially modeled by followingSwitchInitializesLocal. Establish definite assignment from the complete closed enum case set, lower the carrier through a typed flow local, and load only after all normally completing arms assign it. Abrupt arms need no value; missing, guarded, open, or non-exhaustive cases remain rejected or require an explicit default. Do not initialize arbitrary unproven locals, weaken HxcIR validation, or special-case atlas code.
acceptance_criteria: A minimized ordinary-Haxe fixture returns and locally binds primitive and direct-record values from exhaustive closed-enum switches; HxcIR contains a definitely initialized typed carrier and validates; missing/non-exhaustive and malformed carrier cases fail at the source or HxcIR boundary; abrupt return/throw arms are handled without fake values; Eval and strict warning-clean native C traces match; generated reducible C is allocation-free, hxrt-free, deterministic, and uses structured switch/if output; Caxecraft can return to the direct value-switch spelling and its atlas pilot passes.
close_reason: Implemented target-owned exhaustive enum-abstract proof for statement/value switches, defensive direct-record initialization, structural ISO C abort on forged values, focused Eval/native regressions, HxcIR diagnostics, and documentation; focused and broad lowering gates passed.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: The generated base content-pack adapter provides a second ordinary reproducer: BaseContentPack.itemMaximumStack returns an exhaustive switch over BaseItem enum abstract values. Pinned Haxe Eval returns correctly; haxe.c reaches HXC9000 because the switch-exit block of the non-void function has no value. This blocks haxe_c-xge.20.4.1's generated-C proof. Keep the direct value-switch Haxe spelling and fix definite value transport generically.

title: Document why Reflaxe.C uses Haxe 5 while sibling targets use 4.3.7
description: The owner asked for a local, evidence-based comparison of the checked-in toolchain pins in haxe.elixir.codex, haxe.ruby, haxe.rust, haxe.go, and haxe.ocaml. Reflaxe.C intentionally differs because its exact Haxe 5 custom-target carrier can establish C platform facts before typing; contributors need a concise warning about TypedExpr/stdlib/server drift and about not copying Haxe 4 Cross assumptions into this compiler.
design: Add one bounded sibling-context section to docs/toolchain.md. Treat sibling pins as an inspection dated 2026-07-20, not a cross-repository compatibility guarantee. Reuse ADR 0007 and the Haxe 4.3.7 carrier audit instead of duplicating their full evidence.
acceptance_criteria: docs/toolchain.md names all five inspected sibling checkouts and their observed 4.3.7 pins; explains in plain language why Reflaxe.C remains exactly on 5.0.0-preview.1; distinguishes project-specific architecture from a general claim that Haxe 5 is always better; lists actionable contributor differences around custom-target activation, typed AST, stdlib snapshots, conditionals, server compatibility, and pin upgrades; changes only this repository and links the existing ADR/audit authority.
close_reason: Documented the 2026-07-20 inspected .haxerc pins for haxe.elixir.codex, haxe.ruby, haxe.rust, haxe.go, and haxe.ocaml (all 4.3.7) alongside this repository's exact 5.0.0-preview.1 pin. The guide explains the target-earned custom-target/PlatformConfig reason, TypedExpr and stdlib drift, #if c timing, server version isolation, preview risk, and contributor rules without recommending a universal Haxe 5 migration. Toolchain policy, CI policy, Governance (111 tests), formatter, and diff checks pass.

title: Add local two-player split screen and controller-first mod hooks
description: After the first complete single-player Creative/Adventure milestone, add local two-player split screen as a deliberate second-phase capability. Both players use the same typed gameplay, CaxeMap, and CaxeFlow model; controller input works out of the box, and keyboard/controller assignment is explicit. The editor and scenario format gain only the general player/team/race/versus/co-op concepts needed for creators to build cooperative puzzle adventures, versus arenas, and races—including It-Takes-Two-like asymmetric mechanics—without hard-coding one campaign or embedding a scripting runtime.
design: Keep simulation deterministic and renderer-independent. Represent player identity, team, per-player inventory/checkpoints/objectives, shared versus private triggers, spawn groups, finish conditions, and viewport/camera policy as small closed typed concepts. Render two viewports from one world simulation and measure duplicate draw/cull cost. Input actions remain semantic and device-independent; support two common gamepads plus documented keyboard fallback, hot-plug/reconnect, assignment UI, pause/focus behavior, and English/Spanish prompts. Preserve single-player file compatibility. Do not network-enable the design accidentally; online replication, rollback, and matchmaking are separate research.
acceptance_criteria: A documented second-phase milestone runs two local players in deterministic split screen with controller-first setup; same-device assignment and reconnect are usable; CaxeMap/CaxeFlow can author at least one co-op puzzle, one race finish, and one versus rule without source changes; single-player scenarios remain compatible; headless traces cover per-player/shared state and input ordering; native CI covers supported controller adapters; render/runtime budgets and generated-C quality remain within declared gates; accessibility and en/es-MX prompts are complete.

title: Stabilize HxcIR source anchors across Haxe server cache reuse
description: The span-lowering performance work found that the pinned Haxe compiler can expose different TypedExpr positions before and after its process-local module cache is populated. In a repeated portable/release request, otherwise identical HxcIR changed an entry block from SpanFixture.hx:47:72-49:3 to 48:3-48:31, and one parenthesized binary expression shifted by one column. Semantics and generated C remained unchanged, but exact HxcIR source evidence was not byte-stable. The span report matrix therefore remains cold; do not normalize this difference away as a test-speed shortcut.
design: Reproduce the first-request/cached-request TypedExpr shapes with the pinned compiler and locate the smallest target-owned stable anchor. Decide whether declaration positions, a typed frontend source-fact record, or another compiler-supported position should own function/body anchors. Preserve precise instruction positions where they are stable. Do not blanket-strip source spans, parse source text heuristically, or treat semantically different source locations as equal. Keep request-local state and malformed/absolute-path validation intact.
acceptance_criteria: A focused warm-server test proves exact HxcIR and diagnostic/source-anchor stability across first, repeated, reordered, and profile/build-changing requests; the fix covers one-expression blocks and parenthesized binary expressions; cold HxcIR snapshots remain unchanged unless an intentional reviewed source-anchor correction is documented; no blanket source-position normalization is introduced; HxcIR, typed-AST, all-source, span, snapshot-owner, and compiler-server gates pass.

title: Make repository writing plain-language and educational
description: The user wants the repository to be a pleasant learning experience. Generalize the existing beginner-readable commit-message rule so source comments, diagnostics, examples, and documentation prefer plain language, define unavoidable technical terms, lead with purpose and observable behavior, and link to deeper contracts without losing precision. Apply the rule immediately to the span-lowering performance explanation that exposed the need.
design: Add a repository-wide AGENTS.md writing contract. Keep normative terminology exact, but introduce it after a short plain-language definition and concrete example. Improve docs/span-lowering.md and docs/test-performance.md so readers understand fixed arrays, spans, borrowing, lowering, runtime-free output, and the distinction between feature compile cost and exhaustive test-harness cost. Preserve deep implementation and evidence sections for expert reference.
acceptance_criteria: AGENTS.md contains a generalized readable/educational writing directive covering code, comments, diagnostics, examples, and docs; the span feature and performance docs define their core terms in plain language and link to deeper detail; focused ownership/policy checks pass; prose does not weaken bounded capability or safety claims.
notes: Implemented the generalized readable/educational writing contract in AGENTS.md and applied it to docs/span-lowering.md plus docs/test-performance.md. The guide now defines fixed array, span, borrowed, lowering, HxcIR, and runtime-free before the detailed contract, and explicitly distinguishes exhaustive test-suite wall time from ordinary feature compile time. Verification passed through capability, typed-boundary, governance, Beads-plan, fixture/snapshot ownership, diagnostics, security, full span semantics/native, full Caxecraft differential/O2, license, and staged guards.
close_reason: Repository-wide plain-language teaching guidance is durable in AGENTS.md; the span and test-performance docs apply it without weakening exact safety/support boundaries; all relevant policy, span, Caxecraft, native, snapshot-owner, and security gates passed.

title: Document the Caxecraft compile-time C seam and cross-target adapter plan
description: Explain every current #if c site at the source and user/architecture documentation levels. Record how the verified custom target supplies the define, that Haxe removes inactive branches at compile time, what the C and non-C carriers do, which behavior remains shared, and why Eval evidence is not a shipped portability claim. Define the long-term adapter and differential-testing plan for Rust/JavaScript experiments without imposing a universal IR or renderer.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every current Caxecraft #if c seam has an accurate inline explanation of its representation or test-plumbing role.
- The example README explains activation, compile-time elimination, supported invocation, current conditional inventory, and user-facing portability limits.
- The domain design inventories every site and gives detailed staged storage/input/render/resource adapter guidance, extraction criteria, and guardrails against scattered target branches.
- Haxe formatting, fixture policy, the Caxecraft C/Eval differential suite, and the centrally managed Caxecraft snapshots pass.
close_reason: Documented every current compile-time seam inline and in the README/domain design; recorded exact activation semantics, limitations, long-term adapter plan, and guardrails. Haxe format, fixture policy, C/Eval domain QA, and central snapshots pass.

title: Centralize exhaustive HxcIR traversal and enforce a validated freeze boundary
description: The Float32 reachability work made a broader architectural risk concrete: whole-program HxcIR traversal is duplicated across runtime-intent analysis, primitive-helper selection, abort selection, use analysis, dependency/header selection, dumping, validation, and emission. Several focused scans intentionally use catch-all cases, so a future child-bearing IR variant can be valid and emitted while remaining invisible to an unrelated dependency or ABI analysis. Separately, CBodyLowering validates an HxcIRProgram but downstream APIs accept the same raw type; RuntimeRequirementAnalyzer states that it requires validated HxcIR while checking only the schema number. Add the smallest output-inert infrastructure that makes traversal coverage and the validated/frozen phase boundary executable before the next substantial HxcIR family is admitted.
design: Add one authoritative deterministic HxcIR child/walk/fold schema with exhaustive closed-variant handling and explicit policies for structural children versus semantic references. Migrate generic whole-program analyses incrementally without changing output. Have HxcIRValidator produce a typed validated wrapper that downstream runtime/helper/CAST-lowering consumers require; raw programs remain available only to builders, malformed fixtures, and validation tests. Treat the validated program as frozen/read-only after construction. Document the node-admission checklist and linear phase boundary. Do not introduce a general pass manager, analysis cache, CAST transform framework, new semantic operation, or universal Reflaxe IR.
acceptance_criteria: An authoritative deterministic traversal covers every HxcIR program/module/type/type-reference/function/block/instruction/place/terminator/failure/cleanup child with no catch-all that can silently classify a child-bearing constructor as a leaf; constructor/sentinel coverage fails when traversal decisions are missing; runtime-intent, helper, abort, and cross-program type/dependency scans use the shared traversal or an explicitly documented exhaustive scoped variant; HxcIRValidator is the only production constructor of a typed validated/frozen program and downstream analysis/emission APIs reject raw HxcIR at compile time; malformed fixtures still exercise raw validation; generated artifacts and registered snapshots remain byte-identical; cold/warm/order determinism, all-source typing, HxcIR negatives, runtime planning, direct imports, native smoke, and full governance pass; docs record phases, ownership, admission questions, and why pass-manager/cache/CAST traversal work remains deferred.

title: Preserve conditional-expression results across HxcIR join blocks
description: The Caxecraft domain exposed a general valid-Haxe lowering defect. A primitive conditional expression consumed directly as a closed-record field or direct-call argument can lower its result in a conditional branch/join, then use that value from a later instruction without a block parameter or stable local load. HxcIRValidator correctly rejects the program with HXC9000 (value is not available at this instruction). Reproduced in PlayerPhysics.step when ternary Float values were record fields and in CaxecraftTrace when a Bool-to-Int ternary was passed directly to mix(). The example currently uses explicit locals/statement assignments, which are semantically equivalent but should not be required.
design: Minimize both shapes independently. Fix conditional-expression lowering so the join defines a value available to its continuation, preferably through the existing result local/load or an explicit block parameter rather than relaxing validation. Preserve left-to-right evaluation and do not reconstruct the value in C. Keep aggregate construction and call argument lowering consumers oblivious to the CFG implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Add minimized positive fixtures for (1) a primitive ternary used directly in a closed-record constructor field and (2) a primitive ternary used directly as a direct-call argument. Both must validate through TypedExpr -> schema-9 HxcIR -> structural C, run under strict C11 at O0/O2, and match Eval exactly. HxcIR must show a valid join/result handoff with no cross-block temporary use, reversed input and repeated/compiler-server renders must be deterministic, and existing evaluation-order/aggregate/function/Caxecraft gates must pass. Add a focused negative validator fixture proving that genuinely unavailable cross-block values remain HXC9000.
notes:
Caxecraft's native ResizeLayout pilot added a second production call-argument reproducer on 2026-07-21: SetWindowSize(requestedWindowWidth, PilotScript.requestedWindowHeight(...)) reached HXC9000 because the first conditional scalar was unavailable after lowering the second inline conditional argument. Materializing both requested dimensions before the direct Raylib call compiles without changing semantics. Remove that documented temporary local once the general join/result handoff is fixed.
The authored-controller scheduler exposed the same cross-block value defect inside an enum constructor: earlier payloads were held as block-local SSA values while a later conditional payload moved lowering to a join. The active fix stages direct enum payloads using the same left-to-right flow-local protocol already used by calls and records; FlowCarrierFixture now owns a minimized enum-payload case.
close_reason: Preserved left-to-right values across HxcIR joins for calls, records, and now direct enum payloads; focused evaluation-order plus function, aggregate, and HxcIR matrices pass.

title: Design and implement an ergonomic hxc dev/watch loop
description: Give reflaxe.c projects one obvious development command that watches the complete declared build-input graph, reuses a safely owned Haxe compiler server, incrementally regenerates and compiles C, and optionally restarts the built program. The design should learn from reflaxe.elixir's HaxeBuildInputs, HaxeWatcher, HaxeServer, mix haxe.watch, status/error reporting, and successful-output promotion, while accounting for C's additional codegen, native compile/link, runtime-slice, header, and process-restart stages.
design: Add an hxc dev or hxc watch surface only after the normal hxc configuration, command router, native build plan, and build command exist; it must be a thin orchestration mode over those same typed models rather than a parallel build system. One-shot hxc build remains direct and deterministic. A long-running dev command owns any haxe --wait process explicitly, keys reuse by project root plus exact toolchain/config/target/profile identity, never attaches to an unrelated external server by default, records a recoverable non-secret cookie, and cleans up children on signals. Discover watched inputs from the effective typed configuration and recursive HXML/native dependency graph, support explicit extra inputs for macro reads, debounce/coalesce platform events, and provide a bounded polling fallback. Preserve the last known-good executable/library while a rebuild fails; publish generated/native artifacts only after a successful phase using existing ownership and atomic replacement contracts. Optional run mode should forward arguments safely, restart only after successful link, and terminate the prior child with a bounded graceful-to-force policy. Human and versioned JSON event modes should expose invalidation reasons, phases, timing, diagnostics, server ownership, and child lifecycle without stdout corruption. Benchmark cold, warm, no-op, single-Haxe-edit, header-edit, and relink cycles. Do not promise source-level hot code reload; this is fast rebuild plus optional process restart.
acceptance_criteria: A documented hxc dev/watch command builds once, watches a canonical inspectable input graph, and rebuilds the minimal safe Haxe/codegen/native stages on create/change/delete/rename events across supported hosts. One-shot build does not spawn or leak a compiler server; watch mode owns, reuses, validates, relocates, and reliably stops its server and optional child process, including stale-cookie and occupied-port cases. Failed rebuilds emit source-positioned diagnostics and retain the last good published artifacts; successful rebuilds atomically publish outputs and optionally restart the program with safely forwarded arguments and exit reporting. Human and JSON event streams are deterministic and tested. Recursive HXML, classpath, config, macro extra-input, generated ownership, native source/header, runtime-plan, toolchain, and removed-input invalidation have executable tests. Watcher event storms are debounced without dropping a final change, symlink/path escapes fail closed, and Ctrl+C/deadline tests leave no orphan processes. A reproducible benchmark records cold/warm/no-op/edit-to-ready latency and guards a reviewed p95 budget. The hello and Caxecraft docs demonstrate the same command without bespoke watcher scripts.
notes: Observed performance signal from generated-C readability work on 2026-07-19: a cold Caxecraft C render with the large HxcIR/static-initialization report enabled took about 47 seconds on a busy development host, while the earlier quick end-to-end run took about 127.7 seconds. These are diagnostic observations, not portable baselines. Before choosing a different implementation language or host, add request-local phase timings for Haxe typing, source-fact capture, lowering subphases (including span lowering), validation, naming/layout, report serialization, output writing, and native compile/run. Keep heavy dumps opt-in; distinguish cold, warm, no-op, one-module edit, generated-C-only native, and full CI paths; cache only immutable facts with explicit invalidation; batch and parallelize independent native lanes. Set reviewed p95 budgets from reproducible idle-host measurements. Eval remains the differential oracle even if a future native hxc host accelerates orchestration or selected analyses.

title: Build a sanitized cross-target semantics research bundle and GPT-5.6 prompt
description: After the active compiler and toolchain priorities are resolved, prepare a self-contained research package for a GPT-5.6 Pro architecture study. The study must examine whether Haxe source, TypedExpr, portable APIs, capability contracts, standard-library parity, and differential tests are sufficient for applications shared across the C, Rust, Go, Elixir, Ruby, JavaScript/TypeScript, and OCaml target family; it must separately identify evidence that would justify any shared semantic analysis or IR. Curate committed source snapshots from reflaxe.c, haxe.rust, reflaxe.go, haxe.elixir.codex, haxe.ruby, genes, haxe.ocaml/hxhx where relevant, and the pinned upstream Haxe compiler source. Do not copy Git history, Beads databases, dependencies, build products, local paths, credentials, or unrelated untracked files.
design: Treat docs/hxc-ir.md and docs/research/repo-patterns.md as the current evidence-based hypothesis: TypedExpr is already the common frontend IR, portable observable contracts should be shared first, and target-specific semantic plans/ASTs preserve target strengths. The prompt must invite falsification and compare strings, numbers, null, exceptions, collections, dynamic/reflection, concurrency, I/O, ownership, ABI, runtime selection, target capabilities, macros, and standard-library ownership. Build the archive from explicit manifests or committed-tree exports, record repository revisions and omissions, scan the staged tree and final archive for secrets and absolute paths, and verify archive contents and extraction.
acceptance_criteria: A detailed GPT-5.6 Pro prompt asks concrete architectural questions, supplies repository context, distinguishes portable contracts from compiler representations, and requests phased experiments plus decision criteria. A machine-readable manifest records every included repository, revision, selected paths, licenses, exclusions, dirty-state handling, and checksums. The ZIP contains only curated committed sources and the prompt/manifest, excludes .git, .beads, node_modules, caches, generated outputs, credentials, absolute local paths, and unrelated untracked files, and passes secret/path scans plus extraction verification. The prompt explicitly evaluates when a shared analysis or IR would help, when it would be counterproductive, how target-native strengths remain available, and which stdlib/capability/differential-test infrastructure is required. The bundle is produced only after higher-priority compiler/toolchain work and its local path and size are reported without claiming the archive is a versioned release artifact.
close_reason: Delivered the reproducible GPT-5.6 Pro cross-target semantics prompt and sanitized 14-repository committed-source bundle. The 29,156,439-byte ZIP passed pinned Gitleaks scans, absolute-path and secret heuristics, CRC and safe-extraction checks, forbidden-path review, and a byte-for-byte rebuild; its SHA-256 is 3d3da78fa84a7ad15be68dc5c4c9d292fece4d507df6cfd694ff53205e5c3e95. The archive is explicitly a local research artifact, not a release.

title: Document TypedExpr and HxcIR architecture boundary
description: Explain why Haxe TypedExpr is already the shared high-level IR, when direct TypedExpr-to-target-AST lowering is sufficient, and why haxe.c retains a narrower semantic HxcIR for C-sensitive sequencing, places, failure, cleanup, lifetime, bounds, representation, and runtime-intent decisions. Record sibling Go, Rust, Elixir, and OCaml target architectures and define evidence-first criteria for any future shared Reflaxe semantic layer. Clarify that changing the compiler implementation language to OCaml would improve representation ergonomics but would not remove the Haxe-to-C semantic gap.
design: Keep HxcIR target-owned and deliberately smaller than TypedExpr. Do not mirror the Haxe AST or extract a universal Reflaxe IR. New HxcIR forms must name a semantic invariant that cannot remain safely implicit until CAST emission. Treat sibling repository observations as descriptive evidence, not normative dependencies.
acceptance_criteria: docs/hxc-ir.md contains the detailed rationale, alternatives, layer ownership, sibling comparison, implementation-language analysis, and future shared-layer admission criteria; docs/architecture.md gives the concise operative rule and links to the detailed contract; docs/research/repo-patterns.md records the inspected sibling pipelines accurately; documentation links and repository policy checks pass without changing capability claims.
close_reason: Documented TypedExpr/HxcIR ownership, direct-lowering alternative, sibling architectures, universal-IR failure modes, evidence-first shared-layer criteria, and implementation-language implications. Verified: npm run test:hxc-ir; npm run test:governance-policy; git diff --check.

title: Polish Caxecraft as a public showcase and compiler QA example
description:
Present Caxecraft as a compelling but evidence-bounded showcase once gameplay, performance, and e2e gates are real.

Create a concise build/run/controls guide, architecture walkthrough, RaylibHx raw-versus-semantic comparison, generated-C inspection guide, reproducible performance report, platform support table, troubleshooting, and an automated fresh-checkout smoke. Add deterministic screenshots or short media only from the tested build and retain enough source-to-generated-C examples for readers to see the direct raylib calls and runtime plan.

The narrative should emphasize Haxe ergonomics, native C integration, transparent escape hatches, and compiler QA without calling the compiler generally complete, production-ready, portable, or faster than C.

Non-scope: a release announcement before gates pass, hand-edited generated artifacts, benchmark cherry-picking, or branding the future Rust/JavaScript experiment as delivered.
acceptance_criteria:
- A new user can provision, build, run, understand controls, inspect generated C, and reproduce the declared benchmark from the documented path.
- Media and metrics identify the exact source commit, raylib lock, platform/toolchain, and configuration that produced them.
- The walkthrough contrasts representative raw and semantic calls and shows their generated direct C shape and exact runtime/build plans.
- Capability/product claims match the machine-readable manifest and every platform/performance statement links executable evidence.
- Fresh-checkout documentation tests and the complete example gate pass without ../raylib, developer-machine paths, or unstated global setup.
notes: Caxecraft is a product incubator as well as compiler QA. Public showcase material should distinguish current in-repository evidence from the later standalone extraction owned by haxe_c-xge.35, while presenting the game and child-friendly creation experience as real quality goals rather than disposable demo scope.

title: Prove RaylibHx packed-consumer and extraction readiness
description:
Prove that the incubated companion can become an independent raylibhx-style Haxelib without forcing a premature repository split.

Stage an exact package artifact containing public raw/semantic source, generated inventories/locks as appropriate, license and provenance notices, documentation, target/toolchain compatibility metadata, and tests. Install it into an isolated Haxelib repository and build Caxecraft as a consumer with no source-repository shortcut.

Resolve the eventual package name and compatibility posture against the existing hxcpp-specific raylib-hx project through the architecture decision. Extraction must preserve the C target as the current supported backend while leaving public APIs free of private compiler implementation imports.

Non-scope: publishing to Haxelib, moving Git history, supporting hxcpp/Rust/JavaScript automatically, bundling raylib binaries, or closing incubation before the evidence passes.
acceptance_criteria:
- An isolated pack/install/consume test builds and runs Caxecraft without private repo classpaths, sibling paths, unpublished generated files, or ambient global dependencies.
- The staged artifact has deterministic contents, appropriate raylib and companion license/provenance notices, version/support policy, ownership documentation, and precise capability/omission tables.
- Public package source imports only stable public Haxe/c.* contracts; private compiler modules and test seams are absent.
- Raw and semantic APIs, generated-source ownership, upgrade/regeneration workflow, rollback, and post-extraction maintenance boundaries are documented.
- The extraction checklist has objective pass/fail gates and identifies any remaining blockers; completing this task authorizes a later split but does not perform or publish it.

title: Expand RaylibHx to a complete precise-or-omitted raylib 6.0 inventory
description:
Grow the coherent Caxecraft core into an extraction-quality view of the complete public raylib 6.0 header after the generic E6 bindgen and lock machinery exists.

Every public type, alias, field, enum, constant, function, callback, variadic surface, pointer, resource, and platform-conditioned declaration must appear exactly once in a deterministic inventory. Representable raw declarations are emitted mechanically from pinned Clang facts. Unsupported or unsafe declarations remain explicit omissions with a reason, diagnostic policy, required compiler capability, and owner. Curated semantic wrappers remain separately owned.

The coverage model must distinguish declaration presence, ABI verification, compile evidence, runtime exercise, ownership review, and semantic-wrapper support. A narrow passing fixture must never promote a neighboring API.

Non-scope: silently binding private raylib internals, treating rlparser JSON as ABI authority, auto-generating unreviewed semantic wrappers, promising every platform configuration, or publishing the package.
acceptance_criteria:
- The complete raylib 6.0 public header has a deterministic one-to-one inventory with no catch-all and no unclassified declaration.
- Supported raw externs regenerate byte-identically from the exact lock and compile against the pinned headers; unsupported forms fail closed with named owners.
- ABI probes and drift reports cover all admitted layouts/constants/signatures and clearly distinguish source additions, removals, changes, and target-conditioned differences.
- Pointer depth, constness, nullability, retained/borrowed lifetime, ownership, callbacks, variadics, thread affinity, and failure behavior are machine-readable and reviewed.
- Representative tests cover every declaration family, while Caxecraft continues to consume only its minimal coherent subset.
- A clean regeneration changes only centrally owned generated artifacts and never embeds checkout, temp, locale, timestamp, or discovery-order facts.

title: Add chunked rendering and measured Caxecraft performance
description:
Optimize Caxecraft only after preserving a measured playable baseline. Introduce a small chunk grid, dirty-chunk invalidation after edits, and visible-face extraction, then select the narrowest raylib rendering technique justified by evidence.

Candidate techniques include instanced cube drawing or generated chunk meshes. The choice must account for FFI breadth, ownership/lifetime, rebuild cost, memory, draw calls, GPU/driver behavior, and generated-code inspectability. Resource-owning APIs require explicit typed ownership and cleanup on every exit edge; they must not be smuggled into the first raw-core binding.

Keep deterministic terrain/gameplay unchanged. Retain the baseline renderer as a regression/oracle configuration where practical.

Non-scope: a general renderer, ECS, occlusion engine, GPU-specific shader architecture, arbitrary-distance streaming, aesthetic effects, or an unmeasured fast claim.
acceptance_criteria:
- Before/after benchmarks record scene, seed, viewport, raylib build, compiler/target, warmup, sample method, frame/update time, draw calls, rebuild time, memory/allocation counts, generated C size, and native binary size.
- Dirty chunks rebuild only when affected; hidden faces are omitted; edits update neighboring chunk boundaries correctly.
- The steady-state loop performs no heap allocation and selects no new hxrt feature unless a separately accepted semantic requirement proves it unavoidable.
- The selected batching path has explicit ownership, deterministic cleanup, failure handling, and sanitizer coverage.
- Results are compared with a small equivalent hand-written C/raylib baseline under the repository benchmark policy; differences and limitations are reported honestly.
- No performance, zero-cost, or optimized claim is added to capability/product documentation unless the reproducible thresholds and regression gates pass.
notes:
Implemented a fixed 4x4 horizontal chunk grid (8x16x8 each) with a checkerboard-proven 3072-face partition and 49152 total fixed face slots. TerrainChunkCache persists derived faces without heap/hxrt, invalidates an edited owner plus only face-sharing boundary neighbors, and rebuilds dirty chunks before the existing two opaque atlas batches; water remains the third batch. Eval/native C + sanitizer probe passes exact maximum, repeated-edit, boundary, corner, and atlas-count cases. Real macOS Memory move-jump-edit pilot passes twice identically: 2744 terrain faces, 3 total terrain draw calls, 20 cumulative rebuilds after initial 16 plus edits, 0 rebuilds on final steady frame, valid cache, state hash f69783bd. Normal generated tree has no benchmark clock/storage, immediate baseline, goto, allocation call, hxrt symbol, or raw-C workaround. Benchmark-only former full-world scanner and chunk-cache variants both compile and retain identical semantic pilot checks. Protocol v5 measures 2 warmup + 12 frames across 7 repetitions on supported clocks. Local timing is honestly blocked on pinned raylib 6.0 Memory/GetTime returning constant zero on macOS (haxe_c-d8f); Linux Memory is the headless timing authority. Still required before closure: paired Linux measurements/report, memory/size accounting, and the acceptance-required equivalent handwritten C/raylib comparison or an explicitly approved scope split.
Added a single Linux-headless benchmark:caxecraft-renderer workflow.
